## The `API` container has a deployable, and it is one codebase deployed twice (2026-08-23, session 144)

**[ADR-083](decisions/ADR-083.md), `status: proposed`, approval line unsigned.** [OVERVIEW](architecture/OVERVIEW.md) section 2's C4 diagram had drawn `API [/api/v1]` inside the Merit boundary since 2026-08-13 and section 3's container table never rowed it, so every endpoint [API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) specifies had no deployable to live in. [`apps/api`](../apps/api) exists, and section 3 rows it.

**Three rulings, and the second is the one with a mechanism under it.** The API is its own deployable, not a server inside `apps/portal`. It is **one codebase deployed twice**, the surface chosen at startup. **Fastify 5** runs it, under `node --experimental-strip-types`, with no build step ever.

**The placement argument is not the origin argument, and reaching for the origin argument would have got it wrong.** [P1 section 2.1](plans/P1-monorepo-scaffold.md)'s route-group sentence is about the admin console's separate origin, and [INFRA](architecture/INFRA.md) puts the portal and the API on the **same** origin, so that argument does not decide this. The sentence that does is [API_CONTRACT section 1](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md): the three UI surfaces are its clients and have _"no privileged back door"_. **A surface that contains the API has one by construction**, because a handler in the same package is an import away. [M04 section 4](plans/M04-trader-portal.md) already said it from the portal's side, _"M4 owns no endpoint"_, and `RI-04` closes it mechanically: section 2 draws three arrows into `API`, and an app may not depend on an app.

**The 404 is what makes the second ruling structural rather than a preference.** [API_CONTRACT section 12](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) requires **403** for a trader session on `/admin/*` and **404** for `/internal/*` from the public origin. 403 is what a permission check returns; **404 is what an absent route returns**. So the route set is selected at startup and the public deployment registers no operator path. A second codebase would have bought the same 404 and a second transcription of the error model, the idempotency rule and the pagination rule.

**The partition is over path prefixes and never over the contract's section numbers, and section 9 is why.** It is headed _"Ops and internal (admin origin only)"_ and holds `GET /health`, marked **Public**, beside `GET /internal/health/deep`, marked admin-origin only. Reading the heading puts the liveness probe on the admin origin.

**Four framework properties measured, not assumed**, against `fastify@5.12.1` on Node `v22.22.2`: it runs under `--experimental-strip-types` with no build, an unregistered route answers **404**, `parseAs: 'buffer'` delivers the raw bytes before parsing that the webhook HMAC needs, and its 49-package tree declares **zero install scripts**, which is what `onlyBuiltDependencies: []` makes an admission decision. **Nothing is installed**: the `catalog:` block belongs to sessions 145 and 147, so `pnpm-lock.yaml` gains one importer entry and no package, and the workspace still declares zero runtime dependencies.

**The dispatching brief's candidate approval clause did not survive being checked.** It read _"section 2's container list and section 3's container table name the same set"_. They do not and correctly never will: `packages/rules-engine` and `packages/rithmic` are rows with no box, because a C4 context diagram draws deployables and datastores and not libraries. The clause is asserted in the one direction that was false: **every container section 2 draws inside the Merit boundary has a row in section 3's table.**

**Two twin defects are reported and untouched, both outside the fence, and the first is the higher-value one.** `RI-04`'s `DEPLOYABLES` list in [`repo-invariants.mjs`](../packages/tooling/checks/repo-invariants.mjs) is the literal `['site', 'portal', 'admin', 'worker']`, so the fifth deployable gets none of its three assertions and the invariant is now narrower than the tree it names. And [INFRA section 2](architecture/INFRA.md)'s Railway table names four services where this ruling needs six.

**The position on this branch:** `node scripts/corpus/gates.mjs check` is <!--gen:gate_count-->33<!--/gen--> of <!--gen:gate_count-->33<!--/gen-->, `pnpm run verify` is clean end to end at **104 files, 1,486 passed and 1 skipped** against `origin/main`'s measured **103 and 1,476**, and `check:invariants` is 7 of 7. **P3's wave 3 was declined because its fences were paths inside a deployable that did not exist; `apps/api/src/**` is nameable now.** Nothing is signed.

## The worker's replay self-audit folds the engine's `replay`, and the second code path is closed (2026-08-23, session 140)

**No ADR.** [ADR-078](decisions/ADR-078.md) ruled the export and recorded this file as the consequence it did not carry: _"`apps/worker/src/batch/replay.ts` is NOT migrated onto the export. The second code path still exists on `main` after this entry."_ It does not any more.

**[M01 section 3.7](plans/M01-rules-engine.md) says there is no second code path, and there was one.** `auditAccount` folded `advanceDay` in its own loop, and **four things the engine's `replay` already expresses were restated there**: the arrival order, the settlement grouping, the assertion handling and the terminal break. Three needed reconciling. The fourth needed deleting: `advanceDay` refuses every day after `closed` or `graduated`, so the old loop broke one day later on that refusal and **the set of folded days was identical either way**.

**A REFUSAL IS RECONCILED BY FOLDING TWICE, AND THAT IS NOT WHAT 3.7 FORBIDS.** `replay`'s contract is that the array is contiguous or there is no array, so it throws on the first refused day and discards the prefix; the audit wants the prefix, so a `ReplayAssertionError` is caught once and the marks before `error.tradingDay` are folded again. **3.7 forbids a second EXPRESSION of the fold, not a second CALL to it**: calling one implementation twice cannot drift from itself. **The second call cannot refuse and the reason is structural** -- `replay` throws on the FIRST refusal from inside its loop, so every earlier day has already folded from the identical prior chain. **The cheaper option is refused rather than unseen**: widening `replay` to hand back the prefix is out of fence AND would reopen a contract ADR-078 ruled.

**What did not move.** B.2's stored row is never re-hashed, and that asymmetry is now **structural rather than documented**: the recomputed side is a `StateHashSubject` with no hash field at all, so there is nowhere left to smuggle a re-hash of the stored row in. B.4 step 1's scoping by `engine_version` and `calendar_revision_id` ([ADR-047](decisions/ADR-047.md)) is untouched in both call sites, and `OI-14` still throws on an empty in-scope set with rows present.

**`replay`'s signature is narrower than the loop it replaces, and the narrowing is asserted rather than applied silently.** One plan, one opening anchor, one calendar for a life. Four equalities are checked across the history -- `account_id`, `plan_version_id` (INV-16), `opened_on` ([ADR-051](decisions/ADR-051.md)) and the calendar slice by identity -- and all four are unreachable on well-formed port output, which is what makes them cheap.

**The refusal path had no test, and it is the one whose expression changed.** One was written against the loop-and-break FIRST, watched passing there, **watched REJECTING two perturbations**, committed on its own, and only then re-run against the engine fold. `GS-071`'s 250-day funded life is compared against the rows `foldAccountDay` itself produced: **250 identical digests, then 43 fields a day**, watched rejecting a dropped settlement.

Drizzle generates types from the **TypeScript** schema, so here the SQL is the source and `schema.ts` is the transcription: the generation runs the opposite way from the one the clause assumed, and drift is a wrong answer at runtime. A mechanical assertion over the `CREATE TABLE` bodies replaces it. **ADR-008's Drizzle choice, its plain-SQL-migrations consequence and its `scopedDb` clause are untouched; exactly one sentence moves.**

**THE MOST USEFUL THING THIS SESSION FOUND IS THAT ITS OWN SUITE DID NOT DISCRIMINATE.** A seeded violation scoping `accounts` by **`user_id`** instead of `identity_id` passed **all 22 assertions**, because the predicate test took its expected column FROM THE RULE and so asserted the code against itself. **The registry is declared and never derived, and three tables are why.** A mechanical FK walk returns 25 tables and is wrong on `treasury_balances.recorded_by` (which would scope **the firm's treasury** to whichever admin typed the attestation), on `impersonation_sessions.admin_user_id` (the admin's identity, not the subject's) and on `sessions.device_fingerprint_id` (whoever shares a device). Each produces a query that returns rows, for the wrong identity, with no error anywhere.

**No ADR.** This is a check catching up to a ruling that was already signed. Seed C (`apps/api` absent) covers the first loop. All three reverted.

Its `covers` line now says so. Deriving the list from `readdirSync('apps')` was refused as a different check with a different failure mode -- a stray directory would become a deployable by existing -- and the change that was taken is the one that makes the next drift loud rather than silent.

## The ADR registry and the session ENTRY table are generated spans, and the CLAIM table never will be (2026-08-24, session 152)

**[ADR-088](decisions/ADR-088.md) is `proposed` and unsigned.** The two tables that every session transcribes a row into are now the generated spans `adr_registry` and `session_entries`, derived from the entry files themselves and rewritten by `gates.mjs generate`. **[decisions README](decisions/README.md) falls from a per-session write to zero; [sessions README](sessions/README.md) falls to the claim and the strike.** That is a reduction and not an elimination, and the entry says so rather than claiming a halving it does not deliver.

**THE BRIEF'S MEASUREMENT REPRODUCES AT 25 OF 25 AND ONLY UNDER ONE FRAMING, WHICH IS THE POINT.** Over the last 25 raw commits [sessions README](sessions/README.md) is touched by 9; over the last 25 non-merge commits, 11; over the last 25 **`--first-parent`** commits, which is one merge and therefore one session each, **25 of 25**. The unit that matters for contention is the session, so the figure is right and its derivation is written down, because a later reader running `git log -25` gets 9 and concludes the premise collapsed. Per file over those same 25 merges: sessions README 25, [STATE](STATE.md) 18, [decisions README](decisions/README.md) 10, [INDEX](INDEX.md) 10, [`gates.mjs`](../scripts/corpus/gates.mjs) 4, [STRATEGY](testing/STRATEGY.md) 2. **The two tables generated here are the first and the third.**

**THE MOTIVATING DEFECT IS ALREADY REPAIRED AND THE ENTRY REFUSES TO OVERCLAIM.** [Session 149](sessions/2026-08-23-session-149.md) found twenty ADR rows carrying a stale status word; today all 85 files are `accepted` and **zero rows disagree with their own heading**. Generation fixes no live drift there. It makes the recurrence impossible, which is prevention, and the ADR argues prevention.

**A SECOND DRIFT WAS LIVE, AND NO GATE COULD SEE IT.** [`2026-08-20-session-95.md`](sessions/2026-08-20-session-95.md) holds **three** `##` sections against **one** ENTRY row, in the registry whose own rule is that a thing not in the index does not exist. [ADR-064](decisions/ADR-064.md) section 1 is signed and says identity is `(log file, section heading)`, so the generated table is one row per section and session 95's two orphans appear by construction. The directory went **145 files, 185 sections, 183 rows** to 185 rows, two ADDED and none removed or changed.

**THE ROWS ARE NOT DERIVABLE FROM THE HEADINGS AND THAT WAS CHECKED AT SOURCE.** Session 49's four rows carry text its four headings never had. So each `##` section gains one machine-readable index line, **backfilled verbatim from the row that already existed, inventing nothing**: 183 taken literally and 2 derived from session 95's own headings. The byte guarantee was proved twice independently, by strip-and-compare inside the writer and by `git` reporting 185 lines added, 0 deleted and 0 additions that were not markers. The index marker is a different comment prefix from the span marker, so it is invisible to `spansIn` and `CI-06g` and `CI-06t` cannot mistake it for a span.

**TEN ADR HEADINGS MOVED, EXACTLY ONE LINE EACH, AND THE `status:` TOKEN WAS NOT TOUCHED.** Five were **enriched** to carry the richer sentence their README row already held ([ADR-064](decisions/ADR-064.md), [065](decisions/ADR-065.md), [070](decisions/ADR-070.md), [071](decisions/ADR-071.md), [073](decisions/ADR-073.md)) and five were **capitalisation-normalised** ([ADR-052](decisions/ADR-052.md), [053](decisions/ADR-053.md), [055](decisions/ADR-055.md), [069](decisions/ADR-069.md), [072](decisions/ADR-072.md)). The plan said eleven: **[ADR-080](decisions/ADR-080.md) was the eleventh and needed no edit**, because its heading already matched the majority convention at 52 files to 16 and it was the ROW that differed. Enriching first puts the better sentence in the document rather than in the index, which is [ADR-034](decisions/ADR-034.md)'s _generate the fact_ rather than its _delete it and point at the source_.

**THE CLAIM TABLE IS NOT GENERATED AND MUST NEVER BE.** A claim precedes its file by design; generating it would delete the reservation mechanism and reinstate the collision it was built after. Its **State** column IS derivable -- it reads `WRITTEN. Struck` exactly when an entry exists -- and deriving it is **named in the ADR as a refused refinement**, because it would pull half the claim table into the generator and blur that line.

**A THIRD OCCURRENCE OF THE MISFILED-REGISTRY-ROW DEFECT WAS FOUND BY THE GENERATOR AND REPAIRED.** An `ADR-079` row sat inside [decisions README](decisions/README.md)'s _Gate closures_ table rather than in the ADR table, written by [session 135](sessions/2026-08-22-session-135.md). Wrapping the span over the run that included it deleted the Gate closures section outright, and **`CI-06n` caught that** at six `gates/` files with no row, which is the gate doing precisely its job on a change designed to make it vacuous.

**WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY STOPS ASSERTING.** `CI-06n` goes vacuous for **two of its five registries**: both directions now hold by construction for `decisions/` and `sessions/`, and it still covers `data-model/`, `golden-scenarios/` and `edge-cases/`. `CI06U_REGISTER`'s sessions-README entry **stays**: its duplicate first cells are [ADR-061](decisions/ADR-061.md)'s T3 case, and generation makes them structural rather than accidental without resolving them. **No `CI-06x` gate was written and the letter stays unclaimed**, on the brief's own condition and [ADR-082](decisions/ADR-082.md)'s line 124: if the rows are generated, the status-drift gate has nothing left to check.

**Flagged and not fixed:** [STRATEGY](testing/STRATEGY.md)'s `CI-06g` row reads _"no document states a quantity a script can derive ... unless the number sits inside a generated span"_. A span may now carry a **table**, so that row understates the gate. It is the `CI-06g` row, not the gate-inventory row the fence granted, and this session adds no gate.

**The position on this branch:** `node scripts/corpus/gates.mjs check` is <!--gen:gate_count-->33<!--/gen--> of <!--gen:gate_count-->33<!--/gen-->, `falsify.mjs` clean-and-dirty over 56 scope cases and 10 loader cases, `pnpm run verify` green. ## Six Railway services, and `portal-api` retires as a fused process name (2026-08-24, session 154)

**[ADR-089](decisions/ADR-089.md) is `proposed` and unsigned.** [INFRA](architecture/INFRA.md) section 2 named four Railway services, [ADR-083](decisions/ADR-083.md) needs six, and the entry that found it declined the second half with _"renaming it is not free: it is a Railway service identity"_ and handed the decision to an INFRA session. This is that session, and **the second half is the one that decides whether anything moves at all.**

**SIX SERVICES: `site`, `portal`, `api`, `admin`, `api-admin`, `worker`.** The count was derived rather than taken from ADR-083's consequence line, because it rests on a claim about the platform that no document had stated: **`apps/api` deployed twice is TWO services and not one service running two instances.** [`surface.ts`](../apps/api/src/surface.ts) resolves `MERIT_API_SURFACE` with **no default**, and INFRA scopes environment variables **per service** in two separate places, so a single service hands both of its instances the same value and there is no second surface. **The failure is silent**: both processes start cleanly and serve a coherent route set, and if the shared value is `operator` the public origin answers **200** where [API_CONTRACT section 12](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) requires **404**, which is ADR-083's whole structural argument dying on one merged environment.

**`portal-api` IS A STALE FUSED PROCESS NAME AND WAS NEVER AN ORIGIN LABEL, and the finding sits one document upstream of where the brief pointed.** [ADR-007](decisions/ADR-007.md)'s `Decision:` line reads _"the four services (site, **portal API**, admin, worker)"_: two words of **prose**, no hyphen. INFRA hyphenated it into a code-spanned identifier, [`apps/portal`](../apps/portal) transcribed that into a string constant, and a test pinned the constant. **A description became an identity in three transcriptions and no ruling**, which is [ADR-074](decisions/ADR-074.md)'s subject from the direction that document does not watch.

**The publish decision is now SOUND in two of the three directions `DELTA_MANIFEST` names, and the entry's own title says which one it is not.** `plan_versions_publish_decision_recorded` proves a simulation run was NAMED and nothing about what it says, because a `CHECK` cannot read another table. `0047` adds `assert_publish_decision_is_sound()` on two attachments: **`OI-29 check A`, the run's status must be `complete`**, and **`OI-29 check B`, when the run names a plan version it must name the row being published**. No table, no column, no index, no `CHECK`; `tables`, `indexes` and `checks` are all unchanged from `0046` and `triggers` goes 16 to 18.

**Check A is written `= 'complete'` rather than `<> 'failed'`, and that is the difference between a control and a patch.** `simulation_runs_status_known` admits four values, so negating the state that motivated the guard leaves `queued` and `running` through, and a queued run has produced no numbers at all. **Check B is stronger than the state it closes**: same plan, different version is the identical defect, so the test is the ROW.

Installing it would define the rule contract's canonical serialization to be `jsonb::text` in passing, and `jsonb::text` **is not canonical over numbers**: measured, `{"a":1.0}` and `{"a":1}` digest differently, so a draft re-saved with a trailing zero would be **refused while being the same contract**. It wins on a fact, that **nothing in `apps/` writes a `plan_version`**, and a control that would run in a code path nobody has written is not a control. **But the application publish path is the only mechanism that could ever close `OI-29b`**, because it can call the TypeScript a digest needs. The two are ordered, not one refused.

**The reservation cited the wrong file and the mandatory grep is the only reason anyone knows.** `plan_versions_publish_decision_recorded` lives at [`0045:236`](../packages/db/migrations/0045_simulation_runs.sql), not in `0004`; `0004` is the right citation only for `0004:183`'s statement of the trigger's cost, which `0045:48` quotes from there. **The instruction exists to catch a constraint cited before a LATER migration superseded it and it caught an ORIGIN cited too early**, which is the mirror case and the same grep. The misattribution stands in the `ADR-087` allocation row's neighbours and in [P3 section 8](plans/P3-ledger-billing-identity.md), both outside session 148's fence, reported rather than edited.

**A fourth check was available, costs nothing, and is deliberately not installed.** `completed_at <= published_at` is not one of the three. A money-path migration that installs an unruled constraint because it was cheap is how a schema acquires rules nobody decided.

## `CI-06/retired-constraints`: the second sweep of a supersession becomes a gate (2026-08-24, session 173)

**[P4-portal-and-site](plans/P4-portal-and-site.md), `status: draft`.** The first phase plan in this corpus written by **consuming measurements that already existed** rather than by measuring from scratch: fourteen module logs, sessions 157 to 170, produced in fourteen containers against fourteen module plans.

**THE HEADLINE IS AN AGGREGATE NO SINGLE SESSION COULD PRODUCE, AND IT REPRODUCES.** Eight of the fourteen wrote the same sentence in different words. Re-derived here by command rather than taken: **98 of 100 `SD-Mnn-nn` rows are `landed`**, against **7 of 111 tables transcribed into [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts)**, an accessor whose entire interface is `__brand`, `identityId` and **`rows()`**, and **zero routes in any deployable**. The database was built ahead of the application across the whole estate, and no module measurement could see more than its own share of it.

**THE PHASING CONSEQUENCE IS THE PART NO MODULE PLAN CAN STATE.** **Ten of the fourteen proposed the same first slice** -- their own tables into `schema.ts` and `scope.ts` -- for ten different table sets, in **one pair of files whose registry is total by a `satisfies` clause**. That is not ten pieces of work. **The transcription is a phase-level artifact**, which is [P3](plans/P3-ledger-billing-identity.md)'s `pnpm-lock.yaml` lesson on a file nobody thinks of as shared. **Who owns those two files across phases is a ruling nobody has taken** and it is the single decision that most changes how many remaining phases can run concurrently.

**P4'S THREE PRECONDITIONS ARE EACH AN ARTIFACT `CI-06` ALREADY PROBES.** A `build` script in any `apps/*/package.json` (`CI-07`), `@playwright/test` in the lockfile (`CI-08`), and `fastify` in the lockfile (`VG-3` **and** `VG-6`). **Each probe reports ARRIVED on the commit that delivers it while its row still reads waiting**, so every artifact-bearing slice must move its `Closure` cell and shrink the unprobeable register in the same commit. This is [session 146](sessions/2026-08-24-session-146.md)'s `CI-04` shape three times over. **`VG-10` is the trap**: it is chained on `CI-07` **AND** waiting on a bucket, the only conjunctive row in the table, so it must NOT be expired alongside `VG-2`.

**THREE OF P4'S FOUR DONE-CLAUSES NAME AN ARTIFACT THAT DOES NOT EXIST.** The slop-score pass (`SS-01` to `SS-08`, a Playwright pass by [DESIGN_SYSTEM section 8](design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md)'s own first sentence) returns zero hits in code; the parameter lint returns zero; `GS-143` and `GS-144` are `blocked`. **Only the disclosure check exists**, at [`disclosure.ts:61`](../apps/site/src/render/disclosure.ts). **All 42 golden scenarios P4's four modules own are `blocked / no-fixture-format`, zero writable.**

## The schema-ownership ruling, and all three of P4's readings permitted the same number (2026-08-24, session 179)

**[ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md), `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED.** [P4](plans/P4-portal-and-site.md) section 10 item 1, its own _"single decision that most changes how many of the remaining phases can run concurrently"_. **A RULING ONLY: no transcription, no table added, and `git status --porcelain packages/db` reports zero.**

**THE FINDING IS THAT ALL THREE READINGS P4 NAMES PERMIT EXACTLY ONE CONCURRENT TRANSCRIBING SESSION.** Once for the estate is one session then unbounded; once per phase is one, because [DELIVERY_PLAN](DELIVERY_PLAN.md)'s phases are sequential and P4 already splits its own thirteen tables into two serial slices; once per module with a literal queue is one at depth 22. **P4 asks which reading is best on an axis the three readings do not differ on**, because all three treat the pair as a resource to be held.

**RULED: reading 3, ONCE PER MODULE, with both of P4's undefined terms defined because each was doing the serialising.** **The OWNER is the TABLE and not the module** -- a table is registered once, by the first session that needs it, and the registration is never re-argued, because the `why` states the table's tenancy rather than the reader's use. **The QUEUE is the TYPE CHECKER and not a document** -- no roster, no holder; a session computes its slice from `TABLE_KEYS` on the tree it opened. **As ruled the ceiling is N, bounded by table-set disjointness rather than by the file.** Both halves are load bearing: either alone still serialises.

**THE OWNER CANNOT BE THE MODULE, AND IT IS MEASURED BY AN AGGREGATE NO MEASUREMENT SESSION COULD COMPUTE.** Over all 47 migrations and all 22 `M*.md` plans: **54 of 111 tables are named by MORE THAN ONE module plan**, `accounts` by **21 of 22** and `identities` by 16, 53 by exactly one, and **4 by none** (`payment_disputes`, `affiliate_statements`, `ledger_halts`, `identity_signal_weights`). Fourteen sessions measured fourteen modules blind to each other, and **"does my table set overlap anyone else's" is the one question none of them could answer.**

**THE COLLISION ALREADY HAPPENED INSIDE THE WAVE, ON FOUR TABLES.** [Session 159](sessions/2026-08-24-session-159.md)'s `M5-1` and [session 169](sessions/2026-08-24-session-169.md)'s `M20-a` claim the same four wallet tables; 159 wrote the collision down and 169 declared the two files _"M20-a's alone"_. **Both are right about their own plan**, which is why a per-module owner cannot decide it and per-table registration can.

**FOUR CONCURRENT-MERGE HAZARDS WERE SEEDED AND WATCHED IN A THROWAWAY WORKTREE RATHER THAN PREDICTED**: the same table twice in [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts) is **`TS2451`**, the same key twice in `TABLES` is **`TS1117`**, a declared-but-unregistered table is refused at the call site with **`TS2345`** naming `ScopedTableKey`, and two branches adding disjoint tables conflict **textually in all three files**. **So [P4](plans/P4-portal-and-site.md) section 9's `pnpm-lock.yaml` analogy is false in the half that matters**: a lockfile keep-both merge is a plausible wrong file nothing checks, and every keep-both merge on this pair is a compile error. **A conflict a machine finds and a machine checks is a rebase.**

**ONE HAZARD IS SILENT AND IT IS THE ENTIRE COST OF THE RULING.** [`scoped-db.test.ts`](../packages/db/test/scoped-db.test.ts) states one table-to-SQL-name map **twice**: `SQL_NAME` at `:256` is `Readonly<Record<TableKey, string>>` and total, `DDL_NAMES` at `:394` is a bare array and is not. Delete one pair from `DDL_NAMES` and `tsc --noEmit` exits **0** while the suite passes at **25 tests against a baseline of 26** -- the drift assertion for a registered, scoped table disappears, **the count goes DOWN, and nothing reports it**. **RULED: [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts) declares the column set the database has TODAY, and the drift assertion stops reading one `CREATE TABLE` statement and starts REPLAYING the migration set.** The fold's vocabulary is **CLOSED AT ONE MEMBER and its default is FAIL**: `ADD COLUMN` is folded, and `DROP COLUMN`, `ALTER COLUMN` and `RENAME` stay offenders that turn the suite red. **The refusal `schema.ts`'s own header describes is NARROWED and never deleted**, so a drifted table now has its full effective column set compared -- a comparison that did not exist for any table before -- and **no table is ever registered by being excused from the assertion**.

Over all 47 migrations, with the assertion's own algorithm: **`ADD COLUMN` on 11 tables, `ALTER COLUMN` on 2, `DROP COLUMN` on ZERO, `RENAME` on ZERO**, twelve distinct tables of 111. **Ten of the twelve are `ADD COLUMN` and nothing else and P4's three are all in that ten.** The two zeroes are the load-bearing numbers: a fold for a shape with no instance would be a vocabulary nobody has checked, so the first `DROP COLUMN` or `RENAME` to arrive turns the suite RED and buys its own entry.

[Session 145](sessions/2026-08-23-session-145.md)'s seed was re-run too: `coupon_redemptions` scoped by `coupon_id` fails naming the column and quoting its DDL. `mid_health` with `card_settled_count` dropped from the transcription fails at 11 columns against 12.

That divergence was found by [session 157](sessions/2026-08-24-session-157.md) and is left where it was found.

**[ADR-094](decisions/ADR-094.md)'S FOLD APPLIES NOTHING TO ANY OF THE FIVE, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** No `ADD COLUMN`, `DROP COLUMN`, `ALTER COLUMN` or `RENAME` touches any of the six across all 47 migrations. **The two later `ALTER TABLE`s that do touch this set are both constraint work and the fold reads and discards both**: [`0028`](../packages/db/migrations/0028_supersede_plan_version_immutability.sql) re-states `correlation_groups_is_a_group` over `cardinality`, and [`0029`](../packages/db/migrations/0029_phone_identity_and_auth.sql) supersedes `identity_signals`' `kind` CHECK with a wider one over ten values, adding `phone` and `phone_carrier` for [ADR-039](decisions/ADR-039.md). **The second is a transcription fact even though it is not a column fact**: the table is read as of the last migration, and a reader taking `0002`'s list as current would be eight of ten.

The comment now names the live constraint alone. **Adding [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts) to that gate's register would have been widening a register to fit a comment**, which is the same move as weakening a gate to pass it.

**`risk_flags` IS THE ONE TABLE HERE WHERE "REGISTERED" AND "TRADER-READABLE" HAD TO BE SAID APART.** A scope rule answers **how a row reaches an identity** and not who may read it. `INV-M7-10`'s no-detector-detail promise is enforced on `evidence_packs` by [`0008`](../packages/db/migrations/0008_risk.sql)'s `evidence_packs_trader_gets_no_detector_detail`, which is a **different table and is not registered here**, and nothing in this rule grants a trader a read of `evidence` or `flag_type`. `account_id` is not the scope because it is **nullable**: `entity_cap`, `payment_velocity` and `name_mismatch` are identity-level findings with no account named, so a derived rule through `accounts` would silently drop exactly the flags that are about the person. **Severity 4 is why the table is money-adjacent**: [ADR-040](decisions/ADR-040.md)'s `G-HOLD-REQUIRED` holds a payout on an unresolved 4+ flag, so a rule returning another identity's flags would hold the wrong person's money.

**`INV-M7-02` IS STILL CONTRADICTED BY THE TREE AND THIS SESSION DID NOT REPAIR IT.** [Session 161](sessions/2026-08-24-session-161.md) measured that the invariant names a **permission** as its enforcement and that [`0026`](../packages/db/migrations/0026_roles_and_grants.sql) creates three roles and no detector role. **Repairing that is a migration and this fence has none.** The `risk_flag_status` enum is transcribed with all four members because a reviewer legitimately moves a flag through them, and the file says so rather than letting the enum read as the missing control.

STORED`, and both are the module's policy expressed in DDL precisely so a careless write cannot make a money notification silenceable or the registration-OTP kind rate-limit exempt. **Declaring them as plain booleans would compile, would satisfy the column-name comparison, and would be a false statement about the one axis nothing here checks.** The two composite primary keys, `notification_preferences (identity_id, kind, channel)` and `otp_send_budget (scope_kind, scope_key, evaluated_on)`, are transcribed for the same reason: they are table-level clauses the column comparison cannot see.

That is [ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md) section 4's fourth row arriving three more times, loud in all three files each time.

**`TABLE_KEYS.length` IS 53 OF 111 AND IT IS COMPUTED FROM THE REGISTRY RATHER THAN ADDED UP FROM THE LOGS.** 30 plus M16's five plus M19's five plus M06's thirteen is 53 arithmetically, and the figure written into the tree is the one read back out of `TABLES` after the third merge, cross-checked against `SCOPE_RULES` and `SQL_NAME` for key-set equality before any number was written. **The other 58 stay unreachable through either accessor.** The count is restated in five places and every one was recomputed: [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts)'s header twice as a spelled word, [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts)'s registry docblock once, and [`scoped-db.test.ts`](../packages/db/test/scoped-db.test.ts) three times as a literal, in a comment, in a test NAME and in two `expect(...).toBe(N)` assertions. **A test name is a document stating a derivable count and no gate looks at it**, which is [ADR-034](decisions/ADR-034.md)'s rule reappearing where nothing enforces it.

**NO TABLE COLLIDED, SO FIRST-WRITER-WINS DECIDED NOTHING AND NO `why` WAS RE-ARGUED.** The three table sets are disjoint from each other and from the 30 already on `main`, measured by set difference over the keys of `TABLES` on each branch against `main` before the first merge rather than discovered during it. **Every session registered its full slice and no session's rows came out.** Session 191's branch had already merged `main` at session 190's four commerce tables, so its side carried four tables `main` carries too; the merged file declares each of them once.

Every conflict here was resolved structurally, by rebuilding each file from `main`'s copy plus whole declarations lifted from the branch, and **`pnpm run typecheck` was run to exit 0 with zero `error TS` after each of the three merges rather than once at the end**. That is [ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md) section 4's central claim holding: the type checker is the queue, and it is the only thing that sees this.

**ALL THREE REFUSALS SURVIVED THE MERGE UNREGISTERED, CHECKED BY NAME.** `identity_links` ([session 192](sessions/2026-08-25-session-192.md)), `dedupe_matches` ([session 194](sessions/2026-08-25-session-194.md)) and M16's sixth table `otp_challenges` ([session 193](sessions/2026-08-25-session-193.md), under [ADR-094](decisions/ADR-094.md)'s `ALTER COLUMN` refusal) appear in no declaration and no registration site in any of the three files; `trading_calendar` is likewise still unregistrable and untouched. **A merge that registered one of them to resolve a conflict would be a session weakening a gate to finish.**

## M10's three integration tables enter the transcription, and the disclosure of a fact is owned by the person it is about rather than by the actor whose event produced it (2026-08-25, session 198)

**THREE OF THREE, AND THE HONEST FORM OF THAT NUMBER IS THAT M10 HAS FOUR SCHEMA DELTAS AND ONLY THREE OF THEM ARE TABLES.** `integration_contracts`, `integration_dispatches` and `support_context_views` are in [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts) and [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts); `SD-M10-04` is `identities.support_contact_ref`, a column on a table [session 145](sessions/2026-08-23-session-145.md) registered first, so it needed no registration and got none. **53 of 111 becomes 56 of 111**, at **1 root, 22 owned, 7 derived and 26 firm**, so **30 of the 56 are reachable through the scoped accessor**. The slice was **computed from `TABLE_KEYS` and not received**: none of M10's three was registered when this session opened. `git fetch origin main` immediately before asserting it and again before the log returns `3c9c2d3` both times, **no sibling of sessions 195 to 203 merged**, so both figures are true at this commit and will have moved by the merge, which is [ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md)'s design rather than a defect.

**M10 IS INTEGRATIONS, SO THE TENANCY QUESTION IS _WHAT IDENTITY IS THIS ROW ABOUT_, AND ON EVERY ONE OF THE THREE IT PARTS FROM _WHOSE ACTION CAUSED IT_.** `integration_dispatches` is **OWNED by `identity_id` with `nullable: true`**, which is `ledger_accounts`' shape: [`0018`](../packages/db/migrations/0018_integrations.sql) states the requirement in the direction that decides the rule, that the dispatches which are not about a person **must not be findable by an identity search that returns them anyway**, and `identity_id = $1` excludes them without a second predicate because SQL NULL never equals anything. The row is about the person disclosed and never about whoever's action produced the event: `GET /admin/identities/:identityId/disclosures` is every field ever sent about this identity, per vendor, and a privacy deletion request and a vendor breach ask that identical question. `support_context_views` is **OWNED by `identity_id`, NOT NULL**, and the row is about **the trader who was read** rather than the agent who read, which is `impersonation_sessions`' question one surface out with the same answer.

**`psp_webhook_events` WAS READ BEFORE ANYTHING SIMILAR WAS CLASSIFIED, AND IT IS WHERE `integration_dispatches` PARTS FROM THE NEAREST REGISTERED ROW.** [Session 190](sessions/2026-08-25-session-190.md) made that table `firm` because its nullable `purchase_id` is **bound by the handler DURING processing**, so a rule through it would answer _whose row is this_ differently before and after a re-drive. `integration_dispatches.identity_id` is decided when the dispatch row is written and **none of `queued`, `sent`, `failed` or `dropped_by_guard` moves it**, so the nullability here is a permanent property of the dispatch rather than a late binding. That ruling was **taken as it stands and not re-argued**, which is [ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md)'s first-writer-wins in the direction it costs nothing.

## M13's five unregistered tables enter the transcription, and the fifth is one the module's own measurement did not list (2026-08-25, session 199)

**[M13](plans/M13-trader-analytics-journal.md)'s tables under [ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md): the owner is the TABLE, the first writer wins, and the queue is the type checker. FIVE OF FIVE, AND THE FIVE ARE NOT [SESSION 164](sessions/2026-08-24-session-164.md)'s FIVE.** `contract_specs`, `fills`, `round_trips`, `journal_entries` and `analytics_snapshots` are in [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts) and [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts). **`TABLE_KEYS.length` IS 58 OF 111 AT THIS SESSION'S BASE AND 61 OF 111 MERGED**, at **1 root, 22 owned, 12 derived and 26 firm**, read back out of `SCOPE_RULES` after the merge rather than added up.

**THE SLICE WAS COMPUTED AND THE COMPUTATION MOVED IT.** Matching all 111 `CREATE TABLE` names against [M13](plans/M13-trader-analytics-journal.md) whole-word returns **eleven**, of which **six were already registered** -- `accounts`, `daily_marks`, `rule_states`, `plan_versions`, `plan_version_sizes` and `certificates` -- and their rules were taken as they stand and not re-argued. **So `daily_marks` came out of [session 164](sessions/2026-08-24-session-164.md)'s `M13-c` list and `contract_specs` came in**, which is `DEP-M13-03` and [M13:249](plans/M13-trader-analytics-journal.md)'s _"Tick values come from `contract_specs`, never from a multiplier in analytics code"_. **164 measured the accessor slice under the pre-[ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md) reading, where a firm read was somebody else's table**; under the ruling a table M13 reads and nobody has registered is M13's session's whatever its class. **That is [ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md)'s "a session cannot know its own slice size before it runs" arriving in both directions at once**, and the count is reported as five of five with the substitution named rather than as five of five full stop.

**`journal_entries` IS THE TWO-COLUMN SHAPE AND IT IS NOT THE TWO-COLUMN REFUSAL, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS WHY ONE IS REGISTERED AND `identity_links` IS NOT.** `identity_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES identities(id)` is the author; `account_id` is **NULLABLE**, because `scope` is CHECKed to `('day','round_trip')` and a day-scoped entry need name no account. **One column is total over the table and the other is not**, so scoping through the account returns a strict subset of a person's own notes -- chosen by whether they happened to attach one -- with no error anywhere. `identity_links` has no such asymmetry: both its columns are `NOT NULL REFERENCES identities(id)` under a canonical-order CHECK, so **a choice is available here and is not available there.** Registering `journal_entries` makes it READABLE and nothing else: `deleted_at` is a tombstone rather than an end state, a scoped read returns soft-deleted rows, and `DEP-M13-06`'s missing grant is untouched.

**`contract_specs` IS `firm` AS A DECISION AND THE CALL-SITE REFUSAL WAS EXECUTED.** A per-identity slice of an instrument's tick value is not a smaller version of it; the composite key `(symbol, effective_from)` is transcribed rather than replaced, because a spec change is another row and that is what makes a figure computed months ago reproducible. A probe naming all five keys against `scopedDb(...).rows(...)` under `tsc -p packages/db --noEmit` returns **exactly one error, `TS2345: Argument of type '"contractSpecs"' is not assignable to parameter of type 'ScopedTableKey'`**, and the four scoped keys compile. **vitest cannot see that refusal at all**, which is why it is watched here and at `CI-01` and not in the suite.

**[ADR-094](decisions/ADR-094.md)'s FOLD APPLIES NOTHING TO ANY OF THE FIVE AND THE FOLD WAS NOT WIDENED.** Re-derived over all 47 migrations with the suite's own multiline match: no `ADD COLUMN`, `DROP COLUMN`, `ALTER COLUMN` or `RENAME` touches any of them, so **none of the five is one of the twelve**. The only later `ALTER TABLE`s in the set are [`0028`](../packages/db/migrations/0028_supersede_plan_version_immutability.sql):179-187 dropping and re-adding `round_trips`' two array constraints on `cardinality` where [`0022`](../packages/db/migrations/0022_analytics_journal.sql):64-66 wrote `array_length` -- **constraint work the fold reads and discards**, and neither name is retired, checked against the 16 `DROP CONSTRAINT` statements less the 9 same-name re-adds. **[`0022`](../packages/db/migrations/0022_analytics_journal.sql) still reads `array_length` on disk and is not what the database enforces**, so the comment in `schema.ts` names the supersession rather than leaving the next reader to find it. `otp_challenges` and `trading_calendar` stay refused and neither is M13's.

**`SD-M13-01` SAYS `uuid[]`, THE TRANSCRIPTION SAYS `bigint[]`, AND THE PLAN WAS NOT EDITED.** [`0022`](../packages/db/migrations/0022_analytics_journal.sql):45-46 and [`round_trips.md`](architecture/data-model/round_trips.md) are `bigint[]`, `fills.id` is `bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY`, and [M13:69](plans/M13-trader-analytics-journal.md)'s cell could never have referenced a fill. **The DDL is the source; moving the frozen plan is `M13-b` and needs an ADR, and this session has no ADR number because a transcription rules nothing.** Neither array is a second path to an identity, because every fill named in one belongs to the same account the round trip does.

**THE `rule_states` GRANT FORK IS UNTOUCHED AND MUST NOT READ AS RESOLVED.** [`0026:157`](../packages/db/migrations/0026_roles_and_grants.sql) revokes `rule_states` from `merit_analytics` while `AN-M13-04` **is** `rule_states`; `ADR-091` is unsigned and is the founder's. `rule_states` was already registered and its rule was not opened. **A scope rule says which ROWS reach which identity through the accessor and a `GRANT` says which ROLE may reach the table at all**; registering grants nothing and revokes nothing, so `M13-a` is exactly as open as it was.

**THREE OF THE FIVE ARE READABLE AND EMPTY**, and that is the correct state for a transcription rather than a gap: **no migration inserts a row into `contract_specs`** ([session 164](sessions/2026-08-24-session-164.md), still true, and `DEP-M13-03`'s consequence is _"every per-instrument figure is wrong in a way that looks right"_), `round_trips` has no deriving code because that is `M13-d`, and `analytics_snapshots` has no batch. **Presence in `TABLE_KEYS` is reachability and not availability.**

**THE TYPE AND NULLABILITY AXIS IS STILL ASSERTED NOWHERE**, now over sixty-one tables, and this session adds to what depends on it: three new `nullable` flags, two `bigint[]` arrays, a `char(3)` currency, an exact-rational price pair, and a `bytea` digest declared as a custom type rather than approximated as `text`. **Nothing here closes that gap and nothing here implies it is closed.**

**THE FOLD APPLIES NOTHING TO ANY OF THE FOUR, MEASURED RATHER THAN INHERITED.** Over all 47 migrations, no `ADD COLUMN`, `DROP COLUMN`, `ALTER COLUMN` or `RENAME` names any of the four. **The two later `ALTER TABLE`s that do touch this set are both constraint work the fold reads and discards**: [`0028`](../packages/db/migrations/0028_supersede_plan_version_immutability.sql) supersedes `wallet_dormancy_review_was_noticed` with a `DROP CONSTRAINT` plus an `ADD CONSTRAINT`, and [`0031`](../packages/db/migrations/0031_payout_hold_and_identity_restriction.sql) adds `wallet_withdrawals_live_freeze_blocks_settlement` and rebuilds an index. **Neither of [ADR-094](decisions/ADR-094.md)'s two unregistrable tables is M20's**, so the fold was not widened and nothing was excused.

**THE FINDING IS THAT ONE OF THIS SLICE'S TWO TRAPS IS CAUGHT BY NOTHING, AND IT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN FEARED.** `wallet_entries.ledger_transaction_id` is `uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES ledger_transactions(id)` and reads exactly like the `hop` `ledger_entries` makes to `ledger_accounts`. ## M04's slice: two of four registrable, and both of the other two are refusals (2026-08-25, session 195)

**[M04](plans/M04-trader-portal.md)'s tables enter [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts) and [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts) under [ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md), minus whatever was already registered. `plans` (firm) and `passkeys` (derived through `users`, one hop) are the two that landed. NO ADR, NO MIGRATION, NO NEW DOCUMENT, and [M04](plans/M04-trader-portal.md) was read and not edited.**

**THE SLICE WAS COMPUTED AND NOT RECEIVED, AND THE METHOD IS STATED BECAUSE THE ANSWER DEPENDS ON IT.** M04 owns no endpoint: its section 4 records one obligation per endpoint it CONSUMES, so the module's table set is what those endpoints read rather than what the module writes. Taken from section 4's thirteen rows plus sections 3.8 and 3.9, that set is **22 tables. Eighteen were already registered** -- `accounts`, `identities`, `users`, `sessions`, `daily_marks`, `rule_states`, `plan_versions`, `purchases`, `certificates`, `kyc_verifications`, `kyc_funnel_events`, `identity_phones`, `contact_channels`, `phone_change_requests`, `economic_calendar`, `economic_calendar_loads`, `impersonation_sessions` and `impersonation_page_views` -- **which is the shape a portal slice was expected to have and is reported rather than argued away.** Not one of the eighteen `why` fields was re-opened.

**`main` DID NOT MOVE WHILE THE SLICE WAS BEING COMPUTED, AND THAT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** `git fetch origin main` returns `3c9c2d3` with `TABLE_KEYS` at 53 at the session's open and again immediately before this section was first written, so **the slice this session computed is the slice it registered**, with nothing already taken by a sibling and nothing forced in by the registry's own totality. **Then `main` moved, and the last paragraph of this section is what that cost.**

**THE TWO REFUSALS ARE THE PART WORTH READING, AND `events` IS THE ONE THIS SESSION FOUND.** `GET /accounts/:id/timeline` is M04 section 4's own row and its `TimelineItem.kind` is `event_name`, so the portal's timeline reads `events`. **It is left unregistered and, on [session 192](sessions/2026-08-25-session-192.md)'s model, NOT DECLARED IN [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts) AT ALL**, because a declared-but-unregistered `pgTable` is one no drift assertion compares. The reason is that **no column can be chosen**: [`0017`](../packages/db/migrations/0017_events_and_audit.sql) gives it `identity_id uuid NULL REFERENCES identities(id)` **and** `account_id uuid NULL REFERENCES accounts(id)`, with **no CHECK tying them and neither one required**, so an `owned` rule on the first drops every account-level row and a `derived` hop through the second drops every identity-level row -- and **[EVENTS](architecture/EVENTS.md) section 2 rows the portal's timeline `TL` as a PER-ACCOUNT view while M04 section 5 consumes identity-level events (`phone.verified`, `phone.change_requested`) on the same screen**, so both halves are genuinely read and neither column covers them. **The payload is the second reason and it is the one no scope rule can reach**: `kyc.dedupe_hit` carries `matched_identity_id` and `identity.merged` carries `merged_identity_id`, so a row whose own tenancy column is correct still names a DIFFERENT identity inside `jsonb`, which is exactly what `INV-M4-06` forbids the portal to receive. **This is [ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md) section 3's named-and-unruled class in a fourth shape** -- not two identity columns like `identity_links` and `dedupe_matches`, but one identity column beside one account column -- **and a transcription rules nothing, so it is reported and no ADR number was taken.**

**`otp_challenges` IS THE SECOND AND IT IS ALREADY RULED.** [`0029`](../packages/db/migrations/0029_phone_identity_and_auth.sql) writes `ALTER COLUMN email_normalized DROP NOT NULL`, [ADR-094](decisions/ADR-094.md) closes the fold's vocabulary at one member with a default of FAIL, and [session 193](sessions/2026-08-25-session-193.md) already executed the refusal. M04 consumes `POST /auth/otp`, so the table is in this slice and it stays out. **Widening the fold to fit it would be weakening a gate to pass it.**

**REGISTERING `plans` FALSIFIED A COMMENT ON A TABLE THIS SESSION DID NOT OWN, AND THE REPAIR IS IN THE SAME DIFF.** [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts)'s `plan_breaker_state` block read _"`plan_id` CARRIES NO `.references()` because `plans` is not one of this file's tables"_. It is one now. The file's rule is that a column carries a reference **only when** the `CREATE TABLE` body declares the FK inline **and** the target is one of this file's tables; both `0004:59` and `0016:127` always declared theirs inline, so **the second half of the condition changed and the first never did**, and `plan_versions.plan_id` and `plan_breaker_state.plan_id` now claim the reference the rule permits. **This is [ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md)'s "a session cannot know its own slice size before it runs" arriving as PROSE rather than as a table**: a registration made a sentence elsewhere in the file untrue, and leaving it would have been the cheaper move and the wrong one.

**NEITHER NEW TABLE CARRIES A LATER COLUMN CHANGE**, re-derived over all 47 migrations with the suite's own multiline match rather than inherited: no `ADD`, `DROP` or `ALTER COLUMN` and no `RENAME` touches `plans` or `passkeys`, so **the fold applies nothing to either and both comparisons are byte-identical to a `CREATE TABLE` read**. The eight drifted tables already registered are unaffected.

**FOUR CONTROLS WERE WATCHED FIRING, EACH RESTORED AFTER.** **The trap first, because it is the one that compiles**: `passkeys.via` set to `plans`, a firm key, leaves `pnpm run typecheck` at **exit 0 with zero `error TS`** and turns **two** assertions red, the bounded chain one saying _"passkeys derives through passkeys -> plans, and plans is firm, so a scoped read of it constructs no predicate and throws"_. **`transports` deleted from the transcription** fails `passkeys: the TS column set equals the set as of the LAST migration`, so the per-table assertion is live on this session's own table. **`plans` declared `owned` on `code`** is refused by the DDL check quoting `code text NOT NULL UNIQUE` back against the requirement that an owned column declare `REFERENCES identities(id)`, which is the check that exists because a rule asserted against itself passes. **`TS2739` naming `plans` and `passkeys`** was watched before `SQL_NAME` was completed, which is [ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md) section 5's mapped type doing the job the hand-maintained array used to fail at.

**TWO GAPS ARE NAMED AND NEITHER IS CLOSED, AND NOTHING IN THIS SESSION IMPLIES OTHERWISE.** **Column TYPE and NULLABILITY are still asserted nowhere**, now across 58 registered tables, which is why `credential_id` and `public_key` are declared as the `bytea` custom type and `transports` as a `text[]` array rather than approximated: on the one axis nothing checks, a transcription that lies compiles and passes. **`passkeys.credential_id` is UNIQUE across the whole table rather than per user**, which is WebAuthn's rule and not a scope, and the `why` says so, because uniqueness is the kind of fact that reads like a reason to skip the hop.

**THE PREDICTED CONFLICT ARRIVED, IN FIVE FILES, AND IT COST ONE RESOLUTION.** [Session 197](sessions/2026-08-25-session-197.md) merged first, so **`main` moved from `3c9c2d3` to `92ea3d9` while this branch was open** and [ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md) section 4's fourth row happened exactly as written: a textual conflict in [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts), [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts), [`scoped-db.test.ts`](../packages/db/test/scoped-db.test.ts), this file and [sessions/README](sessions/README.md). **The two table sets are disjoint** -- M08's `affiliates`, `affiliate_creatives` and `affiliate_clicks` against M04's `plans` and `passkeys` -- **so every table survived, no `why` was re-argued, and first-writer-wins decided nothing.**

## Integration batch A: sessions 196, 202 and 195 land together, and ADR-092's one predicted collision is settled by first-writer-wins (2026-08-25, integration session)

**THE REGISTRY IS 64 OF 111 AND 64 WAS RECOMPUTED FROM `TABLE_KEYS.length` RATHER THAN ADDED UP FROM THE THREE BRANCHES.** At **1 `root`, 26 `owned`, 11 `derived` and 26 `firm`**, so **38 of the 64 are reachable through the scoped accessor** and the other 47 tables through neither. **No ADR, no session number, no migration, no new document; an integration transcribes nothing and rules nothing.**

**THE PER-SESSION COUNT IS SIX, ZERO AND TWO, AND THE ZERO IS THE POINT.** [Session 196](sessions/2026-08-25-session-196.md) registered six -- `payout_requests`, `payout_transfers`, `wallet_entries`, `wallet_withdrawals`, `wallet_spend_limits` and `wallet_dormancy`. [Session 202](sessions/2026-08-25-session-202.md) registered **none**, because all four tables it claimed are 196's four and 196 merged first. [Session 195](sessions/2026-08-25-session-195.md) registered two, `plans` and `passkeys`. **56 to 62 to 62 to 64.**

**[ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md) SECTION 8 ITEM 4'S ONE NAMED INTERSECTING PAIR IS RESOLVED THE WAY THE RULING SAYS AND NOT BY JUDGEMENT.** The owner is the TABLE, the first writer wins, a registration is never re-argued: 196's four declarations and 196's four `why` fields stand whole and 202's four rows come out whole. **Nothing was merged, averaged or picked between.** Both texts were read before either was dropped, which is the check the rule needs and does not itself perform.

**THE TWO SESSIONS AGREE, AND THE AGREEMENT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** All four tables are `class: 'owned'`, `column: 'identity_id'`, `nullable: false` in both transcriptions, and the four `pgTable` declarations are **byte-identical in code** on the two branches, differing only in comment and `why` prose. Two sessions reading [`0011`](../packages/db/migrations/0011_wallet.sql) independently, with no roster and no coordination, produced the same column sets, the same types and the same tenancy. **There is no disagreement for the founder to rule on**, which is a different and better outcome than a disagreement resolved by a merger.

## Tranche B integration: five transcription branches land as one, then tranche A lands first and the `plans` collision is settled by dropping session 203's copy, registry 80 of 111 (2026-08-25, session 204)

**FIVE OF FIVE, MERGED IN THE DISPATCHED ORDER, THEN `origin/main` MERGED A SIXTH TIME AFTER TRANCHE A OVERTOOK THIS BRANCH.** [Session 198](sessions/2026-08-25-session-198.md)'s M10 three, [session 203](sessions/2026-08-25-session-203.md)'s M21 two, [session 199](sessions/2026-08-25-session-199.md)'s M13 five, [session 201](sessions/2026-08-25-session-201.md)'s M18 three and [session 200](sessions/2026-08-25-session-200.md)'s M17 four. **The registry reaches 80 of 111**, at **1 root, 34 owned, 14 derived and 31 firm**, so **49 of the 80 are reachable through the scoped accessor**. **No ADR, no migration, no new document and no transcription**: an integration session rules nothing, and this one wanted no ADR number, which was the stop condition it never reached.

**`pnpm run typecheck` WAS RUN AFTER EACH OF THE SIX MERGES AND NOT ONLY AT THE END**, exit 0 with zero `error TS` every time. That is what makes the table below a record rather than a reconstruction: a tail-splice is caught at the merge that caused it, so the bisect never had to run.

**The arithmetic is the check and it is stated rather than implied.** Tranche B alone is 56 + 3 + 2 + 5 + 3 + 4 = **73**. Tranche A took `main` to **64**, its eight being M05's six, M04's `passkeys` and `plans`, with M20's four rebasing out under first-writer-wins. **The intersection of the two tranches is exactly one table, `plans`**, so the merged registry is 64 + 17 - 1 = **80**, and the suite is 85 + 16 = **101**. Read back off the merged tree: `TABLE_KEYS` **80**, `SCOPE_RULES` **80**, `SQL_NAME` **80**, `pgTable` declarations **80**, duplicate keys **0**.

**THE `plans` COLLISION BECAME REAL AND WAS SETTLED THE WAY ADR-092 SAYS, NOT BY MERGING THE TWO COPIES.** [ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md) section 8 item 4 named one intersecting pair (`M5-1` and `M20-a`); this is the second, found after dispatch. **`main` carried M04's copy first, so M04's stays and session 203's was DROPPED** from [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts), from [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts)'s imports, `TABLES` and `SCOPE_RULES`, and from `SQL_NAME` in the suite. `plans` now appears **exactly once in each of those five sites**, and the surviving `why` is session 195's. **The failure mode if it had been merged instead of dropped is `TS1117`, which is loud, and it was never reached.**

**THE AGREEMENT WAS VERIFIED AT BOTH SOURCES BEFORE THE DROP, NOT ASSUMED.** Both sessions declare `plans` **`firm`**, both give no scope column and say there is no correct one, and both give the same four reasons in different words: the catalogue's root has no identity column, the link runs the other way (a version names its plan, an account names its version), `is_active` delists and never deletes, and it is `plan_versions`' reason one hop up. **Two sessions that never spoke reached the same ruling, so there was nothing to escalate and the registration was not re-argued.** Had they named a different class or scope column, that would have been the founder's question rather than this session's, and it would have been reported instead of resolved.

**EVERY RESOLUTION WAS STRUCTURAL AND NONE WAS A HUNK-LEVEL KEEP-BOTH.** Five of the six conflicted textually in all five files. Each of the three code files was rebuilt from **one side's whole copy** and the other's **WHOLE declarations** re-appended, after asserting the incoming branch byte-identical to its base from its first declaration to its last. **On the tranche A merge the direction was deliberately inverted**: the files were rebuilt from **`main`'s** copy rather than this branch's, precisely so that M04's `plans` is the copy that survives, and this branch's sixteen non-`plans` declarations were appended to it. The hazard is measured rather than feared: every `pgTable` ends with the same `createdAt` / `updatedAt` / `});` tail, so git aligns the hunk on lines two unrelated tables merely happen to share, each side ends MID-DECLARATION, and a keep-both splices one table's columns into another's object literal.

**ONE LIFT WAS REFUSED RATHER THAN TRUNCATED, AND THAT REFUSAL IS WHY THE DECLARATION IS WHOLE.** [Session 199](sessions/2026-08-25-session-199.md)'s `analytics_snapshots` uses the three-argument `pgTable` form for its composite primary key and closes on a bare `);` where every other declaration closes on `});`. The splitter ran off the end and **threw instead of ending the declaration at the wrong line**. **A resolver that had silently taken the last `});` it found would have produced exactly the splice this session existed to avoid, and it would have COMPILED**, because what follows a truncated declaration is another valid one.

**THE REGISTRY SIZE IS A LITERAL IN SIX PLACES, NOT FIVE, AND EVERY ONE WAS RECOMPUTED FROM `TABLE_KEYS.length` RATHER THAN INCREMENTED.** The sixth is [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts)'s drifted-table sentence, which moves only when a registered table carries a later `ADD COLUMN`. **Both tranches moved it and each knew only its own half**: tranche A made it NINE for `payout_requests`, tranche B made it NINE for `promotional_credit_grants`, and **the merged answer is TEN carrying both**. That was **derived** by replaying every `ALTER TABLE` across all 47 migrations with the suite's own multiline match rather than taken from either side: **ten registered tables carry `ADD COLUMN` and ZERO carry `DROP COLUMN`, `ALTER COLUMN` or `RENAME`**, so [ADR-094](decisions/ADR-094.md)'s closed vocabulary still refuses nothing that is registered. **Two sides each incrementing a count to the same number is the shape that merges green and wrong**, and deriving it is the only thing that catches it.

**ONE STALE FIGURE THAT BELONGED TO NO MERGED SESSION WAS CORRECTED AND IS NAMED RATHER THAN QUIET.** The `` `identity_links` IS ONE OF THE NN `` sentence is 111 minus the registry size and arrived on `92ea3d9` reading **58** where the tree carried 56 and the figure should have been 55, disagreeing with `the other 55` two lines above it. [Session 203](sessions/2026-08-25-session-203.md) caught the same thing from its own side. Both now derive from the one number.

**THE SEVEN DELIBERATE REFUSALS ALL SURVIVE ALL SIX MERGES, CHECKED BY NAME AFTER EVERY ONE**, each at zero occurrences in `TABLES` and zero in `SCOPE_RULES`: `identity_links`, `attributions`, `affiliate_commissions`, `dedupe_matches`, `otp_challenges`, `trading_calendar` and `competitor_plan_models`. **`identity_links` still carries no `pgTable` declaration at all**, which is session 192's stronger form of the refusal and was not "fixed" here; `affiliate_commissions` stays out because `DerivedRule.via` is typed `TableKey` and cannot name the unregistered `attributions`, and **no merge, in either tranche, made that registrable**.

**`CI-06u` CAUGHT THE KEEP-BOTH HAZARD IN THE DOCUMENTS RATHER THAN THE CODE, TWICE.** Keep-both is right for an APPENDED section and wrong for a KEYED registry row, and both kinds live in [`sessions/README`](sessions/README.md). Sessions 198 to 201 each struck their own claim row in place, so the two sides of the hunk held one key in two states and keeping both made the register answer _has 198 been written_ with yes and no at once; the tranche A merge did the same for 202. **The struck `WRITTEN` row was kept in every case and the stale `CLAIMED` duplicate dropped**, and no row's text was edited. All of 194 to 203 now read struck, once each, in numeric order.

**The position:** `pnpm run typecheck` exit 0 with **zero `error TS`**; [`scoped-db.test.ts`](../packages/db/test/scoped-db.test.ts) **101**; `pnpm run gates` <!--gen:gate_count-->33<!--/gen--> of <!--gen:gate_count-->33<!--/gen-->; `pnpm run verify` exit 0. **No session's STATE section or log was edited**, all nine carried through the six merges untouched, and nothing needed a file outside the fence. **`E2` READ REMAINS PENDING on the sixteen money-path tables this branch adds** and on the sixty-four before them, which this session neither discharges nor narrows.

## M02's seven tables enter the transcription, and the one plan that is not approved does not reach any rule written here (2026-08-25, session 205)

**Seven of seven, and nothing had been claimed by a sibling.** `account_status_history`, `platform_account_refs`, `provisioning_queue`, `platform_entitlements` (all [`0007`](../packages/db/migrations/0007_accounts.sql)), `ingest_files`, `raw_ingest_rows` (both [`0013`](../packages/db/migrations/0013_ingest.sql)) and `reconciliations` ([`0014`](../packages/db/migrations/0014_marks.sql)) are in [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts) and [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts). **80 of 111 becomes 87 of 111**, 33 `firm` and 54 reachable, every figure recomputed from `TABLE_KEYS.length`. **Three migrations for one module** is M2's shape rather than a mis-derivation: the provisioning half sits in the accounts file, the ingest half in `0013`, and the reconciliation half beside `daily_marks`.

**THE PREMISE WAS VERIFIED BEFORE A LINE WAS TRANSCRIBED, AND IT HOLDS.** [M02](plans/M02-rithmic-bridge.md) is the ONE plan in the corpus that is not `approved`, held at `review` by [ADR-005](decisions/ADR-005.md) pending the Rithmic vendor call. Both stop conditions were checked rather than assumed. **All six schema deltas `SD-M2-01` to `SD-M2-06` are already folded into merged migrations**, checked one at a time against the migration set, so there is no table in the slice whose `CREATE TABLE` is unmerged -- `SD-M2-02`'s word _"new"_ for `platform_account_refs` is the plan's, written before the reconciliation landed it. **And not one of the sixteen `V-M2-nn` rows changes a tenancy column or a join path.** Twelve move the wire format, the parser, cadence, corrections, sandbox and streaming. The four carrying `Blast: model` were read individually: `V-M2-05` lands on the already-registered `daily_marks`; **`V-M2-09` is the closest and it stops one column short**, moving the BILLING UNIT while `platform_entitlements.account_id` stays `NOT NULL` and `platform_user_ref` stays `text NULL` with no foreign key; `V-M2-10` would change `platform_account_refs`' PRIMARY KEY, which under this rule is the burn rather than the tenancy; `V-M2-11` would empty two tables of rows and change no rule about whose rows they are. **What is provisional in these tables is their CONTENT and not their CLASS**, and the transcription says so at the point of use.

**FIVE `derived` THROUGH `accounts` IN ONE HOP AND TWO `firm`.** `ingest_files` is firm because a vendor file carries rows for every account that traded the session, its only foreign key points at ITSELF, and the tenancy runs the other way -- `fills`, `raw_ingest_rows` and `reconciliations` all point IN. The quarantine machine is why the grain is the file: a `quarantined` file has committed no downstream rows, so at the moment the row matters most there is no account row anywhere to reach it through.

**`raw_ingest_rows` CARRIES THE SLICE'S FINDING, AND THE WRONG RULE IS GREEN.** The forward derivation through the firm `ingest_files` is the trap [ADR-094](decisions/ADR-094.md) already names and the bounded chain assertion catches it. **The REVERSE edge is worse and nothing in the package catches it**: `fills.raw_row_id bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES raw_ingest_rows(id)` is a declared foreign key in the direction the derived-rule assertion accepts, so `derived via fills, localColumn id, foreignColumn raw_row_id, semi-join` was **SEEDED AND WATCHED PASSING -- `typecheck` exit 0 and the suite GREEN at 108 of 108** -- rendering `exists (select 1 from "fills" where ("fills"."raw_row_id" = "raw_ingest_rows"."id" and exists (select 1 from "accounts" ...)))`. It answers a DIFFERENT QUESTION: which raw rows produced a fill on this person's accounts, rather than whose raw row this is. Only some raw rows become fills, and an EOD balance row, an unparsed row and **every row of a quarantined file** become none -- so the reading silently drops exactly the rows a dispute is argued from. **That is [session 202](sessions/2026-08-25-session-202.md)'s `wallet_entries` finding recurring on a different table: the green suite is not the check, the reading of the DDL is.**

**Two more seeds watched failing loudly.** `reconciliations` declared `derived via ingestFiles` fails the bounded chain assertion **by name**; `provisioning_queue.payload_hash` deleted from the transcription fails the per-table drift assertion with the column named. Both files were restored and `git status --porcelain` reported clean before the next command ran.

**[ADR-094](decisions/ADR-094.md)'S FOLD APPLIES NOTHING TO ANY OF THE SEVEN**, re-derived over all 47 migrations with the suite's own multiline match: no `ALTER TABLE` names any of them in any shape, so all seven are among the 99 undrifted. **The drifted-table sentence was DERIVED rather than left alone**, because it is the one number nothing in the suite checks: replaying `ADD COLUMN` across the whole registry returns **exactly ten**, and **zero** carry a refused verb, so the sentence stays **TEN** and now reads _of the eighty-seven_.

**`payload_hash` and `sha256` are `bytea` CUSTOM TYPES and not `text`**, on the file's own rule, and two enums join from [`0001`](../packages/db/migrations/0001_extensions_and_enums.sql): `provisioning_status`, whose `confirmed_inferred` is a distinct state rather than a synonym, and `ingest_file_status`. The binding rule over the pair -- `set_risk` may never reach `confirmed_inferred` -- stays a table CHECK and is not restated as a type.

**ONE NON-EDIT IS REPORTED RATHER THAN MADE**, on [session 203](sessions/2026-08-25-session-203.md)'s precedent. Registering these two ingest tables satisfies [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts)'s _"only when"_ condition for `daily_marks.ingest_file_id` and for `fills.ingest_file_id` and `fills.raw_row_id`, whose comments read _"not one of this file's tables"_ and are wrong after this branch merges. `.references()` is compared by nothing in this package and touching a table that is not this slice's is the tail-splice hazard tranche 1 paid for, so all three are left and named.

## `P4-d`: Fastify enters the catalog and the route registry is a DIRECTORY LISTING, so the fifteen route slices behind it stop being serial (2026-08-25, session 209)

**[ADR-100](decisions/ADR-100.md), `accepted`. THIS REPOSITORY NOW ANSWERS AN HTTP REQUEST.** `apps/api` composes route modules and serves [API_CONTRACT section 9](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md)'s liveness row, and both of ADR-083's deployments were watched doing it over a real socket.

**THE DELIVERABLE IS THE SHAPE, WHICH IS WHAT `P4-d`'s ROW SAID IT WAS.** That row's money column is the only one in [P4](plans/P4-portal-and-site.md) section 8 carrying a consequence instead of a yes or a no: _"the registry's SHAPE decides whether M19's seven route slices serialize."_ **A route module is one file under `apps/api/src/routes/` that default-exports `defineRoutes({ name, routes })`, `discoverRouteModules` reads the directory and imports every `.ts` file in sorted order, and no file outside that directory imports anything inside it.** So a slice that adds a route **adds one file and edits nothing another slice edits**, and the **fifteen** slices [P4](plans/P4-portal-and-site.md) section 9 rows behind that file -- `P4-f`, M03's two, M05's two, M16's three and [M19's seven](sessions/2026-08-24-session-168.md) -- touch fifteen disjoint paths and merge in any order.

**`apps/api/src/routes/index.ts`, WHICH SECTION 9 NAMES AS A BARRIER, IS NOT CREATED AND IS NOT NEEDED.** There is nothing for a later slice to register into. That is the barrier removed rather than scheduled, and it is the largest single lever this phase had on every later phase's concurrency.

**THE THREE PROPERTIES AN ARRAY GIVES FREE WERE BOUGHT BACK RATHER THAN ASSUMED**, each watched in [`registry.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/registry.test.ts): `defineRoutes` is typed `(m: RouteModule) => RouteModule` so `tsc` reports a malformed module **in the module's own file**; discovery **throws** on any `.ts` file that is not a valid module and on a name that is not its filename stem; and `compose` refuses a duplicate `METHOD /path` across the module set **before** the surface filter. **That third one is strictly stronger than an array**, which would have merged both copies and left Fastify to refuse the second registration at startup.

**A MODULE DECLARES A PATH AND NEVER A SURFACE, AND THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO FIELD FOR ONE.** `compose` classifies every declared path with [`surface.ts`](../apps/api/src/surface.ts)'s `classifyPath` and registers only what this process serves, so [ADR-083](decisions/ADR-083.md) section 4's 404 stays the router's. **Watched in two processes composing the SAME module set**: `GET /api/v1/internal/jobs` answered **404 `application/problem+json`** on `api` and **200** on `api-admin`, and the public process logged `"registered":["GET /health"],"withheld":["GET /internal/jobs"]`. No permission check ran on either side.

**THE `VG-12` ADMISSION IS 46 PACKAGES AND THE CHECK WAS RUN RATHER THAN WAVED THROUGH.** Closure **233 to 279**, 0 removed; **46 of 46** resolve to a registry entry carrying a `sha512` integrity hash and none to a tarball, a git reference or a link; **zero** declare `preinstall`, `install` or `postinstall`, so `onlyBuiltDependencies: []` is unchanged; `pnpm audit --audit-level=low` exit 0. `5.12.1` is the version [ADR-083](decisions/ADR-083.md) section 5 measured and is also what the registry resolves as latest.

**`VG-3` AND `VG-6` MOVE OFF THE LOCKFILE ONTO `scopedDb` NAMED UNDER `apps/api/src`, AND THE GATE WAS WATCHED FAILING ON THE GOOD NEWS FIRST.** `CI-06/vg-inventory` went to **29 of 30** on the catalog commit, naming both rows, **before either cell moved**. The new artifact is [API_CONTRACT section 1](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md)'s own mechanism for what both rows are about -- _"Every authenticated handler resolves the caller to an identity and reads through `scopedDb(identity)`"_ -- and a lockfile key could only ever say a server was possible. The probe was watched firing on a seeded `scopedDb` and **not** firing on `scopedDbFixture`.

**THE FALSIFY SEED BROKE, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN WORKING RATHER THAN A DEFECT.** [`falsify.mjs`](../scripts/corpus/falsify.mjs)'s `CI-06/vg-inventory` seed planted a `fastify` key while both rows waited on one; with a real key present the anchor stopped existing and the case **threw** instead of passing, taking `pnpm run falsify` to 1 problem. **A harness that had matched loosely would have appended a second key and reported green.** The seed moved onto the live artifact and scope cases went **69 to 70**.

**TWO FINDINGS ARE REPORTED AND NOT REPAIRED, AND NEITHER IS THIS FENCE'S.**

- **NO `start` SCRIPT IN THIS ESTATE HAS EVER RUN.** `node --experimental-strip-types` resolves a specifier to the file it names and does not map `./x.js` onto `x.ts`. `apps/api`, `apps/admin` and `apps/worker` all declare that runtime and all three die with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on their own first relative import. **[ADR-083](decisions/ADR-083.md) is not edited and its ruling 3 is not weakened**: its section 5 measured a scratch program whose specifiers matched, and this tree's convention was not in that measurement. **The repair was EXECUTED in a scratch copy to prove it sufficient** -- `./x.js` to `./x.ts` plus `allowImportingTsExtensions` in the tsconfig, without which `tsc` reports `TS5097` -- and `apps/api/tsconfig.json` is outside this fence while the other two deployables are outside it entirely.
- **[ADR-085](decisions/ADR-085.md)'s SIGNED CLAUSE IS THE EIGHTH OF THE DRIFTED-ENUMERATION CLASS [ADR-099](decisions/ADR-099.md) section 4 named.** It says `29 of 29` where the tree is 30 of 30, and says the gate is watched failing when a real `fastify` key is seeded, which now reopens nothing. **Its ruling is untouched and correct.** A signed entry moves by a superseding ADR, so `CI-06/vg-inventory/fastify-near-miss` is **retained verbatim** rather than deleted or repointed, because that clause cites it by name.

**THE PLAN DISAGREES WITH ITSELF IN TWO PLACES AND BOTH ARE REPORTED RATHER THAN RESOLVED SILENTLY.** `P4-d`'s Contents cell lists no ADR file while rowing `ALLOCATION` (its row) and `INDEX` (its row), which on this tree is the generated `adr_count` span and nothing else, so both cells hold nothing unless an ADR lands; and section 11 rule 8 names `P4-d` by name as owing one. And that cell rows `gates.mjs` and not `falsify.mjs`, while **section 9, which section 8 says is the table to read**, rows `falsify.mjs` for `P4-d` -- and it had to be edited, because the seed inside it breaks on this slice's own artifact.

**The position:** `pnpm run typecheck` exit 0 with **zero `error TS`**; `apps/api` **10 tests to 37**; the suite **1,611 to 1,638 passed / 1 skipped** over 109 files; [`scoped-db.test.ts`](../packages/db/test/scoped-db.test.ts) **101**, untouched; **8 of 8** invariants with `RI-09` needing no change; **30 of 30** gates; `pnpm run verify` **exit 0**; `pnpm run falsify` 30 gates clean-and-dirty over **70** scope cases and 10 loader cases; `falsify:ci CI-01` **12 of 12** with `git status --porcelain` empty immediately after. **`0048` stays free, no `SD-nn` moves, and nothing on the money path was touched.**
