## Session 232: `apps/api` joins the admission list, and ADR-112 turns out to have unblocked everything a session can DO and nothing that makes one (2026-08-27)

**[ADR-120](decisions/ADR-120.md), `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED. MONEY PATH, auth, and the `E2` line-by-line read is owed on every line of it.**

**`DB_ADMITTED` HAS A MEMBER IN IT FOR THE FIRST TIME AND THE MEMBER IS `@merit/api`.** [ADR-117](decisions/ADR-117.md) ruling 4 refused to pre-admit it and [session 218](sessions/2026-08-26-session-218.md) and [session 220](sessions/2026-08-26-session-220.md) each declined to take the admission as a side effect, writing the argument into [ADR-113](decisions/ADR-113.md) section 6. **None of that is overturned.** Clause 1 rules that the test is not whether the need is real -- ADR-109 said it was real and ADR-117 refused anyway -- but whether the need is the SUBJECT, because a control whose design is *"adding a name here is the admission decision"* is defeated the first time the decision is taken by somebody who was thinking about a checkout. **The price ADR-117 section 4 named was paid in full and watched**: with the manifest line added and the list still empty, `check:invariants` exits 1 at **9 of 10** naming `apps/api/package.json`, and making it green again cost exactly the second diff that entry predicted.

**THE MEASUREMENT THE DISPATCH DID NOT PREDICT, AND IT IS ONE SENTENCE.** [ADR-112](decisions/ADR-112.md) unblocked **everything a session can DO and nothing that makes one.** Read a session, revoke one, list them, stamp `elevated_at`: all four are an address through the scoped door and all four land. Mint a session, and resolve a person from the address they typed: neither has a door, and neither is a predicate problem.

| | Blocked by | Whose |
|---|---|---|
| **an INSERT onto a `derived` table** | `ScopedTx.insert` takes `OwnedTableKey` and `sessions` is `derived`, because the accessor cannot establish the parent is this identity's without a read the caller could have skipped or a race | [ADR-102](decisions/ADR-102.md) section 4 names the construction and does not build it. `packages/db`, the founder's |
| **a pre-identity READ** | `users.email` is UNIQUE and `users` is `owned`, so resolving an address to a person needs the person. `firmDb()` refuses an `owned` key and `SystemReason` is two words a request handler is not in | **[ADR-109](decisions/ADR-109.md) clause 1's ground has MOVED.** It closed the vocabulary because a third reason would buy a door with no predicate; ADR-112 supplied the predicate and nothing has revisited it |

**FOUR OF SIXTEEN, REPORTED HONESTLY.** `sessionByToken`, `logout`, `listSessions` and `revokeSession` are wired against the real accessor; `IdempotencyStore`'s identity arm is complete, which discharges [ADR-109](decisions/ADR-109.md) clause 3 for the population that has a door. **The other twelve raise with their own named blocker** rather than one shared sentence, so a 503 from `POST /auth/verify` is a different fact in the log from a 503 from `POST /auth/passkey/login/options`. **A DEPLOYMENT STILL CANNOT MINT A SESSION**, and that is stated rather than buried.

**THE SESSION TOKEN CARRIES ITS OWN IDENTITY AND THE CLAIM IS A HINT THE DATABASE IS NEVER ASKED TO TRUST.** `<identityId>.<secret>`, with the stored `refresh_token_hash` over the WHOLE string, so a rewritten prefix is refused twice and independently: the digest changes, and if it somehow did not, `scopedTx` ANDs the tenancy predicate onto the address. **The identity is not read off the row, it is proved by the row coming back**, because `sessions` carries `user_id` and no `identity_id`. There is a parser and no minter, because nothing can insert the row a minter would mint for.

**FOUR FINDINGS REPORTED RATHER THAN WORKED AROUND, each of which stops a method.** `phone_change_requests` has **no preview column** while `PhoneChange.new_phone_preview` is required on three responses. `Me.max_accounts` appears in **no table in any of the 47 migrations** and is a plan parameter. `otp_challenges.code_hash` has **no specified digest anywhere in the corpus** and no salt column and no key id, so the correct answer is a keyed MAC with nowhere to keep the key. And nothing in this tree DELIVERS a code, so a `requestOtp` answering `sent: true` would be worse than a 503.

**THREE FORCED WIDENINGS. THE SESSION LOG NAMED TWO BEFORE THEY WERE TAKEN AND THE THIRD ANNOUNCED ITSELF.** `CI-06/vg-inventory` goes red at **31 of 32** the instant `scopedDb` is named under `apps/api/src`, which is the gate failing on good news exactly as designed, and its own finding says to re-rule the row. `VG-3` and `VG-6` now wait on **a `services:` block on `ci.yml`'s `integration` job**, which is the gap [ADR-102](decisions/ADR-102.md) section 16 and [ADR-112](decisions/ADR-112.md) section 9 have each already named in the same words, and `VG_PROBES` shrinks by the arrived entry on the precedent its own comment records from [ADR-100](decisions/ADR-100.md). **THE THIRD IS THE ONE WORTH THE MOST**: `pnpm run falsify` reported `DID NOT FAIL` on that gate, because its seed planted a `scopedDb` call while both rows waited on one and a real one is now there. **A harness whose seed still passes after its artifact has arrived has stopped watching anything**, and ADR-100 hit the identical thing one artifact ago from the other side, where the anchor vanished and the case THREW. `scoped-db-near-miss` is RETAINED VERBATIM because ADR-100 is `accepted` and cites it by name, `services-on-another-job` is added beside it, and **scope cases go 79 to 80**. **A near-miss case named after the ARTIFACT it bounds becomes uneditable the moment an ADR cites it, and this register now carries two stranded that way**; reported rather than repaired. **A possible collision with session 233 on `scripts/` is reported rather than resolved quietly.**

**WATCHED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** Eight seeded mutations, every one failing by name and every one reverted against a byte-identical copy; the admission seeded away (three assertions red, `9 of 10`) and seeded STALE (five red); the new `VG` probe seeded present (**31 of 32**) and seeded onto a different job (**32 of 32**, which is the substring trap it is scoped against); and session 218's compile refusal re-run, `ElevationFactor` widened with `'sms_otp'` reporting `TS2578` on all four `@ts-expect-error` lines.

**AND A ROUND TRIP AGAINST A REAL POSTGRESQL 16, THROUGH FASTIFY'S OWN ROUTER**, reported as evidence and not claimed as a gate, because `ci.yml`'s integration job has no database. All 47 migrations applied under `ON_ERROR_STOP=1` giving 111 base tables and one view. **A handler holding A's session and naming B's session id answers 404 and BOTH ROWS ARE STILL LIVE afterwards**; the same handler naming A's own session answers 204 and exactly one row moves. Below the router, `A` presenting `B`'s idempotency key gets `key_held_elsewhere`, which is [ADR-109](decisions/ADR-109.md) section 6's landmine executed for the first time; and with `sessions_elevated_by_factor_check` DROPPED and `sms_otp` written into the row, the read boundary refuses rather than elevating.

**`CI-05` WENT RED ON THE FIRST PUSH AND THIS IS THE SECOND TIME.** `gitleaks git .`, one leak, `generic-api-key` at `apps/api/test/auth-backend.test.ts:83`, this branch's own commit, reproduced locally against the same pinned binary with the tarball digest matching [`ci.yml`](../.github/workflows/ci.yml)'s pin. **A fake base64 value bound to `const secret`**, which is the rule's exact shape and the same shape as the last occurrence: the rule is not wrong, and the test needed neither the entropy nor the keyword. **THE FIX ALONE DOES NOTHING AND IT WAS MEASURED AGAIN**: `gitleaks dir .` reports no leaks while `gitleaks git .` still reports one, because the scan reads commit PATCHES, so the working-tree scan reports the opposite of the truth. The repair was a history rewrite over this branch's own commits plus `git push --force-with-lease`, **authorised before it was run**, which is the order the last occurrence followed. **THE FIRST ATTEMPT WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY REDONE**: over `<base>..HEAD` it reached THROUGH the merge's second parent and rewrote [session 233](sessions/2026-08-27-session-233.md)'s five commits, so `origin/main` stopped being an ancestor of the branch. It was caught by asking that question of the result rather than assuming it, reset from `filter-branch`'s own backup ref, and re-run with `--not <main tip>`. **A rewrite that renames commits the base branch already carries has widened past its own branch, and nothing in the tooling says so.** Verified in the shape CI sees rather than in the working copy: a `--single-branch` clone scans **`no leaks found`**, `git log --all -S<the literal>` returns nothing there, the rewritten tree is **byte-identical** to the pre-rewrite tip, and the merge's second parent is `main`'s own commit. **A `.gitleaksignore` fingerprint was refused** for the reason the last occurrence gives: it buys green by keeping the thing that should not be there.

## The M12 machine exists, and `input_digest` is a ruling about what is INSIDE it (2026-08-27, session 234)

**`P4-g` had waited on `CI-09`'s replay self-audit leg since 2026-08-20 and was unblocked by [#312](https://github.com/lam2-coder/meritfutures/pull/312).** The nightly statistics run is now at [`apps/worker/src/batch/statistics.ts`](../apps/worker/src/batch/statistics.ts): it reads authoritative closed-session facts, computes all seven signed definitions, and writes **one immutable `published_statistics` row per window per measure per grain cell**.

**THE DIGEST IS TAKEN OVER THE COMPUTATION'S OWN ARGUMENT, NOT OVER A DESCRIPTION OF THE QUERY**, which is [ADR-122](decisions/ADR-122.md) clause 1 and the entry's whole subject. `canonicalFact` walks the fact objects with `Object.keys` and THROWS on a value it cannot frame, so an input the arithmetic can see and the digest cannot is **unexpressible rather than test-caught**, and a `number` reaching a money field is loud rather than silently unhashed.

**IT EXCLUDES THE ANSWER, AND THAT EXCLUSION IS WHAT MAKES IT WORTH TAKING.** `value`, `numerator`, `denominator` and `sample_size` are outside it, so **two runs whose digests MATCH and whose values DIFFER is an arithmetic regression** rather than an invisible one. `measure` is outside it too, so `ST-04`'s mean and median carry ONE digest and two values, which is the pair's reproducibility stated. **What it cannot cover is named rather than widened**: `published_statistics` has no `engine_version` column, no migration was in the fence, and folding a worker version into the digest bytes was REFUSED because it would make every deploy look like a data change.

**IMMUTABILITY WAS CHECKED BEFORE IT WAS CODED AND IS LEFT TO THE DATABASE.** [`0026`](../packages/db/migrations/0026_roles_and_grants.sql) revokes `UPDATE, DELETE` from `merit_app` AND `PUBLIC`, `published_statistics_window_uq` refuses the second row, and [ADR-112](decisions/ADR-112.md) removed both verbs from every handle. So the machine **does not read the published series and does not skip a published window**: it computes, it writes, and the unique index decides. The approval line is that refusal executed.

**TWO STRUCTURAL FINDINGS ARRIVED FROM BUILDING AGAINST THE SCHEMA RATHER THAN READING IT, AND BOTH ARE REPORTED RATHER THAN REPAIRED.** `statistic_definitions_live_uq` gives a statistic **one live row carrying one `window_spec`**, so the corpus's twice-stated *"each statistic carries both a trailing-window and a lifetime form"* has no shape in the table as landed; and **`INV-M12-06`'s k-anonymity floor has no number anywhere in the corpus and no column in the schema**, so `min_sample` per cell is what exists and `ST-03`, ruled `min_sample` *"None"*, is the one it does not cover.

**THREE OF THE SIX GLOBAL DEFINITIONAL CHOICES NEED NO CODE AT ALL**, which is why they cannot drift: never-traded accounts are in the denominator because nothing removes them (`G-1`), an account still in evaluation has no outcome and so produces no fact (`G-2`), and `accounts.purchase_id` is `NOT NULL UNIQUE` so a reset is a second row and counting accounts is counting attempts (`G-3`).

**A SEED THAT PROVED NOTHING IS RECORDED AS PROVING NOTHING.** The first falsification added a value derived FROM the facts to the digest and turned zero tests red, correctly: a value the facts already determine can move no comparison. The seed that discriminates folds in something the facts do not determine, which is the computed value, and it turns the `ST-04` pair test red. *"I mutated the digest and the suite went red"* is not the claim; *"I mutated what the digest depends on"* is.

**Measured on the merge with `origin/main` at `e3782d4`, which is the SECOND merge and the one the figures name: 32 of 32 gates, 10 of 10 invariants, `pnpm run verify` exit 0, `pnpm exec vitest run` 150 files / 2,646 passed / 1 skipped.** On the first merge, at `ad4eb3c`, the same run was 148 files / 2,613 passed / 1 skipped; session 232's `apps/api` suites are the difference and neither figure is this session's to claim. **`VG-1` was RED on both merges and on `main` itself for a reason outside this branch**, and it is recorded because a green run today is not evidence the gate was always green: `gitleaks git .` found a `generic-api-key` at `apps/api/test/auth-backend.test.ts:83` in commit `89874dbf`, which was reachable from `claude/auth-wiring` and from NEITHER `main` NOR this branch. Session 232 rewrote that branch, `89874dbf` is unreachable from any ref, and `gitleaks git .` over this merge reports **no leaks found** across 1,324 commits.** `statistics.test.ts` carries 60 cases and four seeded mutations were watched failing and reverted byte-identically. **MONEY PATH, `E2` READ PENDING, NOT MERGED.**

**THE DISPATCH'S PREMISE ABOUT `OI-14` IS REFUTED AT SOURCE AND THE ROW STILL CLOSES.** The brief reads *"#315 DID THAT"*. It did not: [#315](https://github.com/lam2-coder/meritfutures/pull/315) added the `accountsAudited === 0` guard, which is [ADR-073](decisions/ADR-073.md) section 5's EMPTY BOOK, and [ADR-123](decisions/ADR-123.md) section 4 says in its own words that the entry *"does not close `OI-14`'s row"*. `OI-14`'s guard is `storedRows > 0 && inScope === 0` and it predates that entry. **The row is closed on the case that asserts THAT guard**, which now pins the message rather than the class, because three guards in the file throw `ReplayAuditRefusal`. **Both guards were falsified independently**: neuter either alone, with nothing else touched, and exactly one case goes red; neuter the other and the two swap.

**THE FINDING, EXECUTED RATHER THAN REASONED.** A port that names an account in `accountsWithStoredState()` and hands back no rows and no days for it makes `runReplayAudit` RETURN `{"accountsAudited":1,"storedRows":0,"inScope":0,"matched":0,"diverged":0}`. **Neither guard sees it**: `accountsAudited` is 1, so ADR-073's is silent, and `storedRows` is 0, so `OI-14`'s conjunct is false. **An audit that compared nothing reporting clean is `FM-17` at its widest.** It is [ADR-123](decisions/ADR-123.md) section 7's rejected alternative, and that rejection reads *"a port that returns an account id and no rows for it ... the audit has something to say about the account"*. **That is two inputs and the entry priced one.** With days present the audit is loud, four divergences, and the rejection is right; with days absent it is silent. **Both halves are executed in the suite** and the silent one is PINNED AS A HOLE with a comment saying the day it goes red is the day the hole closed. **Not fixed here**: reversing an argued rejection on `INV-04`'s right-hand side is a ruling, and `ADR-129` was reserved against a different condition.

## The portal renders, and the classification the dispatch cited does not exist (2026-08-27, session 261)

**`apps/portal` has two rendered screens.** `apps/portal/src/app/(purchases)/ports.ts` serves `/purchases` (`SC-M4-06`) and `/certificates` (`SC-M4-08`) out of one route group, against the view modules that had existed and rendered nothing since P4-h. **It is UNWIRED**: session 250's `next.config` and `app/layout.tsx` had not landed, so `next build` still exits 1 for the missing layout and the segment shipped honestly unwired on [session 223](sessions/2026-08-26-session-223.md)'s pattern.

### `ADR-149` is NOT TAKEN, and the reservation's own reason is the finding

The `149` row and the `261` row both read *"Certificates are a public artifact and `GS-302` is `restricted`; a rendered certificate is the first place that classification is tested"*. **Every citation under that sentence resolves and the inference does not.** [`0001`](../packages/db/migrations/0001_extensions_and_enums.sql):27 is `CREATE TYPE identity_status AS ENUM ('active', 'restricted', 'closed')`, [ADR-041](decisions/ADR-041.md) refused a fourth value **of that enum**, and `GS-302` impersonates a **`restricted` identity**.

**`identity_status` is an identity's status and not a classification of data**, and no data-classification vocabulary exists anywhere in this corpus. A rendered certificate therefore tests nothing about one. The word travelled from an enum of identity states into a sentence about data sensitivity because the word was the same, which is [session 95](sessions/2026-08-20-session-95.md)'s recurring error class with the citation checked and the inference not.

**What a public certificate may carry IS settled, in two places that agree.** [M11](plans/M11-certificates-social-proof.md) `INV-M11-01` enumerates the claims and closes them with *"and nothing else"*; [M04](plans/M04-trader-portal.md) `AS-M4-03` rule 3 states the same set as absences. The condition was *"if the corpus does not settle it"*, so no entry is minted and the `149` row is amended in place under [ADR-065](decisions/ADR-065.md) T3.

### The control that ships instead, and the leak it caught

`publishedCertificate()` builds its result **field by field from a closed allowlist** rather than by spreading the view model, so a field added to `CertificateView` later cannot reach a public artifact until somebody writes its name in the list. **`certificate_id` does not cross it**, on `SD-M11-01`'s own reason for separating the primary key from the public `code`: the token can be rotated after an incident only while the key it replaced is not already published.

**The refusal path was publishing that id through an error message**, and the assertion is written over the rendered bytes rather than over the model's fields, so it failed. A value reaches a page through an `alt`, a `title` or an error string without ever appearing in a visible field.

### Four reads named, two of which nobody owns

`GET /purchases` and `GET /plans/:planId/versions/:version` are session **253**'s and in flight. **`GET /accounts/:accountId/certificate?kind=` is approved in [API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) section 6 and is claimed by no session in the 250 to 264 wave**, and **no contract row serves `content_documents` to the portal at all**, which leaves `INV-M4-09`'s required disclosure with no wire source. `GET /certificates`, M11's trader-facing list carrying the `deferred` state, is in no `API_CONTRACT` section.

**Two things measured and reported rather than taken**: [`view/certificates.ts`](../apps/portal/src/view/certificates.ts) and [`view/disclosure.ts`](../apps/portal/src/view/disclosure.ts) each declare an error class with a TypeScript parameter property, which `node --experimental-strip-types` refuses to load; it does not bite the portal because [ADR-095](decisions/ADR-095.md) moved its start script to `next start`. Rendering forced no change to either file.

### `CI-07` reopens on this commit and is left RED, deliberately

`CI-06/gate-inventory` reports one finding: `CI-07`'s artifact, *"a `page`, `layout` or `route` file under `apps/*/src/app/`"*, **has arrived**, so the row reopened on the commit that delivered it. **That is [ADR-073](decisions/ADR-073.md) disposition (b) failing on good news exactly as designed**, and [`apps/portal/package.json`](../apps/portal/package.json)'s own note predicted this reopen when the `build` script landed.

**RESOLVED, AND THIS SECTION FORECAST IT WRONG TWICE IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS.** Session 250 merged as [#349](https://github.com/lam2-coder/meritfutures/pull/349) and its commit `9ba14bee`, *"close CI-07: write the stage the first rendered document reopened"*, adds the `build-and-bundle` job to [`ci.yml`](../.github/workflows/ci.yml). **`gates.mjs check` is 33 of 33 on the merge, `falsify.mjs` is clean, `repo-invariants.mjs` is 11 of 11, and `pnpm --filter @merit/portal build` exits 0** with `/purchases` and `/certificates` in Next's own route table.

This section first said the choice was *"250 first, or 250's commit carries `CI-07`'s disposition"*, then corrected that to *"landing 250 does NOT turn the row green; the repair is `P4-i`'s"*. **The correction was the wrong one.** `ADR-138` section 7 was read accurately and quoted accurately, and the inference from it treated **a snapshot of a live branch as a settled ruling**; 250 wrote the stage in a commit that did not exist when it was read. **That is this session's own headline error class, a citation checked and an inference carried one step too far, pointed at its author**, and it is recorded rather than overwritten.

**What was right is the part that cost something to hold.** The gate was not weakened, the fence was not widened, [STRATEGY](testing/STRATEGY.md) was not edited from a portal-page branch, and no re-ruling was taken. `ADR-138` section 7's refusal, *"a re-ruling today would be relaxing a register to keep it green"*, is what the closed row vindicates: it went green because somebody wrote the missing stage, which is the only honest way a waiting row closes.

## `OI-25` closes: the fixture backlog is DERIVED, and a count that had already drifted by forty was found by the mechanism on its first run (2026-08-27, session 245)

**The backlog is no longer a number somebody maintains.** Every count in [section 39](testing/golden-scenarios/39-fixture-status-and-blockers.md)'s two summary tables, and the row total in its opening sentence, is a generated span whose query is [`scripts/corpus/fixture-backlog.mjs`](../scripts/corpus/fixture-backlog.mjs) reading the rows below. `node scripts/corpus/gates.mjs generate` writes them and a hand edit is a `CI-06g` finding on the next run, so **the number can be read and can no longer be typed**. [ADR-133](decisions/ADR-133.md) is the ruling, `status: proposed` and unsigned. Not money path.

**ONE THING HAD ALREADY BEEN BUILT AGAINST `OI-25` AND IT IS WHY THIS IS A GAP AND NOT A HOLE.** `CI-06/fixture-inventory` assertion 5 already COMPARED both summary tables to the rows, in both directions, and its own finding text named what it could not do: *"This is a hand-maintained count over hand-maintained rows (`ADR-034`) and `CI-06g` cannot reach it, because it is not a generated span."* **So the number was CHECKED and still STATED.** A checked-but-stated number is retyped by hand every time a row moves, and the gate that refuses a wrong value is also the gate that tells the typist which value will pass.

**THE RECEIPT: 276 AGAINST 316.** [Section 39](testing/golden-scenarios/39-fixture-status-and-blockers.md)'s opening sentence stated its own row count and was **wrong by forty**, in the document whose next paragraph reads *"EVERY COUNT ABOVE WAS RECOMPUTED BY READING THE TREE AND NOT BY ADJUSTING THE PREVIOUS ONE"*. It was silent to `CI-06g` (not a span), to `CI-06/derivable-counts` (three reasons, plus that gate's own stated false negative for a count that has already drifted), to assertion 5 (a prose sentence and not a term row), and to 32 green gates. The repair was one line of generator output and needed no judgement.

**THE FINDING IS BIGGER THAN THE SPAN, and only one third of it is a hole.** `CI-06/derivable-counts` cannot see this number because (1) there is no vocabulary entry for the population, (2) the recogniser is value-anchored and no query returned any of these values, and (3) **a SUMMARY table row is excluded BY SHAPE**. The first two are properties the gate declares. The third is a hole: the exclusion's stated argument is that a table row is *"a per-row datum whose number belongs to that row rather than to the document"*, which is **true of a data row and false of a summary row** whose number is a population over the document's own rows. **Measured with a probe rather than argued**: identical text, identical value, identical noun, once as prose and once as a summary row, gives one finding and one silence.

**IT IS NAMED AS OWED AND NOT NARROWED HERE.** The narrowing is an edit to `gates.mjs`, where sessions 243 and 244 are live; a noun entry is not free, because one for `written` would now fire on section 39's own *"43 are written"*, where the number is a SUBSET that happens to equal the whole population; and it is `OI-26`-shaped, a gate that does not exist, rather than `OI-25`-shaped, a count that is stated. **A live instance already stands in the tree**: [ALLOCATION](decisions/ALLOCATION.md) row 125, session 237's own reservation, states its population in a table row and will be wrong the moment 237 lands.

**WHAT A LATER READER WILL GET WRONG.** `CI-06/fixture-inventory` assertion 5 **changed what it asserts and stayed green through the change**. It catches no typist now, because nobody types the number; it cross-checks **two independent readers of the same rows**, the derivation script and the runner's own loop, which is the `sql_tables` against `tables` arrangement and is exactly what a span alone does not buy. **The merge hazard is that somebody makes the two readers one.** They look like duplication and they are the assertion.

**FALSIFIED, WITH THE NEGATIVE CONTROLS AS THE HALF THAT MATTERS.** Five perturbations in a copy of the tree, never in the working tree. Three moved a row and moved the derived counts by exactly one in the right direction, one of them round-tripping to the byte. Two were negative: a blocker term nobody declared, and the runner's vocabulary declaration renamed. **Both REFUSED**, naming the offending row and line, and the runner reported `ERROR` with a non-zero exit rather than a smaller backlog over a tree that looked clean. **A derivation that classified an unreadable row as nothing is a failure mode the stated number at least could not have**, which is why closure of the partition is asserted rather than assumed.

**THE HARNESS CAUGHT THE ONE THING THIS SESSION BROKE.** [`falsify.mjs`](../scripts/corpus/falsify.mjs)'s `bumpFixtureSummary` matched digits sitting directly against the emphasis, which is no longer where they are. **Two landed cases broke and both ANNOUNCED THEMSELVES**, one as `SEED IS STALE` and one as `CONTROL DID NOT FIRE`, which is the distinction that harness rests on. The span markers are optional in that pattern now rather than required.

**THE CHECK RAN FOR ONE OF THE THREE AND IT PASSED.** [Session 248](sessions/2026-08-27-session-248.md) merged at `078e0ac` roughly six minutes after this branch was pushed, moving **seven** `format-cannot-express` rows to `covered-elsewhere` and leaving two blocked with rewritten citations. **The prediction was written from that session's own account of its work and from the cells it typed, BEFORE the generator was run**, which is the only order in which it proves anything: one term down by seven, one up by seven, `blocked` down by seven, the row total unmoved, every other term unchanged. **`gates.mjs generate` produced exactly that, and both partitions close on the merge result.** The derivation reproduces every number session 248 typed by hand, independently and without being shown them. **Sessions 237 and 249 have not landed** and the same three questions apply to each on its merge. **No figure is written here on purpose**: reading one out of this section instead of deriving it would defeat the thing that just landed.

**AND THE FENCE'S KEEP-BOTH CLAIM DID NOT HOLD, WHICH IS THIS ITEM'S OWN SUBJECT ARRIVING AS EVIDENCE.** The four-session split was expected to make every conflict in [section 39](testing/golden-scenarios/39-fixture-status-and-blockers.md) an APPEND. The row-level conflicts were. **The summary tables were a REVISION**, because session 248 had retyped three counts while this branch replaced the same cells with spans, and keep-both there would have produced a table carrying two rows per term, which is the table-corruption class that once passed every gate in this repository. **The cause is the defect and not the fence**: under a check, a session that moves rows MUST retype the summary, so it is forced into the one region every other session is also touching. Once those cells are spans nobody types them, and the collision stops existing for every session after this lands.

**[Session 237](sessions/2026-08-27-session-237.md) landed at `1e4f82b8`**, ruling `no-fixture-format` in [ADR-125](decisions/ADR-125.md) and moving seven rows already asserted and passing, with citations rewritten across the whole population. ## `P6` planned against the tree, and tier 2 splits down the middle by KIND rather than by content (2026-08-27, session 265)

**[P6-live-tier](plans/P6-live-tier.md), `status: draft`. Eleven slices, four waves, fences BY FILE, collisions BY FILE, and the closed vocabularies each slice may NOT take named on its row.** [DELIVERY_PLAN](DELIVERY_PLAN.md)'s `P6` row names six contents and no `P6-*.md` existed.
**THE ANSWER IS A THIRD SHAPE AND NOT A REPEAT OF EITHER NEIGHBOUR.** [P4](plans/P4-portal-and-site.md) found its contents mostly built and nobody saying so; [P5](plans/P5-payouts-and-wallet.md) found four writes blocked behind one file. **P6's contents split by KIND: every piece of tier 2 that is ARITHMETIC or a TYPE is built and tested, and every piece that is a CONTAINER, a TRANSPORT or a STORE is in no document a session can build from.** [`live-liability.ts`](../apps/admin/src/live-liability.ts) computes [M06](plans/M06-admin-ops-console.md) section 3.5's figure today with its three terms tiered separately and `authoritative()` refusing the result; [`stream.ts`](../packages/rithmic/src/simulator/stream.ts) emits `LiveAccountTick` and folds byte-identically into the rendered EOD CSV; [`view/as-of.ts`](../apps/portal/src/view/as-of.ts) already declares `Tier` and `Tiered`.
**THE WORD `WebSocket` OCCURS IN NO DOCUMENT UNDER [`docs/architecture/`](architecture/OVERVIEW.md).** `grep -rli websocket docs/architecture/` returns nothing. [OVERVIEW section 2](architecture/OVERVIEW.md)'s container diagram draws one Rithmic arrow and it is `Worker <-->|SFTP CSV out, reports in|`; section 3's table has no live-tier row; [API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) has no section a socket could be written in. **ADR-020's third stated content is in no architecture document at all**, and saying where it lives is `P6-b` and `P6-g`.
**AND THE LIVE CACHE IS NAMED ONLY EVER AS THE OBJECT OF A GRANT.** `INV-M2-14`, [SECURITY](architecture/SECURITY.md) `C-26`, `FM-M12-08`, `FM-M13-07`, [RB-05](ops/runbooks/RB-05-rithmic-sftp-failure.md) and `GS-132` all state a permission over it and **none states a medium**. There is no `SD-nn`, no migration, no table. **[`0026`](../packages/db/migrations/0026_roles_and_grants.sql) creates four roles of which exactly ONE is an application role**, and `merit_app` holds `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES` plus a `DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` clause covering every table a later migration creates. **So the separation four approved documents describe gets FURTHER AWAY when a table is added**, and the repair is a fifth role, which is a migration and a ruling.
**THE CONTRADICTION IS [ADR-154](decisions/ADR-154.md)'S AND THE CONDITIONAL FIRED.** [ADR-020](decisions/ADR-020.md) rules that the real feed plugs in *"exactly as the batch pipeline already does"*. **That mechanism is a FILE**: `INV-M2-11`'s stated enforcement is *"the simulator emits files, not objects"*, `GS-084` asserts *"no downstream code branches on source"*, and [`index.ts`](../packages/rithmic/src/index.ts)'s header refuses the simulator satisfying `PlatformAdapter` because *"a simulator that satisfied the interface would be a mock at the parser boundary, which is the one thing STRATEGY section 2 rejected by name"*. **`streamLive` hands its consumer objects and there is no parser to skip.** Both remaining readings are refused by landed documents, so the entry rules the seam moves from the ARTIFACT to the TYPE, reaches `streamLive` and no other operation, and states what replaces `GS-084`'s property. **The definitional sentence ADR-020 itself links, [GLOSSARY:299](GLOSSARY.md)'s *"v1 ships one implementation (Rithmic)"*, is one of the two clauses the ruling edits.**
**TWO OF FOUR DISPATCH CLAIMS DID NOT SURVIVE THE MEASUREMENT THEY ASKED FOR, AND THE METHOD IS WHY.** The brief said *"54 registered routes across a `public` and an `operator` surface"* and told this session to build the server rather than grep. Built: `public` registers **36** and withholds 18; `operator` registers **19** and withholds 35. **54 is the UNION and no surface registers it**, because `GET /health` is registered by both. The correction is load bearing for P6 rather than cosmetic: the trader's socket is served by the deployment that registers 36 and the founder's by the one that registers 19, and **the `withheld` list IS [ADR-083](decisions/ADR-083.md)'s operator 404**. The portal figure was exactly right at 12, one of which is Next's own `/_not-found`.
**AND `GS-132` AS WRITTEN ASSERTS SOMETHING TWO GREEN INVARIANTS ALREADY GUARANTEE.** Its registry text poisons the live cache and asserts the engine byte-identical *"because it never reads it"*. **`RI-01` and `RI-07` mean `packages/rules-engine` declares no workspace dependency and reaches no Node builtin**, so it cannot read a cache of any kind and its output is byte-identical under any cache state including a non-existent one. **The reachable failure is the batch assembling the engine's INPUTS from a tick**, so `P6-k`'s row puts the assertion there and says so in the test body rather than only in a plan. That is the *"control that exists and enforces nothing"* class caught before the control is written.
**P6'S TWO NAMED GATES ARE NOT WAITING ON A FIXTURE RULING, WHICH IS THE INVERSE OF P5'S POSITION.** `GS-132` and `GS-133` both read `blocked / no-fixture-format`, and [ADR-125](decisions/ADR-125.md) clause 2 already ruled that term's corpus-wide reason FALSE: *"the blocker that survives is the absent code"*. **They clear when P6 writes them.** [P5 section 10](plans/P5-payouts-and-wallet.md) item 2 could not say that about one of its four clauses.
**FEED LOSS IS A FIRST-CLASS STATE AND THE EVENT MODEL CANNOT EXPRESS IT AS WRITTEN.** [EVENTS](architecture/EVENTS.md) carries an `ingest.*` family including `ingest.file_late` and no `feed.*` family, and its universal rule is *"Events are written in the same transaction as the state change that caused them"*. **A feed that stops opens no transaction.** The corpus has solved the shape twice, at `report_deliveries.due_at` (*"absence is only detectable against an expectation"*) and at `economic_calendar_loads`' coverage bound, and the live feed has neither.

## `P5-a` lands: the accessor learns a range, a null and a lock, and the aggregate `P7` asked for is refused on evidence ([ADR-157](decisions/ADR-157.md), proposed 2026-08-27, session 268)

**[P5](plans/P5-payouts-and-wallet.md)'s lane A had one file in front of it and it now has none.** [`scoped-db.ts`](../packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts) carries a closed three-shape TERM vocabulary admitted on the READ path only, and a ROW lock. `P5-b`, `P5-e`, `P5-g`, `P5-h`, `P5-i`, `P5-j` and `P5-k` were each blocked on at least one of the three admissions and none of them is any more.

**[ADR-112](decisions/ADR-112.md) named its own way out and this is it arriving.** That entry refused a range and an `IS NULL` on one argument, *"a shape a caller can compose freely is a shape a caller can compose wrongly"*, and said in the same sentence that *"every one of them is a diff on this file with an argument attached when a caller needs it"*. `P5-j` sweeps three expiry clocks over two tables, and [`halts.ts`](../packages/ledger/src/halts.ts) has been reading every released halt on every posting since it was written.

### The question `P7` put to this slice, answered rather than deferred

**[P7 section 10 item 1](plans/P7-risk-and-abuse.md) asked this entry for an AGGREGATE and said every `P7` wave-2 slice is blocked without one. [ADR-157](decisions/ADR-157.md) section 5 REFUSES it, and the refusal is on evidence rather than on scope.** `P7`'s own section 3.1 names `D-01` a self-join on `fills` inside a two second window, `D-02` a rolling correlation, `D-03` a variance of sums across a discovered group and `D-14` a sum across a clique. **Not one of the four is served by a scalar aggregate over one table**, so admitting one would have spent the widening, left `P7` blocked on the JOIN it is actually blocked on, and left the next reader a foreclosure that reads as answered.

**`P7` IS PARTLY UNBLOCKED AND THE ENTRY SAYS SO IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** `D-01`'s two second window IS a range term and it landed; a detector can pull its window through `rowsWhere` and join in the runner, paying for every row in the window it did not match. **What a wave-2 slice must not do is widen `SqlExecutorReason`**, and the question a join construction has to answer is written down in the entry so it is not discovered at the file: a joined read has two tables and the tenancy narrowing has to hold on BOTH.

**A second argument, measured rather than asserted.** `SUM` over a `bigint` column returns `numeric`, `pg` hands a `numeric` back as a string, and `Number('9007199254740993')` is `9007199254740992`. **The first money aggregate through this accessor decides how a `numeric` crosses the boundary**, and that is a ruling of its own size rather than a predicate widening.

### The lock is a ROW lock and the two invariants say advisory

[M20](plans/M20-wallet.md)'s `INV-M20-01` and [M05](plans/M05-payout-system.md)'s `INV-M5-07` both name a per-identity and a per-account **advisory** lock. `pg_advisory_xact_lock` is a function call and the only door that would send one is `sqlExecutor`, which is the reach-around [P5](plans/P5-payouts-and-wallet.md) section 11 rule 10 and [P7](plans/P7-risk-and-abuse.md) section 11 rule 10 each foreclose by name. **So the lock is `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the predicate the matching read carries**, which is wider than an advisory lock on the same key, fails in the safe direction, and unlike an advisory lock keyed on a uuid the caller supplies carries the tenancy narrowing.

### What was watched, including the direction this suite fails in

**Nine mutations seeded and all nine caught**, each reverted from a byte-identical copy. **The one worth the most is that the tenancy conjunct dropped from the READ half of the address composition was GREEN on `main`**: [ADR-112](decisions/ADR-112.md)'s suite watches that composition on `updateAt` and `deleteAt`, which take a different builder, so nothing in the tree asserted it on `rowAt`. **Two of the nine break the suite's own READERS** rather than the accessor, because a fold whose helper stops resolving looks exactly like a fold finding nothing wrong.

**Eight compile refusals watched failing by their error.** None is permanently watched, on [ADR-102](decisions/ADR-102.md) section 11's precedent, and **the corpus now owes nineteen**: four from ADR-102, seven from [ADR-112](decisions/ADR-112.md) and eight from here.

**A twenty-one case round trip executed against PostgreSQL 16 with all 49 migrations applied.** Row 8 is the approval clause: a caller scoped to `A` locking `B`'s row got **zero rows, not an error and not `B`'s data**. Row 14 is what makes it mean something: a third connection then locked `B`'s row without blocking, so the refused lock left that row genuinely free. **Rows 10 to 12 are the first time this corpus has watched one of two concurrent transactions LOSE**, which is the sentence `DELIVERY_PLAN`'s *"wallet concurrency green"* clause has been waiting for. It is evidence and not a control: one run, by hand, in the session that wrote the code, with no gate that will run it again.

### Three stale sites repaired and one dispatch citation refuted

[`chart.ts`](../packages/ledger/src/chart.ts) said the predicate-carrying read was *"NAMED AND NOT BUILT"* and it is built; [`halts.ts`](../packages/ledger/src/halts.ts) explained its cost by an accessor limit that has been lifted. **In both cases the limit is now `LedgerTx`'s rather than the accessor's**, and `tx.ts` is outside this fence, so the entry corrects the reason and leaves the cost. [`packages/db/src/index.ts`](../packages/db/src/index.ts)'s header stated the registry size backwards, the two figures having traded places since it was written.

**The dispatch's citation for the migration number is wrong in a way that does not change the answer.** It says [P5](plans/P5-payouts-and-wallet.md) section 7 names `0050` as the next free number; section 7 names `0048` as session **240**'s and names no other. 240 took `0048` **and** `0049`, so `0050` is the first free one, and **this session claims no migration number at all.**

**Left standing:** `SqlExecutorReason` at one member and `SystemReason` at two, with the suite now watching the first for the first time. **No aggregate, no join, no multi-row lock, no strict inequality, no lock timeout, and no schema.** The approval line is UNSIGNED and the `E2` read is owed on every line.

## `streamLive` joins the adapter and the tier-2 seam becomes a TYPE, and the defect was in how a subscription starts (2026-08-27, session 271)

**[ADR-154](decisions/ADR-154.md) IS IMPLEMENTED AND `ADR-160` IS NOT TAKEN.** `streamLive(handler: LiveTickHandler): Promise<Subscription>` is on [`PlatformAdapter`](../packages/rithmic/src/index.ts), carrying [M02](plans/M02-rithmic-bridge.md) section 3.5's own signature rather than a paraphrase of it, and `simulatorLiveFeed` in [`stream.ts`](../packages/rithmic/src/simulator/stream.ts) implements it. **The [GLOSSARY](GLOSSARY.md) entry and [OVERVIEW section 3](architecture/OVERVIEW.md)'s `packages/rithmic` row moved in the same change**, which clause 5 required because [`adapter.test.ts`](../packages/rithmic/test/adapter.test.ts) reads OVERVIEW by name and a test citing a document that says something else is a contradiction that type-checks.
**THE PACKAGE STOPS BEING "AN INTERFACE NOTHING IMPLEMENTS", WHICH `F1` FORECLOSED ON PURPOSE.** `index.ts`'s refusal is NARROWED rather than repealed: it used to say *"IT DOES NOT IMPLEMENT `PlatformAdapter`"* and it now says it implements none of the FILE-MODE operations, with the parser argument undisturbed for all five. In tier 1 the simulator and the vendor share an ARTIFACT, one CSV through one parser; **in tier 2 there is no file, so what they share is `LiveAccountTick`**, which was already built to be it.
**CLAUSE 3 IS ENFORCED TWICE AND THE SECOND ONE IS THE ASSERTION.** `simulatorLiveFeed` returns `Pick<PlatformAdapter, 'streamLive'>`, and **a `Pick` bounds what a consumer may CALL rather than what the object CARRIES**: an implementation that grew an `ingestEOD` beside `streamLive` would satisfy that annotation and every type-check in this repository, so the returned key set is read at runtime, where the extra key is the only place it is visible.
**`GS-084`'s PROPERTY IS NOT CLAIMED FOR TIER 2 AND [`stream-conformance.test.ts`](../packages/rithmic/test/stream-conformance.test.ts) IS WHAT REPLACES IT.** *"No downstream code branches on source"* is purchasable only where both sources write into one directory. What runs instead is the stated invariants over each implementation: `indicative: true`, `bigint` cents, a monotone 1-based `sequence` per account per trading day, and `atUtc` inside `[sessionOpen, sessionClose)`. **They are checked at RUNTIME over delivered ticks rather than declared at the interface**, because a vendor implementation will parse ticks off a wire where every field arrives `unknown` and one cast restores each guarantee by assertion.
**THE RULING SETTLED THE SEAM AND NOT THE START, AND THE START IS WHERE THE DEFECT WAS.** [M02](plans/M02-rithmic-bridge.md) names `Subscription` and this corpus defines it nowhere. The first implementation pumped one tick per MICROTASK, type-checked, delivered every tick and passed every invariant. **A microtask queued inside `streamLive` runs before the caller's `await` continuation**, so the first tick reaches the handler while the consumer is still waiting for the `Subscription` that would let it close, and `close()` from inside the handler is a temporal-dead-zone reference. A feed whose subscription cannot be closed from its handler is a feed whose subscription is decoration, which is the synchronous-loop defect in a better hat. **Delivery is one turn of the event loop per tick for that reason and for no other**, and `setImmediate` takes no duration and reads nothing, so the no-clock constraint over `src/` is untouched.
**THREE SEEDED DEFECTS WATCHED FAILING**, including the cheap implementation the suite exists to refuse: a feed that delivers its whole day inside `streamLive` satisfies every invariant and fails both close tests. The other two are a tick stamped at the session close and a `sequence` that never advances.
**A FOURTH ENUMERATION SITE EXISTS AND CLAUSE 5 NAMES THREE.** [`packages/rithmic/README.md`](../packages/rithmic/README.md) carries the five operations, *"the interface is declared and nothing implements it"* and *"`PlatformAdapter` is still unimplemented"*. **All three are false on this commit and all three are outside `P6-a`'s fence**, so they are reported with the patch written out rather than reached for. The constitution and [`research/DATA_CAPABILITIES.md`](../research/DATA_CAPABILITIES.md) also enumerate the five and neither is a defect: one is frozen and moves by ADR, the other is a dated survey.
**`Subscription` CARRIES `close()` AND NOTHING ELSE, DELIBERATELY.** Feed loss is [P6](plans/P6-live-tier.md) section 3.4's, the shape of a staleness claim is the server's under [ADR-152](decisions/ADR-152.md), and a `Subscription` that grew an `onLoss` would be this slice writing `P6-d`'s contract inside a package `P6-d` does not touch.
**NO MIGRATION, NO `SD-nn`, NO `SystemReason`, NO `SqlExecutorReason`, NO DEPENDENCY AND NO GATE**, and [M02](plans/M02-rithmic-bridge.md) was read and cited and not edited. **`pnpm run verify` exit 0: 11 of 11 invariants, 33 of 33 gates, `falsify.mjs` clean, 170 test files / 3,098 passed / 6 skipped**, against the dispatch's `main` baseline of 169 / 3,091 / 6, which reproduced exactly. **`P6-b` is SERIAL behind this branch on `OVERVIEW`.**

## `P6-d` lands: the live tier enters the contract as a PAYLOAD, and the approval clause was FALSE until it was run (2026-08-27, session 272)

**[ADR-161](decisions/ADR-161.md), `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED. [API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) section 6.1 gains the live dashboard channel, section 8 gains the live Open Liability, and [EVENTS](architecture/EVENTS.md) gains section 5.4's `feed.*` family. Both live surfaces are PAYLOADS and neither is a `METHOD /path`.** No code, no migration, no `SD-nn`, and the cache, the container, the socket and the win-day projection are all refused to this slice.

**THE ENTRY WAS REQUIRED RATHER THAN CONDITIONAL AND THE REQUIREMENT HELD FOR A REASON BIGGER THAN THE FREEZE.** [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md) already makes an edit to a covered document an entry rather than a commit, which is what [ADR-153](decisions/ADR-153.md) paid for this morning over one verb. **What forced a ruling rather than a transcription is that tier 2 has no shape [API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) already carries**: section 1's conventions each presume a client that asked, a base path, a content type, an `Idempotency-Key`, a cursor and a per-endpoint rate limit, while `HTTP_METHODS` in [`registry.ts`](../apps/api/src/registry.ts) is closed at the five verbs the contract uses and `compose` keys on `METHOD /path`. **A socket upgrade is none of them**, so the trader's live surface enters as a PAYLOAD with no `METHOD /path` heading and the address stays `P6-b`'s and the framing stays `P6-g`'s.

**THE CLAUSE THAT BINDS ANOTHER SLICE WITHOUT TAKING ITS RULING IS THAT THE SECTION IS THE SURFACE.** [`surface.ts`](../apps/api/src/surface.ts) says `public` *"serves API_CONTRACT sections 3 to 7 and 10"* and `operator` *"serves sections 8 and 9"*, and it withholds **by prefix** rather than by an endpoint list, *"a second transcription of the contract, going stale the first time a route is added"*. **So an operator live path outside `['/admin', '/internal']` is withheld from the public deployment by nothing at all**, which is [P6](plans/P6-live-tier.md) section 10 item 2's failing direction closed at the contract rather than at a review of `P6-g`'s diff.

**THE APPROVAL CLAUSE'S FIRST FORM WAS FALSE, AND THE ONLY REASON ANYBODY KNOWS IS THAT IT WAS RUN BEFORE IT WAS CLAIMED.** It read *"every `METHOD /path` under section 8 or section 9 begins with one of `OPERATOR_PREFIXES`"* and it **fails on `GET /health`**, which section 9 rows in its own table as public and which [`surface.ts`](../apps/api/src/surface.ts) registers on BOTH surfaces deliberately, because a constant response *"discloses nothing the origin's own reachability does not already disclose"*. **A clause naming a prefix cannot see a deliberate exception; the application's own classifier already carries it as a third path class.** The clause now imports `classifyPath`, `surfaceServes` and `LIVENESS_PATH` from that file rather than restating either the rule or its exception, holds over every section 8 and 9 endpoint, and has been watched failing on a seeded `/live/liability`.

**THE DEGRADATION IS ONE OBJECT AND NOT TWO MESSAGES, WHICH IS `INV-M4-12` AT COMPILE TIME.** A frame carries the tier and the numbers together and the two arms share no field name for the same quantity, so a component cannot read `live_pnl_cents` off a fallback frame and cannot render either number without narrowing past the label. **This is [`figure.ts`](../apps/admin/src/figure.ts)'s idiom on the trader's side**, where an absent figure *"carries no `cents` field, which is the point"*. **And the first frame on any subscription is an `authoritative` one**, because a client sent only live frames that then loses its transport holds no last-closed values and freezes at the last live number, which is the failure `GS-133` and [RB-05](ops/runbooks/RB-05-rithmic-sftp-failure.md) step 1 are both about.

**`feed.*` IS PRODUCED BY THE EXPECTATION SWEEP AND BY NEITHER THE FEED NOR THE INGEST, AND THAT IS WHAT KEEPS TWO LANDED SENTENCES TRUE.** A feed that stops opens no transaction, so [EVENTS](architecture/EVENTS.md) section 1's *"events are written in the same transaction as the state change that caused them"* would have nothing to attach to; and `INV-M2-14` makes streaming ingest **write-only into the live cache**, so an ingest that also wrote `events` would be a second writer in the one place the corpus describes as having exactly one. **The sweep's own expectation row changing state IS the transaction**, which is `report_deliveries.due_at`'s shape and `economic_calendar_loads`' shape reused rather than a rule amended for one family.

**THE DISPATCH'S "ZERO UNCOVERED" IS TRUE OF A NARROWER CLAIM THAN IT SOUNDS, AND THE MEASUREMENT WAS RUN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** Against `CompositionReport.registered` on both surfaces: **zero registered routes are undefined** and **zero rows of section 12's matrix are uncovered**, which is [ADR-153](decisions/ADR-153.md)'s clause holding exactly as written. **The other direction has carried six endpoints the contract defines and nothing registers all along**, `GET /accounts/:accountId/marks`, `/timeline`, `/eligibility`, `/certificate`, and `GET /admin/loss-ratios` and `/admin/cusum`, the last two sharing a heading with an endpoint that IS registered. **This slice adds none of its own**, and a draft of it did: a `### GET /admin/liability/live` heading turned [`admin-reads.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/admin-reads.test.ts) red, because that file parses every `### GET /admin` row out of the contract and asserts the unserved set exactly. **No slice's fence in [P6](plans/P6-live-tier.md) holds that file**, and the repair was not to widen the fence but to notice that fixing an operator PATH is the same transport ruling this entry refuses to take for the trader.

**AND THE ROUTE FIGURE IN THE DISPATCH IS THE UNION AGAIN**, as [P6 section 5.1](plans/P6-live-tier.md) recorded this morning: `public` registers 36 and withholds 18, `operator` registers 19 and withholds 35, and `GET /health` is the one path both register. **54 is the union and no surface registers it.**

**Two things are named for whoever owns them rather than taken.** The live channel has **no rate-limit row**, because section 11 states limits per endpoint and this subsection defines none, and section 11 is outside this fence: it belongs with the mechanism, which is `P6-g`. And **`GS-133`'s registry row has no named owner for its status**: [P6](plans/P6-live-tier.md) gives `P6-k` the `GS-132` row of the fixture registry by name and only that row, while `GS-133` is `P6-i`'s assertion and `P6-i`'s fence lists no registry file.

**Measured on this branch with `pnpm install` run first: `pnpm run verify` exit 0, 33 of 33 gates, 11 of 11 invariants, 169 test files / 3,091 passed / 6 skipped, `falsify.mjs` exit 0.** No code changed, so the test figures are the tree's own.

## The portal gets a transport: one file, one cookie, no store, and the assertion narrowed rather than deleted (2026-08-27, session 273)

**[ADR-162](decisions/ADR-162.md), `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED. [`apps/portal/src/http/client.ts`](../apps/portal/src/http/client.ts) is the first and only file in `apps/portal` that performs a network call, and `app/payouts/` is the one segment wired to it.** No migration, no `SD-nn`, no `apps/api` change, no `packages/db` change, and the other five segments still render from fixtures.

**THE FIRST `fetch` IN THIS APPLICATION WAS A DECISION SOMEBODY MADE ON PURPOSE, WHICH IS WHAT THE ASSERTION EXISTED TO FORCE.** [`surface.test.ts`](../apps/portal/test/surface.test.ts) had failed on `fetch(`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `WebSocket` and `EventSource` since session 111, stating *"Asserting it now means THE FIRST `fetch` WRITTEN HERE IS A DECISION SOMEBODY MAKES ON PURPOSE rather than one that appears in a diff."* **It is NARROWED PER NEEDLE rather than deleted or allowlisted by file**: `fetch(` moves from *no file* to `src/http/client.ts`, and the other three still hold at **zero files**, so a client reaching for `EventSource` fails the same test that a second segment reaching for `fetch` does. **Watched failing on a real seeded second transport file** rather than only on a seeded string.

**THE MEASUREMENT THAT CHANGED THE SHAPE OF THE SESSION IS THAT `apps/api` SETS NO CORS HEADER ANYWHERE.** No `@fastify/cors`, no `Access-Control-*` in any route module. **So the browser cannot be the client**, whatever the cookie's `SameSite` value permits: the request is refused across the origin boundary before the cookie question is reached, and `credentials: 'include'` would additionally need `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`, which is a change to the deployable serving the whole public surface. The client therefore runs in the portal's server, reads the inbound request through `next/headers`, and forwards **exactly `merit_session` and never the whole `Cookie` header**.

**THE CACHE DECISION IS `no-store` AND ITS DECISIVE REASON IS NOT STALENESS.** [M04 section 1.2](plans/M04-trader-portal.md) and `INV-M4-04` both require it, and either alone would have been an argument about a wrong number. **The third reason is that every response on this surface is identity-scoped**, so a cache key that omits the session serves one trader's payouts to another, which is `FM-M4-03`, *"the single most common vibe-code fatality"*. **The safe design is the one with no store to leak**, and it is stated in source rather than inherited from a framework default.

**`get` RETURNS `unknown` AND A GENERIC `get<T>` IS REFUSED**, because a type parameter the caller supplies is a cast the compiler cannot check and a transport that validated shapes would have to know all of them. **Narrowing lands in the segment, beside the transcription that declares the shape**, and `app/payouts/source.ts`'s guard checks **every field the view reads rather than a subset**: a partial guard reads as a complete one at the call site and crashes on the field it skipped.

**THE DISPATCH'S ONE FALSE PREMISE WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN INHERITED, AND IT IS THE FINDING.** The prompt stated that `GET /payouts` and `GET /accounts/:accountId/eligibility` *"are both registered by `apps/api` today"*. Built from `discoverRouteModules()` and `buildServer({ surface: 'public', modules })` and read off `CompositionReport.registered`: **`GET /payouts` is registered and `GET /accounts/:accountId/eligibility` is not.** The accounts module registers `GET /accounts` and `GET /accounts/:accountId` and stops, and its own header calls `/eligibility` *"somebody else's endpoint"*; [session 272](sessions/2026-08-27-session-272.md) rowed the same absence from the other direction the same morning. **So `load` asks nothing of the endpoint that does not exist**, because a request to an unregistered path returns 404, the client correctly maps that to `not_found`, and a screen rendering it would tell the trader their ACCOUNT was not found.

**WHAT THE SEGMENT GAINED IS SMALL AND IT IS REAL.** `load` performs `GET /api/v1/payouts` through the client, and the screen's `missing` list **shrank from a constant to a measurement**: it names the eligibility endpoint alone when the payouts read succeeded and both when it did not. `./view.ts`, `./sections.ts`, `./page.ts` and `./wire.ts` are untouched, which is the promise the old `source.ts` header made -- *"`load` below gains a `ready` branch and NOTHING ELSE IN THIS SEGMENT CHANGES"* -- kept literally, and [`payouts-segment.test.ts`](../apps/portal/test/payouts-segment.test.ts) still asserts no network call in that directory and still passes unchanged.

**ONE THING IS REPORTED RATHER THAN REPAIRED, AND IT IS THE FENCE HOLDING.** `PayoutCenterLoad` has two arms and no error arm, so a `GET /payouts` that returns 500 renders exactly as a missing endpoint does. That is `source.ts`'s own *"`unavailable` IS NOT AN ERROR STATE"* argument cutting the other way now that a request can fail. **The repair needs `./sections.ts` to render an error arm and `./page.ts` to branch on it, and this session's fence holds neither**, so it is in [ADR-162](decisions/ADR-162.md) section 5 and in the pull request rather than reached for. The client already carries what the arm would need.

**`P6-h` INHERITS CLAUSES 1 AND 2 WHOLE AND HAS ONE ENTRY TO ADD.** [P6 section 6](plans/P6-live-tier.md) makes the socket slice depend on this client for the base URL and the session policy *"rather than inventing a second one"*, and section 8 forbids it to delete the needle. **The transport table is per needle, so that slice moves `WebSocket` from zero files to `src/live/client.ts` and writes no second origin resolution and no second cookie policy.**

**`next/headers.js` CARRIES ITS EXTENSION FOR A MEASURED REASON.** `next@16.3.2` declares no `exports` map, [`tsconfig.base.json`](../tsconfig.base.json) sets `moduleResolution: NodeNext`, and `apps/portal` is `"type": "module"`, so `next/headers` is `error TS2307` and `next/headers.js` resolves under both `tsc --noEmit` and `node --input-type=module`. **This is the first import of `next` in this repository**, so nobody had paid for that finding before.

**Verified in pieces, because `pnpm run verify` no longer fits one timeout. 33 of 33 gates, 11 of 11 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, `format:check` clean, 172 test files / 3,136 passed / 6 skipped, and `falsify.mjs` reporting all 33 gates clean and dirty with `git status --porcelain` empty immediately after.** The dispatch baseline of 170 / 3,115 / 6 reproduced exactly before anything changed.

## Section 6's four account sub-resource reads are registered, one is served, and three refuse by name (2026-08-27, session 284)

**No ADR, no migration, no `packages/db` change, no `API_CONTRACT` change, no `apps/portal` change.** This was transcription against an approved contract, so it took no number: `API_CONTRACT` section 6 had already decided all four shapes.

**FOUR CONTRACT ROWS THAT NOTHING REGISTERED NOW EXIST ON THE ROUTER.** `GET /accounts/:accountId/marks`, `/timeline`, `/eligibility` and `/certificate` are declared by [`apps/api/src/routes/account-reads.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/account-reads.ts) and registered on the public surface. **Measured from `CompositionReport.registered` on a server built from the modules discovered on disk, never from a grep**, on both surfaces: `public` goes from 36 registered to 40 and `operator` holds at 19, which is [ADR-083](decisions/ADR-083.md) section 4's rule that the admin deployment answers 404 by having nothing there rather than by running a check.

**ONE OF THE FOUR IS SERVED END TO END AND THREE REFUSE BY NAME. THE COUNT IS REPORTED RATHER THAN ROUNDED.** `/marks` reads real `daily_marks` and `rule_states` rows through the accessor and renders section 6's `MarkListItem`. The other three raise `AccountReadsBackendUnwired` carrying the blocker and answer **503 `service_unavailable`**, which is `databaseAuthBackend`'s shape (four of sixteen) and `databaseAccountsBackend`'s (two of three) taken as they stand: a fixture serving real traffic is worse than a 503, and a refusal that carries the blocker is worth more than one that shrugs.

**THE THREE BLOCKERS ARE MEASUREMENTS AND NOT JUDGEMENT CALLS, AND EACH NAMES ITS OWNER.**

**`/timeline` has no door.** `events` is in neither `TABLES` nor `SCOPE_RULES` (`TABLES` parsed: 104 members), so no scope class reaches it. [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts) states the refusal and its reason: `identity_id` and `account_id` are both nullable with no CHECK tying them, so a rule naming one drops every row of the other kind, while [EVENTS](architecture/EVENTS.md) section 2 rows the portal timeline as PER-ACCOUNT and [M04](plans/M04-trader-portal.md) section 5 consumes identity-level events on the same screen. The payload is the second refusal: `kyc.dedupe_hit` carries `matched_identity_id` inside `jsonb`, which no scope rule can express and which `INV-M4-06` forbids the portal to receive. **Registering it is `packages/db`'s file and this session did not hold it.**

**`/eligibility` IS A SCHEMA DELTA AND THAT IS THE SESSION'S MOST VALUABLE FINDING.** `INV-M5-02` requires both payout endpoints to call `evaluatePayout` with identical inputs, and **its `RuleState` argument is not persistable in this schema**: the engine type requires `lifetimeSettledCents`, `breached` and `breachKind`, [`0015_rule_states.sql`](../packages/db/migrations/0015_rule_states.sql) declares none of the three, and **`lifetime_settled_cents` appears in no migration in the tree at all**. Supplying them would mean inventing a lifetime money total and a breach verdict on a money read; deriving the total by summing `payout_requests` is the aggregate [ADR-157](decisions/ADR-157.md) section 5 refused on evidence; and writing a second evaluator instead is exactly what `INV-M5-02` exists to forbid. **The repair is a migration, and a transcription session rules nothing.**

**`/certificate` is blocked on ONE named field.** Section 6 types `image_url` as a non-nullable "signed, time-limited" URL, and `certificates` ([`0020_public_surface.sql`](../packages/db/migrations/0020_public_surface.sql)) carries `code`, `claims`, `signature` and `signing_key_id` and **no image location column**, so there is not even a stored value to sign. [M11](plans/M11-certificates-social-proof.md) section 5 rows this endpoint as shared with M4 and states that "M11 owns what is behind both"; the card renderer, the CDN origin and the URL signer are all M11's and none exists. Inventing an origin would also break [`origin.ts`](../apps/admin/src/origin.ts)'s rule that a real hostname is a deployment fact and never a value this repository writes down. **Every other field of the response is readable from `certificates` today**, which is why the refusal names one field rather than the endpoint.

**THE SHAPES ARE DECLARED IN FULL FOR ALL FOUR**, on `accounts.ts`'s ruling about `AccountProgress`: the refusal is about WIRING and not about SHAPE, and a port whose type was also missing would be a blocker nobody could measure the size of. Each of the three is now one method body away from serving.

**A NEW MODULE RATHER THAN `accounts.ts`, AND THE ARGUMENT IS IN THE FILE.** That file had already declined in writing -- its `RuleStateRow` note calls `engine_gates` and `context_gates` *"`/eligibility`'s and somebody else's endpoint"*. Three reasons the split is right rather than merely inherited: [ADR-100](decisions/ADR-100.md)'s module list is the directory listing and is never written down, so a new file collides with nothing while an edit puts this diff in the same file as every later change to `GET /accounts`; the ports and the tables are disjoint, so merging would give `start.ts`'s single `useAccountsBackend(...)` line a backend most of which refuses; and none of the four paths is declared anywhere else, so `compose`'s duplicate refusal has nothing to catch. **The four are ONE module rather than four** because they are one path family with one tenancy resolution and one 404 shape, landing on one branch in one session.

**TENANCY IS THE ACCESSOR'S ON ALL FOUR AND THE ACCOUNT IS RESOLVED FIRST, WHICH IS NOT A CONVENIENCE.** `scopedDb(identityId)` ANDs tenancy onto the address, so `rowAt('accounts', { id })` on identity A naming identity B's account reaches zero rows and becomes the 404 section 1 requires. **A read that narrowed only by the id in the path would still be tenancy-safe and would answer 200 with an empty page for a stranger's account id**, which is the existence oracle section 1 forbids stated in the other direction. Asserted in two halves on `accounts.test.ts`'s split: structurally, that A naming B's account opens only the scoped door with A's identity and stops at the account read; behaviourally, over a store that models the AND, that the answer is 404 and never 403 and never B's data. The negative control is there too.

**TWO PLACES THE CONTRACT UNDERDETERMINES `/marks` ARE RULED IN THE FILE AND REPORTED IN THE PULL REQUEST RATHER THAN SETTLED QUIETLY.** What `corrected` means on a day carrying two marks -- one item per day, the current row, with the flag saying the day was corrected, because the alternative plots a superseded balance on an equity chart as a fact about somebody's money -- and the list envelope, which section 1 supplies generically and section 6's own `GET /wallet/entries` row writes out longhand.

**ADR-157's RANGE TERM IS USED WHERE IT WAS BUILT TO BE USED AND NOTHING ELSE WAS REACHED FOR.** `atMost` bounds the cursor read above on both halves of the join; the accessor still offers no `ORDER BY` and no `LIMIT`, so the order and the page are folds in the route, which is `accounts.ts`'s own split and keeps money arithmetic out from behind a database in the suite. **No `SqlExecutorReason` member, no `SystemReason` member, no `pg` import, no cast past a key type, and `packages/db` untouched.**

**Reported and not repaired: `accounts.ts`'s header states that `apps/api/package.json` does not declare `@merit/rules-engine`, and it does**, since session 252 added it for `routes/payouts.ts`. **The refusal that sentence supports survives on its other half** -- `0004_catalog.sql`'s "there is no plan parameter anywhere in application code", and `trading_calendar` unreachable through every door -- so nothing about `readProgress`'s 503 changes. That file is outside this fence.

**Verified in pieces, because `pnpm run verify` no longer fits one timeout. 33 of 33 gates, 12 of 12 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, `format:check` clean, 173 test files / 3,183 passed / 6 skipped, and `falsify.mjs` exit 0 with `git status --porcelain` empty immediately after.** The dispatch baseline of 172 / 3,137 / 6 was reproduced exactly before anything changed.

## The accounts segment is wired, and it has the error arm the payout centre does not (2026-08-27, session 285)

**[ADR-162](decisions/ADR-162.md) executed for `app/accounts/`. No ADR taken, no migration, no `SD-nn`, no `apps/api` change, no `packages/db` change, and [`apps/portal/src/http/client.ts`](../apps/portal/src/http/client.ts) is untouched.** Two of the six segments are now wired to the one client; `calendar`, `referrals` and `(purchases)` still render from fixtures and each is blocked on an unregistered read.

**THE DISPATCH'S ENDPOINT ROW WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND ONLY THE COMPOSITION REPORT SETTLED IT.** The prompt rowed this segment as *"WIRABLE NOW  accounts  all endpoints registered"* and named two reads. Built with `discoverRouteModules()` then `buildServer({ surface: 'public', modules })` and read off `CompositionReport.registered` at `e444ab6`, this segment needs **four**: `GET /accounts`, `GET /accounts/:accountId` and `GET /plans/:planId/versions/:version` were registered and **`GET /accounts/:accountId/marks` was not**. **A prompt has now been wrong about this twice in two sessions**, which is the same lesson session 273 recorded from the other side: a grep over route files and a dispatch table are both derived, and the built server is not.

**SESSION 284 REGISTERED THE MARKS ROUTE IN THE SAME WAVE, AND THE SCREEN STILL NAMES IT.** The measurement was re-run against the merged tree and it moved: `GET /accounts/:accountId/marks` is registered now. **That is a stale wiring rather than a stale claim, and the tense is corrected in source rather than the sentence deleted.** The route exists and this application still cannot read it, for two reasons that are each somebody else's file: [`api/types.ts`](../apps/portal/src/api/types.ts) **transcribes `MarkListItem` and no list envelope at all**, while the endpoint answers section 1's `{ data, next_cursor }`; and **nobody has ruled what the portal does with a cursor**, which matters here because `toEquitySeries` takes `as_of_trading_day` as an argument precisely because *"the newest row in THIS PAGE is the newest row the client happens to hold"*. A limit and a follow-or-not are a decision, and inventing one inside a `load` is how it gets made by nobody. So SC-M4-02 is wired end to end and SC-M4-03 performs both reads it can and names the marks endpoint as the one it is waiting on.

**THE LOAD TYPES HAVE THREE ARMS, AND THE THIRD IS THE ONE [ADR-162](decisions/ADR-162.md) SECTION 5 ITEM 1 REPORTS MISSING ON THE PAYOUT CENTRE.** `ready`, `unavailable` (**nothing failed**: no `MERIT_API_ORIGIN`, or an endpoint nobody serves yet) and `error` (**a registered endpoint refused or failed**, carrying the `PortalErrorKind` the client mapped and the status it was mapped from). **It is a decline at authorship rather than a repair**: this segment had no load type at all, so writing `ready | unavailable` and reporting the hole would have been reproducing a known defect on purpose in the one segment positioned to avoid it. A 500 and an unregistered route no longer render the same screen, and **a 404 on another trader's account reaches the trader as "not found"** through `toPortalErrorKind`, which is `INV-M4-07` working rather than a wording this segment chose.

**THE GUARDS CHECK EVERY FIELD THE VIEWS READ AND `progress` ON EVERY PHASE.** Only the funded branch of `toProgress` reads `win_days`, `traded_days`, `consistency`, `cadence` and `ladder`, so a guard that checked the phase in the response it happened to hold would pass on an eval account and crash on the next funded one, on the screen `SC-M4-03` calls the one somebody opens when something looks wrong. **Every `_cents` and `_bp` field is checked as an INTEGER**, on `app/payouts/source.ts`'s argument: `format/money.ts` refuses a non-integer, and this refuses it one layer earlier where the answer is an honest error state rather than a crash inside a component.

**`isPinnedPlanSource` DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLAIM `PlanVersionResponse`.** This segment reads three of that type's eight fields, and a predicate returning `value is PlanVersionResponse` after checking three would be [ADR-162](decisions/ADR-162.md) foreclosure 5's partial guard with the sign flipped: not a guard that skipped a field the view reads, but one that claimed five fields nobody checked. So the predicate names exactly what it verified.

**`accountsSource()` AND `AccountsSourceNotWiredError` ARE REPLACED RATHER THAN LEFT STANDING**, which is what [`ports.ts`](../apps/portal/src/app/accounts/ports.ts) itself asked for: *"WHOEVER WIRES THE PORTAL OWNS REPLACING THIS FUNCTION AND NOTHING ELSE IN THIS SEGMENT."* **The test that asserted the throw is NARROWED into a stronger claim rather than deleted**: it used to prove that one of the three screens was unreachable, and it now proves that a trader with no accounts, an unwired endpoint and a refusal render as three distinct screens.

**One limit of the client is reported rather than reached for.** `ApiSuccess` is `{ ok: true, body: unknown }` and carries no status, so a `2xx` whose body fails the guard is reported as `server_error` with `status: null`: there is no number at this layer and inventing `200` would put one in the server's mouth. Widening `ApiSuccess` is a change to [ADR-162](decisions/ADR-162.md)'s file and this fence does not hold it.

## The `kyc` segment reads through that client, and the write it could have made is refused with an argument (2026-08-27, session 286)

**[ADR-162](decisions/ADR-162.md) executed rather than amended. No new ADR, no migration, no `SD-nn`, no `apps/api` change, no `packages/db` change, and [`apps/portal/src/http/client.ts`](../apps/portal/src/http/client.ts) is untouched.** `apps/portal/src/app/kyc/` performs `GET /kyc/status` through the one transport file. **`POST /kyc/session` is not called**, and the reason is a fence rather than an absence.

**BOTH ENDPOINTS WERE MEASURED REGISTERED, WHICH MAKES THE REFUSAL THE HARDER ARGUMENT AND THE ONLY HONEST ONE.** `discoverRouteModules()` then `buildServer({ surface: 'public', modules })`, reading `CompositionReport.registered` on this tree: 36 routes on `public`, 18 withheld, **`GET /kyc/status` and `POST /kyc/session` both among the 36**. Session 273's dispatch named two registered endpoints and only one was, so this one was re-derived from the application rather than trusted.

**THE WRITE IS REFUSED TWICE OVER AND NEITHER FENCE WAS WIDENED TO REACH IT.** [`apps/api/src/routes/kyc.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/kyc.ts) says `openVerification` *"WRITES TWO ROWS IN ONE TRANSACTION"* -- a `kyc_verifications` row and a `kyc_funnel_events` row at `session_created` -- and that *"it is a new row every time and there is no update on this port"*, which puts starting a session inside [`surface.test.ts`](../apps/portal/test/surface.test.ts)'s *"nothing that changes a trader account exists in this app"*, whose forbidden list already carries `kycSubmit`. **Independently, the transport cannot express it**: `ApiClient` declares `get` and no second method, so a POST from this segment is either an edit to [ADR-162](decisions/ADR-162.md)'s file or a second `fetch(` the suite fails on by name and line. **No needle in `surface.test.ts` was narrowed, because nothing here needed it narrowed**, and session 158's rule in that file is that *"a session that deletes an entry instead of narrowing it has removed the control while appearing to satisfy it."*

**THE GUARD ADR-162 CLAUSE 5 REQUIRES WAS ALREADY IN THIS SEGMENT AND NOW READS THE WIRE.** `screenKycStatus` takes `unknown`, screens the WHOLE payload for a document-shaped key before it reads one field, and refuses a non-string on any of the five contract fields. The wiring is one line handing it `ApiResult.body`, which is what that clause means by *"narrowing lands beside the transcription that declares the shape"*: the check was written months before a transport existed and did not have to be invented under time pressure beside a `fetch`.

**A WRONG STATE ON THIS SCREEN IS A COMPLIANCE STATEMENT, SO FAIL-CLOSED IS ASSERTED ON THE RENDERED BYTES.** [`apps/api/src/routes/accounts.ts:824`](../apps/api/src/routes/accounts.ts) carries the posture for this class one deployable over: a chain whose head cannot be named *"fails closed, because the alternative is reporting somebody verified on the strength of an ordering this table does not declare."* **Fifteen failure modes, every payload claiming `verified`** -- 401, 403, 404, 429, 500, 503, no response at all, a non-object body, an array, a missing field, a non-string state, a state the enum cannot produce, a placement the `0003_kyc.sql` CHECK cannot produce, a document on the wire, and an internal-tier sentence -- **each renders no verified badge, no state attribute, and a named content state carrying copy a trader can read.** Never verified, and never a blank that reads like neither. **Watched failing on a real seeded defect** that returned a fabricated verified status on a refused read, reporting `401 renders no verified badge` with the offending markup printed.

**IT DOES NOT SUBSTITUTE `kyc_required` ON A FAILURE, AND THAT IS WHERE IT DIVERGES FROM `accounts.ts` ON PURPOSE.** That function computes a value the API will state; the screen renders a value the API stated. A `cookies()` outside a request scope, a bug in a path, or anything else propagates, because converting those would make every fault in this application look like a deployment nobody configured.

**THE CLIENT IS BUILT INSIDE `status()` AND NEVER AT MODULE SCOPE.** `serverApiClient()` closes over ONE session cookie; a client built once when the module loaded would serve the first trader's session to every trader afterwards. That is `FM-M4-03` reached by a `const` at the top of a file, and nothing in the type system says so, which is why it is written down.
