## The two operator paths out of a held payout, and the audit trail the CHECK erases (2026-08-27, session 288)

**[`apps/api/src/routes/admin-payouts.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/admin-payouts.ts) registers [API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) section 8's `POST /admin/payouts/:id/release` and `POST /admin/payouts/:id/enforce`.** No ADR number, no migration number, no `packages/db` change, no contract change, and the route registry needed no edit at all because [`registry.ts`](../apps/api/src/registry.ts)'s module list **is** the directory listing.

**MEASURED FROM THE APPLICATION AND NOT FROM A GREP, BEFORE AND AFTER.** `discoverRouteModules()` then `buildServer({ surface, modules })`, reading `CompositionReport`. Before: neither path was in `registered` **nor** in `withheld` on either surface, so they did not exist; `public` 36 registered / 18 withheld, `operator` 19 / 35, 17 modules. After: `operator` registers both and withholds neither (21 / 35), `public` withholds both and registers neither (36 / 20), 18 modules. **`withheld` is what produces the public deployment's 404 and its own comment says so**, so both lists are the evidence rather than one standing in for the other.

**`payout_requests_hold_is_complete` IS A BICONDITIONAL AND THESE TWO ENDPOINTS ARE THE ONLY THINGS THAT WILL EVER CROSS IT.** [`0031:62`](../packages/db/migrations/0031_payout_hold_and_identity_restriction.sql), read at the source and quoted in the module's header: at any status other than `held_pending_review`, **all five** of `held_at`, `hold_flag_id`, `hold_expires_at`, `hold_tos_clause` and `hold_reason` must be `NULL`. [ADR-158](decisions/ADR-158.md) finding 9 is confirmed at source. Both writes therefore blank all five in one statement, and a write that blanked four is refused by Postgres and by nothing else in this tree.

**SO THE CONSTRAINT IS READ OUT OF THE MIGRATION BY THE SUITE AND COMPARED WITH THE `SET` CLAUSE, COLUMN FOR COLUMN.** CI-04 has no database ([ADR-085](decisions/ADR-085.md)), so that refusal does not run in CI; the comparison is mechanical, it fails if the `SET` clause omits a column the CHECK names, and it fails equally if it names a sixth. That is CLAUDE.md's own remedy for the class of error the reconciliation session paid for -- *"prefer a new CI gate over a bigger model whenever the error is checkable"* -- reached with a test rather than with a model.

**WHAT IS LOST IS NAMED IN THE CODE, IN THE SUITE AND IN THE PULL REQUEST, AND IS NOT WORKED AROUND.** The contract's `released_hold` and `enforced_hold` carry four members, so of the five columns the write blanks, **`hold_reason` reaches nobody**. And after either call the row cannot say it was ever held at all: `payout_requests` no longer distinguishes a request held for forty-seven hours from one never flagged, and `GET /payouts` correctly returns `hold: null` for both. **The whole durable record is the [`admin_actions`](architecture/data-model/admin_actions.md) row's `before`**, which this module writes with all five columns under their database names, plus the hold's own flag and ToS clause in `evidence_refs`. A migration is sacred once merged, so the constraint cannot be repaired from a route file, and a shadow column beside it would be a second record of the hold that the database does not constrain -- worse than the hole, because the five columns are complete-or-absent by construction and an unconstrained duplicate is neither.

**THE RELEASE POSTS `LT-01`, AND THAT IS THE ONE NON-OBVIOUS CALL IN THE SESSION.** [ADR-040](decisions/ADR-040.md)'s own table: a held request has nothing posted and `frozen` is entered *"from `approved`, after LT-01 posted"*, so `approved` is the post-`LT-01` state; [`payouts.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/payouts.ts) does not post while the hold stands and says in terms that *"the ledger is the discriminator ... and it is what makes release mean 'approve and pay' on a hold"*. **The deferred posting has exactly one home and it is this endpoint**, and a release that moved the status and posted nothing would mark a payout paid that never paid. The posting is built by `payouts.ts`'s own `lt01()`, **imported rather than retranscribed**, so this module names no ledger account and holds no ledger arithmetic; every amount comes off the stored row (`INV-M5-02`); and the `LedgerTx` is a port the wiring supplies, exactly as `PayoutTx.ledger` is. **The enforcement posts nothing**, because a held request has posted nothing to reverse.

**THE LEDGER KEY IS THE REQUEST'S OWN STORED ONE, AND THE STRING IS IDENTICAL TO THE ONE `payouts.ts` WOULD HAVE USED.** `ledger_transactions.idempotency_key` is `text NOT NULL UNIQUE` and `INV-M5-06` is the same key on every attempt, so `` `${PAYOUT_ENDPOINT} ${stored}` `` makes `LT-01` for one payout request **one posting whichever door reaches it**: a second one is refused by the database rather than by the application remembering not to. A key naming this endpoint instead would have let the two doors mint two postings for one approval and both would have committed.

**ADR-157's ROW LOCK IS THE FIRST STATEMENT OF EVERY TRANSACTION AND NO ADVISORY LOCK IS TAKEN.** `lockAt('payoutRequests', { id })` is `rowAt` plus `FOR UPDATE` on the same predicate; two operators resolving one hold is the case it exists for, and the second blocks, reads a row whose status has moved, and gets `conflict`. The suite asserts that nothing reads `payout_requests` unlocked.

**`INV-M5-23`'s SHAPE IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN COMMENTED.** The 401 and the 403 are decided **before** `operator()` opens a transaction, so a `readonly` operator's refusal writes no `admin_actions` row, no snapshot and no row change. The suite asserts the recorder is empty on both refusals rather than only asserting the status code.

**TWO THINGS ARE REPORTED RATHER THAN REPAIRED AND BOTH ARE INHERITED.** [ADR-158](decisions/ADR-158.md) finding 1, `payout_requests.approved_at` is `NOT NULL DEFAULT now()` so a held request already carries a false approval time: **this endpoint holds the true instant and deliberately does not write it**, because writing it would destroy the request instant irrecoverably to correct a value already dispositioned, while `admin_actions.created_at` records the release durably and append-only. Overwriting is the lossy direction. And the contract's own enforce paragraph: **no column holds `failure_note`**, so an enforced payout reaches the trader with a null note.

**Verified in pieces. 33 of 33 gates, 12 of 12 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, `format:check` clean, 173 test files / 3,178 passed / 6 skipped, and `falsify.mjs` clean. The dispatch baseline of 33 / 12 / 0 / 0 / 172 / 3,137 / 6 reproduced exactly before anything changed.**

**[ADR-163](decisions/ADR-163.md), `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED. **THE PLAN RECOMMENDED AN ANSWER AND PERMITTED A REFUSAL, AND THE RECOMMENDATION IS TAKEN WITH THE ARGUMENT THE NUMBER WAS RESERVED FOR.** The address is [`apps/api`](../apps/api) on the two deployments that already exist. **The argument is that the operator 404 is a property of the ROUTE SET and the route set is chosen at STARTUP by the one file that resolves `MERIT_API_SURFACE`**, so a live channel served by any other process is withheld by a second copy of the prefix rule or by nothing at all, and [ADR-161](decisions/ADR-161.md)'s `F5` has already priced the second copy as *"a second transcription of the contract, going stale the first time a route is added"*.

**THE ADDRESS IS AN ORIGIN AND NOT ONLY A PROCESS, AND THAT IS WHERE THE SIXTH DEPLOYABLE COSTS THE MOST.** [INFRA section 3](architecture/INFRA.md) hard rule 3 says the C-08 IP allowlist and the admin origin's Cloudflare rules *"are scoped to the origin rather than to a service, so they covered `api-admin` from the day [ADR-083](decisions/ADR-083.md) ruled it into existence"*. **So an operator live channel running where `api-admin` already runs inherits the control by running there, and one running on an origin nobody added to the allowlist is outside it while every check in this repository stays green.** This corpus has already made the smaller version of that mistake once, naming one service where two run, and [ADR-089](decisions/ADR-089.md) is the correction.

**THE SIXTH DEPLOYABLE IS THE DANGEROUS CANDIDATE PRECISELY BECAUSE IT IS REFUSED BY NOTHING, AND THAT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED.** `apps/live/package.json` plus `apps/live/src/api/v1/admin/liability.ts`, a sixth application directory holding a path that spells an operator route on the operator surface, takes `node packages/tooling/checks/repo-invariants.mjs` to **11 of 11 and exit 0**: `RI-04` and `RI-09` both iterate a hand-written five-name list and neither reads `apps/`. **`RI-04`'s own `covers` says so** and [session 153](sessions/2026-08-24-session-153.md), which widened that list to five, recorded the gap as open on purpose, *"deriving the list from disk was refused as a different check with a different failure mode"*. **So the approval clause is that different check, run once by hand in the entry, and not a gate this session found weak.** The directory was removed and the tree is clean.

**TAKING THE RECOMMENDATION MEANS THE DISPATCH'S OWN WORDING DOES NOT HAPPEN, AND THE ENTRY SAYS SO RATHER THAN LETTING A LATER READER FIND AN ABSENCE.** [P6 section 8](plans/P6-live-tier.md)'s `P6-b` row says *"INFRA section 2.1 gains its service"* and *"section 3's table gains its row or rows"*. **The live tier has no container of its own**: the channel is `apps/api`, the ingest is `worker`, the adapter is `packages/rithmic` and its row landed yesterday, and the cache is `164`'s. So both tables gain amended cells, INFRA section 2.1's heading still reads six, and the phase's smallest diff is its whole finding.

**THE DIAGRAM GAINS THREE ARROWS AND NO LIVE-CACHE NODE, AND THE OMISSION IS WRITTEN UNDER IT.** `Rithmic` to `Worker` for the indicative ticks, `API` to `Portal` and `API` to `Admin` for the frames, dotted throughout, **with the dotted edge carrying the diagram's only new vocabulary: delivery nobody asked for, labelled indicative on the number itself.** The leg from the ingest to the channel is a STORE, and two of [P6 section 10 item 1](plans/P6-live-tier.md)'s three readings draw nothing at all: a table inside `DB`, or a process-local store inside `API`. **Drawing one would settle a ruling this slice does not hold.**

**AND THE ADDRESS CONSTRAINS THAT MEDIUM WITHOUT CHOOSING IT.** The channel is served by two services, and [INFRA section 2.1](architecture/INFRA.md) already reasons about a service running more than one instance while pinning no instance count. **So a process-local live cache is per-instance rather than per-firm, and two clients of one account can hold different numbers with nothing wrong anywhere.** The plan knew the other half: that reading *"makes `GS-132`'s poisoning step untestable from outside"*.

**WHAT IS LEFT TO `P6-g`, AND THE ONE CLAUSE THAT BINDS IT.** The mechanism is entirely that slice's: whether `HTTP_METHODS` gains a member, whether the registry keys on something other than `METHOD /path`, whether the channel is composed or registered beside `compose`, and the rate-limit row [ADR-161](decisions/ADR-161.md) section 5 item 1 hands it. **The constraint is that the live channel's contract path sits under `BASE_PATH` and its withholding is `surfaceServes` evaluated on that path at startup**, in the process that resolved the surface, because [`surface.ts`](../apps/api/src/surface.ts)'s `assertContractPath` refuses a path carrying the base path and a socket registered beside `compose` is served identically by both deployments. **On `API_SURFACES` the entry is not silent and not a prohibition either**: the address creates no requirement for a third member, so a third one is something `P6-g` would be buying rather than needing, and that slice's entry owes the reason.

**FOUR THINGS REPORTED AND NOT TAKEN.** **`P6-c`'s fence holds neither [OVERVIEW](architecture/OVERVIEW.md) nor [INFRA](architecture/INFRA.md)**, and under two of its three available media it changes one or both, so that amendment is owed and unowned. **Whichever process serves the operator's live figure needs arithmetic that lives in `apps/admin` and `RI-04` forbids an app depending on an app**, which constrains `P6-j` and does not discriminate between addresses. **[`packages/rithmic/README.md`](../packages/rithmic/README.md) still carries the three sentences [session 271](sessions/2026-08-27-session-271.md) reported false**, outside that fence and this one. **And [INFRA section 2.1](architecture/INFRA.md) says *"no row of this section's table has ever held a hostname"* while its own Origin column holds two**, which is a sentence written before that column existed; it is inside this fence and it is a claim about [ADR-089](decisions/ADR-089.md)'s intent, so it is reported rather than rewritten.

## `P7-c` lands as a RULING and returns its migration number: the pass-rate CUSUM is recomputed and never stored ([ADR-167](decisions/ADR-167.md), proposed 2026-08-27, session 281)

**[P7 section 10 item 3](plans/P7-risk-and-abuse.md) held this slice for a founder answer, the answer was delegated, and what was delegated was the authority to CHOOSE rather than permission to assume.** Three readings, one taken, and the two that lose are costed rather than dismissed. **`S_t` is folded at read time from a series [`0007`](../packages/db/migrations/0007_accounts.sql) already carries, and no column, table or row anywhere holds it.**

**Reading 1 -- `metric` joins the primary key -- is refused on a MONEY-PATH DEFECT and not on the key change.** After the widening, `state text NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('armed', 'paused', ...))` governs the added rows and [API_CONTRACT:798](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md)'s `per_plan.sales_paused` derives from `state = 'paused'`, so an **advisory** statistic whose own panel gloss at [M06:96](plans/M06-admin-ops-console.md) is *"inspect before the funded wave"* acquires a column that spells a **revenue pause**, one `UPDATE` away, on the table [`INV-M5-12`](plans/M05-payout-system.md) is written about. It is also not insertable honestly: `min_sample integer NOT NULL CHECK (min_sample > 0)` forbids even the zero, so a CUSUM row must invent a minimum sample it does not have.

**Reading 2 -- a second table -- is refused on [`0049`](../packages/db/migrations/0049_reserve_coverage_snapshots.sql)'s OWN objection, with `0049`'s own remedy structurally unavailable.** That file's founder-read item 1 is *"a ratio stored beside its own numerator invites recomputation drift, where the stored `rcr_bp` and the stored `bounded_near_term_cents` disagree with each other in the same row. A ratio the database computes cannot disagree with its own inputs"*, and it bought its way out with a `GENERATED` column. **A `GENERATED` column is a row-local expression and `S_t` is a recurrence over the row before it**, so the drift `0049` named comes back one migration later on the same rail with no way to police it. Its parameter columns also have no source: `mu_0` and `sigma` are `DEP-M6-05`'s and [M06:556](plans/M06-admin-ops-console.md) puts `DEP-M6-05` in **Wave 4**.

**THE PLAN'S OWN STATED REASON FOR THE WINNING READING IS CORRECTED RATHER THAN REPEATED.** Section 5.3 says storing `S_t` makes it no more reproducible; **storing it makes the value RETRIEVABLE and not CHECKABLE**, and reproducibility comes from the parameter history rather than from a cached output. **A stored `S_t` that disagrees with a replay of the same series is worse than no stored `S_t`, because it yields two answers and no rule for which is right.**

**P7 RULE 17's SECOND CLAUSE DOES NOT SURVIVE THE ARITHMETIC, AND GETTING IT RIGHT IS WHAT REMOVES THE FLOAT.** Every operand of `S_t = max(0, S_(t-1) + (x_t - mu_0 - 0.5*sigma))` is a **rate** -- `x_t` a pass rate, `mu_0` its in-control mean, `sigma` its standard deviation, the threshold *"4 to 5 sigma"* of it -- **so the statistic IS commensurable with a basis point and is NOT commensurable with `ratio_bp`, which is a LOSS ratio carried in the same unit.** A column with the right unit and the wrong quantity is what *"column for column"* mistook for a fit. `integer` suffices and the bound is a multiplication rather than an assumption: the daily increment is at most `10000` basis points, so `int4` is unreached for **588 years**. **The slack is configured directly as `k_bp` and `sigma` is never halved on the evaluation path**, because halving an odd basis-point value truncates with a constant sign and **a recurrence is exactly the shape where a per-step rounding stops being negligible**. **[ADR-157](decisions/ADR-157.md) finding 8's numeric-transport ruling is NOT reached and the line that would reach it is named**: the moment `x_t` is computed with a SQL `COUNT` or `SUM` rather than by counting rows.

**THE FALSE DISPOSITION IS IN TWO PLACES AND THE DISPATCH NAMED ONE.** [DELTA_MANIFEST](../packages/db/DELTA_MANIFEST.md) section 26's `OI-01` register row says `plan_breaker_state` is `per_plan` **"column for column"** -- stronger than `0049`'s own text, which at least enumerates the five columns it checked -- and it is in the register rather than in a migration header, so it is the copy a reader reaches first. **Corrected in section 27 and never in `0049`**, on section 22's precedent: the defect is prose, there is nothing to supersede, and [E2](../MERIT_BUILD_MASTER_PROMPT.md) makes a merged migration unedittable.

**THE UNDERLYING GAP IS NOT CLOSED AND THE ENTRY SAYS SO.** The CUSUM had neither storage nor inputs; it now has a ruling about the first and still nothing about the second. [`apps/admin/src/page.ts:156`](../apps/admin/src/page.ts) already lists `P-M6-06` as **pending on `DEP-M6-05`**, quoting `FM-M6-07`: *"an uncalibrated CUSUM either constant alarms or none, which is the same as no chart."* **`P7-k` renders that absence rather than manufacturing a number**, which is the console's own existing disposition rather than a new one. **What needs a versioned home when the harness lands is the PARAMETER SET and not the statistic**, and [`detector_definitions`](../packages/db/migrations/0008_risk.sql) is named as the shape that already exists for that job and deliberately **not** taken, because it is `P7-d`'s file and its `is_sensitive` column is `P7-j`'s evidence-pack strip list.

**`OQ-M6-02`'s NUMBER IS UNTOUCHED and the schema half is ruled**, which is [P7 section 5.4](plans/P7-risk-and-abuse.md)'s own separation kept: `min_sample` is one scalar against one `sample_size` and the proposal is a conjunction of two counts over two populations, so the row expresses one term and the second lives in the evaluator or nowhere. **`sample_size` is the DENOMINATOR's count**, sourced from [`0016:116`](../packages/db/migrations/0016_treasury_controls.sql)'s own *"a two-transaction denominator"* rather than from a preference.

**`0051` IS NOT TAKEN AND RETURNS TO THE POOL UNSPENT**, its [ALLOCATION](decisions/ALLOCATION.md) row amended in place to say so, on `ADR-160`'s precedent and on the reservation's own condition: *"a number returned unspent is cheaper than a number taken to justify the reservation."* **No migration, no table, no `schema.ts` registration, no `scope.ts` change, no design record, no `SqlExecutorReason` member and no `SystemReason` member.** `schema.ts` receives **one comment and no code**, because it is the file a later session would edit to add the column the entry forecloses. **`scope.ts` is not touched even by a comment**, on its own rule that every `why` states the table's tenancy and never the reader's use.

**MONEY PATH BY CONTENT and NO `E2` READ IS OWED, because nothing was written that a founder must read line by line.** Approval line UNSIGNED.

## `detector_definitions` is seeded and the seed IS the registry, and eleven of the eighteen rows carry no number (2026-08-27, session 282)

**[`P7-d`](plans/P7-risk-and-abuse.md) is written.** Every detector [M07 section 3.2](plans/M07-risk-abuse.md) names has a `detector_definitions` row with `version`, `parameters`, `effective_from` and `is_sensitive`, on [`packages/db/src/seed/calendars`](../packages/db/src/seed/calendars)' shape: a hand-written source file holding the values, a generator that refuses rather than guesses, and a generated artifact that is committed and reviewed. **No migration, no ADR, no `SD-nn`, no `SqlExecutorReason` member, no `SystemReason` member, no `pg` import, no cast past a key type, and no edit to `schema.ts` or `scope.ts`.** `detector_definitions` was verified as landed DDL at [`0008_risk.sql`](../packages/db/migrations/0008_risk.sql) before a row was written, and the first suite in the test asserts it carries every column a row holds, so a missing column would have been a red test rather than a loader failure later.

**EVERY VALUE CARRIES THE LINE OF `M07` IT WAS READ FROM, AND THE GENERATOR OPENS THAT FILE AT THAT LINE.** A `cite` of the form `<path>:<line>` and a `quote`, resolved by reading the authority and requiring the quote to occur in it verbatim: a paraphrase fails, a drifted line number fails, and a number nobody can point at fails because there is no line to point it at. **197 citations resolve.** The authority itself is digested, because a cite that still resolves against a *different* `M07` has silently changed meaning. This is the assertion [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md) asks for in place of a bigger model, against the error class its own caution names: a claim never checked against its primary source.

**ELEVEN OF THE EIGHTEEN ROWS CARRY NO STATED NUMBER AT ALL, AND THAT IS `OQ-M7-02`'s STATE RATHER THAN A GAP IN THE TRANSCRIPTION.** Seven carry one: `D-01`'s 2 second window, `D-02`'s 20 trading days and -8000 bp floor, `D-09`'s more-than-one destination, `D-16`'s 10000 bp exclusive ceiling on an inferred edge, `D-12`'s zero trading data, `D-13`'s 5 trading days and -9500 bp floor, and `D-18`'s four required legs. The other eleven are `unstated` throughout, each carrying the `M07` phrase that names the knob and no value. **A parameter has three states and they are not interchangeable**: `unstated` sends a later session to find the number `M07` owes, `not_applicable` tells them there was never one, and `stated` is the only one that may carry a value. `D-10` has no numeric threshold because its statistic is a condition; `D-12` writes no `risk_flags` row at all because its output is a watched-cluster set, so its `flag_status` is `not_applicable` and `open` there would be false rather than merely cautious.

**THE POSTURE IS RECORDED AND IT IS UNEXERCISED, WHICH IS THE HONEST THING TO SAY ABOUT IT.** `OQ-M7-02` recommends tuning for recall over precision during beta. That is advice about **which way to be wrong when choosing a number**, and this seed chooses no number. So the posture governs nothing here and will govern the first session that fills a null in.

**AND ITS SECOND HALF IS CONTESTED BY FOUR OTHER PLACES IN `M07`, SO THE SEED WRITES NEITHER READING.** Read literally, *"everything above severity 3 going to the digest"* sends severity 4 and 5 to the digest. That is the band `G-HOLD-REQUIRED` reads to **hold a payout**, the band `SD-M7-02` gives `sla_due_at` to, and the band whose time-to-first-touch is a tracked metric; and it is **severity 1** that `M07` twice sends to the digest. A flag that holds a trader's money for 48 hours while sitting in a digest nobody works is `FM-M7-04`'s documented negligence at the top of the scale. **Routing is not a column of `detector_definitions` and section 3.2 gives no routing value**, so declining to write it costs the seed nothing and is what the fence requires; it is reported for the founder because under [ADR-040](decisions/ADR-040.md) the reading decides whether a high-severity flag reaches a human before the payout auto-releases and pays.

**TWO SENTENCES OF `M07` ARE READ, NAMED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT ENCODED, AND NAMING THEM IS THE POINT.** `D-16`'s own statistic cell says *"Hard links auto-enforce"* and section 7.9's Hard row says *"Auto-enforce."* over `D-08` and `D-09`. **Those are the Behavior column [P7](plans/P7-risk-and-abuse.md) warns is this phase's temptation**, and a seed that merely omitted them would be indistinguishable from one whose author never read them, so the next session would encode them. The source carries a `refusals` block naming both with its authority, the generator requires the block to exist, and the refusal is mechanical rather than trusted to a comment: any parameter whose **value** spells an enforcement outcome is rejected, every row's `flag_status` is `open` or `not_applicable`, and `D-16`'s `auto_enforce` is `not_applicable` because `OQ-M7-05` answers it both ways and **writing either value would settle an open question by being written**.

**`is_sensitive` IS UNIFORMLY `true`, AND THAT IS A FINDING FOR [`P7-j`](plans/P7-risk-and-abuse.md) RATHER THAN A RESULT.** `INV-M7-10` is unqualified and nothing in `M07` designates any detector parameter as trader-visible, so every row is sensitive with its own stated reason and no two reasons are the same. **The consequence is recorded here because this is the file that knows it**: while the column is uniform, a `trader` pack that COMPUTES its strip list from `is_sensitive` and one that strips every detector UNCONDITIONALLY produce byte-identical output, so `GS-112` passes either way and `INV-M7-10`'s mechanism is untested. `P7-j` needs a fixture row with `is_sensitive: false` to tell the two apart and **it cannot come from this seed**, because there is no `M07` line to cite for one. The test carries an assertion that goes red on the day the column acquires its first `false`.

**THE TEST IS THE INTERESTING HALF AND ITS EXPECTED SET IS PARSED RATHER THAN WRITTEN.** A hand-kept list of the detectors `M07` names is one more hand-maintained count that goes stale in the direction that matters, because the stale list would agree with the stale seed. So section 3.2 is parsed out of the authority and the two failures are separate findings, both seeded: a detector `M07` names and the seed forgot, and a detector the seed carries and `M07` names nowhere. **The row ORDER is checked too**, because `M07` runs `D-01` to `D-10`, then `D-15` to `D-17`, then `D-11` to `D-14` and `D-18`, which a set comparison would silently let a seed reshuffle. **The generator can produce 62 distinct rejections and 59 of them are watched failing on their own finding**, plus a test asserting that every `reject()` in it has a seed, a direct reach, or a stated proof of unreachability; the remaining three are backstops the generator's own row construction makes unreachable, named with their proof. **THREE SEEDED VIOLATIONS FAILED ON A MORE SPECIFIC FINDING THAN THE ONE THEY NAMED**, which is exactly what the suite exists to catch: the seeds were wrong and were corrected rather than the generator.

**`D-18` tests `footprint_present IS FALSE` and the value is SEEDED AS DATA** so `P7-h` has something to be checked against rather than a comment to be trusted, and `IS NOT TRUE` is refused there on its own finding. **No float appears anywhere**: the generator walks every number in the generated artifact, and `M07`'s two decimals become `-8000` and `-9500` basis points, which express a Pearson correlation exactly.

**Three things are reported and not decided.** `M07` gives **no version vocabulary** for `detector_definitions.version` and **no effective date**, and both columns are `NOT NULL`; they are declared as `chosen` values with reasons, and the generator refuses a `chosen` value that carries a `cite` at all, because a citation attached to a choice is the defect the whole file exists to prevent. And **no dispatch row exists in [sessions/README](sessions/README.md) for this session or for any of the other ten in this wave**, so [P7](plans/P7-risk-and-abuse.md) rule 1's *"strike your row"* had no row to strike; the entry was added and no dispatch row was invented.

**[`0008_risk.sql`](../packages/db/migrations/0008_risk.sql) makes `audience`, `redaction_profile` and `includes_detector_detail` all `NOT NULL` on `evidence_packs`, and the endpoint that writes those rows accepted no audience at all.** So the generator would have supplied one the caller never named, which [M06 section 4](plans/M06-admin-ops-console.md) forbids in the words this entry implements: *"the redaction profile follows from the audience and is recorded on the pack, not chosen per export"*. `GET /admin/evidence/:accountId` now requires `?audience=` beside `?reason=`, `EvidenceExportRequest` carries the field, and `EvidencePackResponse` echoes it.

**THERE IS NO DEFAULT AND THE NARROWEST ONE IS REFUSED TOO.** `trader` is the profile that would look safest to fall back to, and [`0008_risk.sql`](../packages/db/migrations/0008_risk.sql)'s own `evidence_packs_trader_gets_no_detector_detail` treats it as **the one combination that must be unrepresentable** rather than as a floor. The column exists, in that file's words, so the audience is *"a DECLARED, AUDITED PROPERTY of the export rather than a judgment made in the moment by whoever is answering the ticket"*, and a default is that judgment made by a process instead of by a person. `AS-M6-01`: the audience decides what leaves the building.

The test reads the `CHECK` out of the migration rather than out of a copy.

It is refused rather than relabelled, because overwriting the pack's audience with the requested one is the same disclosure with a truthful label removed. Seeded, it turns red; so does a seeded silent default, and so does a seeded fifth audience name.

**THE SECOND HALF IS A RECONCILIATION AND IT WENT THE OPPOSITE WAY FROM [ADR-153](decisions/ADR-153.md), WHICH IS THE PART WORTH READING.** Section 8 headed three endpoints with one line. **Measured from `CompositionReport` on both surfaces rather than from a grep**: `GET /admin/eligible-forecast` is registered on `operator` and withheld from `public`, and **`GET /admin/loss-ratios` and `GET /admin/cusum` are in NEITHER list on EITHER surface**, a match for either path across both reports returning zero. **So they 404 on the admin origin as well**, which is not the 404 [`registry.ts`](../apps/api/src/registry.ts) describes as *"this list being non-empty and nothing else"*: a withheld path answers on the operator origin, and these are declared by no module at all. **They are NOT deleted.** `GET /auth/otp` was named by no heading, defined nowhere and allocated to nobody; these two are defined by a heading, pinned by [`admin-reads.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/admin-reads.test.ts) as *"a register of contract rows nobody has built"*, and named inside `P7-k`'s own fence. **A backlog and a phantom look identical from outside the tree, and the repair for one is the opposite of the repair for the other.**

**THEIR BODIES ARE DELIBERATELY NOT SPECIFIED.** `P7-k` writes `sample_size` beside `min_sample` and an `insufficient_data` state, neither of which any field on `LiabilityResponse.per_plan` carries; and the CUSUM has no storage at all until `ADR-167` chooses it. A projection cannot be specified over an evaluator that does not exist or a table nobody has picked, and a shape written here is one that slice would have to break.

**`OQ-F4-03` IS NOT RULED, AND NAMING WHICH HALF IS ALREADY CLOSED IS THE POINT.** Whether a regulator pack carries **detector internals** is closed, by [M06 section 7](plans/M06-admin-ops-console.md), the [wave 3 batch 1 gate closure](decisions/gates/wave-3-batch-1-gate-closure-2026-08-14.md) and [EC-071](edge-cases/EC-071.md), which give all four audiences a profile and collapse three into one. Whether an **impersonation record** appears in a regulator pack is open and is **counsel's rather than the founder's**, in [ADR-068](decisions/ADR-068.md) section 3's own words. **A slice that meets a required `audience` parameter must not read the open half as settled by its presence.** `redaction_profile` is likewise not echoed and not ruled: the column carries no `CHECK`, `INV-M7-10` makes the strip list derived from `detector_definitions.is_sensitive`, and the vocabulary is `P7-j`'s.

And **[`admin-reads.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/admin-reads.test.ts) is rowed to no fence in either plan**: `P6` met that and so did this slice, `P7` section 9 fences `admin-reads.ts` to `P7-b` alone while rowing the test nowhere, and any later slice adding a `### GET /admin` row moves it in the same change or lands red.

## `P5-g` lands: the wallet reads, and the hold the screen exists to name has no input in this tree (2026-08-27, session 275)

**[API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) section 6.2's `GET /wallet` and `GET /wallet/entries` are served.** [`apps/api/src/routes/wallet.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/wallet.ts) and [`apps/api/test/wallet.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/wallet.test.ts) are the whole diff besides this section and the log. **No ADR, no migration, no `SD-nn`, no `SqlExecutorReason` member, no `SystemReason` member, no `pg` import, no cast past a key type, and [`scoped-db.ts`](../packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts) untouched.**

### THE FINDING IS THAT `held_cents` IS 0 ON EVERY RESPONSE THIS TREE CAN PRODUCE, AND IT IS THE FIELD THE SCREEN EXISTS FOR

**[ADR-158](decisions/ADR-158.md) clause 6 makes `available_at` null because *"no landed column carries that window's end for a purchase"*. The same absence decides MEMBERSHIP of the hold and not only its release time**, which is half a step further than that clause goes: a credit is held by P-3 when its funding purchase is *"still inside the chargeback window"*, and without the window's end nothing can say whether it is. So `cents` and `since` are exactly as uncomputable as `available_at` is, **a `WalletHold` cannot be constructed truthfully today, and `holds` is empty on every response**. `OQ-M20-02` asks the length and is open; `DEP-M20-03` would make it computable and is unbuilt.

**The failing direction is named rather than left to be inferred.** Rendering `held_cents: 0` says no hold is in force, and no hold IS in force: nothing in this tree places one, and `POST /wallet/withdrawals` cannot evaluate P-3 either, so this read promises a trader nothing the withdrawal leg would then refuse. **What it must not be read as is "P-3 was evaluated and found nothing"**, and `holdsToday` is one function returning one empty array so the day the window lands there is one place to change. **A chosen number of days added to `earliest_credit_at` would be a number this repository invented** ([ADR-139](decisions/ADR-139.md) clause 3), and a migration is outside this fence.

**`P-1` is absent for the contract's reason and not this one.** [ADR-158](decisions/ADR-158.md) clause 5: it holds a WITHDRAWAL and leaves the value spendable, so it is a flag on the external leg and never a member of `holds` here.

### THE BICONDITIONAL DOES NOT REACH THIS ROUTE, AND THE REASON IS WORTH THE PARAGRAPH

[ADR-158](decisions/ADR-158.md) finding 9 makes `payout_requests_hold_is_complete` erase the record of a hold the instant it resolves, so a rendering that read those columns could only ever see LIVE holds. **This file reads `wallet_entries` and nothing else, so the blindness does not reach it** -- and *"add the payout holds to the wallet's holds"* is the obvious next thought and is a category error. **A payout under hold has not settled, `LT-01` has not posted, and there is therefore no `wallet_entries` row for it at all**: it is not money in the wallet being withheld, it is money that has not arrived. Summing it into `held_cents` would make `balance_cents = withdrawable_cents + held_cents` false, which the contract states as an identity.

### THE BALANCE IS `max(id)` AND NOT `max(occurred_at)`, AND EVERY ORDINARY FIXTURE PASSES UNDER BOTH

`balance_after_cents` is a STORED running balance computed at APPEND time, so the current balance is the row appended LAST; `id` is `bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` and `occurred_at` is the business instant, which a correction or a backfill may legitimately set to the past. **The statement's own order is `occurred_at` descending and that is a different question the contract answers separately.** The two disagree only on a backdated row, which is why the suite builds the one world where they do.

### THE COST [ADR-157](decisions/ADR-157.md) SECTION 5 NAMES IS PAID IN FULL, AND THE NARROWING IS BLOCKED BY THE FENCE RATHER THAN BY THE ACCESSOR

*"The rows crossing the boundary are the window's rather than the match's."* **Both endpoints read the identity's WHOLE statement**: `GET /wallet` to render one balance, and `GET /wallet/entries` to render one page of at most 100, on every page. That is [`catalog.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/catalog.ts)'s `GET /purchases` shape exactly.

**`atMost` on `occurred_at` is this endpoint's term by name** -- [`scoped-db.ts`](../packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts) says *"a cursor over `wallet_entries` is `P5-g`'s and an inclusive bound re-reads its boundary row, so if that is unacceptable it is an argument `P5-g` makes rather than one this entry makes for it"* -- **and the inclusive bound is acceptable; this slice makes no argument against it. What is unavailable is the IMPORT.** [`apps/api/src/db.ts`](../apps/api/src/db.ts) is this deployable's one door onto `@merit/db` and re-exports nothing, and [`catalog.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/catalog.ts) declined the same import by name. **A two-line re-export in a file this fence does not hold is the whole of what is missing**, so it is reported rather than reached ([P5](plans/P5-payouts-and-wallet.md) section 11 rule 5). **It is NOT rule 10's reach-around**: nothing here needs the accessor widened, only re-exported.

### THE DISPATCH'S REGISTRY INSTRUCTION IS REFUTED BY THE APPLICATION

The prompt said *"the route REGISTRY entry is an APPEND -- add your row, order by path"*. **There is no row and no list.** [ADR-100](decisions/ADR-100.md)'s registry is the DIRECTORY LISTING: `discoverRouteModules` reads `src/routes/`, and [`registry.ts`](../apps/api/src/registry.ts) states it in capitals, *"SO THE MODULE LIST IS THE DIRECTORY LISTING AND IS NEVER WRITTEN DOWN"*. **Two routes were registered by adding one file and editing nothing.** Measured from `CompositionReport.registered` on both surfaces rather than from a grep: **`public` 36 to 38, `operator` withheld 35 to 37, the union 54 to 56, modules 17 to 18**, and `GET /health` is still the one path both register.

### NINE SEEDED DEFECTS, AND THE NINTH ESCAPED THE FIRST SUITE

**Eight were caught and the lexical tie-break in `isAfter` was GREEN**, because that branch is reached only when a page boundary falls INSIDE one `occurred_at` and no case did. Two cases were added that page across ids 9, 10 and 11 at one instant, where the lexical reading **silently drops entry 9 and the walk ends one movement short with nothing saying so**, and both were watched failing on the reseed. **The escape is the argument for seeding rather than for reading**: the suite was already thirty-seven green cases when it was blind to that branch.

**`typecheck` and `lint` caught two further defects `vitest` could not**, an optional property under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` and an unused import, which is why the three run separately here rather than as one green word.

### Left standing, and named rather than implied

**The `held > balance` guard in `renderWallet` is unreachable today and therefore UNWATCHED**: `holdsToday` returns an empty array on every input this tree can build, and the suite's name says so instead of implying a refusal it does not exercise. **No CLAIM row exists for this session** in [sessions/README](sessions/README.md), whose table ends at 272, so rule 1's strike had nothing to strike and none was invented. **[`db.ts`](../apps/api/src/db.ts)'s header asks that `grep -rln '@merit/db' apps/api/src` return exactly one file and it returns four**, three of them route files that discuss the package in prose; the convention it states is intact, the measurement it states is not, and the file is outside this fence.

**Measured with `pnpm install` run first, each command separately: 33 of 33 gates, 11 of 11 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, 171 test files / 3,153 passed / 6 skipped**, against the dispatch's `main` baseline of 170 / 3,115 / 6, which reproduced exactly before anything was written. **The `E2` line-by-line read is owed on every line of the route.**

## `P6-c` lands: the live cache gets a medium, a fifth role, and a REVOKE that runs against `0026`'s own default ([ADR-164](decisions/ADR-164.md), proposed 2026-08-27, session 278)

**[P6 section 10 item 1](plans/P6-live-tier.md) held this slice for a founder answer, the answer was DELEGATED to the session by [ALLOCATION](decisions/ALLOCATION.md)'s `164` row, and reading 1 of three is argued and taken: a Postgres table plus a fifth role.** [`0050_live_cache_and_role.sql`](../packages/db/migrations/0050_live_cache_and_role.sql) creates `live_account_state` and `merit_live`. **Migration `0050` is SPENT and does not return to the pool.**

**THE SENTENCE THE SLICE STARTS FROM WAS EXECUTED RATHER THAN BELIEVED.** [`0026`](../packages/db/migrations/0026_roles_and_grants.sql) ends with `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES ... TO merit_app`, so on the `0001`..`0049` tree a bare `CREATE TABLE zz_hazard_demo (id int)` returns **`t` on SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE** for the application role, with nothing granting it. **The separation four approved documents describe really does get further away when a table is added**, and that is now a transcript in [DELTA_MANIFEST](../packages/db/DELTA_MANIFEST.md) section 27 rather than a reading of a file.

**THE DEPARTURE FROM SIX PRECEDENTS IS ONE VERB AND IT IS THE WHOLE FILE.** [`0032`](../packages/db/migrations/0032_trading_calendar_holidays_coverage_revisions.sql), [`0039`](../packages/db/migrations/0039_economic_calendar.sql) and [`0049`](../packages/db/migrations/0049_reserve_coverage_snapshots.sql) each `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE` against that default, because each is implementing **append-only**. `FM-M12-08` is *"the stats worker holds no read grant on the live cache"* and [SECURITY](architecture/SECURITY.md)'s threat row is *"the engine has no read path"*, so `0050` revokes **`ALL`**, from `merit_app` and from `PUBLIC`. `merit_live` is `0034`'s shape and not `0026`'s: enumerated grants, **no `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` anywhere in the file**, and two belts.

**THE COST IS NAMED AND DELIBERATELY NOT SPENT, WHICH IS THE ONE THING A LATER SESSION MUST NOT MISS.** [`client.ts`](../packages/db/src/client.ts) opens **one pool from one `DATABASE_URL`**, and [INFRA section 5](architecture/INFRA.md) gives `merit_app` to *"API and worker at runtime"*. **So one process is one role, and while the API and the worker share `merit_app` no grant in PostgreSQL can separate "the API may read the cache" from "the stats worker may not".** [ADR-164](decisions/ADR-164.md) clause 4 rules that any process reading or writing the cache connects as `merit_live` and **refuses to say which process that is**: the address is `P6-b`'s and the mechanism is `P6-g`'s. **`F1` forecloses the cheap escape**, which is granting `merit_app` `SELECT` and making `FM-M12-08` false without anything failing.

**THE OTHER TWO READINGS ARE PRICED RATHER THAN DISMISSED.** A process-local store is refused on **`GS-132`**, which is the phase's own stated done-condition and requires the cache **populated from outside** the process that writes it; it is also at least two caches, because [INFRA section 2.1](architecture/INFRA.md) deploys `api` and `api-admin` as two services. **A second stateful service is refused on a ground [OVERVIEW section 3](architecture/OVERVIEW.md) does NOT supply, and the entry says so.** Neither limb of the pg-boss sentence transfers: a discardable cache needs no backup or restore, and `INV-M2-14` makes the ingest write nothing but the cache, so there is no second write for a transaction to be atomic with. **What refuses Redis is that it makes the separation a convention again** -- an absent import in the worker rather than a permission -- and permission is the word all four documents use.

**THREE COLUMNS ARE REFUSED AND EACH REFUSAL IS A MERGED-MIGRATION ARGUMENT.** No `kind`, because it is `SimWaypoint['kind']` and `V-M2-16` is unanswered, and a `CHECK` over an unconfirmed vendor vocabulary can never be corrected. No `at_utc`, because nothing in the landed contract reads it and storing the feed's clock beside ours invites staleness to be computed from the wrong one, which [ADR-152](decisions/ADR-152.md) clause 1 forbids. No `projected_floor_distance_cents`, because the floor is a rule threshold the engine owns. **And no monotonicity trigger**: the guard is `P6-f`'s upsert predicate and is recorded as OWED, which is why the trigger count moves **20 to 20**.

**THE STORE IS NOT APPEND-ONLY AND THAT SETTLES AN OPEN QUESTION ONE PHASE OVER.** [ADR-020](decisions/ADR-020.md) says *"Tier 2 is a view"*, so there is no history to keep, no expiry sweep, and no `DELETE` for `merit_live`. **[P6 section 3.5](plans/P6-live-tier.md)'s "does the accessor need a range term" resolves to NO**, and `P6-c` therefore never depended on `P5-a`.

**THE FENCE HAS TWO CELLS IT SHOULD NOT HAVE AND ONE IT LACKS, AND BOTH HALVES WERE EXECUTED.** `live_account_state` is **NOT registered** in [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts) or [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts), on [ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md)'s rule as [`scoped-db.test.ts`](../packages/db/test/scoped-db.test.ts)'s own adjacent comment quotes it -- *"the first session that NEEDS a table registers it"* -- and this slice writes the store, the role and the grant and **no reader**. [`0049`](../packages/db/migrations/0049_reserve_coverage_snapshots.sql)'s `reserve_coverage_snapshots` is the identical call one paragraph up in the same test. **What the fence lacks is that test file**, whose `expect(createdTables).toBe(112)` counts `^CREATE TABLE` over the **whole migration set**: any table-creating migration fails it, registered or not, and it was watched failing at 113 against 112. **A fence that authorises a `CREATE TABLE` and withholds that file authorises a red tree.** The count is corrected and never relaxed, and the comment beside it now records the eventual `derived` via `accounts` rule so the session that needs it does not re-derive it.

**WHAT IS OWED, NAMED FOR THE SLICES THAT OWN IT.** `P6-f` inherits the upsert's monotonicity predicate and the fact that **its ingest cannot run inside the batch worker's process** under clause 4, because that process is `merit_app`. `P6-g` and `P6-j` inherit the registration (three files, not two) and the read path's principal. **Neither a `SystemReason` nor a `SqlExecutorReason` member was added**, and the operator's cross-account live read will need one and must NAME the need rather than take it.

**Measured on this branch with `pnpm install` run first: 33 of 33 gates, 11 of 11 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, 170 test files / 3,115 passed / 6 skipped, and the baseline was reproduced on the dispatch SHA before anything changed.**

It now builds TEN ROUTES plus the framework's own not-found**, and `CI-07` builds both UI deployables rather than one. The shell is `next.config.mjs`, the root layout, a build seam and one `page` per surface; **`src/routes/`, `src/render/`, `src/content/`, `src/catalog/` and `src/stats/` are UNCHANGED**, and every page calls into them. `SITE_SURFACES` is the navigation and `derivedPaths`' three per-version addresses are the three dynamic routes.

The step was therefore not merely missing: a comment asserted it should not exist. Both are repaired in one diff, and the build step landed **after** the pages, because a build step that fails is not a gate.

**[ADR-095](decisions/ADR-095.md) RULING 4's CARVE-OUT WAS NOT WRITTEN, AND THAT IS THIS SESSION'S REAL FINDING.** The ruling admits one cache-control hook on `apps/site` and `INV-M9-04` makes revalidation part of the publish transaction's definition of done. **Its contract path is `POST /internal/revalidate`** ([M09](plans/M09-marketing-site.md) section 4, and `catalog/ports.ts` declares it), **`/internal` is an `OPERATOR_PREFIXES` entry in [`surface.ts`](../apps/api/src/surface.ts), and `RI-09` refuses any file putting an operator prefix directly below a routing root in a deployable that is not `apps/api`.** Writing the carve-out exactly as ruled turns an invariant red. Both were correct when written and [ADR-138](decisions/ADR-138.md) landed after ADR-095; **no ADR was allocated to this session and none was taken**, so the collision is reported. **`INV-M9-04` has no mechanism on this ref and cannot acquire one without a ruling.**

**`INV-M9-05` MOVED TO THE LAYOUT AND DID NOT WEAKEN, AND THE SPLIT IS THE POINT.** The footer is structural, so a new page cannot omit the disclosure by being new. The block a dispute quotes is a `content_documents` row carrying the version acceptance was recorded against, no endpoint serves one, and `siteDisclosure` returns `null` rather than minting one: **the footer falls back to the GLOSSARY sentence, marked in the markup as an interim source, while `page()` and `planPage()` still refuse a null disclosure**, so a marketing surface with no citable block renders no marketing copy at all. The footer obligation and the page model's precondition are two controls and only one of them has a fallback. That is [`apps/portal/src/app/layout.tsx`](../apps/portal/src/app/layout.tsx)'s move, copied rather than re-derived.

**NOTHING IN THE APP READS A CLOCK, WHICH IS `catalog/types.ts`' OWN SENTENCE KEPT TRUE.** The build stamp is read from `MERIT_SITE_BUILT_AT`, validated as an ISO-8601 UTC instant and cast in exactly one place; a build handed none has no stamp rather than a fresh one. **An unconfigured build is a STATE and not a crash**: every port read resolves to a reason string, so `next build` prerenders honest pages instead of dying, and no page shows a stand-in figure.

**Two environment variables are declared in the app and in no document.** `MERIT_SITE_API_BASE_URL` and `MERIT_SITE_BUILT_AT`. [INFRA](architecture/INFRA.md) section 2.1 rows the `site` service with `MERIT_API_SURFACE` *"not set"* and names no other variable for it; INFRA is frozen and outside this fence, so they are carried as owed rather than written in from outside.

**ADR-095 `F3` is carried unrepaired, as dispatched.** Under `next start` the regeneration cache is per process, so `revalidatePath` reaches one replica and `INV-M9-04` has a replica-count precondition no document states.

## The hourly expiry sweep, and the third clock nothing in this tree can release (2026-08-27, session 291)

**[`apps/worker/src/sweeps/expiry.ts`](../apps/worker/src/sweeps/expiry.ts) and [`ports.ts`](../apps/worker/src/sweeps/ports.ts) build [P5](plans/P5-payouts-and-wallet.md) section 8's `P5-j`: the hourly expiry sweep, ONE job over the THREE clocks [CRON_INVENTORY](ops/runbooks/CRON_INVENTORY.md)'s release-job table gives it, on that page's own rule that a second sweep is a second thing to stall.** MONEY PATH, `E2` READ OWED, DO NOT MERGE UNREAD. No ADR number, no migration number, no `packages/db` change, no contract change, and [`admin-payouts.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/admin-payouts.ts) was read line by line and not touched.

**THE THREE CLOCKS ARE THREE DIFFERENT ACTS AND A SWEEP THAT TREATED THEM IDENTICALLY WOULD BE WRONG IN THE DIRECTION THAT LOOKS CORRECT.** The hold releases to `approved`, blanks all five hold columns and **posts `LT-01`** (`INV-M5-17`, [ADR-040](decisions/ADR-040.md): a held request has posted nothing, so release means approve **and pay**). The withdrawal halt blanks three columns, **leaves the rail's `status` untouched** (`INV-M20-13`, because collapsing an orthogonal halt into the rail's status column is `SD-M5-06`'s named mistake) and **posts nothing** (`INV-M20-14`: the money is already the trader's). Each of the four ways to get that wrong reads as "the sweep releases everything", so the suite asserts all four in the negative by counting what the ports were asked to do.

**THE THIRD CLOCK'S RELEASE IS NOT WRITABLE BY ANY CODE IN THIS TREE, AND THAT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** A `payout_requests` freeze reaching expiry releases (`GS-109`) and its target is `settled`: [STATE_MACHINES](architecture/STATE_MACHINES.md) draws `frozen --> settled` under `G-FREEZE-CLEARED` and [ADR-040](decisions/ADR-040.md) states it in terms, and there is no `frozen --> approved` edge to take instead. Then **four things stand in the way and none of them is this fence**: `payout_requests_settled_has_days` ([`0010:151`](../packages/db/migrations/0010_payouts.sql)) makes `settled` require `settled_at`, `settled_trading_day` and `effective_trading_day`; `effective_trading_day` is the exchange session calendar applied to an instant and **[`merit/no-calendar-in-expiry-path`](../packages/eslint-plugin-merit/rules/no-calendar-in-expiry-path.js) bans that import in this exact path by glob** under [ADR-042](decisions/ADR-042.md), a rule whose own header names THIS SWEEP as the failure it was written for and whose glob this file is the first to match; settlement additionally means the win-day reset and floor recompute of `INV-M5-07`, whose **`applySettlement` EXISTS**, at [`packages/rules-engine/src/payout/settle.ts:88`](../packages/rules-engine/src/payout/settle.ts), and takes a `calendar: CalendarSlice`, **so calling it needs the very import that rule forbids**. **THIS SESSION FIRST CLAIMED THE FUNCTION DID NOT EXIST AND THAT WAS FALSE**, from a truncated grep read as an absence; the correction makes the conclusion stronger rather than overturning it, because a checkable lint rule is a better blocker than a missing function, and it is the error class [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md) names by name; and **nothing writes `frozen` at all**, because `G-FREEZE-DURING-FLIGHT`'s own row says [ADR-019](decisions/ADR-019.md) made the internal leg one transaction and [ADR-040](decisions/ADR-040.md) routed both remaining cases elsewhere. **So that leg is swept, warned on, and returned as an `unreleasable` finding naming what is absent.** Inventing a settlement instant, a trading day and a win-day reset inside a sweep would be the sweep deciding what settlement IS, on the money path, in the job whose whole purpose is that the clock binds Merit rather than the trader.

**THE LEG IS NOT EMPTY, AND `CI-06l` IS NOT WEAKENED.** It emits `payout.freeze_expiring` at the twelve-hour lead [EVENTS](architecture/EVENTS.md) rules and [ADR-159](decisions/ADR-159.md) clause 6 carries into the payload, which is a producer the registry names this exact job for and which needs none of the four missing things. All three columns still name this one job in the release-job table, that table is untouched, and the honest count is stated instead: **three clocks swept, two released, one reported.**

**THE KEY DISCIPLINE IS SESSION 288'S, FOLLOWED RATHER THAN RE-DECIDED, AND THIS SWEEP IS THE THIRD DOOR.** `ledger_transactions.idempotency_key` is `text NOT NULL UNIQUE`; [`payouts.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/payouts.ts) posts under `` `${PAYOUT_ENDPOINT} ${idempotency_key}` `` and `admin-payouts.ts`'s `releaseLedgerKey` builds the identical string, so `LT-01` for one payout request is ONE posting whichever door reaches it. **This app cannot import either constant**, because `apps/worker/package.json` declares `@merit/rules-engine` and nothing else and `node-linker=isolated` makes an undeclared import unresolvable, so **the suite BINDS the retyped constant by reading both route files as text**. A key naming this sweep would have let three doors mint three postings for one approval and all three would have committed.

**[ADR-157](decisions/ADR-157.md)'S RANGE TERM, ITS `IS NULL` TERM AND ITS ROW LOCK ARE WHY THE SLICE WAS DISPATCHABLE, AND ALL THREE ARE USED AS RULED.** The bound handed to `atMost` is the **sweep's own instant and never the database's**, one instant per run. `isNull()` has exactly one caller, `settled_at` on the withdrawal read, which is `wallet_withdrawals_live_freeze_blocks_settlement` asserted on the READ so the scan cannot see a settled row; **`IS NOT NULL` is refused by that entry and is not needed either**, because `NULL <= x` never matches. The lock is `lockAt(key, { id })`, the first statement of every per-row transaction, and **the precondition is re-read under it**: an operator releasing a hold in the second before this job reaches it produces `superseded` rather than a second `LT-01`. **No advisory lock is taken and none is reachable from the port**, which declares no `sqlExecutor` at all.

**ONE TRANSACTION PER ROW, BECAUSE `FM-M5-13` IS THIS JOB STALLING.** A single transaction over the estate makes one bad row stall every other row, which is the failure the job exists against arriving through the job itself. A refused posting rolls back its own row only, **leaving that request held**, which is the correct direction: a release that could not post must not mark a payout paid that never paid.

**TWO GAPS ARE REPORTED RATHER THAN REACHED AROUND, AND BOTH ARE ONE LINE IN SOMEBODY ELSE'S FILE.** `SystemReason` is `'nightly-batch' | 'operator-console'` and **an hourly sweep is neither of those words**; adding a third is a change to [`packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts`](../packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts), which is `P5-a`'s, so `ExpirySweepIo.transact` takes the unit of work and the wiring decides the authority ([P5](plans/P5-payouts-and-wallet.md) rule 10, followed rather than argued with). And **nothing in this workspace writes an event yet**, so the sink is a port that takes the transaction, which `P5-n` will supply. Nothing here adds a `SqlExecutorReason` member, adds a `SystemReason` member, imports `pg`, or casts past a key type.

**ONE THING THE REGISTRY DOES NOT GIVE THE OTHER TWO LEGS, RECORDED BECAUSE IT LOOKS LIKE AN OVERSIGHT AND MAY BE ONE.** [EVENTS](architecture/EVENTS.md) gives a lead-time warning to the payout freeze alone: there is no `payout.hold_expiring` and no `wallet.withdrawal_halt_expiring`, so of the three clocks the only one anybody is warned about before it fires is **the one whose expiry nothing can act on**. Not repaired here: the catalogue is `approved` and a name is a row only on [ADR-159](decisions/ADR-159.md) clause 1's authority.

**AND `payout.freeze_expiring` FIRES ON EVERY RUN WHILE ITS WINDOW STANDS, WHICH IS THE FAIL-SAFE DIRECTION STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN.** `payout_requests` has no column recording that the warning was sent, adding one is a migration outside this fence, and deriving "the first run after the boundary" from the job's own period would lose the warning entirely on any run that was missed, which is `FM-M5-13` again. **A repeated warning is noise and a missed one is a denial nobody authorized**, so the noisy one is chosen deliberately.

**Verified in pieces, and watched failing.** 33 of 33 gates, 12 of 12 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, `format:check` clean, 177 test files / 3,310 passed / 6 skipped, `falsify.mjs` clean. The dispatch baseline of 33 / 12 / 0 / 0 / 176 / 3,253 / 6 reproduced exactly before anything changed. **Eight mutations seeded into the sweep and all eight caught**, each reverted from a byte-identical copy: the withdrawal leg posting, the withdrawal leg writing the rail status, `clearHold` dropping one of five NULLs, the ledger key naming this sweep, the hold leg not posting, the status precondition not re-read under the lock, the freeze leg guessing a settlement, and the range bound taken per read rather than once.

## The verification page enters the contract, and two leaderboard rows are refused ([ADR-170](decisions/ADR-170.md), proposed 2026-08-27, session 301)

**[ADR-153](decisions/ADR-153.md)'s disease, found a THIRD time and closed on its own subject.** `API_CONTRACT` section 6 has been shipping `verify_url: string; // public verification page` while `grep -n '/verify/'` over that document **exits `1` with no output**. [ADR-168](decisions/ADR-168.md) found it inside the section it was editing and deliberately left it, on the ground that a public oracle over Merit's own payout book is its own ruling with its own session. This is that session, and the dispatch's claim was reproduced at source before anything was ruled.

**TWO ROWS LAND AND TWO ARE NAMED AS OWED, and the honest count is that `M11` section 4's six endpoints are now four defined and two undefined.** `GET /verify/:code` enters section 6.3 and `POST /admin/certificates/:id/revoke` enters section 8. `PATCH /me/leaderboard` and `GET /public/leaderboard` are **refused**, and not for fence discipline: `OQ-M11-03` **is** the public row's field set and that founder question is open, so a shape written here would be this contract answering it in a schema; and `INV-M11-10` requires opt-out to remove **historical entries** while `grep -rl 'leaderboard' packages/db/migrations/` returns one file holding two reserved columns and no table. **The half of `PATCH /me/leaderboard` that could be typed is the half that does nothing**, which is [ADR-040](decisions/ADR-040.md)'s `PayoutListItem` lesson arriving through a verb instead of a union.

**THIS WAS RULED AS A SECURITY DECISION AND THE LOAD-BEARING CLAUSE IS THAT A DEFERRED CODE ANSWERS `unknown`.** So the response union is **three** members where `certificate_verifications.result`'s CHECK is **four**, and the asymmetry works in both directions: `INV-M11-09` defers exactly on an open severity 4+ flag, so a public `deferred` answer would publish that an account is under risk review, which [M07](plans/M07-risk-abuse.md) does not do; and the log keeps the fourth value because a lookup that hits a deferred row is **a leaked token or a 128-bit guess that hit** and a lookup that hits nothing is a typo or `FM-M11-04` in progress, which are different incidents only the table can separate. **That is an allowlist decision under section 1 and not `ADR-040`'s defect**, which is the inverse: there the table cannot hold the value, here it can and the response declines it.

**`INV-M11-05`'s CONSTANT-TIME CLAUSE NAMES THIS ENDPOINT, AND EQUALISING THE WORK CANNOT HONOUR IT.** `ADR-168` ruled the clause out of the image endpoint and its argument is unavailable here. With no response cache and one indexed equality on `certificates_code_uq`, a warm row and a cold row still differ, because the database's own buffer cache reproduces `FM-M11-05`'s tension a layer below any application ruling. **So the mechanism is a measured time floor over a warm hit, a cold hit, a miss and a malformed token alike**, and **a floor set from a p50 is worse than no floor** because it advertises compliance and leaks on the tail an attacker samples. **The row therefore has NO `validation_failed` at all**: a shape check ahead of the lookup is a faster path and hands over the token's alphabet and length at the same time. **The response SIZE channel is named and deliberately not chased**, because it separates a hit from a miss only for a caller who already sent a code, and such a caller learns the same thing from the body.

**`FM-M11-05`'s CACHE IS SCOPED OUT BY ITS OWN TEXT, AND THE REVOCATION DESIGN REQUIRED THAT BEFORE THE CLOCK DID.** Its remedy caches **rendered bytes** keyed by `(code, row_version)`; verify renders no bytes. The stronger reason is `FM-M11-02`: the verify code printed inside a circulating image **is** the recovery path when the image was screenshotted, so an intermediary serving a cached `valid` for a code revoked five minutes ago fails at the one surface that was supposed to be authoritative. The row is `no-store`.

**THE REVOKE ROW WAS WRITTEN FROM `admin_actions`' BICONDITIONAL AND THAT FOUND THE ENTRY'S BEST FINDING.** `initiative` is `NOT NULL` with no default over `('enforcement','trader_request','operational')` and `admin_actions_on_behalf_matches_initiative` makes `on_behalf_of_identity_id` non-null exactly when it is `trader_request`. `certificates.revocation_class`'s four members map onto that vocabulary totally, so **`initiative` is DERIVED and is not a request field**: an endpoint that took it would let an operator record an enforcement as something the trader asked for, which is the exact misattribution that constraint exists to prevent, arriving through a request body instead of a column. **`:id` is the uuid and not the public code for the same kind of reason**: `admin_actions.subject_id` is `uuid NOT NULL`, so an audit row keyed on the rotatable token could not be written at all.

**A DEFERRED CERTIFICATE CANNOT BE REVOKED, AND NAMING THAT NAMES A REAL HOLE.** [M11 section 3.1](plans/M11-certificates-social-proof.md) draws `issued --> revoked` and `deferred --> withheld` and no edge between deferred and revoked; `0020` permits the write, so the refusal is the endpoint's. The alternative encoding, deferred-plus-revoked with class `account_enforced`, was checked and **fails on `AS-M11-05`**, which fixes that class as *"the claim stands"* while a withheld certificate is one Merit never made. **So there is today no endpoint and no column by which an enforcement reaches a deferred certificate**, and `revoked --> issued` is drawn, permitted by the CHECK and served by no route either. Both recorded, neither repaired: `M11` is approved and `0020` is merged and sacred under `E2`.

**SECTION 12 IS DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED AND THE MATRIX ROWS ARE NAMED AS OWED AS ONE SLICE.** `ADR-168` deferred its two because another session held the file; that reason expired and a better one replaced it. Four certificate endpoints now exist in this contract and the coherent matrix slice is **all four at once**. The interesting assertion for `GET /verify/:code` is not the `401` the matrix already carries by prefix for other surfaces: it is that **the response is identical with and without a session**, since an endpoint that enriched its answer for the owner would be an oracle that distinguishes its callers. `POST /admin/certificates/:id/revoke` owes no new row, being reached by three existing `/admin/*` rows already.

**`ADR-168`'s OWN CHECKABLE CLAUSE NOW PRINTS `3` RATHER THAN `2`, AND IT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN REPAIRED** ([ADR-170](decisions/ADR-170.md) section 8.1). The clause was that no certificate heading arrive in this contract without a ruling behind it, and it did that job: this entry is the ruling `ADR-168`'s own section 3 anticipated. **Another session's entry is not edited to make this one's diff quiet**, and the standing count is restated in `ADR-170` for the tree this branch leaves. It is one more argument for a comparison over a count.

**NO ROUTE IS REGISTERED AND THE APPLICATION NOW OWES TEN.** From the composed server rather than from a grep: `discoverRouteModules()` then `buildServer` on both surfaces, union of `CompositionReport.registered` = **62**; contract `METHOD /path` headings with comma lists expanded and query strings stripped = **64**; **10 contract rows registered by nothing**, up from 8, and the two added are this entry's two. The 8 registered paths carrying no heading are `GET /health` and all of sections 9 and 10, excluded on `ADR-168`'s own terms.

**Verified in pieces.** The dispatch baseline reproduced exactly before anything was edited and again after: 33 of 33 gates, 12 of 12 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, `format:check` clean, 183 test files / 3,521 passed / 6 skipped, and 183 / 3,523 / 6 after `origin/main` was merged in. **No migration, no `SD-nn`, no `packages/db` change, no route, no gate, no section renumbered, and `M11`, `0020`, `0025` and `apps/api` untouched.**

## `API_CONTRACT` section 6.3 is built: the two rows `ADR-168` admitted and refused to write (2026-08-27, session 297)

**[`apps/api/src/routes/certificates.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/certificates.ts) and [`apps/api/test/certificates.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/certificates.test.ts), both new, transcribe `GET /certificates` and `GET /certificates/:code/image.png`.** [ADR-168](decisions/ADR-168.md) admitted both rows into the contract and its foreclosure 8 says in its own words that it *"forecloses building any of this ... the rows are the specification a later slice transcribes"*. This is that slice, so it takes **no ADR number, no migration number and no `SD-nn`**, changes no other route module, changes `packages/db` not at all, and changes `API_CONTRACT` not at all.

**THE ROUTE REGISTRY NEEDED NO EDIT AND THAT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** [`registry.ts`](../apps/api/src/registry.ts)'s header states the property, *"the module list is the directory listing and is never written down"*, and the check is `discoverRouteModules()` then `buildServer()` on both surfaces before and after. On the dispatch SHA no `/certificates` path appeared in `registered` or `withheld` on either surface, which reproduces [ADR-168](decisions/ADR-168.md)'s own approval clause; with one new file on disk and nothing else edited, the **public** surface registers both rows and withholds neither, and the **operator** surface registers neither and withholds both. **`withheld` being right is what produces the operator 404 and nothing else** ([ADR-083](decisions/ADR-083.md)): the route is never registered, so the 404 is the router's and the suite asserts it by injecting into an operator server and reading `application/problem+json`.

**THE `.png` IS SECTION 1'S FIRST NON-JSON SUCCESS RESPONSE AND WHAT THAT COSTS IS STATED IN THE FILE RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED.** Four of section 1's conventions are not about a body and survive unchanged: the error model, which section 6.3 restates in terms; the base path; the surface partition; and the rate limit, which section 11 gives this row its own line for. **The one that cannot survive is the response-shape allowlist**, which is where the disclosure guarantee lives everywhere else in the contract, because there is no projection inside a PNG. **So on that row the boundary moves out of a projection function and into a renderer that is not in this repository**, and the suite asserts the metadata and the passed-through body and states that it cannot assert the pixels. `assertPng` is a FORMAT check and never a disclosure one: the path ends in `.png` and the response declares `image/png`, so the eight-byte signature is the smallest version of that claim being true.

**THE DISCLOSURE BOUNDARY IS ASSERTED IN THE NEGATIVE, OVER SEEDS THAT ARE POISONED ON PURPOSE.** Every `certificates` row handed to the route carries an identity uuid, an email, a display name, a cumulative total, a lifetime figure and `revoked_reason`'s internal free text, half of them as columns and half inside the `jsonb` claim, and the case reads the **serialized** response so a value nested at any depth under any key reddens it. **`narrowClaims` is an allowlist over a `jsonb` column and it is the one place in the file where getting it wrong is silent**: `certificates.claims` is `jsonb NOT NULL`, the database constrains nothing about its keys, `INV-M11-01` is the only thing that says what may be in it, and `INV-M11-01` is prose. **`revoked_reason` has no field on the row type at all**, which is stronger than an allowlist that declines to mention it (`INV-M11-07`, `AS-M11-05`).

**TWO CONTROLS ARE ENFORCED BY SHAPE RATHER THAN BY A CHECK, DELIBERATELY.** There is no path through `projectCertificate` on which a deferred row reaches the link signer, so a shareable token for a claim Merit has not made yet cannot be minted even by an edit that forgot the rule ([ADR-168](decisions/ADR-168.md) foreclosure 4, against a `NOT NULL` column). And **a deferred code answers 404 on the wire while being recorded as `deferred` in `certificate_verifications`**, which is exactly what that table's fourth CHECK member buys: the anomaly detector can tell a deferral from a guess and the caller cannot.

**`state` IS DERIVED, THE UNION IS THREE MEMBERS, AND `withheld` IS NOT TYPED**, on [ADR-040](decisions/ADR-040.md)'s `PayoutListItem` lesson one section up. **NO TIMING DEFENCE IS WRITTEN AND NONE IS CLAIMED**: `INV-M11-05`'s constant-time clause names the verify endpoint and section 6.3 states why it cannot reach the image, and [ADR-168](decisions/ADR-168.md) foreclosure 5 exists to stop a later reader recording its absence as a defect. **Every fetch writes `certificate_verifications` before the response is composed, and a rejected write fails the fetch**, because serving the bytes anyway converts an outage of the log into the unmetered oracle `AS-M11-04` and `FM-M11-04` exist to watch, silently and only under load.

**THE IMAGE ROW CANNOT REACH THE DATABASE FROM THIS DEPLOYABLE AND THE OBSTRUCTION IS A RULING RATHER THAN THIS FENCE.** [`apps/api/src/db.ts`](../apps/api/src/db.ts) opens `scoped(identityId, fn)` and `firm(fn)` and says the absence of a third *"is the point"*. The row is unauthenticated, so `scoped` has no identity; `certificates` is `class: 'owned'` in [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts), so it is excluded from `FirmTableKey` and `firm` **refuses it at compile time**; and `FirmDb.rows(key)` has no predicate and no insert, so `certificate_verifications`, which is `firm`, is unwritable through that door as well. The door that reaches both is `systemDb(reason)`, whose vocabulary [ADR-096](decisions/ADR-096.md) clause 3 and [ADR-109](decisions/ADR-109.md) clause 1 each refused to widen. **So the image row is served through an unwired port and answers 503, on [`public-methods.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/public-methods.ts)' and [`economic-calendar.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/economic-calendar.ts)' shape**, and the ruling it needs is reported rather than taken. `start.ts` is outside this fence, so the list's port is unwired too.

**TWO THINGS REPORTED RATHER THAN DECIDED QUIETLY.** The **deferred-and-revoked overlap** is representable, neither CHECK forbids it, and no approved document says which state that row is in; revocation is given precedence, because it is terminal where a deferral is a wait and because `certificates_revocation_is_complete` guarantees it has a class to publish, and the `deferred` and `revoked` blocks still track their own columns so nothing the row holds is discarded. And **`user_agent_class` is not sent at all**: `0025`'s own comment is *"a class, never the string"*, no approved document enumerates the classes, and the digest for `code_hash` and `ip_hash` is likewise fixed nowhere, so this route names what it observed and the sink hashes.

**Verified in pieces, each command separately, and watched failing. 33 of 33 gates, 12 of 12 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, `format:check` clean, 184 test files / 3,574 passed / 6 skipped, `falsify.mjs` exit 0 with the tree clean after it.** The dispatch baseline of 33, 12 of 12, 0, 0, clean, 183 files / 3,521 passed / 6 skipped reproduced exactly before anything was edited, so **this session contributes exactly one test file and fifty-one cases** and the head figure moves with every merge: it read 3,572 before `origin/main` was merged in at `a7796b3`, which brought session 291's own correction and two cases with it. **Four mutations seeded and all four caught**, each reverted from a byte-identical copy: the `jsonb` claim spread, the claim passed through unrebuilt on top of it, the deferred branch's withholding removed, and a rejected verifications write swallowed with the bytes served anyway.

**WHAT IS STILL OWED, NAMED HERE BECAUSE ONE OF THE TWO IS NOW SHIPPED IN A RESPONSE.** `GET /verify/:code` is defined by no section of the contract ([ADR-168](decisions/ADR-168.md) foreclosure 1), and `verify_url` on every issued certificate addresses it, so an issued card now carries a link to a page the contract does not describe. Section 12 owes both rows a negative-authz entry, which [ADR-168](decisions/ADR-168.md) section 4 recorded as owed and which is still owed.

## The three `admin-wallet` rows are served, and the correction meets four constraints nobody had read together (2026-08-27, session 298)

**[`apps/api/src/routes/admin-wallet.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/admin-wallet.ts) (new) registers all three of [API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) section 8's wallet rows: `GET /admin/wallet/reconciliation`, `POST /admin/wallet/:identityId/correct` and `POST /admin/wallet/:identityId/spend-limit`. MONEY PATH BY CONTENT, `E2` READ OWED.** No ADR number, no migration number, no `packages/db` change, no contract change, and **the route registry needed no edit**, because [`registry.ts`](../apps/api/src/registry.ts)'s module list IS the directory listing. Measured from `CompositionReport` and not from a grep, before and after: none of the three paths was in `registered` NOR `withheld` on either surface beforehand; afterwards `operator` registers all three, moving 21 to 24, and `public` withholds all three, moving 20 to 23, with `public` registered unchanged at 42.

**THE HEADLINE IS A MIGRATION NOBODY IN THIS RANGE HAD READ.** [`0038_account_adjustments.sql`](../packages/db/migrations/0038_account_adjustments.sql) is the built door for an admin wallet correction, calls itself *"the first admin route in this corpus that moves money to a NAMED PERSON"*, and its `assert_adjustment_wallet_entry_matches` trigger is what makes a `wallet_entries` row with `provenance = 'correction'` legal at all. [ADR-158](decisions/ADR-158.md) wrote the `correct` contract row from [`0011`](../packages/db/migrations/0011_wallet.sql) alone, across eighteen findings, and **cites `0038` nowhere**. Four disagreements follow and none of them is a gap:

1. **NO COLUMN ANYWHERE HOLDS WHICH ENTRY A CORRECTION CORRECTS.** The contract says `corrects_entry_id` *"Becomes `reference_id`"*; `ADJ-C3` requires `reference_id` to be the ADJUSTMENT's id; and the types settle it independently, since `wallet_entries.reference_id` is `uuid NOT NULL` while `wallet_entries.id` is `bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` and [ADR-158](decisions/ADR-158.md) clause 3 makes `entry_id` a DECIMAL STRING for exactly that reason.
2. **A correcting DEBIT is unwritable unless it exactly reverses a prior adjustment credit**, by `account_adjustments_debit_is_a_reversal` and `assert_adjustment_reversal_is_sound`, which additionally refuse a partial reversal by name. The contract's body carries a free `direction` and no `reverses_adjustment_id`.
3. **Dual control is a `dual_control_approvals` row plus a `dual_control_threshold_cents bigint NOT NULL CHECK (> 0)` column**, and the contract's body carries `second_approver: string`. **The threshold has no wire field and no configured source in this tree**, and choosing one would be a number this repository invented on the cash door.
4. **`reason_code` is `NOT NULL` over the closed vocabulary `goodwill`, `reconciliation_error`, `promotional_credit`**, and the contract's body carries free-text `cause` and `reason` and no code.

**REPORTED AND NOT REPAIRED.** **`insufficient_funds` is not a row in [API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) section 2's canonical code table, which calls itself closed**, and it is named in two endpoints' error lists; 422 is an ASSUMPTION on the evidence that every other business-rule refusal there is 422, held as one constant and asserted in the suite so it fails loudly the day it is ruled. **[`admin-reads.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/admin-reads.test.ts) still pins `/admin/wallet/reconciliation` as unserved and stays green**, because that assertion is scoped to `ADMIN_READ_ENDPOINTS` rather than to the composed surface; it is now stale in meaning and was not edited, being outside this fence.
