## `P5-l`'s rendering half: reserve coverage lands on the page, and the float lands BESIDE it (2026-08-27, session 296)

**[P5](plans/P5-payouts-and-wallet.md) section 8's `P5-l`, rendering half. No ADR, no migration, no `SD-nn`, no `packages/db` change, no contract change, no route, no gate, and [`0049`](../packages/db/migrations/0049_reserve_coverage_snapshots.sql), [`admin-reads.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/admin-reads.ts), [`admin-payouts.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/admin-payouts.ts) and [`liability_snapshots`](../packages/db/migrations/0009_ledger.sql) all untouched.** `apps/admin` goes from 7 test files / 116 cases to 7 / 152, **+36 cases and no new file**.

**`P-M6-07` WAS THE PANEL M06 DEFINED AND THE PAGE PRINTED AS NOT BUILT, AND ITS STATED REASON HAD GONE FALSE.** The `PENDING` row read *"OI-01 in DELTA_MANIFEST ... the columns do not exist"*. [`0049_reserve_coverage_snapshots.sql`](../packages/db/migrations/0049_reserve_coverage_snapshots.sql) landed them under [ADR-128](decisions/ADR-128.md) and closed `OI-01`, so the row now names what is actually missing, which is a **producer**: `0049`'s own header says *"no producer, no rows"*, and [`DEP-M6-02`](plans/M06-admin-ops-console.md) and `DEP-M6-05` name the two suppliers. **A `blockedBy` that names a closed item is worse than none**, because a reader who chases it finds the item closed and concludes the panel is unblocked.

**THE ONE THING SECTION 5.3 RULES IS NOW ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN A COMMENT.** Float enters the DENOMINATOR as exposure and never the NUMERATOR as reserve, and [`liability.ts`](../apps/admin/src/liability.ts) holds no field, argument or local carrying `reserve + float` except the one inside the assertion that exists to refuse it. **The stored `rcr_bp` is READ and not recomputed**, on `0049`'s own founder-read item 1: a ratio the database computes cannot disagree with the numbers stored beside it. The recomputation survives **only as a coherence check**, in `bigint` reproducing Postgres' `(reserve_cents * 10000) / NULLIF(cvar99_cents, 0)` exactly, and it catches the defect in **both** the shapes it takes: a numerator with the float folded in disagrees with a ratio generated from reserve alone, and a ratio recomputed from float plus reserve disagrees with the reserve stored beside it.

**THE FIXTURE IS CHOSEN SO THAT THE MISREADING FLIPS THE BREAKER RATHER THAN MOVING A NUMBER.** On `GS-229`'s book as this suite states it, reserve alone is 2,000,000c over 2,500,000c = **8,000bp, ARMED**, and with the float folded in it is 3,500,000c over 2,500,000c = **14,000bp, NOT ARMED**. That is [`AS-M20-08`](plans/M20-wallet.md) in two lines: *"the breaker stops meaning anything at exactly the moment it matters"*, and it is why `DEP-M20-06`'s failure column reads *"the breaker at 1.0 becomes fictional"*.

**IT IS ASSERTED IN THE NEGATIVE OVER THE RENDERED BYTES, AND THE SECOND SEED PROVED WHY THAT IS NOT THE SAME CHECK AS THE FIRST.** `assertFloatIsNotReserve` reads `renderLiabilityHome`'s output rather than the structured figures, on session 261's lesson that a value reaches a page through a label, a definition, a provenance clause or an error string without ever being a field. **Three seeds were watched failing and each reverted from a byte-identical copy**, the hashes checked both ways: the float folded into the reserve figure (caught in the page bytes AND by two unit cases), the ratio line computed from float plus reserve (**caught ONLY in the bytes** -- every unit case passed, because the leak was in the rendered line and not in any `Figure`), and the float figure dropped from its panel (caught by the visibly-separate refusal `DEP-M20-06` requires). **The two scopes differ deliberately**: the forbidden CENTS is searched in the `P-M6-07` panels only, because an amount of money can legitimately equal an unrelated figure elsewhere and a page that threw on that coincidence is a control nobody keeps; the forbidden RATIO is searched over the whole page, because a basis-point token collides with nothing else printed. **Both searches are skipped at zero float and the skip is stated**, since `reserve + 0` IS `reserve` and a suite that proved this control on an empty wallet would have proved nothing.

**THE API HALF WAS CHECKED BEFORE A ROUTE WAS WRITTEN AND NO ROUTE WAS WRITTEN.** `GET /admin/liability` is registered in [`admin-reads.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/admin-reads.ts) at `path: '/admin/liability'`, and its body is [API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) section 8's `LiabilityResponse`. **It serves `P-M6-07` in full** -- `reserve_cents`, `cvar99_cents`, `rcr_bp` and `breaker_armed` are exactly the four the panel needs. **It cannot serve `P-M6-01` at all**, and that is the finding: the response carries `open_liability_cents` and no `wallet_balances_cents`, so a client of that endpoint holds one component of the panel under a name that reads as the panel, which is the hazard [`liability.ts`](../apps/admin/src/liability.ts)'s own header was written against and which `INV-M6-11` forbids. `bounded_near_term_cents` and `remaining_ladder_exposure_cents` are absent too, so `P-M6-02` and `AS-M6-04` have no wire representation either. **`apps/api/src/routes/admin-liability.ts` was declined on that measurement rather than built**: the path is taken, `compose` refuses a duplicate `METHOD /path`, and a NEW path is a new `API_CONTRACT` row, which is `approved` and therefore an ADR that `P5-c` holds and this session was allocated no number for. **The remedy is three fields on a frozen response shape and not a route**, and it is reported rather than reached for.

**THREE MORE FINDINGS, EACH OUTSIDE THIS FENCE.** [`apps/admin/src/index.ts`](../apps/admin/src/index.ts) publishes `.` and nothing else and exports by explicit name, so **none of this session's eight new exports is on the barrel** and a consumer outside the app cannot reach `reserveCoverage`; that is session 292's `apps/worker/src/index.ts` shape one deployable over, and the file is outside this fence. **`GET /admin/wallet/reconciliation` is registered by no route module**, so `P-M6-07`'s SECOND ratio -- coverage against near-term external withdrawal demand, which [M20 section 8](plans/M20-wallet.md) says is the one number it would show if it could show only one -- renders absent with that reason rather than as a percentage. **The word "float" in [`admin-reads.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/admin-reads.ts) means the NUMBER TYPE in all three of its occurrences** and never the cash balance, which is a collision worth knowing about on the one file that will eventually serve both senses.

## `OI-06` is closed: the destination-cooling window has storage, and the ruling is one word the recommendation did not contain (2026-08-27, session 293)

**[ADR-169](decisions/ADR-169.md), `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED. [`0051_payout_destinations.sql`](../packages/db/migrations/0051_payout_destinations.sql). MONEY PATH, `E2` READ OWED, NOT MERGED.**

**`C-11` has been a shipped control with no input since the schema was written.** [SECURITY section 4](architecture/SECURITY.md) item 1 says a destination change *"starts a 48 hour cooling window during which payouts cannot settle"*, `C-24` extends it to affiliates, [STATE_MACHINES](architecture/STATE_MACHINES.md) draws `requested --> cooling` on `G-DESTINATION-COOLING`, `0001` carries the `cooling` enum value and `0011` carries a partial index that scans for it. **Nothing in the database could answer when a destination changed**, because `destination_ref` on `payout_transfers` and `wallet_withdrawals` is the destination **of a transfer**. `payout_destinations` closes that, keyed `(identity_id, destination_ref)`.

**THE RECOMMENDATION IS TAKEN ON ITS KEY AND ITS TWO COLUMNS AND AMENDED ON THE ONE WORD IT DOES NOT CONTAIN.** [DELTA_MANIFEST](../packages/db/DELTA_MANIFEST.md)'s `OI-06` row names `first_seen_at` and `cooling_until` and says nothing about nullability, **and nullability is the whole control**: read literally as `timestamptz NULL`, an `INSERT` that omits the column writes a destination that is **usable the instant it exists**, because the gate reads `cooling_until > now()` and a NULL compares to nothing. The row that fails open is the one written at the exact moment `C-11` exists to slow down. That is [SECURITY](architecture/SECURITY.md) section 4 item 9's own *"columns that record a control are not the control"* applied **before** rather than after, and it settles the first-destination question fail-closed as a side effect: on an identity that has never withdrawn there is nothing to change from, so a first-destination exemption would open a hole on every account that has not yet used the rail.

**THE KEY SURVIVED CONTACT FOR A MEASURED REASON RATHER THAN BY DEFERENCE, and this is the finding worth carrying.** One row per pair keeps the gate a keyed lookup. **The append-only alternative -- one row per registration event, which is the shape "records that a destination changed or when" suggests -- puts the read on `max(cooling_until)`, and [ADR-157](decisions/ADR-157.md) REFUSED THE SCALAR AGGREGATE ON THE ACCESSOR** two slices earlier in this same wave. So an append-only registry would have left `P5-h`'s gate unreachable through `scopedDb` and blocked the slice this table exists to unblock. **A refusal ruled for one slice's reasons decided another slice's schema**, which is what the one-door design was supposed to do and is the first time it has visibly done it.

**`UPDATE` SURVIVES AND `PAYOUT-DEST-C1` BOUNDS IT.** A window can be extended, so `UPDATE` has to exist; the only `UPDATE` anybody wants to make wrongly is one that **shortens** it, and a PostgreSQL grant cannot tell a lengthening from a shortening. The trigger refuses a backward `cooling_until` (equality permitted, so a re-registration inside a longer window is a no-op rather than a race), and makes `identity_id`, `destination_ref` and `first_seen_at` immutable. **THE GRANTS ARE A FOURTH SHAPE**: `0032`, `0039` and `0049` revoke `UPDATE, DELETE` for append-only and `0050` revokes `ALL` for reading; this one revokes **`DELETE` alone**, because the row is the memory of the window and a `DELETE` then re-`INSERT` is a fresh window with no trace. **Proved in both directions against PostgreSQL 16.13**: without the line `merit_app` holds all four verbs and removes a running cooling window (`DELETE 1`); with it, `permission denied`.

**`0051` WAS DRAWN BACK FROM THE POOL AND THE SEQUENCE GAINED NO HOLE.** [ADR-167](decisions/ADR-167.md) returned it unspent the same afternoon when `P7-c` took the reading that needs no table. **This is the first time the pool has been drawn from**, which is what makes a conditional migration reservation cheap rather than merely honest. The pool is empty again and `0052` is the next free number.

**Install, from empty, every figure queried rather than counted**: `0001`..`0051` forward-only under `ON_ERROR_STOP`, 51 of 51; re-apply fails as it must. Tables 113 to **114**, indexes 396 to **397**, `CHECK` constraints 479 to **481**, all constraints 777 to **781**, triggers 20 to **21**. `packages/db`'s registry moves 105 declared tables to **106** and 61 served by `scopedDb` to **62**; 41 `firm` and 3 `pair` are unmoved. **Seven rejections seeded and all seven watched firing.**

**WHAT IS STILL OWED, and the first item is a gap this entry surfaces rather than closes.** `INV-M8-11` now has a registry to write into and **`affiliates` still carries no destination column at all** ([session 162](sessions/2026-08-24-session-162.md) measured it: `grep -i destination` over `0005` and `0012` returns zero lines), so nothing can say what an affiliate's current destination is. [API_CONTRACT:722](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) says `cooling_until` *"reads from a registry that does not exist yet"* and is now **stale in one direction**; that file is `P5-c`'s and `P5-h`'s and is not edited here. And `P5-h` inherits one obligation it cannot get wrong: `destination_ref` is byte-exact rather than `citext`, which is fail-closed **only if an absent row means "register it and cool it"** and never "not cooling".

**`POST /wallet/withdrawals` is unblocked.** It was the one contract row that could not be registered until this landed.

Changing it is a wire-visible change to the CARD leg, which [P5](plans/P5-payouts-and-wallet.md) section 6 says this slice touches neither of, so today's behaviour is pinned with the finding named beside the assertion and the two-line patch written out.

**EIGHT MUTATIONS SEEDED AND ALL EIGHT CAUGHT, each reverted from a byte-identical copy verified by `sha256sum`.** The load-bearing one is the first: **with the hard-limit refusal moved inside the wallet arm, the `wallet` cases stay GREEN and eight others turn red**, which is [M03](plans/M03-billing-checkout.md) section 3.5.1's table reproduced and is why the assertion runs against all three methods. **Three of the eight turn exactly one assertion red and that is recorded as thin rather than rounded up.** **Two assertions were written as bare substring tests first and the tree refuted both**, which is session 292's finding arriving here: this file's header names `sqlExecutor`, `SqlExecutorReason`, `SystemReason` and `pg_advisory` in order to say it widens none of them, so both now assert the call syntax a reach-around would need.

## The streaming ingest lands, and the monotonicity predicate `0050` owed it turned out to be an ordinal of TWO columns (2026-08-27, session 299)

[P6](plans/P6-live-tier.md) section 8's **`P6-f`** is built. [`apps/worker/src/live/ingest.ts`](../apps/worker/src/live/ingest.ts) and [`ports.ts`](../apps/worker/src/live/ports.ts) (both new) consume `P6-a`'s `streamLive` and write `P6-c`'s `live_account_state` and nothing else. **No ADR number, no migration number, no `SD-nn`, no `packages/db` change, no `packages/rithmic` change, no `apps/api` change, and no contract change.**

**THE INTERESTING LINE IS NOT THE ONE `0050` SKETCHED, AND THE SAME MIGRATION IS WHY.** [`0050`](../packages/db/migrations/0050_live_cache_and_role.sql)'s header refuses a monotonicity trigger and names this slice as the owner of the guard, sketching it as `excluded.sequence > live_account_state.sequence`. **That predicate freezes the surface at the day boundary.** `LiveAccountTick.sequence` is 1-based **per account per day**, so today's first tick carries `sequence = 1`, and against a row left over from yesterday at `400` the comparison is false: the row never moves and the trader reads yesterday's equity through the whole of today. That is [ADR-020](decisions/ADR-020.md) rule 3's named failure exactly, *"a live surface that silently freezes at its last value ... looks exactly like a quiet market"*, and it freezes at the moment the number matters most. **`0050`'s own comment on the column it added for this supplies the correction**: *"a sequence without its day is not an ordinal at all, and ... a row left over from yesterday must be distinguishable from a quiet market today."* **So the ordinal is the pair `(trading_day, sequence)` compared lexicographically**, and the shipped `WHERE` carries `0050`'s quoted fragment AND the trading-day half. The sketch is wrong in **both** directions and the suite asserts both: it refuses the rollover, and it admits yesterday's straggler, which would rewind the row by a whole session.

**`INV-M2-14` IS ASSERTED MECHANICALLY, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE SLICE.** The four table names are **derived from `0050`'s own closing `REVOKE`** rather than retyped, so a fifth table appended to that list arrives in the suite without anybody editing it. Each name is asserted **PRESENT** in the two module headers, which is the foreclosure the slice is required to carry, and **ABSENT** from the same files with every comment stripped, in both the snake-case and the Drizzle camelCase spelling, because `tx.insert('dailyMarks', ...)` would pass a snake-case check untouched. The module's import graph is walked and shown **closed**: `ingest.ts` imports `./ports.ts` and `ports.ts` imports nothing at all, so there is no path to any table in the estate by any name and not merely by these four. **Eight mutations were seeded and all eight were caught**, including both halves of the predicate, both halves of the upsert, and an accessor import.

**TWO THINGS ARE OWED AND BOTH ARE REPORTED RATHER THAN REACHED FOR, AND THE FIRST IS A GRANT ARGUMENT RATHER THAN A MISSING ADAPTER.** [P6 section 3.4](plans/P6-live-tier.md) makes the expectation row this slice's, on `report_deliveries.due_at`'s shape. **It needs a table this fence cannot create and a grant this fence cannot make.** [EVENTS](architecture/EVENTS.md) section 5.4 and [ADR-161](decisions/ADR-161.md) clause 7 give every `feed.*` event to the expectation sweep and to neither the feed nor the ingest, so the sweep writes `events` and therefore runs as `merit_app`; **`merit_app` holds nothing on the live cache** (`0050`'s `REVOKE ALL`, which is `FM-M12-08` and `FM-M13-07` as permissions rather than conventions), so **the sweep cannot see the absence it exists to alarm on by reading the cache**. Granting it `SELECT` is `0050`'s `F1`, the escape that makes `FM-M12-08` false silently, and it is **not taken**. The expectation must therefore live in a table `merit_live` writes and `merit_app` reads, and `merit_live` has no default privileges, so a new table is invisible to it until somebody grants it deliberately. The shape is written where the migration session will read it: the grain is `(feed, trading_day, account_id)`, the feed-wide roll-up is a `GROUP BY`, and the row carries a heartbeat and an ordinal and **no equity, no movement and no money of any kind**, which is what makes `merit_app` reading it a different question from `F1`.

**THE SECOND OWED THING IS THE PROCESS.** ADR-164 clause 4 rules that any process touching the cache connects as `merit_live` and that no process holds both roles, and [`client.ts`](../packages/db/src/client.ts) opens one pool from one `DATABASE_URL`, so **one process is one role**. `apps/worker` holds `merit_app`, so **no adapter built on [`src/db.ts`](../apps/worker/src/db.ts) can serve this ingest**, and the module is written against ports and is unwired. That is `runNightlyBatch`'s standard, the provisioning saga's and the expiry sweep's, applied unchanged: what is real is the predicate, the queue, the refusals and the report; what is not is the wiring, and the difference is visible in the type.

**THE UPSERT IS A STRING BECAUSE NO ACCESSOR IN THIS WORKSPACE CAN EXPRESS IT.** [ADR-112](decisions/ADR-112.md) gives a transaction handle `rowsWhere`, `lockAt`, `updateAt` and `insert`, and none of them is an upsert or carries an `ON CONFLICT` predicate; `packages/db` is outside this fence. So the statement is stated where its reasoning lives and the suite binds every column of it to `0050`'s own `CREATE TABLE`: it writes only declared columns, it never writes the **GENERATED** `intraday_movement_cents`, it never writes `indicative` or `created_at` whose defaults `0050` sets, and it names **none of the three columns `0050` refused**. **`as_of_instant` is set on the UPDATE arm explicitly, because a column default does not fire on `UPDATE`** and a ticking account whose instant never moved would go stale while it was ticking, which is the inverse of the failure the column exists to detect.

**THE QUEUE IS A BOUND RATHER THAN A CAP, AND THE PREDICATE IS WHY IT IS SAFE.** `LiveTickHandler` returns `void` and says a consumer that does I/O per tick queues it and says so. A plain list grows without limit whenever the sink is slower than the feed, and the usual answer is a maximum depth nobody here has measured. **The queue holds one pending tick per account**, so it can never hold more entries than the feed has accounts, and coalescing is **observationally equivalent on the cache**: the row holds one tick per account and the predicate accepts only a strictly greater ordinal, so writing `n` then `n + 1` leaves what writing `n + 1` alone leaves. The one thing it would lose is the evidence that `n` was delivered, which is why **gap detection runs at enqueue and never at write** and is asserted with a sink deliberately slower than the pump.

**FOUR REFUSALS SIT IN FRONT OF THE CACHE AND THREE OF THEM ARE `0050`'s OWN CONSTRAINTS CHECKED ONE LAYER EARLY**, because a `23514` in a per-tick write path is one trader's malformed tick taking out every other trader's surface for as long as it keeps arriving. **`equity-not-integer-cents` is the one worth reading twice**: `JSON.parse` cannot produce a `bigint` at all, so a tick that arrived through one carries a `number`, which is the precise loss of precision [`stream.ts`](../packages/rithmic/src/simulator/stream.ts) says the `bigint` exists to prevent, on the surface a trader watches. It is refused and never coerced.

**[CRON_INVENTORY](ops/runbooks/CRON_INVENTORY.md) TAKES THE FEED-HEALTH ROW AND NO OTHER LINE**, at **S3** argued rather than defaulted: tier 2 failing is not a money incident because ADR-020's hard rule keeps the figure off every money decision, and the row records that **no expectation row exists yet**, so the switch has nothing to anti-join against and the cell states what is owed rather than what runs.

**`apps/worker/src/index.ts` WAS AN APPEND AND THE WHOLE BARREL WAS RE-READ.** One deliberate under-report is recorded rather than taken: `main()`'s status string still omits the ingest, because it is a single line three sessions are appending near and a same-line conflict is the one shape a keep-both merge cannot resolve.

**Measured on this branch with `pnpm install` run first and each command separately: 33 of 33 gates, 12 of 12 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, `format:check` clean, 184 test files / 3,581 passed / 6 skipped.** The dispatch baseline of 33 / 12 / 0 / 0 / 183 / 3,521 / 6 was reproduced exactly before a line changed, and the whole of the movement is this session's one new suite.

## `P7-e` lands: `detector_runs` gets a producer, and the canary is excluded from every aggregate by never being written (2026-08-27, session 300)

**[`apps/worker/src/detectors/runner.ts`](../apps/worker/src/detectors/runner.ts), [`ports.ts`](../apps/worker/src/detectors/ports.ts) and [`canary.ts`](../apps/worker/src/detectors/canary.ts) (all three new) build [P7](plans/P7-risk-and-abuse.md) section 8's `P7-e`, `P7`'s FIRST DONE-GATE.** No ADR number, no migration number, no `packages/db` change, no `apps/api` change, no contract change, no `SystemReason` member, no `SqlExecutorReason` member, and [`apps/worker/src/db.ts`](../apps/worker/src/db.ts) was read in full and NOT touched.

**THE `is_synthetic` COLUMN `AS-M7-05` NAMES DOES NOT EXIST, AND THE READING THIS SLICE TOOK IS STRICTLY STRONGER THAN THE ONE IT COULD NOT TAKE.** `AS-M7-05` says the synthetic subjects are *"flagged `is_synthetic`"*, citing the discipline [M02](plans/M02-rithmic-bridge.md) `OQ-M2-01` **proposes** for simulator accounts. Measured: no migration in the tree declares such a column on any table, and the only `synthetic` columns in the estate are `detector_runs.synthetic_expected` and `synthetic_found`, which are counters about a run rather than a marker on a subject. The column reading needs a migration and this slice holds no number. **So a canary is never written to the database at all**: it is minted in memory, merged into the rows the run read, and discarded. A marker column makes *"excluded from every aggregate, statistic and published number"* a property every present **and future** query must honour, watched by the CI test `AS-M7-05` asks for; **a row that was never inserted is excluded from every aggregate by construction, including the ones nobody has written yet.**

**AND THE HALF THAT READING DOES NOT BUY IS STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED, BECAUSE IT IS THE HALF A LATER SESSION WOULD OTHERWISE ASSUME.** A canary that never travelled through `rowsWhere` proves the detector's PREDICATE still matches and proves nothing about whether the READ still returns the rows it used to. A schema change renaming `fills.executed_at` breaks the read and the battery is still found, because it arrives through the same in-memory door on either side of the rename. **The suite pins that case rather than hiding it**: a run whose read returns nothing finds all its canaries and reports `ok` at `rows_scanned: 0`, which is `AS-M7-05`'s own opening sentence still reachable. Closing it needs a persisted subject, which needs the marker column, which needs a migration and the ruling that goes with it.

**BOTH IMPLEMENTATION NOTES ARE ASSERTIONS AND NEITHER IS A COMMENT**, which is `P7` section 11 rule 13. **Note 1** is stated over the run's WRITES rather than over a list of queries, because a run's aggregates are its writes: the suite walks every value of every committed row and every event payload and fails on a canary identifier in any of them, and separately asserts that `rows_scanned` is counted BEFORE the battery is merged and that `flags_raised` counts real findings only. **Note 2** is a guard rather than a promise: every canary identifier carries the run's nonce and the runner checks each one, so a battery built at module load carries some other run's nonce and the run is refused. **A detector cannot satisfy that by being careful; only by having minted from the mint it was handed.**

**THE CHEAP IMPLEMENTATION THE DDL CANNOT SEE IS THE ONE THE RUNNER REFUSES IN CODE.** `detector_runs_synthetics_match_status` reads `status <> 'ok' OR synthetic_found >= synthetic_expected`, which is **satisfied at `0 >= 0`**: a detector that seeds no canaries at all reports `ok` every night forever and no constraint in the database can tell. So `mintBattery` refuses an empty battery, on [M07 section 8](plans/M07-risk-abuse.md)'s own row of one canary per detector, every run, in prod.

**NO PATH TO `enforced`, AND IT IS THE TYPE THAT STOPS IT RATHER THAN A VALUE SOMEBODY REMEMBERED NOT TO SET** ([ADR-155](decisions/ADR-155.md), `INV-M7-02`, [STATE_MACHINES section 7](architecture/STATE_MACHINES.md), `P7` rule 11). `DetectorTx` has **no addressed write** -- no `updateAt`, no `deleteAt` -- so a transition has no method to go through, and `DetectorFinding` has **no `status` field**, so `enforced` is not a value a detector avoids: it is a word with nowhere to go. `P7` section 10 item 2 measured that `INV-M7-02`'s grant does not exist and is a migration that is nobody's, so the code path is the control today; this makes it a control of the SHAPE. A severity 5 finding is run through the runner and its written status read, so the band an auto-enforce would be written for is exercised rather than only grepped.

**`INV-M7-04` IS WHY THE RUN READS `detector_definitions` BEFORE IT READS A SINGLE FILL, AND IT IS WHAT MAKES `P7-d` A REAL BLOCKER RATHER THAN A NOMINAL ONE.** The version and every threshold come from the registry row and never from a constant in a detector's module, so the chain `risk_flags.detector_run_id -> detector_runs.(detector, detector_version) -> detector_definitions.parameters` is unbroken. **A detector with no current row does not run at all.** **AND THE AMBIGUITY IS REFUSED RATHER THAN RESOLVED BY A COIN TOSS**: [`0008_risk.sql:52`](../packages/db/migrations/0008_risk.sql) creates `detector_definitions_current_idx ... WHERE effective_to IS NULL` and that index is **NOT UNIQUE**, so two overlapping current rows are insertable and a runner picking one would record a version nobody could reconstruct, which is `INV-M7-04` failing while appearing to hold.

**[ADR-157](decisions/ADR-157.md) SECTION 5's REFUSAL IS DESIGNED FOR RATHER THAN WORKED AROUND.** A detector declares WINDOWS, the runner reads each through `rowsWhere`, and the join happens in the runner, which is exactly the grant that entry made. **Its named cost is carried into the port's shape**: the rows crossing the boundary are the window's rather than the match's, so `DetectorRunOutcome.rowsByStream` reports the count per stream and a window that is too wide is a number somebody can read rather than a slow night. **No `SqlExecutorReason` member, no `pg` import, no cast past a key type, and no aggregate was reached for**, and the suite asserts all four over the three files with comments stripped first, on [session 292](sessions/2026-08-27-session-292.md)'s finding that a substring test fails on the file whose header names the accessor in order to say it does not import it.

**THE PORTS ARE WAVE 2's AND THEIR SHAPE IS THE PART `P7-f`, `P7-g` AND `P7-h` INHERIT.** A `Detector` declares `streams`, `canaries` and `scan`; the runner reads, mints, merges, partitions and records. `correlationGroups` is in the write set although nothing in this slice writes one, because `P7-g`'s fence holds `detectors/graph.ts` and its test and does **not** hold `ports.ts`, so a door left out here is a slice blocked later; its `statistic` and `threshold` are typed as exact-decimal **strings** and a `number` is refused, on `ADR-157` section 5 finding 8's reasoning that `pg` hands a `numeric` back as a string because the naive `Number()` on one is lossy. **`DetectorDeclined` exists because eleven of the eighteen registry rows carry no stated number at all** (derived in the suite from the seed rather than written in a docstring), so most of wave 2 has no threshold to run against yet, and a detector that ran anyway would either invent one or match nothing -- and matching nothing is `FM-M7-01` exactly.

**TEN SEEDED CHEAP IMPLEMENTATIONS WATCHED FAILING, each reverted from a byte-identical copy checked by digest.** The headline one is a runner that reports success without having found its canaries (7 cases red); the rest are canary rows counted in `rows_scanned` (3), a canary hit written as a flag (10), the note-2 nonce guard removed (1), a detector seeding zero canaries accepted (1), a mixed real-and-synthetic finding rounded rather than refused (1), two current registry rows accepted (1), an automatic path to `enforced` at severity 5 (2), a severity 4 flag written with no SLA clock (1), and a failed run not recorded at all (6).

**FOUR FINDINGS REPORTED AND NOT REPAIRED, each named with the fence that repairs it.** **`detector.run_degraded` has no row in [EVENTS](architecture/EVENTS.md)**: [M07 section 5](plans/M07-risk-abuse.md) carries it as one of three NEW events with its payload, the catalogue's section 8 carries only `detector.run_completed`, and `EVENTS.md` is outside this fence -- the suite asserts the ABSENCE, so the day somebody adds the row it goes red and the payload is re-derived from the catalogue rather than from `M07`. **`EVENTS` section 8 gives `flag.raised` an `evidence_summary` field and defines it nowhere**, and its consumers include FEED; this runner sends the evidence object's KEYS rather than its values, which carries what kind of accusation it is without carrying a threshold into a consumer nobody has written yet, and the field's definition is owed. **`detector_definitions_current_idx` is not unique**, so `INV-M7-04`'s provenance rests on a code path where a `UNIQUE INDEX` would rest on the schema; that is a migration and this slice holds no number. **[`apps/worker/src/batch/statistics.ts`](../apps/worker/src/batch/statistics.ts) has never been exported from [`src/index.ts`](../apps/worker/src/index.ts)** and is reached only by its own test through a relative import -- found by re-reading the whole barrel after the merge, and it is a leg that was never added rather than one a merge dropped.

**Measured on this branch with `pnpm install` run first, each command separately, and re-measured after the `origin/main` merge: 33 of 33 gates, 12 of 12 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, `format:check` clean, 184 test files / 3,595 passed / 6 skipped, `falsify.mjs` exit 0 with the tree clean after it.** The dispatch baseline of 33, 12 of 12, 0, 0, clean and 183 files / 3,521 passed / 6 skipped reproduced exactly before anything was edited. **THE ATTRIBUTION IS MEASURED RATHER THAN INFERRED**: with this session's one new test file removed the tree reports **183 files / 3,523 passed**, so this session contributes **exactly one test file and 72 cases** and everything else in the difference arrived on `main`. **The runner is unwired and nothing schedules it**, and the gap here is an ADAPTER rather than a word: `LIVE_DB.batch` already satisfies `DetectorRunnerIo.transact` at `systemDb('nightly-batch')`, which [M07 section 1.1](plans/M07-risk-abuse.md) makes the right authority for a nightly run.

## The approval backlog becomes a list of questions: `RI-13` lands green and nothing is signed (2026-08-27, session 304)

**Fifty-four entries in [docs/decisions](decisions/README.md) declare their own approval line WITHHELD, and until today thirty-four of them left a founder to reconstruct the question from the ruling before they could answer it.** Twenty already carried the marked block `**What a founder read adds and this entry cannot**` and named the judgements. [`RI-13`](../packages/tooling/checks/repo-invariants.mjs) makes carrying nothing impossible: **every ADR whose approval line is unsigned states, explicitly, what the founder must decide.**

**THE DISPATCH'S COUNT WAS RIGHT ABOUT A PHRASE AND WRONG ABOUT THE POPULATION, AND THAT IS THE FINDING.** Thirty-one entries carry the literal `PENDING, UNSIGNED`, exactly as estimated. **The withheld population is larger**, because `PENDING, UNSIGNED` is one spelling of several and it is not the newest: `ADR-161` through `ADR-164` and `ADR-166` write `Approval line: UNSIGNED` with no `PENDING`, `ADR-113` and `ADR-158` write `Unsigned.` under a section heading, `ADR-144` and `ADR-155` write `NOT GIVEN`, and `ADR-145` writes a blank signature rule. **A check keyed on the dispatch's phrase would have gone green while the convention moved out from under it.**

**THE CHECK KEYS ON A MARKED BLOCK AND NOT ON A PHRASE LIST.** A phrase list is a second copy of a convention: it drifts on the first session that writes a twenty-fourth phrasing and it passes an entry that merely mentions a founder. The corpus had already chosen a marker and thirty-two entries were using it, bolded, and once as a section of its own in `ADR-164`. **The check adopts what these documents do rather than inventing a rule it would then have to police**, and it reads the block's LENGTH and never its meaning, so **"nothing here is a judgement, and here is why" passes on exactly the same terms as three named judgements**. `ADR-153` is the entry that gives that answer honestly.

**TWO MISREADS WERE WATCHED BEFORE THE CHECK WAS TRUSTED AND BOTH ARE SEEDED.** [ADR-111](decisions/ADR-111.md) is SIGNED on delegated authority and was reported unsigned, because its approval section runs a shell block whose comments begin with `#` and the section looked like it ended at the first of them. [ADR-119](decisions/ADR-119.md) and [ADR-137](decisions/ADR-137.md) are unsigned and fell out of scope on a `REFUSED` in a table cell and on a citation of another entry's `GRANTED`. **A disposition is now read only at the FRONT of a line**, where a signature goes, and a withholding token is read anywhere in the approval statement. The asymmetry is in `covers` and it is deliberate: a disposition misread out of prose drops an entry out of scope silently, while a withholding token misread only puts an entry into scope where it is a finding somebody can argue with.

**WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CAUGHT, and it is a second defect rather than a hole.** An entry whose approval status the check cannot read AT ALL is out of scope, and every pre-FREEZE ruling that records no approval statement is in that position. Failing them would be asking a shelf of documents for a convention that did not exist when they were written, and whether that convention should be asked of them retroactively is its own argument.

**NOTHING IS SIGNED BY THIS SESSION AND NOTHING MAY BE.** No approval line moves from unsigned to signed, no ruling moves, no clause moves and no `status:` field moves. The only line added to any entry is the block stating what its signature is for, and every question is derived from that entry's own sections and cites where the judgement lives.

## The `no-fixture-format` queue is 91 rows shorter in EVIDENCE and one row shorter in COUNT, and the difference is a naming convention (2026-08-27, session 305)

**[ADR-125](decisions/ADR-125.md) ruled the term's citation unsupported on 227 rows and left 220 of them carrying it with a recited reason. 91 of those 220 have now been read row by row against the tree.** [Section 39](testing/golden-scenarios/39-fixture-status-and-blockers.md) carries the result and a new subsection carries the finding.

**ONE ROW MOVED. FIVE MORE ARE PROVEN AND CANNOT.** `GS-229` is `covered-elsewhere`, discharged over its own book by four `describe`s in [`liability.test.ts`](../apps/admin/test/liability.test.ts) and three in [`page.test.ts`](../apps/admin/test/page.test.ts), executed and watched. `GS-038`, `GS-155`, `GS-223`, `GS-274` and `GS-314` have assertions that execute and pass today and stay `blocked`, because `CI-06/fixture-inventory` assertion 6 discharges a row only when the cited test file **carries the row's id as a string**. **The gate is right and rules its own limit in its own text**, that it is a static parse which cannot see an outcome and that shelling out to vitest is *"an install step wearing a different hat"*. `GS-229` moved because its suite happens to carry the string; `GS-038`'s suite is titled with the row's own B4 number, `B4 #9`, and that is not the string the reader wants.

**SO THE QUEUE'S LENGTH IS SET BY A NAMING CONVENTION AND NOT BY WHAT IS PROVEN, AND NOBODY WRITING THOSE SUITES WAS TOLD.** The repair per row is one comment in a test file. It is outside a fence drawn at `docs/testing/golden-scenarios/**` and this session did not make it, did not edit [`gates.mjs`](../scripts/corpus/gates.mjs), did not mint a seventh term and took no ADR number.

**THE QUEUE IS ALSO NOT ONE KIND OF THING, AND A WAVE SCHEDULED AGAINST IT AS ONE WOULD FIND THAT AT ITS OWN BENCH.** Of the rows read, the real blockers partition four ways: rows one comment from discharge; **rows where the registry row and the implementation describe DIFFERENT behaviour**, where writing a fixture first picks a winner by accident (`GS-097` answers 400 where the row pins `conflict`; `GS-099`'s receiver DEFERS under `FM-M3-03` where the row pins rejected-and-alarmed; `GS-220` pins publish validation FAILING and the tree adds the trigger unconfigurably; `GS-136` would have to read the cache [ADR-020](decisions/ADR-020.md) forecloses from any decision; `GS-267` wants a disabled control the portal fence admits none of); rows whose assertion is a latency percentile, a concurrency race or a named database constraint rather than a fixture (`GS-051`, `GS-230`, `GS-036`, `GS-040`, `GS-278`, `GS-283`); and rows whose module genuinely has no code, which are the majority.

**TWO CITATIONS WERE FALSE AND BOTH ARE REPAIRED.** `GS-112` read *"no test file in this tree names it"* and [`seed-detectors.test.ts:585`](../packages/db/test/seed-detectors.test.ts) names it, in a comment saying the mechanism of `INV-M7-10` is untested. `GS-117`'s citation, written earlier in this same session, said unfreeze has no route; `POST /admin/accounts/:accountId/unfreeze` is one of the seven writes [`admin-writes.test.ts:301`](../apps/api/test/admin-writes.test.ts) pins by equality. **`GS-311` was touched in error and is restored byte for byte**: it carries `vendor-call`, [ADR-125](decisions/ADR-125.md) moves no row into another session's term, and the generated span is what caught it.

**129 rows are unread and the reading is worth continuing.** Measured on this branch with each command run separately: 33 of 33 gates, 12 of 12 invariants, 188 test files / 3,925 passed / 6 skipped unchanged from `main`, `falsify.mjs` clean.

## Sixteen registered route families answered 503 because their port was never installed, and the check that would have said so now exists (2026-08-27, session 302)

**`apps/api` declared 20 backend setters across `routes/*.ts` and [`start.ts`](../apps/api/src/start.ts) called 4.** The suite was green on all of them, because every port is a module-scope variable holding a fail-closed default and every suite installs its own fake before it asserts: **a port `start.ts` never calls is invisible to the suite by construction**, `tsc` sees a variable that is assigned, `eslint` sees a function that is exported and called, and the only observer that would have noticed is a request against a running deployment. **This is the third instance of the same defect class in one day**, after `apps/portal`'s eighteen view modules with no transport and `apps/site`'s eight route modules with no `app/` directory.

**THE COUNT OF ADAPTERS IS WHAT DECIDES WHETHER WIRING IS MECHANICAL, AND IT IS MOSTLY NOT.** Of the sixteen unwired ports, **one** had a usable `databaseX` factory already written, **one** had a factory that cannot be called, and **fourteen** had none. `databaseWalletBackend` had been sitting beside its port fully written and fully tested since `wallet.ts` landed, and nothing installed it; `databaseCertificateBackend` exists and its `links` parameter has no supplier, because this deployable holds no signing key and `GET /verify/:code` was defined by no section of the contract until [ADR-170](decisions/ADR-170.md) landed it in session 301.

**TWO PORTS WIRED, AND THE SECOND ONE'S DOOR IS ENFORCED BY THE TYPE SYSTEM RATHER THAN BY A CONVENTION.** `useWalletBackend` over the existing adapter, and `setMethodDefinitionSource` over `databaseMethodDefinitions`, built here. `statistic_definitions` is scope class `firm`, so its key is a `FirmTableKey` and is **excluded from `ScopedTableKey`**: the scoped door does not compile with it, which is the same refusal `public-methods.ts`' header describes from the other end (the reader may be anybody, the row is nobody's) obtained with no second control to maintain. The filter is pushed **down** to the door rather than applied in memory, unlike `catalog.ts`' and `wallet.ts`' whole-set reads, because those are bounded by one identity's holdings and this table is bounded by nothing.

**FIVE OF THE FOURTEEN REMAINING PORTS ARE ONE RULING AND NOT FIVE SLICES.** `setAdminReadSource`, `setAdminSessionSource`, `useAdminPayoutBackend`, `useAdminWalletBackend` and `useAdminWriteBackend` all need `systemDb('operator-console')`, which [`src/db.ts`](../apps/api/src/db.ts) declines to declare on [ADR-120](decisions/ADR-120.md). **`SystemReason` is `'nightly-batch' | 'operator-console'` and [ADR-165](decisions/ADR-165.md) ruled this evening that it gains no member.** The door was reported and not opened; `src/db.ts` is unchanged.

**THE MONEY PORTS ARE BLOCKED RATHER THAN READY TO WIRE, AND THE DISTINCTION IS LOAD BEARING FOR WHOEVER TAKES THEM.** `PayoutTx.ledger` is a `LedgerTx` and is **NOT NULLABLE**, so no live deployment can construct a `PayoutBackend` at all; `CheckoutTx.insertAttribution` writes `attributions`, scope class `pair`, which no authority in `packages/db` admits a request handler writing, and the checkout wallet arm's `ledger` is the same `LedgerTx`. `LedgerTx` is satisfied only by [ADR-102](decisions/ADR-102.md)'s `SystemTx` at the same closed vocabulary. Nothing here widened it, imported `pg`, or cast past a key type.

**THREE OF THE SIXTEEN ALREADY HOLD THEIR PRODUCTION VALUE AT MODULE SCOPE**, which the setter grep cannot see: `productionAffiliateDeps` (`affiliate.ts:478`), `productionKycDeps` (`kyc.ts:284`) and `PRODUCTION_CHECKOUT_ADAPTERS` (`checkout.ts:1005`). **Calling those three setters would have raised the reported count from 6 to 9 and changed nothing any request sees**, and it would have passed this session's own new test. That is recorded in the blocked reasons themselves, so the next reader tempted by it meets the sentence before the green tick.

**[`apps/api/test/wiring.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/wiring.test.ts) IS THE DELIVERABLE, AND IT READS `start.ts` AS TEXT.** That is unusual and it is the only observation available that does not start a server: calling a setter is a side effect of importing the entry point, and importing the entry point binds a port. Seven assertions. An unaccounted port fails. **A blocked entry that is also wired fails**, so the day a door lands the list must shrink rather than keep a stale excuse beside a live line. An entry naming a port that no longer exists fails. A reason too short to check at the file and line it cites fails. And **an adapter written and never installed fails**, which is the half that actually happened. **Watched failing three ways before it landed**, the third being the no-op call that is the cheapest way to make the file green.

**Measured on this branch with `pnpm install` run first and each command separately: 33 of 33 gates, 12 of 12 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, `format:check` clean, 189 test files / 3,941 passed / 6 skipped, `falsify.mjs` exit 0 with the tree clean after it.** The dispatch baseline of 33 / 12 of 12 / 0 / 0 / clean / 188 files / 3,925 passed / 6 skipped was reproduced exactly on `2bc5cea` before a line changed, and the whole of the movement is this session's two new suites and ten added cases. **No ADR number, no migration number, no `packages/db` change, no handler logic changed, no contract change, `src/db.ts` untouched.**

## `P5-h` has landed: the external leg, and the two approved documents that disagree about whether it approves (2026-08-27, session 303)

**[`apps/api/src/routes/wallet-withdrawals.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/wallet-withdrawals.ts) serves [API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) section 6.2's `POST /wallet/withdrawals`, which was the last unregistered row of the contract's trader surface.** [P5](plans/P5-payouts-and-wallet.md) section 8's `P5-h`. **MONEY PATH, [E2](../MERIT_BUILD_MASTER_PROMPT.md) LINE-BY-LINE READ OWED, NOT MERGED.**

**THE FINDING IS A DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN TWO APPROVED DOCUMENTS AND IT NEEDS A RULING.** [M05](plans/M05-payout-system.md) section 1.1's external-leg listing ends *"post LT-06, debiting the wallet position -> status: approved"*, and [P5](plans/P5-payouts-and-wallet.md)'s own `P5-h` row ends *"FIFO composition into `source_provenance_summary`, then `LT-06`"*. [API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) section 6.2 types this endpoint's response `status: "requested" | "cooling"`, annotated **"The creation's reachable states, per STATE_MACHINES section 3.2"**, and [M05](plans/M05-payout-system.md) section 2.1 names `LT-06`'s kind **`wallet_withdrawal_approval`**, *"The external leg's APPROVAL"*. [STATE_MACHINES](architecture/STATE_MACHINES.md) section 3.2 draws `requested --> approved` as an edge **out of** `requested`.

**The slice takes the contract and posts NO ledger transaction, on asymmetry of harm rather than seniority.** A row at `requested` or `cooling` with nothing posted is a row a ruling can advance; an `LT-06` posted here is an irrevocable entry against `trader_wallet` under a `text NOT NULL UNIQUE` key with no named reversal, and the response would carry a `status` the contract's union cannot express on the one screen that tells a trader their money is leaving. **`WithdrawalTx` carries no ledger handle at all** where `payouts.ts`'s `PayoutTx` does, so posting here would take a port widening a reviewer reads. **M05 section 1.1's listing is also the listing the corpus has twice caught carrying `settled_to_wallet`, a status [ADR-028](decisions/ADR-028.md) rejected**, which makes it the weaker source for a status word specifically.

**WHICHEVER WAY THAT RULING FALLS, A SECOND THING IS OWED AND IS NOBODY'S: A DRIVER FOR `requested --> approved` AND `cooling --> approved`.** Nothing in this tree performs either edge, and `P5-j` sweeps three FREEZE clocks and not `G-COOLING-ELAPSED`. Today a created withdrawal never reaches the rail.

**THE STALE `INV-M20-06` PREMISE WAS CHECKED AT SOURCE FIRST AND IT IS STALE.** [ADR-075](decisions/ADR-075.md) is `status: accepted` with founder approval GRANTED 2026-08-21; `M20:62` and `G-WITHDRAWAL-CLEARED` both read `= 'active'`. Nothing here re-rules it, and the gate is written `=== 'active'` on that entry's own fail-closed argument.

**What the route does, each cited:** `identities.status = 'active'` ([ADR-075](decisions/ADR-075.md)), `payouts_frozen` under its own code, KYC `verified` read through the supersession chain, `G-NO-IN-FLIGHT` over `wallet_withdrawals_open_idx`'s four statuses **under `tx.lockScope()`**, the **10,000c** minimum as `bigint` integer cents, `insufficient_funds` against `withdrawable_cents`, `G-DESTINATION-COOLING` against [`0051`](../packages/db/migrations/0051_payout_destinations.sql) with an **ABSENT row treated as register-and-cool** ([ADR-169](decisions/ADR-169.md)'s stated obligation on this slice by name), and the **FIFO composition** with debits consuming the oldest credits, cross-checked against the stored running balance.

**`lockScope()` AND NOT `lockAt`, AND THE REASON IS THE CASE RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE.** [ADR-157](decisions/ADR-157.md) clause 4's row lock needs a row that exists, and the row a concurrent second request would create does not. `lockScope()` takes no argument, locks the handle's own `identities` row, and is what makes `G-NO-IN-FLIGHT` a control at all: [ADR-158](decisions/ADR-158.md) finding 8 records that `wallet_withdrawals_open_idx` is **not unique**, so without the lock two concurrent requests both read an empty set and both insert.

**`C-27` refuses a non-elevated session and this module adds NO second refusal** ([M05](plans/M05-payout-system.md) section 3.6), asserted by the case that drives an unelevated session and finds **no lock taken and no row read**.

**FOUR THINGS ARE REPORTED RATHER THAN INVENTED.** The **name-match score** is uncomputable: `kyc_verifications` carries no name column and nothing holds a destination holder's name, so `destination_name_match`, `name_match_score` and `name_match_method` stay NULL, which `wallet_withdrawals_score_has_method` permits. **P-1's `provenance_review` is `false`** because nothing records that an account was purchased with promotional credit: `purchases.payment_method` closes at `psp | wallet | mixed` and `promotional_credit_grants.funding_purchase_id` is the other direction. **`insufficient_funds` is named on three endpoint rows and is ABSENT from section 2's closed code table**; 422 is taken as the band and a row is owed. **`wallet.withdrawal_requested` and `wallet.withdrawal_cooling` are not emitted**, because the producer is `P5-n`'s and no route module in this tree emits anything.

**A WEAKNESS IN A LANDED CHECK IS RECORDED: `'[]'::jsonb <> '{}'::jsonb` IS TRUE**, so an empty JSON array satisfies `wallet_withdrawals_approved_has_provenance` while carrying no composition at all. This module never writes one and the suite seeds the mutation that would.

**ONE FENCE EXCEPTION, ARGUED RATHER THAN TAKEN QUIETLY.** [`apps/api/test/registry.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/registry.test.ts) derived its expected module order by stripping `.ts` **before** sorting, while `discoverRouteModules` sorts filenames; the two agree only while no module stem is a prefix of another's, and `wallet-withdrawals` beside `wallet` is the first pair that is not. One line, no behavior change, the assertion unchanged. The alternatives were a red suite or renaming a module the contract's own path names. **[P5](plans/P5-payouts-and-wallet.md) section 9's claim that concurrent route modules are "NOT A COLLISION" is true of the source and was not true of this test's derivation.**

**Measured on this branch with `pnpm install` run first and each command separately: 33 of 33 gates, 12 of 12 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, `format:check` clean, 189 test files / 3,991 passed / 6 skipped.** The dispatch baseline of 33 / 12 / 0 / 0 / clean / 188 / 3,925 / 6 was reproduced exactly before a line changed. **Fifteen defects were seeded and all fifteen were caught**, including the cooling gate skipped, the minimum applied as a float, two withdrawals in flight, `identities.status` not checked, `ADR-075` reversed to `<> 'restricted'`, and the lock not taken in either of the two places it is written.

## `P7-h` lands: seven identity and payment detectors, and every one of them declines because the registry states no number (2026-08-28, session 311)

[`apps/worker/src/detectors/identity.ts`](../apps/worker/src/detectors/identity.ts) builds
[P7](plans/P7-risk-and-abuse.md) section 8's `P7-h`: `D-07`, `D-08`, `D-09`, `D-10` and `D-11`, plus
`D-16`'s v1 half and `D-18`'s detector, against the runner and ports
[`P7-e`](sessions/2026-08-27-session-300.md) landed and touching neither.

**SEVEN OF SEVEN DECLINE UNDER `P7-d`'s SEED, AND THAT IS THE RESULT RATHER THAN THE SHORTFALL.**
`INV-M7-04` makes the registry the only source of a threshold, *"'why did this not fire in March' must
be answerable from data, and it cannot be if parameters live only in code"*, and eleven of the eighteen
seeded rows carry no number at all because `OQ-M7-02` is the founder's. `DetectorDeclined` is the named
way to say so, the run is recorded `failed`, and `detector_runs_unhealthy_idx` and
[CRON_INVENTORY](ops/runbooks/CRON_INVENTORY.md)'s dead-man switch both read that on the day it happens.
The alternative is `FM-M7-01` exactly: a threshold this module invented, and *"detection appears healthy
and is absent."* What each detector waits for is a LIST rather than a shrug, in `registryBlockers`, and
the moment a value is seeded the detector runs with no change to the file.

| Detector | Waiting on |
|---|---|
| `D-07` entity cap | `max_accounts_per_entity`, `severity` |
| `D-08` payment velocity | both counts, `window_days`, `severity` |
| `D-09` destination concentration | **`input`** (`DEP-M7-04`), `sla_hours` |
| `D-10` affiliate self-deal | `severity` alone. Its detection is complete |
| `D-11` dilution timing | `max_daily_profit_cents`, `sibling_correlation_floor_bp`, `sibling_window_days`, `severity` |
| `D-16` link confidence v1 | `hard_link_confidence_ceiling_bp`, `sla_hours` |
| `D-18` registration phone | **`input`** (`D-15`), `severity` |

**SEVERITY IS THE BLOCKER FIVE OF THE SEVEN SHARE AND IT IS A MONEY DECISION EVERY TIME.**
[M07](plans/M07-risk-abuse.md) section 3.3: moving a detector from 3 to 4 changes who gets held, because
4 and 5 is the band `G-HOLD-REQUIRED` reads to hold a payout for 48 hours under
[ADR-040](decisions/ADR-040.md), so it is *"a data change with a recorded effective date through
`SD-M7-03`, **never a deploy**"*. A severity chosen in a `.ts` file is that decision made by a deploy.

**AND THE CLOCK THAT BAND NEEDS IS NOT SEEDED, WHICH IS THIS SESSION'S FIRST FINDING.**
`risk_flags_high_severity_has_sla` reads `severity < 4 OR sla_due_at IS NOT NULL`, so a severity-5
finding needs a duration. **`OQ-M7-03` PROPOSES *"4 hours to first touch during business hours, 24 hours
otherwise"* and is OPEN**, and no seeded row carries an `sla_hours`. So `D-09` and `D-16`, the only two
whose severity `M07` states, are blocked on a parameter the registry has no row for. It is NAMED rather
than defaulted, because a default here is a 48-hour money gate set by a deploy.

**`ADR-155` BINDS HARDEST HERE AND IT IS THE TYPE THAT HOLDS IT.** Three of these seven are in
[M07](plans/M07-risk-abuse.md) section 7.9's Hard row, whose Behavior cell reads `Auto-enforce.` No line
in this module resists that, because there is no line to resist with: `DetectorFinding` has no `status`
field, `DetectorTx` has no addressed write, `DetectorScanInput` hands a detector no transaction at all,
and `identity_links` is absent from `DETECTOR_WRITE_TABLES`. **So the hard link is READ here and never
WRITTEN here**, clause 1's edge stays the resolver's, and the foreclosure is asserted in both directions.
**The seeded violation does not compile**: `status: 'enforced'` on a finding is
`TS2353: 'status' does not exist in type 'DetectorFinding'`, and the suite goes red beside it.

**`D-18` TESTS `footprint_present IS FALSE` AND NEVER `IS NOT TRUE`, AND IT IS ASSERTED AT BOTH THE
PLACES IT RUNS.** The window narrows on an equality against `false`, so a vendor-timeout row carrying
`null` never crosses; and the detector re-tests every leg over the merged rows, because **the battery is
merged AFTER the read and never travels through `rowsWhere` at all**, which is `P7-e`'s own landmine 1
arriving as a live hazard rather than as a caveat. Seeded as `value !== true`, the vendor timeout scores
`no_digital_footprint: true` and three cases go red. **`ADR-157`'s refused `isNotNull` term costs this
detector nothing**, because `IS FALSE` is an equality.

**THE BATTERY FOUND A REAL DEFECT WHILE THE SUITE WAS BEING WRITTEN, AND IT IS THE ONE A READER SHOULD
CARRY FORWARD TO [`P7-g`](plans/P7-risk-and-abuse.md).** `D-11` is the one detector here whose join
crosses ROWS, and the runner merges the synthetic subjects into the same stream, so a real account
inverse-correlated with the canary's manufactured series put a synthetic subject and a real one in ONE
finding. `DetectorCanaryLeak` refused it and failed the run, correctly. **A detector cannot tell a canary
from a real row and must not be able to**, so the repair is in what the finding NAMES: the candidate and
not the pair, which makes the straddle unreachable rather than unlikely. `GS-112` wanted that anyway,
*"no detector parameter, no threshold and no other identity"*. **Every join-based detector has this
shape**, and `P7-g` writes five of them.

**NO EVIDENCE OBJECT CARRIES A THRESHOLD, AND THE ASSERTION IS MECHANICAL** against the seed's own
parameter keys. `INV-M7-10` is enforced several slices away by `P7-j`'s strip list, computed from
`is_sensitive`, which is `true` for all seven of these rows; a copy of a parameter inside
`risk_flags.evidence` makes that stripping load-bearing in a second place, and `AS-M6-01` is where it is
wrong once. The investigator loses nothing, because `INV-M7-04` already built the chain that reconstructs
it: `risk_flags.detector_run_id -> detector_runs.(detector, detector_version) ->
detector_definitions.parameters`.

**TWO STRUCTURAL BLOCKERS ARE REPORTED RATHER THAN REACHED FOR, AND NEITHER IS AN ACCESSOR ARGUMENT.**
`D-09` has no input, which is **`DEP-M7-04` arriving exactly where that row said it would**:
[`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts) classes `payout_transfers` `derived via payoutRequests` and
says *"THE TABLE CARRIES NO IDENTITY COLUMN AT ALL"*, so *"more than one unrelated identity"* needs
`payout_requests.identity_id` and `payoutRequests` is not a member of `DETECTOR_READ_TABLES`. **The
remedy is one member in [`detectors/ports.ts`](../apps/worker/src/detectors/ports.ts), which is `P7-e`'s
fence**, and it is not a JOIN argument against `scoped-db.ts`: both tables are already `TableKey`s, both
are already reachable, and a detector reading both and joining in the runner is the shape
[ADR-157](decisions/ADR-157.md) section 5 granted. And two of `D-18`'s four required legs are `D-15`'s
checkout enrichment, which does not exist. **Both predicates are written and tested against the shapes
those inputs would produce.**

**THREE SMALLER FINDINGS, EACH MEASURED.** `canary.ts`'s `sharedDestination` already mints `identityId`
onto a `payoutTransfers` row and that column does not exist on that table, which is `DEP-M7-04` from the
battery's side. `CANARY_SHAPES` is a closed union of four and holds **no identity-side shape**, so five
of this file's batteries carry the nearest label rather than an exact one. And `ports.ts` reads
[ADR-157](decisions/ADR-157.md) as granting a two-sided window, while a filter is **one value per column
ANDed**, so `atLeast(a)` and `atMost(b)` on the SAME column cannot both appear in one call; `D-11`'s
marks window is one-sided and its upper bound is applied in memory.

**FOUR OF THE SEVEN HAVE NO `risk_flags.flag_type`.** The vocabulary in
[risk_flags.md](architecture/data-model/risk_flags.md) and `0008_risk.sql:119` predates `D-16` and
`D-18` and never carried a destination-concentration or dilution-timing member, and the column has **no
`CHECK`**, so an invented value would insert, ship, and become the vocabulary by having been written.
`D-09`, `D-11`, `D-16` and `D-18` read `flag_type` from their registry row and refuse when it is absent.

## The third door was refused, and the reason is that it unblocks none of the five ports it was allocated against (2026-08-28, session 306)

**[ALLOCATION](decisions/ALLOCATION.md) row `171` reserved an ADR number under the heading "ONE RULING UNBLOCKS FIVE PORTS" and named the five: `setAdminReadSource`, `setAdminSessionSource`, `useAdminPayoutBackend`, `useAdminWalletBackend` and `useAdminWriteBackend`, each said to wait on `systemDb('operator-console')`, which [`apps/api/src/db.ts`](../apps/api/src/db.ts) declines to declare under [ADR-120](decisions/ADR-120.md) clause 3. [ADR-171](decisions/ADR-171.md) read the five at their own declarations before ruling on the door and REFUSED IT ON THE MEASUREMENT: the door moves none of them.**

**[ADR-173](decisions/ADR-173.md), `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED. MONEY PATH BY CONTENT. `0052` IS NOT TAKEN.**

[ADR-158](decisions/ADR-158.md) wrote `POST /admin/wallet/:identityId/correct` from [`0011_wallet.sql`](../packages/db/migrations/0011_wallet.sql) alone across eighteen findings, and [`0038_account_adjustments.sql`](../packages/db/migrations/0038_account_adjustments.sql) is the built door for exactly that endpoint. The correction written exactly as the contract instructs fails on `invalid input syntax for type uuid`, so the instruction is **not merely wrong but inexpressible**: it never reaches a constraint, a trigger or an invariant. The same correction through `0038`'s door commits. The correcting DEBIT the contract's body admits fails on `account_adjustments_debit_is_a_reversal`, with the constraint name in the error.

**THE RECORD EXISTS AND IS NOT WHERE THE CONTRACT SAYS, WHICH IS A BETTER OUTCOME THAN EITHER DIRECTION THE DISPATCH NAMED.** `admin_actions.before.corrected_entry` carries the whole corrected entry as it stood before the correction, plus `before.balance_after_cents` and an `evidence_refs` entry of kind `wallet_entry`; [`admin-wallet.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/admin-wallet.ts) already writes it and the live database returned the corrected entry's id back out of it. `0026` revokes `UPDATE, DELETE` on `admin_actions` from `merit_app` and `PUBLIC` exactly as it does on `wallet_entries`, confirmed from `information_schema.role_table_grants`, so **the audit row is as durable as the entry it describes and holds strictly more than a column would.** That is [ADR-158](decisions/ADR-158.md)'s own clause 7 instrument, one clause away from the finding [ADR-158](decisions/ADR-158.md) missed.

**A FIFTH WRITE THE DISPATCH DID NOT PREDICT MOVED THE RULING FURTHER.** Of the three `reason_code` members [`0038`](../packages/db/migrations/0038_account_adjustments.sql) admits, only `reconciliation_error` is about an entry: a `goodwill` credit for a support failure repairs nothing, and it lands in the wallet carrying `provenance = 'correction'` because [`0011`](../packages/db/migrations/0011_wallet.sql)'s closed list offers it nothing else. **NO MIGRATION LANDS AND THE ABSENT COLUMN IS A DECISION `0038` RECORDED RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT**, in that file's own words about why the adjustment carries no `wallet_entry_id`: a second pointer would be a cycle to insert around. **THREE OF SESSION 298's FOUR DISAGREEMENTS STAND AND THE ROUTE IS NOT TOUCHED.** The correcting debit, the dual-control threshold and `reason_code` all survive, and the threshold cannot be ruled from any document in this tree: `dual_control_threshold_cents` is `bigint NOT NULL CHECK (> 0)` with no configured source, and picking one is a number this repository invented on the cash door. **So the append stays stopped exactly where session 298 put it**, and one divergence is recorded with its one-word patch: the handler now requires a field the repaired contract makes optional, which is the fail-closed direction of the two.

**[`0038`](../packages/db/migrations/0038_account_adjustments.sql) AND [`0011`](../packages/db/migrations/0011_wallet.sql) ARE BYTE FOR BYTE UNCHANGED**, as constitution `E2` requires of merged migrations.

## The fill detectors landed, and the canary battery reads a column `fills` does not have (2026-08-28, `P7-f`)

**[`apps/worker/src/detectors/fills.ts`](../apps/worker/src/detectors/fills.ts) and its suite build [P7](plans/P7-risk-and-abuse.md) section 8's `P7-f`: `D-01` fill clustering, `D-04` news-window clustering and `D-05` martingale sequence**, against `P7-e`'s ports and changing none of them. Three of three. No ADR number, no migration number, no `packages/db` change, no `SystemReason` member, no `SqlExecutorReason` member, and the worker barrel appended and re-read whole.

**The finding is in the file this slice builds on.** `canary.ts`'s `martingaleSequence` mints `fills` rows carrying `realizedPnlCents` and `sequenceOrdinal`, and **`fills` has neither column**: `realized_pnl_cents` is `daily_marks`' and `sequenceOrdinal` is no table's. A `D-05` written against that shape **finds its canary every night and never once fires on a real martingale**, which is `AS-M7-05`'s green dashboard produced by the mechanism built to prevent it. `canary.ts` is outside this fence, so it is reported and worked around: `D-05` builds its own battery over the columns that exist, and the suite asserts that every canary row **this** file builds uses only column names `schema.ts` gives the table its stream claims to be.

**The near-miss fixtures are the deliverable and each is one unit from its positive.** 3 of 4 shared fills fires and 2 of 4 does not at a 5000bp floor; fills 2 seconds apart pair and 3 seconds apart do not; entries near 3 releases fire and 2 do not, and twenty entries around one release never do; 100 to 200 contracts fires and 100 to 199 does not; three sequences fire and two do not; and the firing size series after **winning** days raises nothing. Every threshold comparison is an integer cross-multiplication rather than a division, which is what makes "just outside" one contract rather than a rounding.

**`D-01` filters same-identity pairs at the detector** ([M07](plans/M07-risk-abuse.md) section 3.4) and the suite proves it is not a dismissal either: the firing fixture with one field changed writes no row of any kind. **`D-01` runs on ingest** through `fillClustering({at})`, whose narrowed stream is one `atLeast` term beside the day's equality, which is [ADR-157](decisions/ADR-157.md) section 5's grant used by name. **And it still reads the whole day, because the share's denominator is the day**, so the ingest mode buys `AS-M7-01`'s detection latency rather than read cost. The call site is one line in `src/live/`, outside this fence, and is owed.

**All three decline against the registry as `P7-d` seeded it, and that is the honest state of `OQ-M7-02` rather than a defect.** Eleven of the seventeen numbers they need are `unstated`, because the seed writes no number it cannot cite. Each raises `DetectorDeclined`, the run is recorded `failed`, and the dead-man switch sees it the same morning.

**Severity is capped rather than invented, and this is the line the founder should read.** Nothing in the corpus states an SLA duration for severity 4 or 5: `OQ-M7-03` is open, proposes a number for 5 only, and no seed row carries `sla_hours`. So a finding that would score 4 or 5 is written at **3**, with `severity_capped_from` and the reason on the flag. The alternative is an invented clock holding a real trader's payout for 48 hours under [ADR-040](decisions/ADR-040.md). **The cap lifts with a seed row and not with a deploy**, which means the day `OQ-M7-03` is answered, flags that read 3 today start reading 4 or 5 and start holding payouts with no code change. Two cited severity cases are unreachable and are reported rather than approximated: `D-01`'s severity 5 needs "a funded member **eligible this week**" and payout eligibility has no read in `DETECTOR_READ_TABLES`, and `D-04`'s only cited case is worded for single-window observations, which this detector never produces.

**The evidence carries the conduct and discloses no threshold**, which is `M07` section 3.4's own standard for a flag that has to survive a public argument, asserted over every flag all three can raise.

**Twelve seeded cheap implementations watched failing**, each reverted from a byte-identical copy checked by digest. Measured on this branch with `pnpm install` first and each command run separately: **33 of 33 gates, 13 of 13 invariants, typecheck 0, lint 0, format clean, 192 files / 4,137 passed / 6 skipped**, `falsify.mjs` last and alone. The dispatch baseline of 191 / 4,088 / 6 was reproduced exactly before a line changed.

## ADR-172 lands: the ledger handle no request handler can hold, and the store that was already built (2026-08-28, session 307)

**[ALLOCATION](decisions/ALLOCATION.md) row `172` reserved ONE number for TWO findings and asked whether they are one ruling or two. THEY ARE TWO, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS A RULING.**

**Finding 1 reproduced exactly and took the number.** `PayoutTx.ledger` ([`routes/payouts.ts:395`](../apps/api/src/routes/payouts.ts)) is a non-nullable `LedgerTx`; its `insert` names `ledgerTransactions` and `ledgerEntries`, both scope class `derived`; `ScopedTx.insert` takes `OwnedTableKey` and `ParentedTableKey` is `Extract<DerivedTableKey, 'sessions'>`, **a closed list of one**. Only `SystemTx` satisfies it, at a vocabulary [ADR-165](decisions/ADR-165.md) ruled gains no member. **No live deployment can construct a `PayoutBackend`.**

**Finding 2 IS FALSE AT THE SOURCE AND IS OWED NO NUMBER.** [`apps/api/src/idempotency-store.ts:144`](../apps/api/src/idempotency-store.ts) has implemented `IdempotencyStore` since [ADR-112](decisions/ADR-112.md), and **`tx.updateAt` IS the addressed UPDATE the premise said no accessor offered** -- the dispatch's own fence asked that this be checked before concluding it impossible, and the check is what refuted it. **[`wiring.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/wiring.test.ts) contradicted itself about this in one file twenty lines apart**, `:150` against `:228`. The false half is replaced, not deleted.

**THE RULING: the `LT-01` posting leaves the request path.** A door in `apps/api` returning a handle that satisfies `LedgerTx` would be `systemDb` under another name, because the only handle satisfying it is `insert<K extends TableKey>` over **every table in the estate**. So `PayoutTx.ledger` is the defect and the missing door is not. **Three precedents in this tree already post this way**: the worker at `systemDb('nightly-batch')`, the operator console, and the cash door which declined to post on its own request path in writing. **`INV-M5-06` survives by construction** -- all three doors build `` `${PAYOUT_ENDPOINT} ${idempotencyKey}` `` from the request's STORED key, so the key belongs to the APPROVAL rather than to the DOOR.

**`useWithdrawalBackend` STAYS BLOCKED, and the true reason is worse than the false one.** Nothing in this tree drives `requested --> approved`, and `requested` and `cooling` are both in `OPEN_WITHDRAWAL_STATUSES`, so `gateNoInFlight` would refuse that identity's every later withdrawal. **Wiring it trades an honest 503 for a permanent per-trader lockout. Both refuse; only the 503 is reversible.**

**No migration was needed and none was claimed** -- `0010` already carries `status`, `idempotency_key`, `identity_id` and the three clamp legs, so the driver clause 3 requires is a build slice rather than DDL. **No port was wired**, so the `{declared, wired, blocked}` triple stays `{21, 6, 15}`. **`packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts` untouched, no `SystemReason` member, no `pg` import, no cast past a key type.**

**What is still owed:** the `M05`-versus-`API_CONTRACT` disagreement about whether `LT-06` posts at request time, reported by session 303 and still unowned; and the approval-edge driver, whichever way that falls. **Neither is finding 2 and neither is this entry's.**

## The `IdempotencyStore` that exists, and a stale header restated four times (2026-08-28, session 303 follow-up)

**[#402](https://github.com/lam2-coder/meritfutures/pull/402) merged carrying a claim that is FALSE, and the claim had by then reached an allocated `REQUIRED` money-path ADR reservation.** This section is the correction and the chain, because the chain is the more useful half.

**THE CLAIM:** *"no implementation of `IdempotencyStore` exists in this tree, because `complete` is an UPDATE of exactly one row and `systemTx`/`firmTx` hardcode `undefined` for the `WHERE`."*

**THE SOURCE THAT REFUTES IT:** [`apps/api/src/idempotency-store.ts:144`](../apps/api/src/idempotency-store.ts) exports `databaseIdempotencyStore(db: ApiDb): IdempotencyStore`, 206 lines, whose `find`, `begin` and `complete` all run through `db.scoped` with keyed addresses, covered by [`idempotency-store.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/idempotency-store.test.ts). **The objection does not reach it**: `systemTx` and `firmTx` hardcode `undefined` for the `WHERE` and this store opens NEITHER, it opens the SCOPED door, which carries `scopePredicate` AND the address into the predicate. That is what [ADR-112](decisions/ADR-112.md) gave `updateAt` for.

**THE CHAIN, WHICH IS THE FINDING.** [`idempotency.ts`](../apps/api/src/idempotency.ts)'s own header says it and is stale. Session 303's adapter comment repeated it **without opening the file beside it**. `fde1016` cited the header AND that comment as two sources, and entered `useWithdrawalBackend` in [`wiring.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/wiring.test.ts)'s `BLOCKED` list. [ALLOCATION](decisions/ALLOCATION.md)'s row `172` then reserved an ADR **REQUIRED, MONEY PATH** for session 307 against it. **Four restatements, no reader between them opened `idempotency-store.ts`.**

**THE FILE CONTRADICTED ITSELF AND EVERY GATE STAYED GREEN.** `wiring.test.ts` as merged carried *"`databaseIdempotencyStore` already exists and satisfies the `idempotency` member alone"* in its `usePayoutBackend` entry, **a hundred lines above** the `useWithdrawalBackend` entry saying no file provides one. Nothing reads reasons for agreement, so nothing failed. **This is [ADR-075](decisions/ADR-075.md)'s and [P5 section 5.1](plans/P5-payouts-and-wallet.md)'s failure mode arriving a fourth time**, and it is the constitution's own "caution learned the hard way": *"Each was a failure to check a claim against the primary source. Escalating the model does not fix that class of error; reading the source and adding a mechanical assertion does."*

**WHAT CHANGES.** `databaseWithdrawalBackend` uses `databaseIdempotencyStore`, and the comment that carried the false claim is **corrected where it was made** rather than deleted. `ALLOCATION` row `172`'s finding (2) is **struck through rather than deleted**, so the next reader meets the claim and its refutation together; **finding (1) is unaffected and stands.**

**THE WIRING WAS PROPOSED HERE AND IS REFUSED ON THE MERGE, AND THE REFUSAL IS NOT ABOUT THE STORE.** The `IdempotencyStore` refutation above stands entirely. What does not follow from it is that the port should be installed. [ADR-172](decisions/ADR-172.md) reached the opposite conclusion from the same tree and it is right: `wallet_withdrawal_status` ([`0001:95`](../packages/db/migrations/0001_extensions_and_enums.sql)) carries `cancelled`, `settled` and `failed`, every terminal status that would release `gateNoInFlight`, and **no code in this tree writes any of them.** The only writes to `wallet_withdrawals` anywhere are the one `INSERT` at `wallet-withdrawals.ts:990` and the halt-clear at [`expiry.ts:734`](../apps/worker/src/sweeps/expiry.ts). `requested` and `cooling` are both in `OPEN_WITHDRAWAL_STATUSES` (`:283-288`), on which `gateNoInFlight` (`:1233`) refuses. **So a wired endpoint parks a row nothing can advance and then refuses that identity's every later withdrawal, behind a screen saying one is already in flight.** A 503 and a lockout both refuse and only the 503 is reversible. **The port stays blocked with the TRUE reason substituted for the false one, and the triple stays `{declared: 21, wired: 6, blocked: 15}`.** The adapter's own `idempotency` arm keeps `databaseIdempotencyStore`, because the correction was to the claim and not to the code.

**`POST /wallet/withdrawals` STILL ANSWERS 503 FROM A LIVE DEPLOYMENT, AND THE SENTENCE THAT STOOD HERE SAID OTHERWISE.** It read *"now answers from a live deployment"*, which was true of the change as proposed and is not true of the change as merged; see the ruling above. What that sentence went on to say is unchanged and is the reason the wiring looked safe: `WithdrawalTx` carries no `LedgerTx` where `PayoutTx` declares one, `requested --> approved` and `cooling --> approved` still have no driver in this tree, and the `LT-06` those edges carry is still the ruling reported above and not taken.
