## `P7-g` has landed: one graph detector of five produces an answer, and the aggregate `ADR-157` refused turns out not to have been the blocker (2026-08-28, session 310)

**[`apps/worker/src/detectors/graph.ts`](../apps/worker/src/detectors/graph.ts) and [`test/detectors-graph.test.ts`](../apps/worker/test/detectors-graph.test.ts) build [P7](plans/P7-risk-and-abuse.md) section 8's `P7-g`, against [`P7-e`](sessions/2026-08-27-session-300.md)'s runner and ports and changing neither.**

**THE COUNT IS ONE OF FIVE AND EVERY REASON IS A MEASUREMENT.** `D-02` RUNS, capped at severity 3. `D-03`, `D-13` and `D-14` DECLINE under `DetectorDeclined`, which the runner records as a `failed` run visible to `detector_runs_unhealthy_idx` and to `CRON_INVENTORY`'s dead-man switch on the morning of the day it happens. **`D-12` IS NOT A `Detector` AT ALL.** Every threshold is read from `detector_definitions` under `INV-M7-04` and no literal is compared against, so **the three declines are one founder answer to `OQ-M7-02` away from running** and the decline messages name every missing parameter at once rather than the first.

**[ADR-157](decisions/ADR-157.md) SECTION 5 EXPECTED THE JOIN TO BLOCK THIS SLICE AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS IT DOES NOT.** All five detectors are readable through the accessor: `identity_links`, `identity_signals`, `accounts`, `daily_marks` and `fills` are five `rowsWhere` calls and the joins are ordinary code in the runner. **So no entry against [`scoped-db.ts`](../packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts) is asked for**, and the question that entry wrote down for the JOIN ruling stays unanswered rather than being spent on a cost that is real, measured, and not blocking. **What it costs, executed**: at 60 marked accounts, a 3-account trio and a 20 day window, `D-03` reads 1,320 rows to decide about 60, which is **22 rows read per row that mattered**, and the ratio is the marked population divided by the group so it **GROWS as the group gets smaller**. **Two further costs no clause of that entry names**: a filter carries **ONE narrowing per column**, so a `BETWEEN` crosses as a lower bound and the upper bound is applied in memory; and an empty filter does not compile, so *"the whole table"* is spelled as a narrowing that is true rather than as a cast.

**`GS-118`'s NEGATIVE ASSERTION IS THE MOST VALUABLE TEST IN THE SLICE AND IT IS WRITTEN THE STRONG WAY.** The six-account ring on the 5 trading day path raises no `D-02` flag **and the same run finds its canary**, so *"did not fire"* is distinguishable from *"is broken"*, which a bare zero-flag assertion would have lost. Every pair on the ring is at **-1.0000**, far below the -0.8000 floor, and not one has twenty common trading days. Seeding *"`D-02` ignores its window"* turns exactly that case red.

**`D-13`'s THREE CONDITIONS ARE A CONJUNCTION, PROVED BY THREE NEAR-MISSES EACH OF WHICH SATISFIES TWO OF THEM** -- a disjunction would have fired on all three. **`D-14` WORKS ON POSITIONS RATHER THAN REALIZED P&L**, and its near-miss is the one a reader would omit: **an idle clique sums to zero** and flagging it would fire on every dormant cluster in the estate every night.

**FOUR THINGS NEED A RULING AND ARE REPORTED RATHER THAN REPAIRED.**

| # | Finding |
| --- | --- |
| **A** | **`SD-M7-02`'s clock has no stated duration, so NO detector in this repository can write a severity 4 or 5 flag today.** `risk_flags_high_severity_has_sla` binds the band `G-HOLD-REQUIRED` reads under [ADR-040](decisions/ADR-040.md). The nearest thing to a duration is **`OQ-M7-03`, an OPEN founder question**, which **proposes** rather than states, covers **severity 5 only**, and whose business-hours arm needs a calendar this tree does not have. **This is a fourth blocker on `D-03` invisible from its seed row** and half the reason `D-02` caps at 3 |
| **B** | **`D-12` has no home in [`ports.ts`](../apps/worker/src/detectors/ports.ts).** `M07:122` makes its output *"a watched-cluster set, NOT a flag"*, and `runner.ts` computes `found < expected ? 'degraded' : 'ok'` while `mintBattery` refuses a detector seeding no canaries, so **a `Detector` must return a finding or a group or be degraded every night forever** -- and both become rows. `correlation_groups` cannot hold one either: `statistic` and `threshold` are `numeric NOT NULL`, and a row there is the group FINDING `P7-i` and `P7-j` read, so writing one converts *"watched"* into *"found"*. It ships as `discoverClusters` and the other three call it. Its `runs_at: "funding"` is separately unserved, this runner being nightly |
| **C** | **A canary cannot be sized to the registry parameters it must satisfy**, because `Detector.canaries` takes a mint and not a request. **`D-13`'s is coupled in BOTH directions at once**: fewer marks than the window and the window is unfilled, more and the account is not young, so it must carry exactly `window_trading_days` and any other window makes a healthy detector page |
| **D** | **The `flag_type` vocabulary has no GROUP member.** `0008_risk.sql:119` lists ten types in a comment with no CHECK on the column. `D-02` and `D-13` are inverse pairs and the word fits; `D-03` and `D-14` are group findings and it does not, and minting one is the flags queue's decision. Both decline today, so no row exists to be mislabelled |

**AND `D-14`'s INPUT TABLE IS CONFIRMED ABSENT**, which `ports.ts` left as this slice's finding to make: there is **no `positions` key in [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts) and no `CREATE TABLE` whose name contains `position`**. A net position is derivable from `fills` and the derivation is end-of-day only, so it can never be the *"live"* half `M07:124` names.

**ONE THING THE PLAN EXPECTED TO BE A STOP WAS NOT ONE.** `correlation_groups` **IS** registered in [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts) and [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts) at scope class `firm`. No schema change was needed and none was made.

**`D-02` IS CAPPED AT SEVERITY 3 AND THE CAP IS A MONEY DECISION TAKEN DELIBERATELY.** `M07:151` scores it 4 for *"below the floor with both accounts funded"*, and this module never writes that 4, for two independent reasons: *"below the floor"* means `M07:109`'s statistic, which is the correlation **and comparable size**, and `comparable_size_tolerance_bp` is `unstated`; and severity 4 needs a clock nobody has set. **What it does instead of thresholding size is report it** -- `size_cents_ratio_bp` and `abs_pnl_ratio_bp` on every flag, beside `comparable_size_evaluated: false`.

**THE SUITE FOUND A DEFECT WHILE IT WAS BEING WRITTEN, AND IT IS A RULE RATHER THAN A SLIP.** An early `D-02` evidence object reported `accounts_in_window` and the measurement case read **62 against a population of 60**; the two extra were the canary pair. **`AS-M7-05` note 1 is unqualified, and a detector is blind to its canaries by construction, so a detector may never report ANY count over its own input.** The runner's `rows_scanned` and `rowsByStream` are canary free because it takes them before the battery is merged.

**NO FLOAT ANYWHERE, INCLUDING IN A CORRELATION.** The firing test is `(10000*|Sxy|)^2 >= floor^2 * Sxx * Syy`, an inequality between two `bigint`s with no division and no square root in the decision; the bp figure in the evidence is a separate truncated quantity that decides nothing. A variance ratio needs no root at all, the `D^2` cancelling between numerator and denominator. `numeric` columns are written as exact decimal strings and a `bigint` reaching `jsonb` becomes a `number` only when it is exactly representable.

**Twelve seeded defects, twelve caught**, including the conjunction turned into a disjunction, the correlation comparison reversed, the money band entered, the idle clique flagged, and a barrel leg dropped. **Four of them were MISSES first and the reason is recorded rather than counted as a pass**: `D-02`'s window and `D-12`'s lone-identity refusal are each enforced in two places, so a single-site seed is caught by the other site and the suite stays green.

## ADR-176 lands: the request path records the approval and does not post it, and the key that had to go with it (2026-08-28, session 316)

**[ADR-172](decisions/ADR-172.md) clause 2 applied where that entry reported it and fenced it: [`routes/payouts.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/payouts.ts).** `PayoutTx.ledger` is DELETED and `decidePayout`'s posting arm is REMOVED. **The premises were re-derived at source rather than inherited from the ruling that settled them**, and they hold: `LedgerWriteKey` is `ledgerTransactions | ledgerEntries` ([`tx.ts:64`](../packages/ledger/src/tx.ts)), both scope class `derived` (`scope.ts:513,522`); `ScopedTx.insert` takes `OwnedTableKey` (`scoped-db.ts:1739`) and `ParentedTableKey` is `Extract<DerivedTableKey, 'sessions'>` (`:1540`), a closed list of ONE; so the only handle satisfying `LedgerTx` is `insert<K extends TableKey>` over the whole estate (`:1802`), and a door in `apps/api` returning one would be `systemDb` renamed.

**THE VERIFICATION FOUND ONE THING THE RULING NEEDED AND [ADR-172](decisions/ADR-172.md) DID NOT SEE.** `PayoutRequestInsert` carried no `idempotencyKey` member, while `payout_requests.idempotency_key` is `text NOT NULL` ([`0010:82`](../packages/db/migrations/0010_payouts.sql)) and [`admin-payouts.ts:784,809`](../apps/api/src/routes/admin-payouts.ts) already READS that column on release. **While the posting stood inside the handler the key reached it out of local memory, so the gap was invisible; removing the posting alone would have committed an approval no door could ever post, and the failure would have been silent.** The field is added and stored UNPREFIXED, on `payout_requests_account_idempotency_uq (account_id, idempotency_key)`. **The removal and the field are ONE change, and either one without the other is worse than neither.**

**`INV-M5-06` IS SHOWN AT THREE FILES RATHER THAN CITED.** Both remaining doors are `releaseLedgerKey` character for character (`admin-payouts.ts:916`, `expiry.ts:305`) and **both call sites pass `held.idempotencyKey` off the LOCKED row** (`:1185`, `:667`). The key is a property of the APPROVAL and not of the DOOR, so removing one of three doors that mint the identical string cannot produce a second posting, and `ledger_transactions.idempotency_key text NOT NULL UNIQUE` is what refuses one.

**`usePayoutBackend` DOES NOT BECOME CONSTRUCTIBLE, AND ITS `BLOCKED` ENTRY IS REWRITTEN RATHER THAN SHRUNK.** The recorded reason was the deleted field, so it is now false; a different obstruction was underneath it and **it is a READ rather than a write**. `PayoutSubject.state` is the engine's `RuleState`, which requires `lifetimeSettledCents`, `breached` and `breachKind` ([`types.ts:1004,1009,1010`](../packages/rules-engine/src/types.ts)); **`0015_rule_states.sql` declares none of the three, `lifetime_settled` appears in NO migration in the tree, and no migration names any member of `BreachKind`.** That is **the same blocker a WIRED sibling already carries**: `databaseAccountReads` is installed and `readEligibility` rejects on `ELIGIBILITY_BLOCKER` ([`account-reads.ts:851`](../apps/api/src/routes/account-reads.ts)) for those exact three fields, and `INV-M5-02` is what binds the two endpoints to one `RuleState`. Independently, `ResolvedPlan` is built from `plan_versions.rules` and a `plan_version_sizes` row, both scope class `firm` (`scope.ts:482,487`), which `ScopedTableKey` excludes (`scope.ts:1165`), while `PayoutTx` runs every method on ONE transaction. **A partial backend is REFUSED rather than overlooked**: `listPayouts` and `idempotency` are constructible today, and installing them beside a `transact` that rejects would put a live-looking route in front of the arm that approves payouts.

**FOUR LINE CITATIONS IN [`wiring.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/wiring.test.ts) POINTED AT THE WRONG LINE, AND TWO ARE IN THE ENTRY [ADR-172](decisions/ADR-172.md) WROTE ONE SESSION EARLIER TO REPLACE A FALSE REASON.** `wallet-withdrawals.ts:1233` is `G-WITHDRAWAL-CLEARED`'s KYC term and `gateNoInFlight` is at `:1251`; `:1506` is a `.send({` and the identity arm is at `:1524`; both off by eighteen lines, both checked on `origin/main` before this branch moved anything. Also `admin-payouts.ts:381` for a declaration at `:382` and `admin-writes.ts:266` for one at `:269`. **The claims held at their real lines and the pointers did not**, which is the same drift in its quietest form: nothing fails, and a reader who follows the pointer concludes the reason was invented. **This is the third consecutive session in which that file has been found carrying something nothing checks**, and the gate that would have caught all four -- resolve every `file:line` inside a reason string -- is still not written.

**FOUR STALE "three doors" CLAIMS WERE CORRECTED AT THEIR OWN FILES**, because a diff that falsifies a comment owns that comment: `expiry.ts`, `sweeps/ports.ts`, `wallet-withdrawals.ts` and `admin-payouts.ts`, the last of which had compared its own ledger field to `PayoutTx.ledger` by name. [ADR-172](decisions/ADR-172.md)'s reported landmine about `wallet-withdrawals.ts`'s `IdempotencyStore` comment was **checked and is already closed** at `:950-959`.

**THE SIX `LT-01` COMPOSITION ASSERTIONS WERE RETARGETED, NOT DELETED.** They now run over `postTransaction(recorder, chart, lt01(...))` directly: one header, four entries, two debits summing to `approved_cents`, the signs read off `posting.ts:235-236`, the zero sum and the `bigint` check. Four new source-reading cases pin the removal, which a behavioural suite cannot hold, and they also pin the paired half: **`lt01` must STAY exported here and `admin-payouts.ts` must keep importing it**, so a later session cannot "finish" this ruling by giving each door its own transcription of the legs.

**THE GAP THIS RULING OPENS IS REAL AND IS UNREACHABLE, AND ONLY THE SECOND HALF IS A CONTROL.** Nothing in the tree posts `LT-01` for a request approved with NO hold, because both remaining doors fire on a HELD request being released. The driver is [ADR-172](decisions/ADR-172.md) section 5's, checked at `0010` to need no DDL, and **this entry does not build it**: different deployable, and [ADR-003](decisions/ADR-003.md)'s money-path regime is one objective per session. It cannot be reached because `usePayoutBackend` is unwired, `wiring.test.ts` asserts `start.ts` does not call it, and the route answers 503 before it opens a transaction. **The route answered 503 before this ruling and answers 503 after it.** `INV-M5-21`'s enforcement moves with the posting and is written down where the driver will be: its predicate must be `status = 'approved'`.

**Triple unmoved at `{21, 6, 15}`. NO migration, no `SystemReason` member, no `SqlExecutorReason` member, no cast past a key type, no `pg` import, `packages/db` untouched.** Approval line UNSIGNED, **MONEY PATH, `E2` READ OWED**; section 7 puts three judgements to the founder, including whether `API_CONTRACT` section 6's ordered sentence is amended now that it names a step this route no longer performs. **The wire shape does not change**: `PayoutResponse` carried no ledger transaction id and `estimated_settlement` was already a business-day range.

**Five defects seeded and five caught**, including the one worth keeping: a STORED key prefixed with `PAYOUT_ENDPOINT` typechecks, reads plausibly, and would make every door compose the prefix twice. It is caught because the assertion is `.not.toContain(PAYOUT_ENDPOINT)` rather than "a key is present".

**Baseline reproduced on `main` before anything moved and every command run separately after each file: 33 of 33 gates, 13 of 13 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, `format:check` clean, 204 test files / 4,443 passed / 6 skipped BEFORE and 204 / 4,448 / 6 AFTER.** The five added are four source-reading cases and one retargeted composition case; **no case was deleted.**

**`main` MOVED UNDER THIS BRANCH MID-SESSION AND WHAT IT LANDED READS THIS BRANCH'S DIFF.** `c733fcd` merged `RI-14`, *"No reason claims a named thing does not exist while the tree exports it"*, whose `covers` names [`wiring.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/wiring.test.ts) as the file whose reasons it reads -- **the same file this session rewrote, for the same defect, from a different session on the same night.** It was merged in and re-run rather than waited out. **On the merged head: 33 of 33 gates, `14 of 14` invariants, typecheck 0, lint 0, format clean, 204 files / 4,454 passed / 6 skipped**, and `RI-14` passes over the rewritten `usePayoutBackend` reason: its three absence claims are about a COLUMN and about strings in a migration, not about a name the tree exports. **`RI-14` closes one half of this session's landmine and its own `covers` says which.** It reads EXPORTS and does not resolve a `file:line`, so the four wrong pointers found here would still pass it. **That gate is still unwritten, and it is a smaller ask than it was this morning**, because `RI-14` already parses the reason strings and would only need to resolve what they cite.

## `LT-07`'s credit leg was the wrong half of the finding, and the chart of accounts has never been seeded (2026-08-28, session 315)

**[ADR-174](decisions/ADR-174.md) takes findings (A) and (C), [ADR-175](decisions/ADR-175.md)
takes (B), and the split is argued rather than assumed: they live in TWO TABLES and only one of
them is blocked.** (A) is `ledger_accounts` and `ledger_entries`, (B) is one `text NOT NULL
UNIQUE` column on `ledger_transactions`, and a transaction's key is decided by its own header
while its entries are still undecided. **Migration `0052` is RETURNED TO THE POOL UNSPENT** and no
`E2` read is owed on a migration that does not exist.

**THE RESERVATION ANTICIPATED A HOLE IN THE CREDIT SLOT AND THE MEASUREMENT FOUND THE SLOT BESIDE
IT WRONG TOO.** `LT-06` credits `firm_treasury` `amount_cents` ([M05:135](plans/M05-payout-system.md))
and `LT-07` debits it ([M05:136](plans/M05-payout-system.md)), and
[`posting.ts:235-236`](../packages/ledger/src/posting.ts) writes `+amountCents` on a debit and
`-amountCents` on a credit, so **the external leg returns `firm_treasury` to exactly where it
started**: on the one account [M05:141](plans/M05-payout-system.md) names as where a cash movement
books, in the leg whose own row calls it *"The external leg's cash movement"*. **That holds for
every `kind`**, so the ruling on (A) survives finding (C) rather than waiting on it, and **a code
minted for the credit slot would complete a posting that is wrong in the other slot.** `LT-07`'s
row also names no amount, where every other row in that table does.

**`trader_wallet` IS REFUSED ON ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN ON SCOPE.** `LT-06` already debits it at
approval, so an `LT-07` crediting it would return the trader's wallet to where it started while
the money left the firm. That refusal is worth having because **[ADR-124:33](decisions/ADR-124.md)'s
version of it quotes the row under repair**: *"`LT-02` and `LT-07` both move `firm_treasury`
against the payout wallet position"* is [M05:131,136](plans/M05-payout-system.md) restated, so its
conclusion survives this entry and its stated ground cannot settle the repair. **[ADR-124](decisions/ADR-124.md)
is not amended** and the finding is filed where the repair will be read.

**(C) IS RECORDED AS AN ABSENCE, NO DIRECTION IS INFERRED, AND THE ABSENCE IS LARGER THAN THE
DISPATCH SAID.** Executed against PostgreSQL 16.13 with `0001` through `0051` applied forward-only
under `ON_ERROR_STOP`: **`ledger_accounts` HOLDS ZERO ROWS**, and the database accepted
`firm_treasury` as `'asset'`, as `'liability'` and as `'revenue'` in turn. `treasury_balances.account_code`
carries no foreign key and no CHECK into the chart and its own record says it is anchored outside
the ledger deliberately. **NOTHING SEEDS THE CHART OF ACCOUNTS AT ALL**, the only `kind` literals
in the tree are three fixtures inside a probe written to watch constraints fire, and **four of the
seven codes have no `kind` written anywhere**: `firm_treasury`, `psp_clearing`, `reserve` and
`promotional_credit`. **The five sites that call `firm_treasury` the account where cash books were
weighed and NOT taken as a `kind`**, because the corpus's own arithmetic disagrees with them at
`LT-06` and because nothing in this fence needs the answer.

**SO (A) CANNOT BE CLOSED WHILE (C) IS OPEN**, and [ADR-174](decisions/ADR-174.md) section 3 names
the three available repair shapes and why each needs the absence filled first. **The next session
on this row rules the chart of accounts BEFORE the posting**, which is the opposite order from the
one the reservation anticipated.

**(B) IS CLOSED, AND THE TWO CONVENTIONS WERE NEVER IN CONFLICT.** They are one rule under two
spellings and the rule is that a `ledger_transactions.idempotency_key` **names the EVENT it posts
and never the DOOR that reached it**. `PAYOUT_ENDPOINT` is a module constant three call sites

**`INV-M7-10`'s MECHANISM IS NOW TESTED, WHICH [SESSION 282](sessions/2026-08-27-session-282.md) SAID THE

`sensitiveParameterNames` is driven with a two-row registry whose second row is `is_sensitive: false`, and

costs the most if taken per detector: `severity` and `window_trading_days` are parameters of several
detectors at once, so one row flipped to `false` releases only the names it alone claims. The seed's
uniformity is pinned in its own case, so **the day the column acquires its first `false` this suite goes
red** rather than quietly absorbing it.

**THE SUITE FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN THIS SESSION'S OWN CONTROL AND IT IS THE INTERESTING FINDING.** The
"no other identity" check tested `^uuid$` against each string, which reads a value that IS an identifier
and is blind to one that CONTAINS an identifier. **`tos_clause` is free text an operator writes during a
dispute and `GS-112` REQUIRES a `trader` pack to carry it**, so an investigator who wrote *"coordinated
with account `<uuid>`"* had put another identity into a trader pack through a field the pack must not
drop, and the anchored check saw nothing at all. It is a property of every free-text column a pack
carries. Repaired to a scan within strings, pinned by its own case, and the end-to-end refusal is watched
firing on exactly that clause.

**FOUR FINDINGS ABOUT THE CORPUS, EACH READ AT ITS SOURCE.**

**AND WRITING THAT LOG FOUND A LATENT DEFECT IN [`scripts/corpus/gates.mjs`](../scripts/corpus/gates.mjs),
REPORTED AND NOT REPAIRED.** Its span writer interpolates the generated text into the **replacement**
argument of `String.prototype.replace`, and a replacement string is not literal text: JavaScript gives it
a substitution vocabulary whose members can insert the parts of the subject the match did not cover. A
session-log index line carrying a dollar sign immediately before a backtick therefore wrote **the entire
text preceding the span back into the span**, taking [`docs/sessions/README.md`](sessions/README.md) from
549 lines to 743 with its own frontmatter inside the generated table. **`generate` exited 0 and reported
one span rewritten; `CI-06g` failed on the next run**, which is the gate working. **Re-running `generate`
does not heal it**, because each run rewrites the corruption. The exposure belongs to any span whose query
returns prose rather than an integer. The repair is one line in that runner, passing a FUNCTION as the
replacement so the substitution vocabulary is suppressed, and it is **outside this slice's fence**: the
prose was changed instead, which fixes the occurrence and not the class.

## `P7-k` has landed: the breaker has a producer, `insufficient_data` does not pause sales, and `INV-M5-12` is the write union rather than a comment (2026-08-28, session 320)

**[P7](plans/P7-risk-and-abuse.md) section 8's `P7-k`, the THIRD DONE-GATE.** `plan_breaker_state` landed in [`0016`](../packages/db/migrations/0016_treasury_controls.sql) and [`apps/admin/src/page.ts`](../apps/admin/src/page.ts) has said *"nothing writes it"* ever since. It has a writer now: [`apps/worker/src/breaker/evaluate.ts`](../apps/worker/src/breaker/evaluate.ts) and [`ports.ts`](../apps/worker/src/breaker/ports.ts) beside it, 52 cases in [`test/breaker.test.ts`](../apps/worker/test/breaker.test.ts), plus [`apps/api/src/routes/admin-breaker.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/admin-breaker.ts) and 20 cases behind it. **`GS-113` is the gate and it is asserted with its NEAR-MISS beside it.**

**`INV-M5-12` IS THE WRITE UNION AND NOT A COMMENT, AND THAT IS THE ENTRY'S WHOLE CONTENT.** [M05](plans/M05-payout-system.md)'s evidence column reads *"Structural: the breaker's only effect is a flag read by M3's checkout. There is no code path from any liability signal to a payout block"*, and structural is what it now is: `BREAKER_WRITE_TABLES` has EXACTLY ONE MEMBER, so no payout, wallet, halt or restriction table is reachable through the port at all. **The read side carries `payoutRequests` and the asymmetry is the design**: the loss ratio's numerator IS settled payouts (`P-M6-05`), so a port that could not read them would have no ratio, and one that could write one would be the code path the invariant says does not exist. **Read many, write one.**

**THE SEED THE PROMPT ASKED FOR WAS RUN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND THE SECOND IS THE ONE WORTH READING.** Written straight, `await tx.insert('payoutRequests', ...)` inside the paused branch is a COMPILE ERROR (`TS2345`, *"not assignable to parameter of type 'planBreakerState'"*). Written with the cast that gets past `tsc`, **the typechecker reports ZERO errors** and TEN cases go red, among them the source sweep over write verbs and the fake transaction that refuses any key but `planBreakerState`. That second half is why `INV-M5-12` is enforced at four levels here rather than one: a control that lives only in the type system is one `as` away from gone.

**`insufficient_data` IS THE STATE BELOW THE MINIMUM AND SALES ARE NOT PAUSED THERE, AND THE LADDER'S ORDER IS THE CONTROL.** `decideState` tests the FLOOR BEFORE THE RATIO, always, and the ratio is not consulted below it, because a ladder that computed an opinion and then discarded it is one edit from reporting it. `GS-113` is asserted as `AS-M6-02` writes it: one purchase, one 150,000c payout, a ratio of **151,515bp against a 6,000bp threshold**, and the state is `insufficient_data` with `salesPaused` FALSE. **Its near-miss is the same plan at the floor**, which pauses. Seeding the ladder reversed turns five cases red.

**`sample_size` IS WRITTEN BESIDE `min_sample` ON EVERY ROW AND ON EVERY STATE**, `insufficient_data`, `paused` and `armed` alike, because `INV-M6-07` is *"the ratio is shown next to its sample size EVERYWHERE it appears"*. **`breaker.state_changed` carries both as REQUIRED fields** and its payload is [M06:265](plans/M06-admin-ops-console.md) transcribed field for field, asserted against that line parsed out of the document rather than against a copy. **`breaker.state_changed` HAS NO ROW IN [EVENTS](architecture/EVENTS.md)**, which is `detector.run_degraded`'s position one directory over; the absence is PINNED by a test, so the session that lands the row meets the transcription.

**`ADR-167` SECTION 5's RULING IS APPLIED AND THE TERM IT COULD NOT PLACE IS APPLIED WHERE THE ENTRY PUT IT.** `sample_size` is the DENOMINATOR's count and never the settled-payout count; `OQ-M6-02`'s second term, *"3 settled payouts"*, lives in the evaluator, reaches `decideState`, and **reaches no column at all**. A row whose `sample_size` held the payout count *"would satisfy every CHECK in `0016` and describe the wrong population, and no gate in this repository can see which count an integer is"*, so the gate is a test: seven purchases, one payout, and a `sample_size` of 1 turns eight cases red.

**NO NUMBER IN THIS SLICE IS THIS SESSION'S.** `LOSS_RATIO_POLICY` carries `windowDays: 30` and `thresholdBp: 6000` with `M06:95` quoted on each, and **both `OQ-M6-02` terms ship `unstated` with `null`**. So **the evaluator DECLINES** rather than running on an invented floor, which is `DetectorDeclined`'s shape one directory over: a floor of zero is refused by `min_sample > 0` at the database, and a floor of one is `AS-M6-02`'s launch-week outage with a `CHECK` satisfied. A test asserts both terms are STILL `unstated`, so filling one in is a red suite rather than a quiet commit.

**THE CUSUM IS FOLDED IN INTEGER BASIS POINTS AND RENDERS ABSENT, WHICH IS `ADR-167` CLAUSES 4 AND 5 BOTH.** `foldCusum` is integer addition, subtraction and comparison only; the slack is configured as `k_bp` so `sigma` is never halved on the evaluation path. **The one remaining division is the pass rate's and it is declared rather than hidden**: it truncates downward, at most 1bp per day, and because `S_t` is a running sum the bias accumulates in the direction of NOT alarming, which is the safe direction for an advisory panel and cannot be configured away the way the halving could. An unordered series is REFUSED rather than sorted, because a recurrence over a reordered series is a different statistic.

**THE API HALF DECLARES NO PORT, AND THAT IS A RULING RATHER THAN A CONVENIENCE.** [ADR-166](decisions/ADR-166.md) clause 10 measured `GET /admin/loss-ratios` and `GET /admin/cusum` as *"in NEITHER list on EITHER surface"*; measured again from `CompositionReport` after this module, **operator `registered` moves 24 to 26, public `withheld` moves 23 to 25, and `modules` moves 23 to 24**. Section 8 makes both endpoints *"focused projections of `GET /admin/liability`'s UNDERLYING DATA"*, so a second port would have been the second query [`admin-reads.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/admin-reads.ts) already refuses for `/admin/eligible-forecast` **and** would have moved [`wiring.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/wiring.test.ts)'s `{declared: 21, wired: 6, blocked: 15}` triple, whose file is session 316's this wave. **The triple does not move and the whole `apps/api` suite is green.**

**A POPULATED CUSUM ON THE SOURCE RENDERS AS `null`, AND THAT IS THE ASSERTION THE API SUITE EXISTS FOR.** `LiabilityResponse.per_plan[].cusum` is a NON-OPTIONAL field, so a source hands this module `{statistic: 6.25, threshold: 5.5, alarm: true}` and it must not reach the wire: `DEP-M6-05` is M06 **Wave 4**, so any statistic today is uncalibrated, `FM-M6-07` makes an uncalibrated CUSUM *"either constant alarms or none, which is the same as no chart"*, and `apps/admin` already lists `P-M6-06` as pending naming that blocker. **A second surface drawing the chart the console refuses to draw would be the same failure with a different renderer.** Seeding the pass-through turns it red.

**TWO FIELDS THE PORT CANNOT CARRY ARE STATED ABSENCES AND NOT OMISSIONS, AND BOTH ARE REPORTED RATHER THAN REPAIRED.** `per_plan[].sample_size` is `null` with its blocker named beside it, in `P-M6-09`'s `suppressed` idiom: a body with no field reads as a ratio that never had a sample size. **And `sales_paused` cannot carry the three-state distinction**: `state` has four values, `sales_paused` is `state = 'paused'`, so `false` covers `armed` AND `insufficient_data` and a reader cannot tell *"the breaker is watching and content"* from *"the breaker has no opinion"*, which is precisely `GS-113`'s difference. Both repairs are a field on `LiabilityResponse.per_plan`, which is `admin-reads.ts`'s type and `P7-b`'s file. **The gap is pinned by a test that goes red the day the field lands.**

**A THIRD ABSENCE IS REPORTED AND IT IS A TEST THAT NOW SAYS SOMETHING FALSE BY IMPLICATION.** [`admin-reads.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/admin-reads.test.ts) pins an unserved list, *"a register of contract rows nobody has built"*, and it is **STILL GREEN** after this slice, because it derives `served` from `ADMIN_READ_ENDPOINTS` rather than from `CompositionReport`. `/admin/cusum` and `/admin/loss-ratios` are now SERVED, by another module, and that register cannot see it. **The file is not this slice's fence and no gate caught this**; the repair is to derive `served` from the composition report, which is the measurement `ADR-166` itself used.

**THE BARREL BIT EXACTLY AS THE DISPATCH WARNED, AND THE CONTROL IS NOW MECHANICAL.** [P7 section 9](plans/P7-risk-and-abuse.md) calls `apps/worker/src/index.ts` the phase's largest collision. Deleting BOTH re-export blocks sourced from `detectors/graph.ts`, which is what a keep-both merge produced, leaves **`pnpm run typecheck` at ZERO ERRORS**: a type checker cannot see an export that is simply gone. One assertion catches it, and it is in this slice's own suite: the barrel's leg list, **17 modules**, enumerated and asserted.

**A LATENT DEFECT IN [`db.test.ts`](../apps/worker/test/db.test.ts) WAS FOUND BY WALKING INTO IT.** Its bare-specifier scan matches `from '...'` across a WRAPPED string literal, so an error message whose line ends with the word *"from"* is read as an import of whatever the next line opens with, and it reported `" +\n        "` as a package this deployable imports. [`admin-reads.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/admin-reads.test.ts) documents that exact hazard for its own scan and anchors against it; this one does not. **The message was reworded rather than the scan widened**, because the scan is `P7-a`'s file.

**HALF OF [CRON_INVENTORY](ops/runbooks/CRON_INVENTORY.md)'s NUMBERED FINDING IS CLOSED AND THE ROW SAYS WHICH HALF.** That finding names TWO daily recomputations with no scheduled row, `plan_breaker_state` and `otp_send_budget`, and only the first is this fence's. The new row asserts the QUERY and not the job, on the three rows above it, and it records that **the exemption for `plan_breaker_state.override_expires_at` rests on this job and on nothing else**: an override *"lapses by being recomputed rather than by being released"*, so a stalled evaluation converts a dated override into an indefinite one. **`insufficient_data` must never be alarmed as a failure of the job**, because an alarm on it teaches an operator to override the state that exists to prevent an override.

**Fifteen defects seeded and fifteen caught**, including the named `INV-M5-12` seed in both its forms, the ladder reversed, the payout count in `sample_size`, `min_sample` dropped from the row, the sample size dropped from the alert, the ratio computed as a float, a CUSUM alarm reaching the state, `OQ-M6-02` quietly answered, the CUSUM passed through on the wire, `sales_paused` derived rather than carried, a gap field named `blocked_on` (which turns every 200 into a 500, and is why the name moved rather than the sweep), and both graph legs lost from the barrel.

## The flags queue acquires a data source, and its ordering is one the route refuses (2026-08-28, `P7-i`)

**[`apps/api/src/admin-source/flags.ts`](../apps/api/src/admin-source/flags.ts), [`graph.ts`](../apps/api/src/admin-source/graph.ts) and [`index.ts`](../apps/api/src/admin-source/index.ts) build [P7](plans/P7-risk-and-abuse.md) section 8's `P7-i`.** `AdminReadSource.listFlags` and `readIdentityGraph` have an adapter. Two of the port's six methods, and the other four are named rather than counted.

**`GS-120` IS ASSERTED DIRECTLY AND THE FIXTURE GIVES THE NOISE BOTH OF THE WRONG KEYS.** Fifty D-01 clusters at severity 3 lose to one identity carrying three flags across three families at severity 2. So an ordering by raw flag count fails the case, and so does an ordering by severity, which is the difference between asserting `AS-M7-03` and passing a weaker test that three implementations would satisfy.

**INDEPENDENCE IS THE INPUT AND NOT THE DETECTOR, AND THAT HALF IS ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE.** `M07` section 3.2 gives every detector an Input and [`detectors/canary.ts:122`](../apps/worker/src/detectors/canary.ts) already read that column as the family boundary. **D-01, D-04 and D-05 all read `fills` and write three DIFFERENT `flag_type`s** (`copy_cluster`, `news_window`, `martingale`), so one family per detector, or one family per `flag_type`, scores one poisoned stream at **depth 3** and hands the queue to the adversary who manufactured it. Both readings are seeded and both turn red. **No detector contributes more than one family, ever**, and an unknown detector is its OWN family: fifty flags from an unclassified detector is still depth 1, and a new detector agreeing with two known ones still reads depth 3.

**DEPTH COUNTS `open` AND `investigating` ONLY, AND THE BAND IS BORROWED RATHER THAN MINTED.** It is the set `G-HOLD-REQUIRED` reads under [ADR-040](decisions/ADR-040.md). A dismissed flag is a detector an operator already judged wrong, and counting it would let an adversary manufacture a hundred clusters, have them dismissed one at a time, and **bank every dismissal as permanent corroboration**.

**THE FINDING NEEDS A FOUNDER RULING AND NO NUMBER WAS TAKEN FOR IT: two approved documents state two different sorts for one queue.** [API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) section 8 says *"Sorted by severity then age"*, `risk_flags_queue_idx` is built for it, and [`admin-reads.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/admin-reads.ts)'s `assertFlagOrder` **throws** when severity is not monotonically non-increasing across the page. `AS-M7-03` clause 3 says independent detector families implicated on the identity. **A corroboration page inverts severity BY CONSTRUCTION**, so that assertion refuses this adapter on every page where the control does any work. This slice built `AS-M7-03`'s ordering, because that is the half that is a control rather than a convention; it did not edit `admin-reads.ts`, which is `P7-b`'s file; and it made the collision **mechanical**, reading both sentences out of their own documents and asserting the inversion as a fact. **Nothing 500s today**, because nothing wires a partial port, so this is a blocker ON the wiring rather than a defect IN a deployment. **A reconciliation exists and was deliberately not taken**: the two sentences agree if the queue is a queue of IDENTITIES ordered by corroboration and the contract's sort is the order WITHIN one identity, which is exactly this adapter's second and third keys. Whether that is what the contract means is an ADR. **[CORRECTED BY [ADR-178](decisions/ADR-178.md) SECTION 1 FINDING 7, 2026-08-28, and left standing beside the correction rather than overwritten.]** That reconciliation is NOT what the adapter builds. `compareRanked` compares `corroboration.depth` and never `identityId`, so two identities at the SAME depth interleave by severity: the band is a DEPTH, not an identity. `ADR-178` ruled the collision, `AS-M7-03` clause 3 keeps the first key unamended, `API_CONTRACT` section 8 is amended in place to scope its "severity then age" to the order WITHIN one corroboration band, and `FlagListItem` gained `corroboration_depth` because `assertFlagOrder` cannot check a key it cannot see.

**`admin-reads.ts`'s STATED REASON FOR THE BLOCK IS NARROWED AND NOT RETIRED.** It reads *"WHAT IS MISSING IS NOT AN AUTHORITY, IT IS A SHAPE ... There is no join and no aggregate to reach for"*. For these two methods that is **measured false**: the join is `rowAt` per distinct run and a `Map`, the group-by is `rowsWhere` per identity and a `Map`, and the walk is two `rowsWhere` per identity and a breadth-first search. Neither reaches `sqlExecutor`. It **stands in full for `readLiability`**, and the remaining three methods are unwritten, so [`wiring.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/wiring.test.ts)'s entry is narrowed rather than retired. **That file is session 316's this wave and was not touched**; the triple stays `{declared: 21, wired: 6, blocked: 15}`, asserted in this slice's own suite rather than assumed.

**THE ONE THING `ADR-157` GENUINELY REFUSES IS GENUINELY REFUSED.** `withdrawable_cents` lives on `rule_states`, one row per account per trading day, so the current figure is a per-group maximum, which is a scalar aggregate. It is done in memory at the cost of reading every stored day of every account in the cluster, and the amplification is **reported** rather than left to be found. No `SqlExecutorReason` member, no `SystemReason` member, no cast past a key type, no `pg` import, and **no `@merit/db` import anywhere under `admin-source/`**, asserted by reading the import statements rather than the file text.

**THREE GRAPH RULINGS, EACH ARGUED FROM A PRIMARY SOURCE.** A suppressed edge is **SHOWN and NOT TRAVERSED**: `SD-M7-04` puts the dispute in front of the admin before they act, and `schema.ts` says a suppressed edge *"stops contributing to enforcement"*, which cluster membership IS, because the aggregate is what an operator reads before restricting a set of people. The node cap **REFUSES rather than truncates**, because a partial `aggregate` is wrong and looks right and `AS-M7-04` is that screen; no corpus number rules the bound and it is a parameter with the absence stated. And **two money figures that look like one sum are computed separately**: `nodes[].total_withdrawable_cents` is every account, `aggregate.open_liability_cents` is FUNDED accounts only (`0009_ledger.sql:168`, `P-M6-01`), and the suite asserts they differ on a fixture where an evaluation account carries a balance.

**THE COMPOSITION FILE IS BUILT SO A DROPPED LEG IS A COMPILE ERROR**, which is the answer to the keep-both merge that emptied `apps/worker/src/index.ts` and typechecked. `IMPLEMENTED_ADMIN_READS` names the methods as DATA and the return type is a `Pick` over it, so dropping a method from the object is a missing-property error and dropping a name from the array is an excess-property error: **neither half can be lost quietly and neither can be added alone.** Both directions are seeded and both are caught by `tsc`. `P7-j` adds three lines, all appends to sorted lists.

**EIGHTEEN DEFECTS SEEDED AND ALL EIGHTEEN CAUGHT, AND TWO WERE MISSES FIRST WITH THE REASON RECORDED RATHER THAN COUNTED AS A PASS.** The filtered-page seed passed because the fixture's flag ids broke the tie in the right order for the wrong reason; the ids were renamed so only an implementation reading the rows the filter hid can pass. The local-clock seed passed because CI and this container both run at `TZ=UTC`, where `getFullYear` and `getUTCFullYear` agree, so that property is now asserted at the source instead. **And the suite found a defect in ITSELF**: `GraphFixture` was a plain `interface`, carried no index signature, and **fifteen `tsc` errors sat under a fully green `vitest run`**, because vitest transpiles and does not type-check. The first seed run reported every defect as caught by typecheck and proved nothing; the table above is the honest second measurement.

**Measured with `pnpm install` first and each command separately: 33 of 33 gates, 13 of 13 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, `format:check` clean, 205 test files / 4,505 passed / 6 skipped, `falsify.mjs` exit 0 with the tree clean after it.** The baseline of 33 / 13 of 13 / 0 / 0 / clean / 204 files / 4,443 passed / 6 skipped was reproduced exactly on a branch sitting at `origin/main` before a line changed, and the whole of the movement is this session's one new suite and its 62 cases. **No ADR number, no migration number, no `packages/db` change, `src/db.ts`, `routes/admin-reads.ts`, `routes/admin-writes.ts` and `test/wiring.test.ts` read and NOT edited, and the write side gains no second refusal.**

## The chart of accounts is seeded, four kinds are ruled, and `firm_treasury` turns out to be contradicted rather than silent (2026-08-28, session 321)

**[ADR-177](decisions/ADR-177.md) lands, `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED, and `0052` IS TAKEN** as [`0052_chart_of_accounts.sql`](../packages/db/migrations/0052_chart_of_accounts.sql), `E2 READ: MONEY PATH`. **`ledger_accounts` is the table every posting in this system names and nothing had ever populated it**: 0 rows after `0001` through `0051` applied forward-only from empty. It now holds one, which is the first row it has ever held.

**[ADR-174](decisions/ADR-174.md)'s finding (C) is NOT one absence.** It is three different things wearing one label, and only two of them are silence.

**FOUR KINDS ARE RULED, each DERIVED from a posting the corpus already states**, read through [`posting.ts:235-236`](../packages/ledger/src/posting.ts)'s sign and not from prose about what an account is for. `fees_revenue` is `revenue`: `LT-01` CREDITS it as recognized revenue, while [ADR-067](decisions/ADR-067.md) and [`0038`](../packages/db/migrations/0038_account_adjustments.sql) DEBIT the same account and both say in terms that this *"reduces revenue"*, and [`checkout.ts:1671`](../apps/api/src/routes/checkout.ts) states the conclusion outright in shipped source. `trader_wallet` and `trader_withdrawable` are `liability`. **`promotional_credit` is `liability` DERIVED FROM AN ENFORCED CONSTRAINT rather than from prose**, through [`0038:420-425`](../packages/db/migrations/0038_account_adjustments.sql)'s sign table on a destination that file's own CHECK admits, described by its header as a posting that *"books a liability"*.

**THE OBLIGATION [ADR-174](decisions/ADR-174.md) LEFT TO THIS ENTRY IS DISCHARGED, AND THE DEFECT IS BIGGER THAN THAT ENTRY MEASURED.** It measured `LT-06` and `LT-07` moving `firm_treasury` by zero. **`LT-02` reads backwards too**, in the INTERNAL leg its fence excluded: `LT-02` debits `firm_treasury` at settlement, `LT-06` credits it at approval, `LT-07` debits it at settlement, and **all three read correctly as a `liability` and backwards as an `asset`**, while all five prose sites in the corpus call it the account where cash books. **The arithmetic is unanimous on one side and the prose is unanimous on the other**, so this is a defect in the corpus rather than a gap in it, and no literal written into a merged migration could be right about both halves. `psp_clearing` and `reserve` are refused for lack of a posting, and `reserve` also for lack of a reader, since `SD-M5-03` anchors that figure outside this ledger deliberately.

**THE CHECK ENDS IN `ELSE true` AND THAT IS THE RULING'S OTHER HALF.** The three refused codes fall through it, so the open question is stored in the schema where the next session cannot miss it, and [`chart-of-accounts-kinds.test.ts`](../packages/ledger/test/chart-of-accounts-kinds.test.ts) asserts the absence as well as the four kinds so a code cannot leave that list quietly.

**ONE ROW IS SEEDED AND ONE IS ALL A MIGRATION CAN SEED.** Four of the seven codes are firm-scoped and three are per identity; a migration has no identity to seed against, so the seedable set is the firm codes and only `fees_revenue` among them is settled.

**A DEFECT NOT IN THE DISPATCH BREAKS A CI GATE BY GOING QUIET.** [`probe_ledger_constraints.sql`](../scripts/db/probe_ledger_constraints.sql) seeded its own `fees_revenue` row under `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` with a pinned uuid. Once the seed exists that clause SKIPS the row, the uuid names nothing, and the `LEDGER-C1` block raises `LEDGER-C2` on a dangling account **instead of probing `LEDGER-C1` at all**, which is the constraint the file's own header calls the one that matters most. Repaired to READ the chart, and falsified in both directions: with the seed deleted the new guard fails the build by name, and with the C1 trigger DISABLEd the probe still reports `PROBE FAILED`.

**[ADR-174](decisions/ADR-174.md) SECTION 7's THREE ARMED ASSERTIONS ALL FIRED**, which is exactly what they were armed for, and they are updated to assert the answer rather than deleted. `LT_07_FINDINGS` finding C had gone stale in precisely the half this entry answered.

**THE APPEND-ONLY GRANTS GATE REFUSED A WIDENING AND THE REFUSAL IS RECORDED RATHER THAN ROUTED AROUND.** `merit_app` holds `UPDATE` and `DELETE` on `ledger_accounts` and nothing in the application writes the table at all, so `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE` would cost nothing today and is what four other migrations did on their own tables. It would also make the table append-only by [`assert_append_only_grants.mjs`](../scripts/db/assert_append_only_grants.mjs)'s own definition and so requires amending a FROZEN document. **It is left undone and named**, and **nothing creates a ledger account for an identity at any point**, so the money path stays blocked on an absence this seed does not touch.

**Twenty-two defects seeded and all twenty-two caught, and TWO WERE MISSES FIRST with the reason recorded rather than counted as a pass.** Both have one cause: `0052`'s header argues its ruling at length and quotes its own SQL while doing so, so two separate files read the argument as a statement, one slicing an **empty string that satisfied every loop over it** and one counting two INSERTs where there is one. The empty slice is the dangerous shape because it is green, and it is now a thrown error. **Five further perturbations were seeded to be ACCEPTED and all five were**, which is the hole watched rather than asserted.

**Measured with `pnpm install` first and each command separately: 33 of 33 gates, 14 of 14 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, `format:check` clean, 209 test files / 4,773 passed / 6 skipped, `falsify.mjs` exit 0 with the tree clean after it.** The baseline of 33 / 14 of 14 / 0 / 0 / clean / 208 files / 4,764 passed / 6 skipped was reproduced exactly before a line changed. **`0009`, `0027` and `0038` are byte for byte unchanged, no document is amended, the vocabulary stays closed at seven, no `SystemReason` or `SqlExecutorReason` member is added, and `apps/api/test/wiring.test.ts`'s `{declared, wired, blocked}` triple does not move.**

## `RI-15` lands, and `apps/admin` is the fourth no-server app the register counts three (2026-08-28, session 324)

**[`RI-15`](../packages/tooling/checks/repo-invariants.mjs) IS THE LOCATION HALF OF THE ERROR CLASS [`RI-14`](../packages/tooling/checks/repo-invariants.mjs) READS THE EXISTENCE HALF OF.** `RI-14` settles whether a claim that a named thing does not exist is right, by asking the tree what it exports. It does not read WHERE, and where is what went wrong next: [session 316](sessions/2026-08-28-session-316.md) found **four false line citations** in [`wiring.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/wiring.test.ts), two of them eighteen lines off inside the entry [ADR-172](decisions/ADR-172.md) had written one session earlier to replace a false reason. **The claims held at their real lines and the pointers did not**, which is why nothing failed.

**THREE THINGS ARE ASSERTED AND THE THIRD IS THE ONE THAT NEEDED AN ARGUMENT.** The path resolves to a file in this tree; the file reaches the line; and where the pointer is preceded by a backticked name with nothing but glue between them, that name appears **within two lines** of the line cited, matched case-insensitively. It does not try to read meaning. The proxy is the shape these citations are actually written in: a backticked name, then the pointer.

**THE WINDOW IS TWO AND IT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN CHOSEN.** The widest TRUE citation over the files it reads is one line off, and the narrowest FALSE one on record is three (`admin-writes.ts:266` for a declaration at `:269`). **Two is the largest window that still catches every false citation on record and the smallest that admits every true one**, and the price is stated rather than discovered: a drift of one or two lines passes.

**WATCHED FAILING ON THE REAL HISTORICAL DEFECT, ON THE REAL TREE, AND ONE SEED WAS NOT CAUGHT.** All four false citations of 2026-08-28 were restored into `wiring.test.ts`: `admin-payouts.ts:381`, `admin-writes.ts:266` and `gateNoInFlight`'s `:1233` all fire, at four sites, and **`wallet-withdrawals.ts:1506` does not**, because its sentence reads *"the identity arm this route presents"* and names nothing a runner can look up. That hole is asserted by a case of its own and named in the check's `covers` line. The tree was restored byte for byte and `git status` proved it. **The deliberately quoted history in the corrected entry does not fire either**, so a file that keeps its own false sentence for the next reader to check is not punished for it.

**THE FIRST DRAFT WAS ARMED FOR 215 LINES AND DISARMED FOR THE REST, AND IT REPORTED PASS.** It paired backticks from the start of the file, and `wiring.test.ts:215` uses a backtick as an APOSTROPHE, which inverts every pairing after it: all three restored copies of the historical defect went quiet. It now reads the two backticks immediately before the pointer. **It was found only because the seeds were run on the real tree**: a synthetic fixture nobody wrote an apostrophe into has even parity, so a suite built first and run against fixtures only would have reported twelve green cases over a check that could not see the thing it was written for.

**THE CHECK FOUND THREE FALSE CITATIONS ON `main` ON ITS FIRST RUN, WHICH MAKES THIS THE SIXTH APPEARANCE OF THE CLASS, AND TWO OF THE THREE WERE FALSE THE DAY THEY WERE WRITTEN.** [`routes/payouts.ts:84`](../apps/api/src/routes/payouts.ts) cited `sweeps/ports.ts:226` for `ExpiryLedgerPort`, which is at `:229`, and `:87` cited `admin-payouts.ts:1179` for `AdminPayoutTx.ledger`, whose release arm posts at `:1192`. Both were checked at `e04202a`, the commit that wrote them, and both were already wrong there. **Both are corrected here.** A reviewer who assumes this class is caused by files moving will look for the wrong cause on two of the three.

**THE THIRD IS A FIFTH FALSE CITATION IN `wiring.test.ts` AND IT IS NAMED RATHER THAN ENFORCED.** `wiring.test.ts:168` cites `routes/admin-wallet.ts:538` for `principal(request)`, which is declared at `:601`. **It was TRUE when written**: `563ac3d` wrote it against a tree where `principal` was on `:538` and `224fe5b` then inserted sixty-three lines above it. Session 322 owns that file this wave, so the pointer is not repaired here. Dropping the file from the list to get green would blind the check to the one file it exists for and widening the window to sixty-three lines would blind it everywhere, so `CITATIONS_OWNED_ELSEWHERE` carries **one entry keyed on file, pointer and name together**: it covers that citation and no other, and it matches nothing the moment the pointer is corrected. **Whoever owns that file next repoints it to `:601` and deletes the entry.**

**`docs/decisions` IS DELIBERATELY NOT AN INPUT AND THE REASON IS THE DOCUMENTS RATHER THAN THE NOISE.** An ADR is a dated record of the tree as it was: its citations were true at its date, they go stale by design when the tree moves, and repairing one is an amendment requiring an ADR rather than a commit. `ADR-172`'s `routes/payouts.ts:395` for `PayoutTx.ledger` is 324 lines out today **because [ADR-176](decisions/ADR-176.md) deleted that member**, which is the entry being right rather than wrong. The two findings the check does make over `ADR-170` through `ADR-176` are both it misreading a document written for a reader: a RANGE naming members whose declaring line sits above the range, and a bare pointer whose path is two markdown table rows up. Both are stated as limitations in the `covers` line.

**`apps/admin` IS THE FOURTH NO-SERVER APP AND THE REGISTER AT `:5340` COUNTS THREE.** That sentence reads *"This is the third instance of the same defect class in one day"* and names `apps/portal`'s view modules with no transport, `apps/site`'s route modules with no `app/` directory, and `apps/api`'s twenty declared setters against four called. **There is a fourth and it is not in that count.** Re-derived on 2026-08-28 rather than inherited: [`apps/admin`](../apps/admin) is **2,802 lines across nine `src/*.ts` files with 200 passing tests in eight suites**, its [manifest](../apps/admin/package.json) declares `typecheck` and `start` and **no `build` script**, and `grep -rnE "createServer|\.listen\(|node:http|fastify|express|Response|Request|fetch\("` over `apps/admin/src/` returns **nothing at all**. `main()` at [`index.ts:131`](../apps/admin/src/index.ts) prints *"merit admin: liability home read surface, no server yet"* and returns.

**THE FILE IS HONEST AND THE REGISTER IS NOT, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OF THE FINDING.** `index.ts:126` states it in its own words: *"there is no server here to receive a request carrying them"*, and it goes on to say that a `main` which invented inputs in order to print something would be the confidently wrong number `AS-M6-04` is about. Nothing in that deployable is hiding anything. What was missing is the entry in the place that tracks the class, which is what a register is for. **It matters beyond tidiness**: [ADR-171](decisions/ADR-171.md) refused the operator door because it waits on the admin identity provider, and **separately there is no server on this surface to put a door in**. Two blockers on one surface, one of them unwritten until now, and a plan that sizes the first without seeing the second sizes half the work. **No server was built here**: that is a phase plan's to size and not this session's.

**Measured with `pnpm install` first and each command separately: 33 of 33 gates, 15 of 15 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, `format:check` clean, 208 test files / 4,777 passed / 6 skipped, `falsify.mjs` exit 0 with the tree clean after it.** The baseline of 33 / 14 of 14 / 0 / 0 / clean / 208 files / 4,764 passed / 6 skipped was reproduced exactly on a branch sitting at `origin/main` before a line changed, and the whole of the test movement is this session's twelve added cases. **No ADR number and no migration number**, and `packages/ledger`, `packages/db`, `apps/api/src/routes/admin-reads.ts`, `apps/api/src/admin-source/` and `apps/worker/src/index.ts` are untouched. `wiring.test.ts` was READ, seeded, and restored byte for byte, and never edited.

## Two approved documents ordered one queue differently, and [ADR-178](decisions/ADR-178.md) keeps both by ordering them (2026-08-28, session 325)

**[ADR-178](decisions/ADR-178.md) LANDS, `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED.** [API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) section 8 said *"Sorted by severity then age"* and `assertFlagOrder` enforced that FLAT across the page; `AS-M7-03` clause 3 sorts by INDEPENDENT detector families implicated on an identity. A corroborated page inverts severity **by construction**, so the route refused the adapter `P7-i` built, on every page where the control did any work.

**THE RULING IS THAT BOTH SENTENCES ARE KEPT AND ORDERED.** `AS-M7-03` clause 3 takes the first key and **stands unamended**. `API_CONTRACT` section 8 is **AMENDED IN PLACE** ([ADR-065](decisions/ADR-065.md) T3, which `CI-06f` enforces): its severity-then-age is kept as the order **within one corroboration band**. **The ground is that a control outranks a convention** -- `AS-M7-03` names an attack, an adversary who needs no access to Merit, a failure mode and `GS-120`; section 8's sentence stated an order and no ground at all.

**AND THE CONTRACT'S STRONGEST GROUND IS MEASURED FALSE IN THIS TREE.** *"A client may already depend on the documented order"*: `grep` finds NO client of `/admin/flags` under `apps/admin`, `apps/portal` or `apps/site`, no file outside `apps/api` names `FlagListItem`, and `setAdminReadSource` is still `BLOCKED`, so the route answers 503 before this ruling and after it. **No page has ever been rendered in either order.** That is not why the ruling went this way, but it is why taking it costs close to nothing, and it will cost more every week.

**THE PRICE IS PAID ON THE WIRE, AND IT IS WHAT SEPARATES THIS FROM RULING FOR ONE DOCUMENT AND DELETING THE OTHER'S ENFORCEMENT.** `FlagListItem` gains `corroboration_depth`. Without it `assertFlagOrder` cannot check the key it is asserting, so the only honest move left at the boundary is to delete the assertion, which is weakening a gate to pass it; and an operator is shown a severity 3 above a severity 5 **with nothing on the row that explains it**, which is `AS-M7-03`'s own concern arriving from the other side. **The assertion went from two keys to three and now enforces the control it used to refuse.** A ruling that made the boundary check less would have lost.

## The two handlers ADR-170 specified and deliberately did not write (2026-08-28)

**[`apps/api/src/routes/verify.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/verify.ts) is `GET /verify/:code` and [`admin-certificates.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/admin-certificates.ts) is `POST /admin/certificates/:id/revoke`.** [ADR-170](decisions/ADR-170.md) foreclosure 9 admitted both rows into [API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) and built neither, saying *"the rows are the specification a later slice transcribes, and the `E2` read is owed on the handlers"*. **This is that slice, and the read is still owed.** No ADR number and no migration number was taken.

**THE RESPONSE UNION IS THREE WHERE THE LOG'S CHECK IS FOUR, AND THE COMPILER NOW PROVES THE CONTAINMENT RUNS ONE WAY.** `VERIFY_RESULTS` is declared `satisfies readonly VerificationResult[]`, so a response value `certificate_verifications` cannot record does not compile, while the table keeps `deferred` because a deferred lookup is somebody holding a token that was never issued and an unknown one is a typo. `ADR-040`'s rule is about a union advertising a value the table cannot hold; this is the opposite direction and is what an allowlist is for.

**THE CONSTANT-TIME MECHANISM IS A MEASURED FLOOR AND IT IS APPLIED TO EVERY RESPONSE THE HANDLER PRODUCES, THE 503 INCLUDED.** The `certificate_verifications` write is inside its budget, and an overrun is LOGGED rather than failed, because a p99 ceiling is exceeded roughly one request in a hundred by construction and a 500 on the tail would be a louder oracle than the one the floor closes. **`floor_ms` is bounded below and NOWHERE ABOVE**, and that is reported rather than filled: no approved document gives an upper bound and one invented here would be this route choosing a latency budget the corpus has not chosen.

**THE COPY TABLE IS VALIDATED IN FULL BEFORE THE LOOKUP, AND THAT IS A TIMING CONTROL RATHER THAN TIDINESS.** Read lazily on the branch that needs it, a deployment missing only the `account_enforced` sentence answers `unknown` in milliseconds and `valid` in an error, which is a hit-versus-miss oracle assembled out of the configuration error rather than out of the clock. **`INV-M11-03`'s wording is the one sentence fixed in code**, so no deployment can override it into "this is fake"; the other five and `INV-M11-04`'s disclosure are supplied, because `OQ-M11-02` is open and copy invented here would answer a legal and brand question in a string literal.

**`initiative` IS DERIVED FROM `revocation_class` AND A REQUEST THAT SUPPLIES IT IS REFUSED RATHER THAN IGNORED**, because an operator who sent it believes they set it. `INITIATIVE_BY_CLASS` is typed total over `certificates.revocation_class`'s four members, and `admin_actions_on_behalf_matches_initiative` is satisfied by construction on every one of them rather than by asking the database to refuse.

**TWO FINDINGS CAME OUT OF SEEDS THAT FAILED, AND BOTH ARE PRE-EXISTING AND TREE WIDE.** A `:code` over 100 characters answers **414 in Fastify's own shape**: `application/json`, an `FST_ERR_MAX_PARAM_LENGTH` code section 2 does not define, and **the request path echoed back**. Fastify's `maxParamLength` defaults to 100 and [`server.ts`](../apps/api/src/server.ts) does not set it, so it reproduces identically on `GET /certificates/:code/image.png` and `GET /accounts/:accountId/purchases`. It is a **length oracle ahead of the floor**, which is the half of `INV-M11-05` `ADR-170` foreclosure 3 refuses a shape check to protect, and it escapes the closed status table `server.ts`' own header says exists to prevent exactly this. **Not repaired: the fix is a Fastify option in a shared file or a ruling on what a long path parameter answers.** Second, a `:code` of `..` is normalized by the router to a traversal and answers the router's 404, which is contract shaped and discloses nothing, since a code that is not routable is a code that was never issued.

**THE DISPATCH'S ROUTE COUNT DID NOT REPRODUCE AND THE CENTRAL CLAIM DID.** It said 69 registered; the composition report over both surfaces says **70** distinct `METHOD /path`, which is 45 public plus 26 operator less the liveness probe both serve. Neither of the two rows was registered by anything, exactly as stated. The count is now 72.

**BOTH PORTS ARE BLOCKED, NO ADAPTER IS WRITTEN, AND EACH ENTRY NAMES WHICH ARM HAS A DOOR.** `VerifySource.record` is writable through `db.firm` today, because `certificate_verifications` is scope class `firm`; `lookup` reaches neither door, because the row is read unauthenticated and `certificates` is `owned`. **A backend with one live arm and one that rejects is refused on `usePayoutBackend`'s stated rule.** The revoke carries its own obstruction and it is a CIRCULARITY rather than a missing door: `db.scoped` needs an identity that is a column of the row the door would be opened to read. [`wiring.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/wiring.test.ts)'s triple moves **`{21, 6, 15}` to `{23, 6, 17}`**.

**ONE ASSERTION EXPIRED AND WAS RESTATED RATHER THAN DELETED.** `certificates.test.ts` held that nothing registers `/verify/`, which was right when `ADR-168` wrote it and which `ADR-170` then made false by defining the row. **The clause was not weakened to pass**: its purpose was that no verify row arrive in this deployable without a ruling behind it, and it did that job. It now reads over the MODULE, which is the comparison `ADR-153` section 4 names and which does not go stale on the next entry that lands a row.

## The two digests the plan row names acquire producers, and the alarm is the parameter list rather than the comment (2026-08-28, `P7-l`, session 323)

**[`apps/worker/src/digests/`](../apps/worker/src/digests/ports.ts) is [P7](plans/P7-risk-and-abuse.md) section 8's `P7-l`.** [`0040`](../packages/db/migrations/0040_report_schedules.sql) landed `report_schedules` and `report_deliveries` with **zero rows on merge, deliberately**, "so nothing below can be read as evidence that any digest has ever been delivered". `weekly_loss_ratio_cusum` and `weekly_flag_queue` have producers now, and so does the dead-man switch that watches them.

**`CRON_INVENTORY:35`'s RULE IS A PROPERTY OF A PARAMETER LIST AND NOT A COMMENT.** The alarm asserts the QUERY and never the job's own report, and that is enforced in three places rather than asserted in one: `DigestAlarmIo` carries a transaction and a clock and **nothing a producer could hand it**, so "the run said it worked" is not a value it can be given; [`alarm.ts`](../apps/worker/src/digests/alarm.ts) **imports nothing from `produce.ts`** and the suite reads its source as text, because a type checker cannot see a coupling that is only a call; and the handle the alarm receives **has no `insert`**, so an alarm cannot discharge the window it is complaining about. A job that crashed after writing "success" and a job that never ran are the same fact to the person who did not get the digest, and here they are the same input, because neither is an input at all.

**`GS-288` IS ASSERTED IN THREE SHAPES, BECAUSE THE THREE WAYS A REPORT CAN BE A LIE ARE THREE DIFFERENT FIXTURES.** The named case is `5.1`: the transport succeeds, the producer builds a valid `delivered` row, the insert is swallowed, the run reports **`delivered: 1`**, the table holds **nothing**, and the alarm fires. `5.3` is the run that writes `failed` while a summary would say served, and `5.4` is the job that simply stops after a healthy history. Each is read from `report_deliveries` and none of them consults a run report, because none of them can.

**THE ANCHOR IS UNSTATED AND NO NUMBER WAS INVENTED FOR IT, SO THE CLOCK IS EACH SCHEDULE'S OWN HISTORY.** The CADENCE is a schema fact (`0040`'s generated column, transcribed arm for arm and **confirmed against PostgreSQL 16 for all four digests**). **WHICH weekday, at WHICH hour, in WHICH zone a window closes is stated nowhere**: [CRON_INVENTORY](ops/runbooks/CRON_INVENTORY.md)'s Expected-by cell reads *"the schedule's own window"*, [M06](plans/M06-admin-ops-console.md) section 3.6 names no time, and [WEEKLY_RISK_RITUAL](ops/runbooks/WEEKLY_RISK_RITUAL.md) says *"same time every week"* without saying which. So `DIGEST_WINDOW_ANCHOR` ships **every term `unstated`** with its citation, and the alarm measures elapsed time from a stored instant instead. **What that costs is stated rather than discovered**: it cannot say *"the Monday 09:00 window closed"*, it says *"a full cadence period has passed since the newest window this schedule has any record of"*, which is the same fact reported up to one period late. **The alternative was to invent a weekday**, and an alarm firing against a window nobody agreed to is `GS-287`'s failure with the sign flipped: the manufactured evidence would be against the operator who did deliver.

**`CADENCE_PERIOD_MS.monthly` IS `null` AND A MONTHLY SCHEDULE IS REPORTED AS `cadence_unanchored` RATHER THAN PASSED OVER.** A month has no fixed length and no day-of-month anchor is stated, so the half of the alarm that needs a period says it cannot run; the half that needs none still runs on that schedule. **A 30-day constant would have been a number this slice invented.**

**THE `P7-l` ROW CALLS THESE "the two MUST digests" AND BOTH APPROVED SOURCES DISAGREE.** [M06](plans/M06-admin-ops-console.md) section 3.6's sizing table makes the **daily liability** digest and the **weekly loss ratio and CUSUM** digest the two MUSTs ("They are the C8 ritual's input") and the **flag queue summary** a **SHOULD** ("useful and nothing depends on them"); [ADR-066](decisions/ADR-066.md) section 3 says the same in the same words. So one of the two built here is a MUST and the other is a SHOULD, and **the MUST with no producer is `daily_liability`**, whose content is `P-M6-01`, `P-M6-03` and `P-M6-07`'s reserve coverage ratio and therefore waits on `AdminReadSource.readLiability`, which is `P5-l`'s. **Recorded in the code beside `PRODUCED_DIGESTS` and not repaired.**

**A DIGEST WITH NO PRODUCER GETS NO ROW, WHICH IS `0040`'s OWN DESIGN AND NOT A GAP.** There is deliberately no `skipped` outcome: *"A run that decides not to send writes `failed` with its reason, or it writes nothing and the missing row is itself the finding. Both roads reach a human."* Writing `failed` for a digest nobody has built yet would put a delivery failure in the log for a delivery never attempted, so an enabled `daily_liability` schedule is skipped, counted in the run report, and **reported by the alarm**.

**`GS-290` IS ENFORCED TWICE AND THE SECOND IS THE ONE A FUTURE CALL SITE NEEDS.** `decideOutcome` **downgrades** a send that reached nobody to `failed` whatever the transport claimed, and `deliveryValues` **refuses to build** a `delivered` row with an empty `recipients_attempted` at all. All eleven of `0040`'s `report_deliveries` `CHECK`s are mirrored in TypeScript by name, and **every one of them was watched firing in PostgreSQL 16 in this session**, including the documented surprise that a fifth digest is refused by `cadence`'s `NOT NULL` rather than by `digest`'s own `CHECK`.

**`INV-M6-10` IS SWEPT OVER THE RENDERED ARTIFACT AND NOT ONLY OVER THE TYPE**, because a type says nothing about what a producer put in a string. The flag-queue digest carries **counts and links**, and **the link is to the QUEUE and never to a subject**, which is a reading stated rather than assumed: *"counts and links"* is ambiguous about what a link points at, and a link to `/admin/identities/<uuid>` carries an identifier into an inbox, which is exactly the bulk export this feature was admitted on the promise of not being.

**THE BARREL'S LEGS ARE NOW DATA AND A SEEDED DEFECT PROVED MODULE GRANULARITY IS NOT ENOUGH.** `WORKER_BARREL_LEGS` plus two companion lists make the sweep over `src/` **total**, so a module that is neither a leg, nor behind one, nor deliberately absent fails. **But deleting ONE of a module's two export blocks left the module still a specifier, left `9.1` green and left `pnpm run typecheck` at zero errors**; the 2026-08-28 merge deleted both sides of a hunk and one side is the cheaper accident. `9.4` now reads each of this slice's four modules for its top-level exports and asserts the barrel re-exports **every name**. **Writing the lists found [`batch/statistics.ts`](../apps/worker/src/batch/statistics.ts), which this barrel has never re-exported**; recorded with its reason, not repaired.

**TWENTY-ONE DEFECTS SEEDED AND ALL TWENTY-ONE CAUGHT, AND TWO WERE MISSES FIRST WITH THE FIX RECORDED RATHER THAN THE MISS COUNTED AS A PASS.** The dropped-export-block seed is above. The second: deleting the alarm's re-read of `enabled` changed nothing while the fake honoured the filter it was given, so `4.13` now hands the alarm an adapter that **ignores the filter entirely**, because a filter is a promise about a read rather than a property of the row that came back. **AND THE SUITE FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN THIS SESSION'S OWN CODE**: `report_deliveries_failure_states_its_reason` was written with one negation too many, so every well-formed `delivered` row was refused and every `failed` row accepted; repaired and pinned in both directions.

**TWO FENCE NOTES, BOTH REPORTED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE FOUND.** [`apps/worker/test/breaker.test.ts`](../apps/worker/test/breaker.test.ts) carries a hand-written barrel-leg count that **any** barrel-editing slice invalidates; corrected minimally, 17 to 21, with the reason for the data list left beside it, on the ground that shipping a red suite is worse and that file belongs to a session that has already merged. And **session 320's reported defect in [`db.test.ts`](../apps/worker/test/db.test.ts) bit again**: its bare-specifier scan reads a wrapped message ending in the word *"from"* as an import, one of this session's own comment strings ended a segment that way, and it was reworded inside this fence with a note beside it. **The regex is still wrong and is still nobody's.**

**No ADR number, no migration number, no `packages/db` change, no contract change, no `SqlExecutorReason` member, no `SystemReason` member, no `pg` import and no cast past a key type.** `apps/api` is untouched, so `wiring.test.ts`'s `{declared, wired, blocked}` triple does not move.

**Measured with `pnpm install` first and each command run separately: 33 of 33 gates, 14 of 14 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, `format:check` clean, 209 test files / 4,837 passed / 6 skipped, `falsify.mjs` clean.** The `main` baseline of 33 / 14 / 0 / 0 / clean / **208 files / 4,764 passed / 6 skipped** was reproduced exactly before a line changed.
