## The redaction vocabulary is closed at two, and it was open at exactly one line rather than at a call site (2026-08-28, `ADR-179`, session 327)

**[ADR-179](decisions/ADR-179.md) LANDS, `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED. `evidence_packs.redaction_profile` IS A CLOSED SET OF TWO: `full-detail` and `trader-facts-only`**, in the shape [`scoped-db.ts:197`](../packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts)'s `SystemReason` and [`:1695`](../packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts)'s `SqlExecutorReason` already have, which is a union DECLARED in one place, a source-reading case that says how many members it has, and a widening that is therefore a diff on a test which says why the set is closed. **The ground is that this column is the RECORD OF A PROMISE and not an input to one**: [M06:301](plans/M06-admin-ops-console.md) makes the row the answer to a later argument about what was disclosed, and a free-text label lets two exports that performed the same redaction be labelled differently and lets one row name a redaction **no code in this tree performs**.

**THE OPENNESS WAS NOT WHERE THE ALLOCATION ROW SAID IT WAS, AND THAT IS THE FINDING THIS ENTRY WOULD KEEP IF IT KEPT ONE.** The row described *"a redaction profile somebody invents at a call site"*. Measured in the tree, no call site could: `EvidenceRedactionProfile` was DERIVED from the audience map, so at every call site it was exactly the two values and a third string was already a type error. **It was open at exactly one line, and that line is the line a vocabulary change is made on.** `regulator: 'regulator-detail'` written into the map type-checked **exit 0**, because a derived vocabulary cannot refuse a member: it is whatever its map says, a map wearing a type's clothes. It is now `TS2322` twice, naming the type at the map and at `redactionProfileFor`'s return.

**THE MAPPING AND THE VOCABULARY ARE NOW SEPARATE THINGS AND THAT SEPARATION IS THE WHOLE OF THE CODE CHANGE.** `OQ-F4-03` may yet give `regulator` its own profile, and it is counsel's rather than the founder's ([ADR-068](decisions/ADR-068.md) section 3). Under the derived shape that legitimate MAPPING ruling was a one-line edit that turned red two assertions which are ABOUT THE MAPPING and read as *"update me"* to a session whose ruling is about the mapping, so **the vocabulary would have grown as a side effect nobody argued for**. **NO PARALLEL ARRAY OF THE NAMES IS DECLARED**, on [ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md)'s `DDL_NAMES` landmine that an array typed `readonly T[]` catches an extra member and never a missing one; totality is asserted between the declaration and its one consumer, in both directions.

**EACH MEMBER'S PROMISE IS WRITTEN PER MEMBER, AND THE PROMISE IS THE UNION OF THREE APPROVED STATEMENTS RATHER THAN THE SHORTEST OF THEM.** [M06:485](plans/M06-admin-ops-console.md)'s `GS-112` names five positives and three negatives; [M06:299](plans/M06-admin-ops-console.md) and [EC-071](edge-cases/EC-071.md) name six and four, adding **the computation trace** and **"no comparison against a population"**, and the [wave 3 batch 1 gate closure](decisions/gates/wave-3-batch-1-gate-closure-2026-08-14.md) puts population comparisons at internal and counsel tier with the thresholds. `trader-facts-only` strips four things by four mechanisms and the four negatives map onto them one for one: no detector parameter is the computed sweep and the absent `detectors` section, no threshold is the sweep because **a threshold is a threshold by the NAME it arrives under**, no other identity is the uuid scan, and **no population comparison is the ALLOWLIST**, because such a comparison can only arrive through the `evidence` bag or a `detectors` section and the projection admits neither. `full-detail` strips nothing and **bounds the DETAIL and never the SCOPE**, which is the half its name does not say and the half a reader is likeliest to get wrong.

**TWO SEEDS WERE MISSES AGAINST THE 155 CASES THAT EXISTED, AND THEY ARE WHY THE PROMISE IS ASSERTED AS A SET.** Adding `'detector'` or `'detector_version'` to `TRADER_FLAG_FIELDS` ships the name of the machinery that found a flag into a trader pack, which [ADR-022](decisions/ADR-022.md) puts at internal tier always, **and every one of the 155 passed**. Neither is a registry parameter name, so the computed strip list does not reach them; neither carries a distinctive value the threshold cases search for; and the positives and the negatives were each asserted **one field at a time**, so nothing anywhere said the carried set was EXACTLY the promise. **One-at-a-time assertions do not add up to a set.** Both were re-seeded after the new cases existed and both are caught. **Ten seeds, all ten caught**, including the anchored uuid match `P7-j` repaired, watched deliberately because this ruling is written around that assertion and must not weaken it.

**NO MIGRATION AND NO MIGRATION NUMBER, AND THE CLOSURE'S LIMIT IS STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE FOUND: IT HOLDS AT THE LAYER THAT COMPOSES THE VALUE AND NOT AT THE LAYER THAT STORES IT.** [`0008_risk.sql:257`](../packages/db/migrations/0008_risk.sql) is `text NOT NULL` with no `CHECK` while `audience` beside it at [`:254`](../packages/db/migrations/0008_risk.sql) has one, and [`schema.ts:1836`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts) types the column `text`. **The DDL for both constraints is written out in the entry** for whoever takes the number, the second of them making "the profile follows from the audience" a database rule and being the one worth arguing about, since the mapping is the half most likely to move. `ADD CONSTRAINT` is safe today for a measured reason that will expire: the writer is a port nothing implements and **no `evidence_packs` row has ever been written**.

**THREE THINGS ARE REPORTED AND NOT BUILT.** The **computation trace** is in M06's and EC-071's positive list and not in `GS-112`'s own line; `grep` for `computation_trace` over `packages/` and `apps/` returns nothing, because [M01:772](plans/M01-rules-engine.md) makes a trace a REPLAY through `advanceDay` rather than a column, so the pack carries the trace's INPUTS and the gap is named rather than closed. **The free-text channel is closed for one negative and not for the others**: a uuid inside `tos_clause` has a shape a runner can match and a population comparison written in prose does not. And `evidence.pack_exported` still carries `redaction_profile` and is still not emitted, the catalogue being outside this fence as it was outside `P7-j`'s.

**`INV-M7-10`'s COMPUTED STRIP LIST IS NOT REOPENED and nothing in the mechanism moved.** `apps/api/src/admin-source/index.ts` NOT touched, so no leg of its two keep-both defences was disturbed; `wiring.test.ts` NOT touched and its `{declared, wired, blocked}` triple unmoved; no `SystemReason` member, no `SqlExecutorReason` member, no `pg` import, no cast past a key type, `packages/db` untouched and `0008_risk.sql` byte for byte unchanged. **No admin host anywhere** ([ADR-012](decisions/ADR-012.md)).

**Each command run separately and `pnpm run verify` never run: 33 of 33 gates, 15 of 15 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, `format:check` clean, 212 test files / 4,991 passed / 6 skipped, `falsify.mjs` clean with the tree clean after it.** The `main` baseline was reproduced exactly first and read 33 / 15 / 0 / 0 / clean / 212 files / 4,981 passed / 6 skipped, so the count moves by ten and **every one of the ten is a new case**: no case was deleted and none was weakened.

## `P7` closes: the Loops lifecycle contract set, and the answer to "what are we sending Loops" is NOTHING, with twelve rows saying who owes the declaration (2026-08-28, `P7-m`, session 328)

**[`apps/worker/src/integrations/loops.ts`](../apps/worker/src/integrations/loops.ts) is [P7](plans/P7-risk-and-abuse.md) section 8's `P7-m`, the last unbuilt slice in the phase.** `IN-M10-03`'s outbound lifecycle events through `integration_contracts`' declared field allowlist. **`IN-M10-01` Chatwoot and `IN-M10-02` Metabase were not built and neither is a file in this tree**, exactly as the row says: `DEP-M10-06` is a column-filtered replica and a `SELECT`-only role, and `AS-M10-02`'s strong control is a nightly reconciliation against [M12](plans/M12-transparency-platform.md)'s published definitions, which is a Metabase question. Nothing in this slice needed either.

**THE NAMED DEPENDENCY DID NOT LAND AND THE SLICE WAS BUILDABLE ANYWAY, WHICH IS THE FINDING WORTH CARRYING.** The row gives `P7-m` one dependency: *"`P5-b` for `events`, because a lifecycle dispatch reads the event it is dispatching."* **`P5-b` ran and REFUSED that table.** [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts)'s standing text: *"all five members of the vocabulary were tried against the shape and every one is either refused by a mechanical assertion or silently lossy ... WHAT THE TABLE NEEDS IS A SIXTH CLASS"*, and `P5-b` held no ADR number with which to add one. So there is no registered `events` to read, and reaching around the accessor is the one line `P7` section 11 rule 10 forecloses. **That bounds the slice rather than blocking it, because the allowlist is not a read**: a contract is a declaration about an event NAME and a FIELD NAME, both known without opening a row. The module takes the event as a VALUE, **imports nothing at all**, and the dispatcher that reads the table is owed by whichever session gets `events` a scope class.

**TWELVE TRIGGERS AND NOT NINE, AND THE COUNT IS THE SUITE'S SUBJECT RATHER THAN A FOOTNOTE.** [M10](plans/M10-integrations.md)`:31` and `:165` both say *"the nine [EVENTS section 11] triggers"* and that section carries **twelve**; [session 163](sessions/2026-08-24-session-163.md) found it and reported it rather than editing an `approved` plan. `M10:372` is why it matters: *"Every integration contract has a negative test asserting that a field absent from its allowlist is not transmitted, and the test is GENERATED FROM THE CONTRACT ROWS."* A nine-row table generates a correct-looking suite that never meets `payout.held`, `payout.hold_released` or `identity.restriction_lifted`, **all three of which the corpus marks "always send"**. The trigger list is transcribed from the document and the suite reads section 11 **as text**, so the cardinal `12` appears nowhere as a literal.

**NO FIELD LIST IN THIS SLICE IS THIS SESSION'S, SO ALL TWELVE SHIP `undeclared`, EMPTY AND DISABLED.** `M10:31` says the module carries *"the minimum payload each needs"* and **the corpus never says what that is for any of the twelve**. The payloads in `EVENTS` sections 4 through 8 are what the EVENT carries, which is the superset a contract exists to cut down; deriving twelve allowlists from them would be this session choosing what Merit discloses to a third party, by inference, in a file. This is `P7-k`'s disposition of `OQ-M6-02` on a different subject, and **`0018` already anticipated the state**: `integration_contracts_enabled_has_fields` reads `enabled = false OR array_length(field_allowlist, 1) >= 1`, so a disabled row with an empty allowlist is legal and an enabled empty one is not. The schema can hold *"declared as owed, not yet declared"* and cannot hold *"enabled and sending nothing"*. **No row carries `approved_by`, because no person approved one**, and a placeholder approver would put this session's name in the column whose whole job is to say who authorised a disclosure.

**THE SECOND LAYER IS WHAT SURVIVES THE FIRST BEING FILLED IN.** An empty allowlist is a control a later session retires by declaring one. `FORBIDDEN_FIELDS` is sourced, per event, and **outranks any allowlist**: `EVENTS:407` rules that `payout.held`'s message carries *"the fact, the clause and the date, never the evidence and never the detector"*, and `hold_flag_id` in that event's payload is the detector's flag and the evidence pointer at once. A contract that allowlists it is **REFUSED and not filtered**, because a silent drop would leave a contradictory row in the table looking approved. **`INV-M10-04` is deliberately NOT in that set**: it forbids *"no document, no biometric, no PAN, no full device fingerprint, and no raw IP"*, which are CLASSES, and no column in any of the twelve payloads is named as one. A column list inferred from those five words would be this session deciding which columns are biometrics.

**`guard_expression` CANNOT EXPRESS THE ONE GUARD THIS MODULE EXISTS TO ENFORCE, AND THAT IS REPORTED RATHER THAN REPAIRED.** [`0018`](../packages/db/migrations/0018_integrations.sql) declares the column as *"evaluated over the allowlisted fields only"*. `EVENTS:403` suppresses `breach.detected` *"if the identity is restricted or has an open severity 4+ flag"*, and `M10:232` has the dispatcher *"re-read restriction status, open flag severity, and account state immediately before the send"*. **None of those three is a field of `breach.detected`, whose payload carries no `identity_id` at all.** So the guards are a discriminated union in TypeScript, every row ships `guardExpression: null`, and the finding is asserted in the suite rather than left in prose. **The column is not wrong and was not widened here**: it is narrower than this module needs, and a session holding `packages/db/migrations` owns whatever that costs.

**SEND TIME IS A PROPERTY OF THE PARAMETER LIST**, which is `P7-l`'s shape one directory over. `AS-M10-03`'s ordering is the whole reason `INV-M10-08` exists: the breach fires at 00:20, the flag at 00:40, the restriction at 09:15, and a guard evaluated at enqueue sent a discounted reset offer to a ring at 00:21. `LoopsLiveState` carries restriction, open-flag severity and the last send, and **carries nothing a producer could set to say the guard already passed**; `dispatchToLoops` takes it as a REQUIRED argument and is the only entry point, so a caller that has not re-read live state has no value to pass. **The guard runs BEFORE the projection**, so a suppressed message has no body at all, because a body that exists is one edit from being sent.

**`OQ-M10-02` IS UNTOUCHED AND NO ADR NUMBER WAS TAKEN.** The vendor choice is the founder's, and it did not have to be made to proceed: session 163 measured the cost of the question at *"nothing depends on it except the adapter's own file name"*, and the file name is `P7` section 8's. `LOOPS_INTEGRATION` is the `integration` column's KEY and not a selection. **There is no base URL, no hostname, no credential and no send in this file**, which is [ADR-012](decisions/ADR-012.md)'s discipline on `ADMIN_ORIGIN` read onto a vendor. **The attempt budget ships `unstated`**: `M10:96` draws `retrying --> dead_letter` on *"attempts exhausted"* and names no number, and `integration_dispatches.attempts` carries no ceiling. The two numbers that ARE stated, the seven-day throttle and the severity floor of 4, are cited at the lines that state them and asserted against the guards transcribed from those same lines, so two transcriptions of one document cannot drift apart.

**THIRTEEN DEFECTS SEEDED AND ALL THIRTEEN CAUGHT, EVERY ONE WITH `pnpm run typecheck` AT ZERO ERRORS.** The one worth reading is **the 2026-08-28 barrel merge reproduced deliberately**: deleting BOTH export blocks and the `WORKER_BARREL_LEGS` entry leaves the typechecker silent and turns three assertions red. Deleting only the `export type` block, which is the cheaper accident, is caught by the name-by-name sweep alone. The others: the payload spread (`SELECT *` on an egress path), the forbidden field filtered instead of refused, a contract declared and enabled with no approver, the `unstated` retry budget quietly filled in, the guard moved after the projection, a trigger dropped so the table is eleven, a citation drifted by three lines, the severity floor moved from 4 to 3, `live` made optional, `hasOwnProperty` weakened to `in` so the prototype becomes an egress path, and an `@merit/db` import.

**ONE FILE WAS TOUCHED THAT THE `P7-m` ROW DOES NOT LIST AND IT IS REPORTED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE FOUND.** [`apps/worker/test/breaker.test.ts`](../apps/worker/test/breaker.test.ts) carries a hand-written barrel-leg count, and **`P7-l` wrote in that same enumeration that this would happen**: *"every barrel slice after this one must edit a literal in a file it does not own"*. Two lines, 21 to 22. **The in-fence alternative was to put the module in `WORKER_MODULES_NOT_RE_EXPORTED` and ship a barrel that does not carry the slice**, which is choosing a weaker artifact to avoid a two-line edit, and `P7` section 11 rule 16 puts that beside weakening a gate. Recorded here because it is the second consecutive barrel slice to pay it, and the literal is still nobody's.

**No ADR number, no migration number, no `packages/db` change, no contract change, no `SqlExecutorReason` member, no `SystemReason` member, no `pg` import and no cast past a key type.** `apps/api` is untouched, so [`wiring.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/wiring.test.ts)'s `{declared, wired, blocked}` triple does not move.

**`P7` IS CLOSED FOR ITS DISPATCHED SLICES AND WAVE 4 IS STILL NOT DISPATCHED.** All thirteen of section 8's rows are built. Section 12's Wave 4 remains what it was: `GS-235`'s subject line, `INV-M7-02`'s grant, and the v1.x tier, none of them this slice's.

**Measured with `pnpm install` first and each command run separately: 33 of 33 gates, 15 of 15 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, `format:check` clean, 213 test files / 5,015 passed / 6 skipped, `falsify.mjs` clean.** The `main` baseline of 33 / 15 / 0 / 0 / clean / **212 files / 4,981 passed / 6 skipped** was reproduced exactly before a line changed.

## `apps/admin`'s transport is planned, the central question was already ruled, and the plan is not `P8` (2026-08-28, session 329)

**[WAVE-06](plans/WAVE-06-admin-console-transport.md) LANDS, `status: draft`. A PLANNING SESSION: NOTHING WAS BUILT, NO SOURCE FILE WAS TOUCHED AND NO NUMBER WAS TAKEN.** It is the partition, the slice table and the collision table for the sessions that give the operator console a way to be reached, and it names two blockers it places slices behind rather than routing through.

**IT IS NOT `P8`, AND THE REASON IS A REGISTRY COLLISION RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE.** [DELIVERY_PLAN:132](DELIVERY_PLAN.md) rows **`P8 Hardening`** with contents that are named and are not these, [P6](plans/P6-live-tier.md) section 6 cites it by that name three times as *"P8's D0 battery"*, and [M15](plans/M15-discord-integration.md)'s surface table rows `RS-M15-01` and `RS-M15-03` at **P8**. **The `P<n>-` filename series is that phase table, one file per row**, seven names against seven rows in order, so a `P8-admin-server.md` puts a second meaning on the eighth row of a table every other `P<n>-` file transcribes. **The work is not a new phase either**: [DELIVERY_PLAN:129](DELIVERY_PLAN.md) makes *"the admin liability dashboard including wallet balances, the event feed"* part of **P5's** contents and [:131](DELIVERY_PLAN.md) makes *"the flags queue, two-tier evidence packs"* part of **P7's**, and both bodies of arithmetic exist in `apps/admin` and cannot be reached. **`WAVE-02` was checked before `WAVE-06` was chosen and is spent rather than free**: no document carries the name and [ALLOCATION](decisions/ALLOCATION.md) row `060` reads *"WAVE-02 session A2"*.

**THE PLAN'S CENTRAL QUESTION IS ANSWERED BY AN APPROVED DOCUMENT, TWICE, AND THE WORK WAS TO CITE IT RATHER THAN TO RULE IT.** [`INFRA:43`](architecture/INFRA.md) rows service **`admin`**, codebase `apps/admin`, `MERIT_API_SURFACE` **not set**, origin **`ADMIN_ORIGIN`**, serving *"The operator console"*; [`INFRA:44`](architecture/INFRA.md) rows service **`api-admin`**, codebase `apps/api`, surface **`operator`**, origin **`ADMIN_ORIGIN`, under `/api/v1`**; [`INFRA:53`](architecture/INFRA.md) states the routing rule, *"`/api/v1/*` reaches `api` on `app.meritfutures.com` and `api-admin` on `ADMIN_ORIGIN`; everything else reaches `portal` and `admin` respectively"*; and [`INFRA:71`](architecture/INFRA.md) hard rule 3 says it again from the security side. **So `apps/admin` serves HTTP and never serves `/api/v1`, and `OPERATOR_PREFIXES` is not the alternative to this plan but the other half of it.** `RI-04`, `RI-09` and `RI-11` each already refuse the fused shape mechanically. **What is genuinely undecided is the FRAMEWORK**, which [ADR-095](decisions/ADR-095.md) ruling 2 declined for this app by name: *"`apps/admin` gets none by this entry"*.

**A CONSEQUENCE WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE A SEPARATE-ORIGIN PLAN LOOKS HARDER THAN IT IS: THE CONSOLE'S API BASE URL IS SAME-ORIGIN.** Both services sit on `ADMIN_ORIGIN`, so the client calls a RELATIVE `/api/v1/admin/...` and needs no hostname and no CORS policy at all. `INV-M6-02`'s *"shares no CORS policy with any public surface"* is satisfied by there being no cross-origin request, and [ADR-012](decisions/ADR-012.md)'s *"never written into ... any artifact"* survives a build step **because a relative base URL cannot be inlined into a bundle**. That is stated as a constraint on the client slice rather than discovered by it.

**`apps/admin` MEASURED AND NOT ASSUMED TO BE A SHELL: 2,802 lines across nine modules, 200 passing tests in eight suites, no HTTP primitive anywhere, no `build`, no `dev`, no `src/app/` and no Playwright project.** **It is the ONLY UI deployable left in that state**, which is the half of session 324's finding that has moved: `apps/portal/src/app/` now holds **48 files including 11 pages** and `apps/site/src/app/` **14 including 10 `page.tsx`**, both counted here. **The nine modules are pure folds that take values and return values, and what is missing is every input and every output**: no wire types, no client, no route, no document. **And the two halves of this module were built by different phases against one document and meet nowhere**: the flags queue has a registered route, a composed adapter and NO console code, while the liability home has 1,764 lines of console code, a registered route and NO adapter.

**THREE FINDINGS, EACH WITH THE MEASUREMENT THAT MADE IT.** **(1) THE BARREL OMITS 23 EXPORTED NAMES AND ONE WHOLE MODULE.** [`feed.ts`](../apps/admin/src/feed.ts) is not in [`index.ts`](../apps/admin/src/index.ts) at all (14 exports), `liability.ts` is short by eight and `page.ts` by one. This is [P7](plans/P7-risk-and-abuse.md) section 5.5's class in the fourth deployable, and here **nothing was deleted: the names were never added**. The consequence is not tidiness: the `exports` map publishes `.` alone, so the event feed is unreachable from anywhere in this workspace, **and it is outside [`service.test.ts`](../apps/admin/test/service.test.ts)'s no-mutation assertion, which is the only control the package has over its own exports** and which filters `Object.keys(admin)`. `feed.ts` renders identity and account ids on its subject-named arm. **The repair is green under the existing test and that was READ rather than assumed**: none of the fifteen runtime values the barrel would gain begins with any of that test's 21 verbs. **(2) THE TWO `INV-M6-10` ASSERTIONS READ A LINE ARRAY A RENDERED PAGE WILL NOT USE.** `assertNamesNoSubject` and `assertWithheld` both take `readonly string[]`, and a React page renders a DOM; a slice that builds the document from the structured value and leaves the assertions on the lines **stops covering the served bytes with both suites green**, which is `projectFlag`'s 2026-08-28 miss with a renderer in place of a projection. The plan carries the remedy as a rule every rendering prompt inherits. **(3) `API_CONTRACT` SECTIONS 8 AND 9 CARRY NO EVENT-FEED ENDPOINT**, for a surface [M06](plans/M06-admin-ops-console.md) section 1.1 names as one of five and `feed.ts` implements in 507 lines with 421 lines of tests. Enumerated from the contract rather than grepped. That row is an amendment to an `approved` document and therefore an ADR.

So the plan's citations are checked by nothing mechanical; every one was written from the file and each was re-resolved by a script afterwards.

## The admin barrel carries all 74 of its names, and the next omission is a red suite (2026-08-28, session 332)

**[WAVE-06](plans/WAVE-06-admin-console-transport.md)'s `W6-b`. THE COUNT WAS RE-DERIVED RATHER THAN INHERITED AND IT IS 23, MATCHING SECTION 5.1 NAME FOR NAME.** [`feed.ts`](../apps/admin/src/feed.ts) was missing all fourteen because the module was not a leg at all, [`liability.ts`](../apps/admin/src/liability.ts) eight of thirteen, [`page.ts`](../apps/admin/src/page.ts) one of eleven, and the other five modules were complete at 36 of 36. **The surface is 74 names over 8 modules and the barrel carried 51.** The dispatch said a second measurement that disagreed would be a finding rather than an error; it agrees, and the agreement is the report.

**THE ASSERTION IS THE SLICE AND THE EXPORTS ARE THE SMALLER HALF, WHICH IS WHY THE DESIGN IS ARGUED IN THE FILE RATHER THAN CHOSEN IN A COMMIT MESSAGE.** [`apps/api/src/admin-source/index.ts`](../apps/api/src/admin-source/index.ts) keeps two independent defences against a merge dropping a leg and its header argues both. **The `Pick`-over-data half DOES NOT TRANSFER TO A BARREL OF RE-EXPORTS**, and [`apps/worker/src/index.ts`](../apps/worker/src/index.ts) had already written down why: there is no runtime value here for a type to be taken over, and minting one would put a second copy of the surface in the file whose whole job is to hold one copy of it. **WHAT TRANSFERS IS THE PRINCIPLE, WHICH IS THAT THE TWO HALVES MUST FAIL AT DIFFERENT TIMES.** Section A of [`service.test.ts`](../apps/admin/test/service.test.ts) imports all 74 names FROM THE BARREL by name and binds each to its own module's declaration, so a deletion in `index.ts` is a `tsc` error naming the member, in the gate that was green over the 2026-08-28 worker deletion. Section B reads each module's SOURCE and asserts the barrel re-exports every name it declares. **NEITHER SUBSUMES THE OTHER, AND THE ASYMMETRY IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT: the compile half catches DELETIONS early and by name, and the text half is the only one that can see a name that was NEVER ADDED.** All 23 were never-added, and a name nobody imports is a name nobody misses. **`B.4` is a third property neither reaches**: the barrel's binding must BE the module's binding, so a name re-exported from the wrong place fails while present and type-checking. **`B.5` keeps section A honest**, deriving its coverage from the test file's own source rather than from a second list, so the compile half cannot shrink unnoticed.

**SEVEN SEEDS, ALL SEVEN CAUGHT, AND FOUR LEFT `pnpm run typecheck` AT ZERO ERRORS, WHICH IS THE DEMONSTRATION THE SLICE EXISTS FOR.** Removing `assertFloatIsNotReserve` from the barrel and from section A is **exactly the state `main` was in**, and `tsc` is silent over it while `B.1` and `B.5` go red; removing the `feed.ts` leg entirely is **also the state `main` was in**, and `B.2` and `B.7` catch it. Re-exporting `figure` and `absent` under each other's names, with both names present, is caught by **`B.4` alone** and is invisible to the type checker and the text sweep alike. Deleting one section A line while the barrel is correct is caught by **`B.5` alone**. The two deletion seeds are caught by both halves, with `tsc` naming `renderRow` and `FeedRow`.

**`B.2` SWEEPS `src/` RECURSIVELY THOUGH THE DIRECTORY IS FLAT TODAY**, because `W6-c` adds `src/api/` and `src/http/` and a top-level sweep would stop covering this package on the very next slice, silently and while staying green. **A control that has to be widened by the slice it was written to catch is not a control.** The recursion is exercised by a seeded `src/api/types.ts` rather than by the committed tree. **`ADMIN_BARREL_LEGS` IS DATA AND `ADMIN_MODULES_NOT_RE_EXPORTED` SHIPS EMPTY**, which is the honest starting state rather than an oversight: every module under `src/` is a leg. The escape hatch exists so the first slice needing an unexported module does not have to weaken the sweep to land. **Every later slice adding a module to `apps/admin/src/` now pays one line**, which is the cost `P7-l` recorded for the worker barrel, recorded again here so no later slice discovers it.

**THE BARREL'S OWN HEADER WAS FALSE AND IS CORRECTED IN PLACE.** It listed the event feed among the *"M06 surfaces this package does not contain"* while `feed.ts` sat one directory away exporting fourteen names. **That is `RI-14`'s error class exactly** -- *"No reason claims a named thing does not exist while the tree exports it"* -- **in a file `RI-14` does not read**, its inputs being three named source files under `apps/api` and `apps/worker`. The omission and the false sentence are one defect and not two: a barrel that omits a module omits the module's description of itself too.

**THE NO-MUTATION FENCE WAS NOT MOVED AND THAT WAS READ RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** None of the fifteen runtime values the barrel gained begins with any of the 21 verbs, and the eight type-only names never reach `Object.keys`. `WAVE-06` section 9 says a slice that has to weaken that assertion is a slice in the wrong wave; this one did not have to.

**NOTHING ELSE IN THOSE MODULES WAS REPAIRED**, per the `W6-b` row. Section 5.2's finding about `assertNamesNoSubject` and `assertWithheld` reading a line array a rendered page will not use is `W6-d`'s and `W6-f`'s and is untouched. **`apps/admin/package.json` AND `tsconfig.json` WERE NOT TOUCHED and nothing was needed in them**, session 331 holding `apps/admin`'s framework; the type-only `@merit/rules-engine` import for `Cents` stands unchanged and **no re-export added here makes engine code reachable at runtime from this deployable**.

**NO ADR NUMBER, NO MIGRATION NUMBER, no `SD-M6-nn`, no `GS-nnn`, no `M6-N-nn`, no `SystemReason` member, no `SqlExecutorReason` member, no `pg` import, no hostname and no `fetch`.** `packages/ledger`, `packages/db/migrations`, `docs/plans/M05-payout-system.md`, `docs/architecture/STATE_MACHINES.md`, `docs/plans/WAVE-06-admin-console-transport.md`, `apps/api/test/wiring.test.ts` and `packages/tooling/**` are untouched.

**Measured with `pnpm install` first and each command run separately, `pnpm run verify` never run: 33 of 33 gates, 15 of 15 invariants, typecheck 0, lint 0, format:check clean, 213 test files / 5,035 passed / 6 skipped, `falsify.mjs` clean with the tree clean after it.** The `main` baseline of 33 / 15 / 0 / 0 / clean / **213 files / 5,028 passed / 6 skipped** was reproduced exactly on a branch sitting at `origin/main` (`3c95dda`) before a line changed, and `apps/admin` moved from **200 passing tests in 8 suites to 207 in 8**. **`WAVE-06` section 11 rule 7 states the baseline as 212 files / 4,981 passed, which was `main` when the plan was written and is not `main` now**; the dispatch's figures are the ones that reproduced.

## The in-flight obligation is a firm-scoped liability, no code can hold it, and `0054` returns to the pool unspent (2026-08-28, session 330)

**[ADR-181](decisions/ADR-181.md) lands, `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED, and `0054` IS
NOT TAKEN.** [ADR-174](decisions/ADR-174.md) section 3 declined to rule which account carries the
external leg's in-flight obligation and named three shapes, each of which needed an answer to its
finding (C). [ADR-180](decisions/ADR-180.md) supplied that answer. **This entry rules the shape.**

**THE RULING IS SHAPE (i), AND ITS CLASS AND SCOPE ARE DERIVED RATHER THAN CHOSEN.** The sign is
read out of [`posting.ts:235-236`](../packages/ledger/src/posting.ts) and not assumed. `LT-06`
DEBITS `trader_wallet`, so its open slot is a CREDIT; `LT-07` CREDITS `firm_treasury`, so its open
slot is a DEBIT. **One account rises when the trader's claim is extinguished and falls when the
cash leaves, which is an obligation**, and [ADR-174](decisions/ADR-174.md) clause 3 keeps `LT-07`
firm-only. So: a **FIRM-SCOPED `liability`**.

**NONE OF THE SEVEN DECLARED CODES CAN HOLD ONE, AND EACH REFUSAL HAS ITS OWN STEP.** Two firm codes
are ruled another kind by [`0052`](../packages/db/migrations/0052_chart_of_accounts.sql) and
[`0053`](../packages/db/migrations/0053_firm_treasury_kind.sql), read out of the constraint the
migration set INSTALLS rather than out of either file by name. Three liability codes are per
identity. **The two silences are refused on what the tree says they ARE rather than on their
silence**: [`checkout.ts:1682`](../apps/api/src/routes/checkout.ts) calls crediting `psp_clearing`
booking a receivable, which is an ASSET, and `SD-M5-03` anchors `reserve` outside this ledger on
purpose, so giving it this posting makes the `RCR` numerator grow as withdrawals are approved.

**SHAPE (ii) IS REFUSED ON A COST AND NOT ON BEING WRONG.** Deleting `LT-06` inverts
[M20:156](plans/M20-wallet.md)'s ruled halt behaviour, *"the halt is holding a transfer, not a
claim"*, in a module this session does not own, and
[STATE_MACHINES section 3.2](architecture/STATE_MACHINES.md)'s middle state exists to be the
interval this obligation stands in. **Shape (iii) is refused because a code ruled a liability BY
the posting that needed one is [`0009:46`](../packages/db/migrations/0009_ledger.sql)'s failure
with the direction reversed**, and it would be harder to see because it mints nothing.

**THE SECOND FINDING IS WHY THE MIGRATION NUMBER STAYS IN THE POOL, AND IT IS A MEASUREMENT RATHER
THAN A PREFERENCE.** [ADR-174](decisions/ADR-174.md) finding 3 priced the eighth code at *"TWO
merged migrations and a third statement in TypeScript"*. **It is thirteen files, SEVEN of them
outside this session's fence**, and one is [GLOSSARY](GLOSSARY.md)'s class list, which
[`0027:104`](../packages/db/migrations/0027_triggers_invariants.sql) records as the control that
actually caught `firm_payable`. **A migration widening the vocabulary while GLOSSARY still says
seven has disabled the control that caught the last one.** Two further grounds: `0009`'s CHECK and
`0027`'s `LEDGER-C2` are a two-guard design that one migration defeats by construction, which is
what [`0027:97-100`](../packages/db/migrations/0027_triggers_invariants.sql) anticipates in terms;
and **minting it today unblocks nothing**, because `LT-06`'s debit leg is per identity and nothing
in this tree creates an identity ledger account ([ADR-177](decisions/ADR-177.md) section 7 clause
3). **NO NAME IS MINTED EITHER**, and two spellings are refused in advance: `firm_payable`, because
[`probe_ledger_constraints.sql:84`](../scripts/db/probe_ledger_constraints.sql) uses it as the live
negative fixture, and any `payouts_*` spelling, because that is the internal leg's word and
`SD-M5-07` retired a pooled `payouts` class.

**EXECUTED, NOT BELIEVED.** PostgreSQL 16, `0001` through `0053` applied forward-only from empty
under `ON_ERROR_STOP`, 114 base tables, `ledger_accounts` at exactly two rows. Both guards fire
INDEPENDENTLY, with guard two watched after guard one was dropped inside a transaction, which
[ADR-174](decisions/ADR-174.md) finding 3 asserted from DDL. The `ELSE true` hole is open for
exactly two codes. **AND THE WHOLE SHAPE WAS BUILT END TO END AND POSTS CORRECTLY**: both guards
superseded, a sixth constraint arm, the row seeded firm-scoped `liability`, and `LT-06` and `LT-07`
posted at 25,000 cents with zero-sum, `LEDGER-C1` and `LEDGER-C2` all passing and a global sum of
**0**. The obligation stands at `-25000` cents between the two moments and 0 after both. **The
refusal is about a transcription set and a control, not about whether the arithmetic works.**

**THE ZERO ON THE OBLIGATION ACCOUNT IS NOT [ADR-174](decisions/ADR-174.md)'s ZERO.** That entry's
zero was on `firm_treasury`, the cash account, and it was the fingerprint of the defect. An
in-flight obligation returning to zero once both legs have run is the account doing its job.

**FOUND AND NOT IN THE DISPATCH: `wallet_withdrawals` HAS A TERMINAL `failed` STATE WITH NO LEDGER
POSTING ANYWHERE IN THE CORPUS.** [STATE_MACHINES section 3.2](architecture/STATE_MACHINES.md) draws
`transferring --> failed: G-TRANSFER-EXHAUSTED` and rows it with `wallet.withdrawal_failed`;
[M05](plans/M05-payout-system.md) section 2.1 declares eight transactions and not one of them is a
wallet withdrawal that failed on the rail. **A rail-exhausted withdrawal therefore strands the
obligation**: the wallet claim is gone, no cash left, and the trader's money is in neither place
they could be shown it. **It is the one genuine argument for shape (ii)** and the entry says so.
**No ninth transaction is minted and no id is claimed for one**, because that is a design and a
member of a declared identifier series; the repair is owed and `SD-M5-05`'s `reversal_of` is the
mechanism it will use.

**A SECOND LANDMINE, MEASURED.** `M05`'s line numbers are cited from `docs/` and from merged
migrations and **nothing checks them**: `RI-15` reads six named SOURCE files and its own `covers`
line records that it reads `docs/` *"NOT AT ALL"*.
[`0038`](../packages/db/migrations/0038_account_adjustments.sql)'s header cites `M05:560` for the
batch 1 gate's recognition ruling; `M05:560` is a row of the alarm table and the ruling is at
`M05:151`. A merged migration is never edited, so that citation is stale forever. **This session's
amendment to `M05` is LINE-COUNT NEUTRAL for exactly this reason.**

**`M05` section 2.1's `LT-06` and `LT-07` rows are AMENDED ADDITIVELY.** Each keeps every word it
carried, the `NOT RULED` phrase and the quotation of what it used to read included, and gains what
this entry rules. **Both stay UNPOSTABLE. `packages/rail` is untouched and stays green**, because
this entry mints no code, adds no constraint arm, seeds no row and rewrites neither row's opening
text, which is what [`lt-07.test.ts`](../packages/rail/test/lt-07.test.ts)'s armed assertions watch.
[ADR-177](decisions/ADR-177.md) and [ADR-180](decisions/ADR-180.md) each had to edit that package
and each recorded the fence question in its approval block; this one does not have to.

**No migration number, no code minted, no name minted, no `SystemReason` member, no
`SqlExecutorReason` member, no `pg` import and no cast past a key type.** `0009`, `0027`, `0038`,
`0052` and `0053` are byte for byte unchanged. `apps/api` and `apps/admin` are untouched, so
`wiring.test.ts`'s `{declared, wired, blocked}` triple does not move.

**Fourteen defects seeded against the tree and every one was caught: TWELVE by
[`in-flight-obligation.test.ts`](../packages/ledger/test/in-flight-obligation.test.ts) and TWO by
[`accounts.test.ts`](../packages/ledger/test/accounts.test.ts) beside it.** The two the new file did
not catch are an eighth code added to `0009`'s CHECK alone and to `0027`'s `NOT IN` alone, and the
division is deliberate: `accounts.test.ts` exists to hold those two lists and `accounts.ts` against
each other, and a second file re-reading them would be a fourth copy with nothing checking it.
**Eleven further perturbations were run against a running database, seven refused and four
ACCEPTED**, because a hole is watched rather than asserted, and all eleven behaved as designed.

**Measured with `pnpm install` first and each command run separately: 33 of 33 gates, 15 of 15
invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, `format:check` clean, 214 test files / 5,044 passed /
6 skipped, `falsify.mjs` clean with the tree clean after it.** The `main` baseline of 33 / 15 / 0 /
0 / clean / **213 files / 5,028 passed / 6 skipped** was reproduced exactly before a line changed.

## The framework is ruled for `apps/admin`, and the question underneath it was answered rather than defaulted (2026-08-28, session 331)

**[ADR-182](decisions/ADR-182.md) LANDS, `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED. It is the ruling [ADR-095](decisions/ADR-095.md) ruling 2 declined by name**, in that entry's own words: *"`apps/admin` gets none by this entry: the admin console is M06's and is in no P4 slice, so an entry whose fence is P4 `P4-c` may not decide it."* It is [WAVE-06](plans/WAVE-06-admin-console-transport.md)'s `W6-a`, the only slice in that wave that REQUIRED a number.

**RULING 1: `apps/admin` SERVES HTTP AND IT NEVER SERVES `/api/v1`, AND THE CENTRAL QUESTION WAS TREATED AS LIVE RATHER THAN INHERITED FROM THE PLAN'S NAME.** `apps/api` at `MERIT_API_SURFACE=operator` is `api-admin`, on the SAME `ADMIN_ORIGIN` under `/api/v1` ([`INFRA:44`](architecture/INFRA.md)), separated from the console by path ([`INFRA:53`](architecture/INFRA.md)). Its **27 registered routes** were re-derived over a real `compose()` in this session rather than quoted: 26 modules, 27 registered, 45 withheld on `operator`, and 46 registered on `public`. **Those routes are the console's DATA SOURCE and not a substitute for it.**

**THE LOSING SHAPES ARE PRICED RATHER THAN ASSUMED AWAY, AND THE ONE WORTH TAKING SERIOUSLY WAS NEVER `apps/api`.** Folding the console into the API makes [`INFRA:43`](architecture/INFRA.md) false, takes [`ADR-083:49`](decisions/ADR-083.md)'s back door deliberately, and, because **`RI-04` forbids `apps/api` declaring `@merit/admin`**, moves 2,802 lines out of a directory [`P5-l`](plans/P5-payouts-and-wallet.md) and [`P6-j`](plans/P6-live-tier.md) both hold. **The real alternative was NO FRAMEWORK**, a `node:http` server over [`renderLiabilityHome`](../apps/admin/src/page.ts)'s existing string lines, which costs zero dependencies. **It is refused on a property of the controls.** [ADR-095](decisions/ADR-095.md) ruling 3 forbids a UI serving `/api/v1` or an operator path and exactly two checks enforce it: `RI-09` reads PATHS and `RI-11` reads a routing CONFIG and a directive. **A hand-written router table gives neither anything to read**, which `RI-09`'s own `covers` states at [`repo-invariants.mjs:1334-1335`](../packages/tooling/checks/repo-invariants.mjs), so that shape is **the one in which both mechanical halves of ruling 3 go silent, in the deployable [SECURITY](architecture/SECURITY.md) treats as total loss when owned.**

**RULING 2: NEXT.JS APP ROUTER ON THE CATALOG VERSIONS ALREADY ADMITTED, SO THE FIVE ENTRIES [ADR-095](decisions/ADR-095.md) RULING 1 TOOK GAIN A THIRD IMPORTER AND NO SIXTH ENTRY.** **The `VG-12` closure delta is ZERO and it was diffed rather than argued: 427 package keys in [`pnpm-lock.yaml`](../pnpm-lock.yaml)'s `packages:` block before and 427 after, and the two sorted lists are byte-identical.** The lockfile gained **15 lines, every one inside the `apps/admin` importer block**, and [`pnpm-workspace.yaml`](../pnpm-workspace.yaml) took no diff at all: the slice held that fence. **The session did NOT grant the admission**, because [`STRATEGY:192`](testing/STRATEGY.md) says of one that it is an admission *"a session cannot grant itself"*; the entry recommends that none is needed and says the recommendation is not the answer.

**THE MANIFEST GAINED `build` AND `dev` AND ITS `start` BECAME `next start`, AND THE SCRIPT CHANGE IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE.** `node --experimental-strip-types src/index.ts` starts a module that prints one line and returns, so a platform reads a healthy service where nothing is served: a manifest wrong in the direction that looks like it works. **Both scripts were RUN**: `next build` exits 1 on *"Couldn't find any `pages` or `app` directory"* and `next start` exits 1 on *"Could not find a production build"*, which is wrong in the honest direction.

**THE `tsconfig` DID NOT MOVE, AND THAT REVERSES THE SLICE AS DISPATCHED RATHER THAN QUIETLY SKIPPING IT.** [ADR-095](decisions/ADR-095.md) `F7` places the `jsx` keys and the `dom` lib *"with the first page rather than here"*, and both prior instances did exactly that. The collision argument that justified landing the React type packages early is about `pnpm-lock.yaml` being SERIALIZED across slices, and it does not reach a file one slice touches. **So [`apps/admin/tsconfig.json`](../apps/admin/tsconfig.json) is now `W6-d`'s fence**, and two other fences moved with it: `W6-i` gains [`e2e/tsconfig.json`](../e2e/tsconfig.json), whose `include` names the two app `e2e` directories by hand, and `W6-c` gains the two `ADR-012` assertions nothing in this repository makes today.

**`ADR-012` IS DISCHARGED IN FOUR CLAUSES AND THE ENTRY SAYS WHICH TWO HAVE NO CHECK.** No `NEXT_PUBLIC_` identifier in this deployable ever, which is the single mechanism by which a framework writes a resolved hostname into a client bundle; a RELATIVE API base URL, available only because both services sit on one origin; `ADMIN_ORIGIN` read at request time through [`resolveAdminOrigin`](../apps/admin/src/origin.ts) with no default and a throw when unset; and no `next.config`. **Clauses one and two are rules with no mechanism and `W6-c` is named as the slice that can make them checks.**

**[ADR-171](decisions/ADR-171.md) IS UNMOVED AND WAS RE-MEASURED RATHER THAN CITED.** `admin_actions.actor` is `text NOT NULL` with no foreign key ([`0017_events_and_audit.sql:77`](../packages/db/migrations/0017_events_and_audit.sql)), and `grep -rn "admin_sessions\|admin_users\|admin_actors\|operator_sessions" packages/db/migrations/` returns **zero lines**. **No table in the registry holds an operator, a role or an operator session**, so every write in `M06` and every read's actual rows stay behind an SSO purchase that is the founder's. **This ruling is deliberately IN FRONT of that blocker**: a framework, a manifest and a boundary need no principal.

**TWO STALE REASONS ARE REPORTED RATHER THAN REACHED PAST, AND ONE OF THEM IS THIS RULING'S OWN COST.** [`pnpm-workspace.yaml:144`](../pnpm-workspace.yaml)'s `next:` comment still reads *"in `apps/portal` and `apps/site` and in NO other package"*, which this entry falsifies **in the one file the slice may not touch**, with nothing mechanical to notice; the sentence moves in the commit that carries the founder's `VG-12` answer. And [`apps/admin/src/index.ts:126`](../apps/admin/src/index.ts) still reads *"there is no server here to receive a request carrying them"* in a file **session 332 holds this wave**, so the line is reported and `W6-d` is named as the slice that makes it false in fact.

**One prediction was wrong in the cheap direction.** [WAVE-06](plans/WAVE-06-admin-console-transport.md) rowed [`INDEX`](INDEX.md) as a `W6-a` and `W6-e` collision at one row each; `W6-a` needed none, because `CI-06c` reads the `decisions/` directory row and the per-entry registry is a generated span.

**No migration number, no `SD-M6-nn`, no `GS-nnn`, no `M6-N-nn`, no `SystemReason` member, no `pg` import, and no file outside the fence.** Measured with `pnpm install` first and each command run separately, reproduced on `main` before a line changed and unmoved after: **33 of 33 gates, 15 of 15 invariants, `typecheck` exit 0, `lint` exit 0, `format:check` clean, 213 test files / 5,028 passed / 6 skipped.** `falsify.mjs` ran LAST and ALONE on a committed tree: 33 gates clean and dirty, 80 scope cases, 10 loader cases, **no seed uncaught**.

## `RI-16` reads the corpus's own citations, and the scope argument is the slice (2026-08-28, session 333)

**`RI-15` reads six source files and its own `covers` line records that it reads `docs/decisions` NOT AT ALL.** Both were checked at the source before anything was built and both hold. That left **879 markdown documents carrying 3,463 `file:line` pointers** with nothing mechanical following one of them, which is the half where a wrong pointer is read by the founder at an `E2` review and by every later session that treats the entry as settled.

**THE SCOPE IS THE WHOLE OF `docs/` AND THE THREE EXCLUSIONS ARE BY SHAPE, EACH ONE MEASURED.**

| Population | Count |
| --- | --- |
| Citations carrying a path of their own or a markdown link | 2,340 |
| Excluded: under a dated or session heading | **1,737** |
| **In scope** | **603** |
| Excluded: a bare `:12` with no path and no link | **1,123** |
| In scope carrying a bindable NAME | 5 |
| **Findings** | **4** |

**The first exclusion is `CI-06/derivable-counts`' rule rather than this check's**, applied through its own recogniser: an entry headed with a date or a session number is a record of a measurement made that day, and repairing it would rewrite the record to say something it did not say. **It reaches INSIDE `docs/STATE.md`, which is a live document that accumulates dated sections and that no directory rule could split**, and it puts a new session log out of scope and a new plan in scope on the day each is written with nobody maintaining a list.

**The third exclusion diverges from `RI-15` and the measurement is the argument.** `RI-15` lets a bare pointer inherit the nearest path within six lines and names that as its miss (6). Here inheritance adds fifteen findings inside the scope and **all fifteen are the check guessing a path**: `M05:214` is a plan and a section line, `0011:49` is a migration, `open_ct 17:00` is a clock. **The half of that hole that closes without guessing is closed**: a citation inside a markdown link takes the path the link states, which is 130 more citations, a 27 percent gain, resolved to one file rather than to every file whose name ends the same way.

**FOUR FINDINGS, ZERO REPAIRED, AND THE REASON IS A RULE.** Three are `ALLOCATION` rows `164` and `168` restating [ADR-172](decisions/ADR-172.md)'s finding 1, whose member [ADR-176](decisions/ADR-176.md) DELETED, so there is no line to repoint them at; the fourth is `FOLD-01`'s `DECISIONS.md:483`, a pointer with a line number on a document this tree has never had. All four sit in documents whose frontmatter reads `status: approved`, a change to a frozen document is an ADR rather than a commit, and **this session held no ADR number**. Each is registered in `DOC_CITATIONS_OWNED_ELSEWHERE` with the repair it waits for named, and the register **shrinks only** per `CI-06u`: an entry matching no finding on a later ref is itself a finding.

**POINTING THE SHARED READER AT 19 MB OF MARKDOWN BROKE IT THREE TIMES, ALL THREE INVISIBLE ON SIX SOURCE FILES.** The citation pattern was quadratic on a document with long backtick-free stretches; the line joiner had every leading group optional, so it was tried at every index, and two greedy runs over one character class, which backtracks over every way to split a run of spaces (**a padded markdown table is one 13,000-character line of them**); and the path class dropped a Next.js route group. **`docs/decisions/ALLOCATION.md` did not finish in five minutes and the whole of `docs/` now reads in 0.38 seconds.** The citation grammar is now one reader shared by both checks, and `RI-15`'s ten unchanged cases assert its finding text character for character, which makes them the equivalence oracle for all three repairs.

**Twelve seeded cases, every one in both directions, and four seeds run against the REAL tree** with the finding text recorded and the tree restored byte for byte, proved by checksum: a true citation shifted 39 lines FIRED, a pointer past the end of the file its link names FIRED, a link naming a file this tree does not have FIRED, and the control seeding the same drift under a dated session heading stayed SILENT exactly as `covers` says. **No seed went uncaught.** All four design decisions are additionally watched failing under mutation.

**Measured on this branch with `pnpm install` first and each command run separately: 33 of 33 gates, 16 of 16 invariants, 213 test files / 5,041 passed / 6 skipped.** The `main` baseline of 33 / 15 / 213 / 5,028 / 6 was reproduced before a line changed. The `IMPLEMENTED_ADMIN_READS` plus `Pick` half is about what THAT DIRECTORY implements, which is no feed module, so it is untouched. And [`admin-source-flags.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/admin-source-flags.test.ts) **hardcodes the six method names in two places** and is named nowhere at all. **Implementing an unsigned ruling's port would be asserting the signature the entry is asking for**, so the entry rules and the code waits, with each edit named at its line.

**BOTH SHAPES WERE SEEDED AND BOTH WENT RED, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT EXECUTED RATHER THAN ASSERTED.** A port declared in the new module fails `wiring.test.ts`'s unaccounted check AND its triple AND the new module's own fence test, three cases; a seventh method fails two cases in `admin-source-flags.test.ts`. **Spelling the setter so `DECLARES` misses it was considered and REFUSED BY NAME**: that is weakening a gate to pass it, and a port and the reason it is not wired belong in one commit, which is the regression that file exists for.

## The contract and the tree are diffed for the first time, and they agree exactly (2026-08-28, session 338)

**THE DIFF IS EMPTY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND THAT IS THE MEASUREMENT.**
[API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) declares **72** distinct `METHOD /path` endpoints. The
modules on disk declare **72** routes and `compose()` registers **72** across the two surfaces. The
symmetric difference is **0**: every contract row has a registered route and every registered route
has a contract row. **Nothing in this repository could ask that question before this session**, and
the answer is not the one the slice was priced for.

**THE 35 WAS THE PARSER AND NOT THE CORPUS.** The dispatch's premise was that a backtick regex
returned 35 distinct paths and that the parser rather than the document was wrong. It was. The reader
that gets 72 reads **two structures and says which**: an endpoint HEADING, split on commas so a
segment omitting a method inherits the one to its left, and an endpoint TABLE identified by its first
header cell being exactly `Endpoint`, which is a SHAPE rather than a section number, so a new
endpoint table is read the day it lands and a new prose table is not. **Four headings carry more than
one endpoint and one entry per heading loses five of them**, a failure
[API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) section 8 names in its own words: *"One heading over
three paths reads as one endpoint to anything parsing this document."* **Prose is read NOT AT ALL**,
which is the skip that produced the 35: section 1 spells `POST /accounts/:id/reset` where the heading
spells `:accountId`, and section 12 describes requests that must be REFUSED.

**THE BASELINE WAS REPRODUCED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS BUILT**: `public` **46 registered / 26 withheld**,
`operator` **27 / 45**, over a real `compose()`. **The dispatch's "73 registered routes" is a SUM and
the distinct figure is 72**, because `GET /health` is registered on BOTH surfaces, which is
[API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) section 9 doing what its row says while sitting in an
admin-origin section.

**THE READER STATES ITS OWN COVERAGE AND THE COVERAGE IS DERIVED FROM THE READ.** 59 endpoint
headings and 64 endpoints from them; 2 endpoint tables and 8 rows; 22 headings stating no method and
5 tables keyed on `Code`, `revocation_class`, `Surface`, `Token` and `Test` skipped **with their line
numbers**; **0 anomalies and 0 duplicate declarations**. A position inside a structure it claims to
read, from which it derived no endpoint, is reported rather than dropped, because a parser that
silently drops rows produces a coverage report that looks like success. **It reads the live document
in 0.44 ms**, that being the minimum over ten reads, with 0.67 ms the maximum;
`RI-16`'s reader took over five minutes on one document before three defects in it were found, and
the shapes that made it slow are the shapes this one avoids on purpose.

**ITS TEST'S SUBJECT IS A FIXTURE CONTRACT AND NEVER THE LIVE DOCUMENT**, because session 336 is
adding a contract row concurrently and a suite asserting "72 endpoints" is a check that punishes the
work it exists to support. **The fixture found a REAL DEFECT in the reader**: it required a space
after the method, so a heading whose whole text was a bare `GET` fell into the count of non-endpoint
headings. A malformed endpoint heading, silently dropped, invisible on a document where every heading
is well formed. **Four seeds were then run against the REAL corpus in memory and all four were caught
exactly**, with the document's SHA-256 verified identical before and after; the fourth collapses a
three-endpoint heading and produces **two false findings**, which is the comma split watched being
load-bearing.

**WHAT THE EMPTY DIFF DOES NOT SAY, stated because a green measurement is the one most likely to be
vacuous.** It compares PATHS and nothing else, so a route whose schema, auth factor, idempotency or
rate limit differs from its contract row is invisible to it. It is blind to a surface the contract
never rowed: session 329's finding that sections 8 and 9 carry **no event-feed endpoint** for a
surface `M06` names and [`feed.ts`](../apps/admin/src/feed.ts) implements in 507 lines is in neither
list because it is in neither input. And it says nothing about WHICH surface a route landed on.

TEXT**, and that is refused on the rule

## The liability response is ruled, and the ruling is a projection rather than a field list (2026-08-28, session 345)

**[ADR-188](decisions/ADR-188.md), `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED.** [Session 340](sessions/2026-08-28-session-340.md)'s finding 1 was that `GET /admin/liability`'s contracted response cannot produce the page `W6-d` shipped. It is real. **Its statement was not, and the correction is the first finding**: the response did not carry *"`open_liability_cents` and nothing else"*, it carried `as_of`, `open_liability_cents` and `funded_accounts` of that row while four figures were missing, and **`funded_accounts` is on `liability_snapshots` because [ADR-128](decisions/ADR-128.md) put it there** by `ALTER TABLE` in [`0049`](../packages/db/migrations/0049_reserve_coverage_snapshots.sql).

**THE COMPLETENESS RULE IS A PROJECTION AND NOT A LIST, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** The top-level fields are one [`liability_snapshots`](../packages/db/migrations/0009_ledger.sql) row column for column; the only columns not carried are `id`, a surrogate key, and `computed_at`, which records when a batch ran rather than what any figure describes. A list would be a second enumeration of a table, which is the drift [ADR-034](decisions/ADR-034.md) deletes wherever it finds it; stated as a projection, the next column on that table is on this response by the rule rather than by somebody remembering. The four added are `wallet_balances_cents`, `bounded_near_term_cents`, `remaining_ladder_exposure_cents` and `absorbed_corrections_cents`.

**`open_liability_cents` KEEPS ITS NAME AND THE FOURTH GROUND IS THE ONE THAT IS NOT OBVIOUS.** The column is one component of the panel that shares its name, and [`liability.ts`](../apps/admin/src/liability.ts) renames it on arrival to `withdrawableAcrossFundedCents` for exactly that reason. A wire rename would disagree with a column no migration may edit, and it would **delete the console's one stated mapping site**: kept as the column's name, the adapter's line is a RENAME and a reader stops at it; renamed on the wire, it becomes an identity assignment nobody reads twice, and the boundary where the column stops being the panel would be marked nowhere.

**NO TOTAL IS SENT, AND THE RULE THAT DECIDES IT IS STATED RATHER THAN THE PREFERENCE.** A value is sent when the server knows something the reader does not, and computed by the reader when it is a pure function of fields already on the response. The open liability total is two fields of one row at one `as_of`. A handler-computed total is a third number that can disagree with the two beside it, which is the drift [`0049`](../packages/db/migrations/0049_reserve_coverage_snapshots.sql)'s `GENERATED` column exists to remove and there is no generated column here; and it is the single convenient figure a client can render alone under the panel's name, which is the affordance [`liability.ts`](../apps/admin/src/liability.ts) removed structurally one layer down. **What is given up is stated: neither design is enforced by the payload, so the choice is which failure is visible.**

**A FINDING NOT IN THE RESERVATION BECAME CLAUSE 4.** `reserve` carried a ratio, a numerator and a denominator with **no `as_of` and no anchor**, so `P-M6-07` was as unrenderable as `P-M6-02` and for the same reason. It gains `as_of`, `treasury_account_code`, `treasury_as_of` and `treasury_source`. Dating it with the top-level `as_of` would put our clock on the rail's figure, which is the second of the three reasons `ADR-128` gave for the two tables being two.

**AND THE DISPATCH'S OTHER PREMISE IS TRUE OF EVERYTHING RULED AND FALSE IN GENERAL.** *"`liability_snapshots` already holds every figure"* does not hold for `SD-M6-01`'s `eligible_next_7d_identity_max_cents` and `eligible_next_7d_identity_max_id`, **neither of which appears in any migration**, so `P-M6-03`'s identity maximum, the number [ADR-011](decisions/ADR-011.md)'s same-day top-up trigger reads, is unproducible and deliberately gains no field. That is a schema item with no reserved number.

**NO CODE WAS EDITED AND THE REASON WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED.** The four fields seeded onto `LiabilityResponse` are **three `TS2739` sites in three files**: `projectLiability`, and a typed fixture in each of two suites, **two of the three outside this fence**. Landing the type alone is a red `CI-01` on purpose, and widening the fence to reach the other two is the move this corpus refuses. **The whole suite stays GREEN under that seed**, so `CI-01` is the only thing standing between a half-applied field addition and silence.

**SEVEN THINGS ARE REGISTERED RATHER THAN REPAIRED**, each with the fence that holds it, and the sharpest is that **`LiabilityResponse` exists in three copies and nothing binds any pair**: the contract's block, [`admin-reads.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/admin-reads.ts) and [`api/types.ts`](../apps/admin/src/api/types.ts). `RI-17` compares `METHOD /path` and reads no field, so the ruled shape can land in one copy and not the others with every check green. The check that would close it is `RI-17`'s method applied to fields instead of paths.

**`RI-17` UNMOVED and `CI-06k` UNMOVED, both measured**: a field addition adds no endpoint, and `CI-06k` reads section 12. **No endpoint added, no migration number taken, [`0009`](../packages/db/migrations/0009_ledger.sql) and [`0049`](../packages/db/migrations/0049_reserve_coverage_snapshots.sql) byte for byte unchanged, and no file under `apps/` or `packages/` touched.** 33 of 33 gates, 16 of 16 invariants, typecheck 0, lint 0, `format:check` clean, **220 test files / 5,171 passed / 6 skipped with a TEST DELTA OF ZERO**, against a `main` baseline of 220 / 5,171 / 6 reproduced exactly at `3c456173` before a line changed, `falsify.mjs` clean with the tree clean after it.

## Two screens land, and the 503 the console was told to render is a 401 and a 500 (2026-08-28, session 344)

**[WAVE-06](plans/WAVE-06-admin-console-transport.md)'s `W6-f` and `W6-g` both land, serial, in one session because they share two files.** The flags queue at `/flags` and the identity drill-down at `/identities/[identityId]`, `FlagListItem` and `IdentityGraph` transcribed into [`api/types.ts`](../apps/admin/src/api/types.ts), and `M6-A-43` through `M6-A-54` as 43 cases in two suites. `next build` compiles **three routes** where `W6-d` left one. **They are the two M06 surfaces whose both halves exist**, `listFlags` and `readIdentityGraph` being the two entries in `IMPLEMENTED_ADMIN_READS`, so each renders real rows the day an operator session lands and neither waits on an adapter nobody wrote.

**THE LARGEST FINDING IS A STATUS THE CONSOLE WAS TOLD TO RENDER AND NO OPERATOR ROUTE PRODUCES.** [WAVE-06 section 8.1](plans/WAVE-06-admin-console-transport.md) says *"every one of the 26 operator routes above answers 503 today"* and [`src/app/page.tsx`](../apps/admin/src/app/page.tsx) renders `toAdminErrorKind(503)` on that basis. Measured over a real `compose()` and Fastify's own `inject`, on both branches: **with no admin session cookie an operator route answers 401 `unauthenticated`, and with a cookie present it answers 500 `internal_error`.** [`admin-reads.ts:109`](../apps/api/src/routes/admin-reads.ts) says so at the declaration of `AdminReadError`, *"IT IS A 500 AND NEVER A 404 OR A 503"*, and [`server.ts:155`](../apps/api/src/server.ts) is the mapping. Both routes added here therefore name **no error kind** and carry the two real answers in their blocker prose. **Reported and not repaired**: the plan sentence and `W6-d`'s file are outside this fence.

**SECOND FINDING, FOUND BY A SEED FAILING TO FIRE: `assertNamesNoSubject`'s uuid pattern is `\b`-anchored, so a subject id glued to a word character is not a match.** `linked_to_<uuid>` passes and `linked to <uuid>` throws, run in both directions. That regex is [`page.ts`](../apps/admin/src/page.ts)'s and `P5-l` holds the file, so the flags queue grew a **second leg that fails at a different time**: the pattern leg covers an id from any field, including one in no field of the response, and the value leg asserts the three identifiers the document declines to render are absent from what it served, however they are spelled.

**THIRD FINDING: `GET /admin/identities/:identityId/graph` declares three `_cents` fields and no `as_of` and no source for any of them**, where `GET /admin/liability` declares `as_of` as its first field. **A second, independent mechanism refuses the same render**: [`figure.ts`](../apps/admin/src/figure.ts)'s `ORIGIN_ID` closes the admissible roster at `P-M6-01` to `P-M6-10` and `AS-M6-04`, which are M06 section 3.1's panels, so a figure raised on section 3.2a has no origin to declare either. The drill-down states all three as a named absence in `PendingPanel` shape, beside a second entry naming what section 3.2a asks for that the response has no field for at all. Neither repair is inside any WAVE-06 fence.

**THE TWO `INV-M6-10` SHAPES ARE OPPOSITE ON PURPOSE.** The flags queue names no subject, so its rule is that no subject identifier reaches the served bytes at all. The drill-down names one, so `assertNamesNoSubject` is deliberately **not** called there: it would refuse the page's own subject. Its rule is a **closure** -- every id served is one the query reached, the named subject and the graph resolved from it -- and the root the server answered with is checked against the path first, because a page headed by the id an operator typed whose rows belong to another human is the worst answer this endpoint can give and the one they cannot detect.

**THERE IS NO LIST BEHIND THE DRILL-DOWN AND THAT IS ASSERTED OVER THE DIRECTORY** rather than over an intention: `src/app/identities/` publishes one route carrying a dynamic segment, with no `identities/page.tsx`, no input, no form and no history affordance. **A seeded index route and a seeded search box each turned it red.** No restriction affordance and no restore affordance: `INV-M6-14`'s write is behind [ADR-171](decisions/ADR-171.md).

**THE ORDERING IS THE SERVER'S AND IS NOT RECOMPUTED.** The queue maps `rows` in wire order, the module is asserted to sort nothing by a read of its own source, and a queue that arrives out of order is rendered out of order rather than repaired. `corroboration_depth` is beside the severity **in the words and not only in an attribute**, which is `FM-M6-01` rather than style.

**FOURTH FINDING, AND IT DECIDED THE FILENAMES: `src/view/flags.ts` and `src/view/identity.ts` cannot land as `.ts` without two files this fence does not hold.** `service.test.ts`'s `B.2`, `B.5`, `B.7` and `B.1` and `surface.test.ts`'s section 7 together fence a ninth barrel leg out of this wave entirely, so both view modules land as `.tsx` documents under `src/app/`, which is session 340's constraint inherited and `src/app/liability-home.tsx`'s own shape.

**Fourteen seeded defects, all fourteen caught**, each against the committed shape and each reverted, with the tree clean after every one. Measured with `pnpm install` first and each command run separately, with the `main` baseline reproduced before a line changed: **33 of 33** gates, **16 of 16** invariants, typecheck 0, lint 0, `format:check` clean with the four `.tsx` formatted by hand, **222 files / 5,214 passed / 6 skipped** against a `main` baseline of **220 / 5,171 / 6**, `falsify.mjs` clean with the tree clean after it.

## `apps/admin` joins the CI that guards the other two UI deployables, and the one gate it does NOT join is reported with the bytes (2026-08-28, session 346)

**FOUR PARTS, FOUR COMMITS, ALL FOUR LANDED.** `W6-i`'s Playwright project, the build stage, the
missing `next.config.mjs`, and a `format:check` glob that had never read a `.tsx`. Every one of the
four was a gap another session measured and registered rather than reached for, and none of them
needed an ADR number or a migration number.

**`CI-08` IS AT THREE OF THREE PROJECTS AND THE ROW MOVED IN THE SAME COMMIT AS THE PROJECT.**
Derived from [`playwright.config.ts`](../playwright.config.ts) at reporting time: `site`, `portal`,
`admin`. **24 Playwright tests pass**, up from 16, which is
[DESIGN_SYSTEM](design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md) section 8's four renderings applied to two more surfaces.
The condition `W6-i` was dispatched with is the one that mattered: `CI-06/gate-inventory` never asks
whether a `Contents` cell is TRUE, so a register left saying two would have carried a count that is
false in the direction which looks like success, and nothing in this repository would have said so.
