## Session 347: the ninth ledger transaction, and the proof that it happened (2026-08-28)

**[ADR-189](decisions/ADR-189.md), `proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED. MONEY PATH. [`E2`](../MERIT_BUILD_MASTER_PROMPT.md)
is owed on [`0057`](../packages/db/migrations/0057_terminal_withdrawal_obligation.sql) and is not
discharged by the merge.**

**THE NINTH LEDGER TRANSACTION IS `LT-09`, `wallet_withdrawal_failure`.** It is the exact negation of
`LT-06` with `reversal_of` set, posted in the same database transaction as `transferring --> failed`.
[ADR-181](decisions/ADR-181.md) section 6 found the gap and declined to mint the id;
[ADR-187](decisions/ADR-187.md) minted the account it strands and left the finding open. It is closed.
`SD-M5-05`'s mechanism is used and not redesigned: `LT-06` is reversed, never deleted, amended or
adjusted in place.

**WHAT TRIGGERS IT WAS DERIVED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, AND THE ARGUMENT IS NARROWER THAN THE DISPATCH'S.**
`failed` is not special because the rail gave up. It is the only terminal state reachable from at or
past `approved` that does not itself discharge the obligation. The three terminal states were checked
one at a time: `settled` discharges through `LT-07`; `failed` through nothing, which is the finding;
and `cancelled` is drawn only from `requested` and `cooling`, both before approval, so `LT-06` never
posted. **So `WD-C1` is stated as the property and not as the procedure** -- a terminal wallet
withdrawal leaves nothing standing in `withdrawals_in_flight` -- and it holds on all three, three
different ways, and would hold on a fourth.

**`0057` IS TAKEN AND THE DISPATCH'S BINARY IS REFUSED WITH ITS REASON.** A posting builder and a
trigger prove different things and neither is sufficient. `reversalPosting` makes an inexact reversal
UNREPRESENTABLE by swapping each transfer's two sides and negating nothing, so a partial reversal has
no spelling; it cannot prove that a withdrawal which reached `failed` was ever handed to it, and it
cannot prove the reversal was built once rather than twice. **Both of those are facts about rows.**
The defect being closed is *a state transition happened and no posting followed*, and a builder
proves only what a caller who called it built.

**A SECOND CONTROL WAS MEASURED BEFORE THE MIGRATION WAS WRITTEN.** `ledger_transactions_reversal_of_idx`
is NOT UNIQUE in `0009`. A second reversal of one `LT-06` under a different idempotency key LANDS,
drives the obligation to a debit balance and `trader_wallet` negative, **and leaves the global sum at
zero, so nothing in this database sees it.** It is superseded UNIQUE under its own name and it now
binds `LT-03` and every future reversal.

**THE WHOLE FAILURE PATH WAS POSTED END TO END** against the per-identity rows `0054`'s trigger opens,
after an `LT-01` of 30,000 cents split 25,000 trader and 5,000 firm: `trader_wallet` **-25000**; after
`LT-06`, `trader_wallet` **0** and the obligation **-25000**; the transition to `failed` **REFUSED**
while the obligation stood; after `LT-09` the obligation **0**, the trader's claim back at **-25000**,
global sum **0**.

**FIVE FINDINGS THAT WERE NOT IN THE DISPATCH**, in [ADR-189](decisions/ADR-189.md) section 6. Two are
worth this page. **`0009:103-104`'s comment claims a reversal "may not chain onto another reversal"
and the CHECK beneath it enforces only self-reversal**; executed, and reported rather than closed,
because that is a general ledger rule and `account_adjustments` already enforces it where reversals
are actually written. **And [ADR-187](decisions/ADR-187.md) section 9 nominates the failed-withdrawal
case as the cheapest place to see whether `LT-06`'s and `LT-07`'s slots are one account, and it is not
one**: `LT-09` touches `LT-06`'s slot and no other, so the failure path is silent on that question.
**The good news is that this ruling does not depend on its answer.**

**`0009`, `0027`, `0038`, `0052`, `0053`, `0054`, `0055` AND `0056` ARE BYTE FOR BYTE UNCHANGED, none
of `0056`'s three guards is touched, the vocabulary stays closed at EIGHT, and [M20](plans/M20-wallet.md)
and [STATE_MACHINES](architecture/STATE_MACHINES.md) are NOT amended and neither needed to be.** `M05`
section 2.1 gains one row and one paragraph and loses nothing; `LT-02`'s, `LT-06`'s and `LT-07`'s rows
are untouched. **Measured with `pnpm install` first, each command run separately and `pnpm run verify`
never run, with the `main` baseline at `9dca218d` reproduced before a line changed: 33 of 33 gates, 16
of 16 invariants, `typecheck` 0, `lint` 0, `format:check` clean, and 223 test files / 5,240 passed / 6
skipped against 222 / 5,220 / 6.** Eight defects seeded across the TypeScript, the migration and the
plan and all eight caught; five more seeded into `0057` and caught by the CI probe.

## Two guards that passed while covering less than their own words claimed (2026-08-28, session 348)

**Both repaired, in two commits, and each failure was watched happening before a line moved.**
Neither was found by reading. `assertNamesNoSubject`'s hole surfaced when
[session 344](sessions/2026-08-28-session-344.md)'s seed **failed to fire**, and `VG-2`'s surfaced
when [session 346](sessions/2026-08-28-session-346.md) added a third bundle to a job whose grep
reads a typed list of paths. **A guard that refuses too little is green all the way down**, which is
why both of these survived their own review and why the repair for each began by reproducing it.

**GUARD ONE.** [`apps/admin/src/page.ts`](../apps/admin/src/page.ts)'s uuid was `\b`-ANCHORED, and a
`\b` is a WORD boundary, so a word character on either side removed it and the token stopped
matching. Writing `ID` for a uuid: `see ID`, `manual-review-ID` and `ref:ID` threw, while
`linked_to_ID`, `xID` and `IDy` passed. An underscore is a word character, which is why the first of
those three is the spelling a real payload carries. **`M6-A-55` was written first and 4 of its 7
cases were red on the committed regex.**

**BOTH BOUNDARIES ARE DROPPED RATHER THAN REPLACED BY A LOOKAROUND, AND THE REASON IS A PROPERTY
RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE.** Removing an assertion from a regex can only ADD matches, so the new
pattern refuses a **strict superset** of the old one: **nothing that used to throw now passes**,
asserted over a generated corpus rather than argued. A hex-digit lookbehind was the obvious
alternative and is refused on a measurement: `d` is a hex digit, so `id<uuid>` would still pass, and
`id` is exactly the prefix an operator screen glues onto an identifier. **What the widening newly
rejects: every one of the 94 printable neighbour characters on either side, derived over the range
rather than over three hand-picked cases, plus a uuid shape sitting inside a longer hex-and-dash
run. What it newly accepts: nothing.** The widening is in the NEIGHBOURS and never in the SHAPE,
pinned by four near misses that are still not uuids, because a control that had become "any long hex
string throws" is a control the next screen writer turns off.

**One case outside the fence had to move and it is the session's one fence departure.**
[`flags-render.test.ts`](../apps/admin/test/flags-render.test.ts)'s `M6-A-45` pinned the defect with
a committed `.not.toThrow()`. A guard repaired into a red suite is not a repaired guard, so the case
is REWRITTEN rather than deleted and now asserts what is still true: the two legs fail at different
times and **neither subsumes the other**, a third party's uuid being invisible to the value leg and
a non-uuid identifier being invisible to the pattern leg.

**GUARD TWO.** [`vg2-no-secrets-in-bundle.mjs`](../scripts/ci/vg2-no-secrets-in-bundle.mjs)
hard-coded `BUNDLE_DIRS` to the portal's two directories. **It is a list of paths and not a reading
of the estate**, and its own comment called the portal *"the one deployable that builds a bundle"*,
false since the site's build step landed on 2026-08-27 and falser since `apps/admin` joined `CI-07`
on 2026-08-28. **THE HOLE WAS REPRODUCED FIRST: a real AWS access key id appended to one emitted
file in EACH of the two unscanned bundles, and the committed check exited 0 reporting "no key-shaped
string in client output".**

**Re-derived after all three builds on this tree, because two of the three apps had changed since
the figures in the dispatch:** `apps/portal` 249 files and 5,831,402 bytes SCANNED, `apps/site` 219
and 4,739,239 NOT, `apps/admin` 121 and 4,024,910 NOT. **249 of 589 files and 5,831,402 of
14,595,551 bytes, 42 per cent by file and 40 per cent by byte, and the check printed `PASS` in the
same words a full scan would.**

**THE REPAIR IS A DERIVATION AND THE SOURCE IT IS DERIVED FROM IS THE WHOLE OF THE DECISION.** Three
sources were available. **The job's steps are REFUSED**: parsing `ci.yml` makes the check a MIRROR of
the job, and a mirror can never notice the step that is missing, which is exactly how this hole
opened. **The directories that exist after a build are REFUSED**: the scan then silently SHRINKS
whenever a build is dropped, which is the same partial-green shape rebuilt from a different
mechanism. **The workspace manifests are TAKEN**, because they answer the question from the
DECLARATION rather than from the artifact, so the expected set is known BEFORE the build and **a
missing bundle is RED rather than a smaller number**. `apps` is read out of `pnpm-workspace.yaml`'s
own `'apps/*'` declaration rather than trusted as a constant.

**That gives `VG-2` a second job on purpose, and it closes session 346's finding 3 from the other
side.** `CI-06/gate-inventory` cannot see a new app joining `CI-07`, because that row's activation
condition was satisfied by the first app and the row is Implemented. **A fourth UI deployable
landing with no build step in `CI-07` now turns `VG-2` red instead of turning nothing red.**

**Six legs falsified against a scratch workspace, each watched failing**, so the repository tree was
never seeded: a bundler that declared a build and never built it, a deployable whose build output
this check cannot locate, a workspace that stops declaring `apps/*`, a workspace where nothing
declares a bundle, a key seeded in the second bundler, and the clean fixture passing. **The widened
scan is CLEAN on the real estate: 589 files, 14,595,551 bytes, exit 0, and nothing was narrowed to
get there.** The note now names every deployable and its own figures, so a partial scan cannot print
the same line as a full one. **`ADR-012` holds and no domain is written anywhere, in any file, in
any form**; what this adds is that the admin bundle is now grepped as well, over 121 files and
4,024,910 bytes, and it is clean.

**FOUR FINDINGS, AND THE FIRST IS THIS SESSION'S OWN DOING.**
[`flags-queue.tsx:239`](../apps/admin/src/app/flags/flags-queue.tsx) still calls the pattern *"a
`\b`-anchored uuid"* and [`ci.yml:325`](../.github/workflows/ci.yml) still reports the
one-of-three scan as an open gap; **both are false as of the two commits above and both are fenced
out**, the first as session 350's and the second on this dispatch's NOT YOURS list, and **nothing
mechanical in this repository can see either one**, measured rather than assumed. Second:
**`scripts/**` is outside `format:check`'s glob entirely**, so the directory holding every gate
runner is unformatted-unchecked and the committed `VG-2` file was not prettier-clean; the rewrite is,
and nothing enforces that. Third: **no citation invariant reaches a session log**, so session 344's
`page.ts:184` pointer resolves to nothing while `RI-15` and `RI-16` hold at 16 of 16. Fourth:
**`VG-1` caught this session's own log and cost a red `CI-05`**: the first draft of the session
file wrote the seeded key-shaped string out in full and `gitleaks git .` reported `leaks found: 1`
over 1,987 commits. **The repair is the commit REWRITTEN rather than a `.gitleaksignore` entry**, on
that file's own stated ground, that session 254's four fingerprints are defended only because their
commits are in `main` while this one sat on an unmerged branch nothing is based on. **A document
that describes a secret-scanner falsification is itself scanned by the secret scanner.** Fifth:
**`apps/site` re-derives 32 bytes below session 346's figure with an identical file count**, and
`next build` is byte-reproducible on this tree across three consecutive builds, so the difference is
a tree difference rather than build noise; the likely reading is a table derived before that
session's own `.tsx` reformat landed, reported as a difference and not as a cause.

**NO ADR NUMBER, NO MIGRATION NUMBER, AND ONE SUITE IDENTIFIER**, `M6-A-55`, appended above the
highest in the tree and appearing in exactly one file. **`docs/testing/STRATEGY.md`'s `VG-2` row was
in the fence CONDITIONALLY, on "if what it says becomes false", and the condition was not met**: the

## 2026-08-28 - Session 350: the 503 three documents state, measured across the whole operator surface, and it is two answers rather than one

**[ADR-190](decisions/ADR-190.md) lands, `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED.** [ALLOCATION](decisions/ALLOCATION.md) row `190`, amended in place under [ADR-065](decisions/ADR-065.md) T3. **No migration number is taken and no file under `apps/api/src` is edited.**

**THE SENTENCE IS FALSE AND THE REASON IT SURVIVED TWO SESSIONS IS THAT IT IS TRUE OF MOST OF THE SURFACE.** [WAVE-06](plans/WAVE-06-admin-console-transport.md) section 4.1 says *"every one of the 26 operator routes above answers 503 today"*. Measured here over a real `compose()` and Fastify's own `inject`, **every registered operator route injected one at a time**, which nobody had done: the operator deployment registers **28** routes and withholds **45**; **23** are `/admin/*`; the **ten** served by `admin-reads.ts`'s shared `adminHandler` answer **401 `unauthenticated`** with no admin session cookie and **500 `internal_error`** with one, and the **thirteen** served by the four write backends answer **503 `service_unavailable`** before authenticating at all.

**TWO OF THE RESERVATION'S PREMISES DID NOT SURVIVE.** The sentence is section **4.1**'s, not section 8.1's, and the fence held 8.1 only. And *"a new code is a change to `STATUS_CODE`'s closed table"* is **false**: [API_CONTRACT:82](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) declares `service_unavailable` at 503 in section 2's canonical table, which refutes session 336's *"section 2's canonical table, which carries no 503 and no `service_unavailable`"* at its own line.

**THE RULING IS THAT THE 500 STAYS, ON A GROUND THE RESERVATION DID NOT CARRY, AND IT WAS EXECUTED RATHER THAN ARGUED.** `AdminReadError` has **fifteen** throw sites and only **two** mean *"no source is wired"*; twelve refuse the DATA a wired source returned. With `STATUS_CODE` and `TITLE` patched so a 503 really reached the wire, **12 cases failed across 2 files**, among them *"a liability body carrying a float in cents is refused"* and *"a pack whose digest is not a SHA-256 is refused"*. A 503 would answer *try again shortly* to a float in a money field.

**AND THE FENCE'S CONDITIONAL IS UNUSABLE, MEASURED.** `AdminReadError` was given `readonly statusCode = 503` and **44 of 44 cases still passed with the answer still 500**, because `server.ts`'s `STATUS_CODE` has no 503 key. `admin-reads.ts` cannot move its own status, so it is byte for byte unchanged.

**THE ANSWER IS EIGHT STATES AND NOT TWO**, each pinned by a case, and state **F** -- an admitted operator meeting a second uncomposed port behind the first -- was in no document. **THE THREE 500 STATES ARE ONE DOCUMENT ON THE WIRE DELIBERATELY**: a response that distinguished them would tell an unauthenticated caller which of this deployment's ports are uncomposed.

**THE CONSOLE RULE IS NARROWER THAN A CORRECTED NUMBER: a screen renders no error kind it did not receive.** `apps/admin/src/app/page.tsx` drops `NOT_YET`, the `AdminErrorKind` import and `data-error`; `M6-A-60` sweeps the whole `src/app/` directory with a counterfactual over `http/client.ts`; `M6-A-61` reads the served bytes. **`unavailable` stays in the vocabulary and now has thirteen named producers.**

**TWO FINDINGS REGISTERED RATHER THAN REPAIRED.** The thirteen 503 routes **confirm their own existence to an anonymous caller**, which is the disclosure `admin-writes.ts:823`'s own comment refuses one line before it happens. And **`server.ts` names only 7 of section 2's 16 codes**, so nine cannot be produced by a throw and 18 call sites spell the 503 title by hand; latent, because every 503 in this tree is built and sent rather than thrown.

**ONE OF THE SENTENCE'S SIX HOMES IS REPAIRED AND FIVE ARE REGISTERED WITH THEIR LINE NUMBERS** (`WAVE-06:248`, `:445`, `:581`, `apps/admin/src/http/client.ts:178` and `:198`, `apps/admin/src/index.ts:345`), because the fence was section 8.1 only.

**FIVE SEEDED DEFECTS, FIVE CAUGHT**, tree clean after each. Measured with `pnpm install` first, each command run separately and `pnpm run verify` never run, against a `main` baseline at `9dca218d` reproduced before a line changed: 33 of 33 gates, 16 of 16 invariants, `typecheck` 0, `lint` 0, `format:check` clean, **222 test files / 5,234 passed / 6 skipped** where `main` gives 222 / 5,220 / 6, `falsify.mjs` clean with the tree clean after it, and `pnpm --filter @merit/admin build` still **three** routes.

## The event feed screen lands and its adapter cannot be written, because `events` is not a table key (2026-08-28, session 349)

**[WAVE-06](plans/WAVE-06-admin-console-transport.md)'s `W6-h` lands in full. The feed ADAPTER it was dispatched with does not exist, and the reason is a compile error rather than an unwritten file.** The event feed at `/feed`, both `INV-M6-10` modes, `GET /admin/events`'s query, item and envelope transcribed into [`api/types.ts`](../apps/admin/src/api/types.ts), and `M6-A-55` through `M6-A-61` as 27 cases. `next build` compiles **four routes** where session 344 left three.

**THE LARGEST FINDING IS THE HALF THAT DID NOT LAND. `events` IS NOT A `TableKey` AND [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts) DECLARES NO DRIZZLE TABLE FOR IT AT ALL.** Derived at reporting time by importing the registry rather than by reading a document: `TABLE_KEYS` holds 106 names and the only event-ish members are `pspWebhookEvents` and `kycFunnelEvents`. So a `Tx` naming `'events'`, in the shape [`admin-source/flags.ts`](../apps/api/src/admin-source/flags.ts) and [`admin-source/graph.ts`](../apps/api/src/admin-source/graph.ts) both use, is **`TS2322`, `Type 'SystemTx' is not assignable`**, which was seeded and watched. ## 2026-08-28 - Session 351: the sixth scope class, and the table two sessions were sent to register and neither could

**[ADR-191](decisions/ADR-191.md) LANDS, `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED. [ALLOCATION](decisions/ALLOCATION.md) rows `191` and `0058` amended in place ([ADR-065](decisions/ADR-065.md) T3). MIGRATION `0058` IS RETURNED TO THE POOL UNSPENT.**

**RULED: A ROW THAT REACHES AN IDENTITY TWO DIFFERENT WAYS IS SCOPED BY BOTH, AND THE SIXTH CLASS IS `either`.** One nullable column declared `REFERENCES identities(id)` beside one nullable foreign key to a table that itself reaches an identity, with the predicate their **DISJUNCTION**. `events` is registered under it and is a member of `ScopedTableKey`, which `pair` is not. Registry **106 to 107 of 114**, **63** scoped-reachable, at 1 root / 41 owned / 20 derived / 3 pair / 1 either / 41 firm, every figure derived at the moment of reporting.

**THE RESERVATION'S HARD QUESTION -- WHICH HALF MAY A RULE LOSE -- IS ANSWERED WITH A COUNT AND NOT A PREFERENCE: NEITHER.** Of the **29** catalogue rows carrying the `TL` consumer, **10** name an account and no identity, **9** name an identity and no account, **6** name both, and **4** carry their payload in a prose block the reader cannot parse and are excluded rather than assumed. So an `owned` rule loses at least ten of twenty-nine and a `derived` hop at least nine. **The proxy is stated rather than hidden**: [EVENTS](architecture/EVENTS.md) records no per-event ROW tenancy anywhere, and the payload is the only grain statement the catalogue makes.

**THE CLASS IS NARROW AND THAT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN CLAIMED.** Eight tables in the migration set declare BOTH a column `REFERENCES identities(id)` and one `REFERENCES accounts(id)` -- `risk_flags`, `payout_requests`, `events`, `certificates`, `journal_entries`, `graduation_benefits`, `account_adjustments`, `plan_size_unlocks` -- and **`events` is the only one whose identity column is NULLABLE**. The other seven are correctly `owned`: a `NOT NULL` identity column already covers every row and there is no disjunction to write. **The suite reads that discrimination out of the DDL in both directions**, so a reader that stopped matching fails on the member it must find and on the seven it must refuse.

**PRECEDENCE BETWEEN THE LEGS IS REFUSED, AND IT IS THE CLAUSE A LATER SESSION WILL TRY TO HARDEN.** Guarding the account leg on `identity_id IS NULL` would guarantee no row ever reaches two identity uuids, at the cost of one conjunct. The rows the legs disagree on are the rows a **HARD MERGE** produces: a merge repoints ownership into the surviving `identities` row and `accounts.identity_id` moves with it, while this table is **APPEND-ONLY, no UPDATE, no DELETE** by `0017`'s own comment, so an account-level event written before a merge names the merged identity on the row and the survivor through the account. **Precedence hands it to the identity that no longer logs in and hides it from the person who owns the account**, which is `purchases`' own refusal in this registry -- *"a strict subset of a merged person's purchase history, silently"* -- arriving one table over.

**`events` IS SERVED BY THE SCOPED ACCESSOR WHERE A `pair` TABLE IS REFUSED, AND THE GROUND IS ABSENT RATHER THAN OUTWEIGHED.** [ADR-106](decisions/ADR-106.md) clause 2 excludes a pair table because every row a disjunction returns carries the other party's identity uuid out of a `NOT NULL` column. Here `identity_id` is this person and `account_id` is this person's account: **no row this predicate returns discloses a second party through a tenancy column.**

**THE PAYLOAD OBJECTION IS RULED ON RATHER THAN RESURRECTED, AND A MEASUREMENT IS WHAT DISPOSES OF IT.** Exactly **two** payloads in the catalogue name a second identity -- `kyc.dedupe_hit`'s `matched_identity_id` and `identity.merged`'s `merged_identity_id` -- and **NEITHER IS CONSUMED BY `TL`**, the only trader-facing consumer the legend defines. So the corpus's own catalogue already excludes both from the surface `INV-M4-06` is about, and it excludes them **by a projection**, which is the division the entry rules: a scope rule states which ROWS reach an identity and nothing about what is inside one, which is `idempotency_keys`' sentence out of this same migration set.

**A ROW REACHING NEITHER LEG BELONGS TO NO IDENTITY AND IS RETURNED TO NOBODY**, with no third predicate needed, because SQL NULL never equals anything. **This is the first class in the registry whose `firm` half is a property of the ROW rather than of the table.**

**`0058` IS RETURNED AND THE REASON IS THREE CANDIDATE CONSTRAINTS WRITTEN OUT AND REJECTED.** `CHECK (identity_id IS NOT NULL OR account_id IS NOT NULL)` forbids the firm rows the class exists to admit. A trigger asserting `events.identity_id` agrees with `accounts.identity_id` is **false on purpose after every hard merge** and a probe asserting it would fire on every merged account's history. `CHECK (subject_kind NOT IN ('identity','account') OR ...)` does not catch the actual counterexample, whose subject is a payout request. **The obligation that remains is per-EVENT-NAME over a 117-row catalogue, and a CHECK over an event-name list puts the catalogue in the database and needs a migration per event.**

**THE COUNTEREXAMPLE THIS ENTRY WAS HANDED IS ANSWERED RATHER THAN CLOSED, AND IT IS THE SHARPEST OPEN ITEM.** [`apps/api/src/events.ts`](../apps/api/src/events.ts) calls `payout.freeze_expiring` *"the counterexample any sixth class has to answer"*: its payload names neither tenancy column. **The answer is that a row's tenancy columns and its payload are different things** -- EVENTS.md says `wallet.credited` carries `account_id` on the row *"resolved through `reference_id` at write time"* precisely because the trader timeline is a per-account view -- so a producer writing neither column on a trader-subject event is a **PRODUCER defect**, not a hole in the class. **The failure is SILENT**: the row belongs to nobody and simply never appears in the trader's timeline.

**TWO FENCES WERE CROSSED, BOTH FORCED BY A HARD CONTROL, BOTH REPORTED.** Adding a `ScopeClass` member and one registry entry moved `scope.ts` and `scoped-db.ts` enough to drift **seven** line citations that `RI-15` and `RI-16` make hard -- six in `apps/api/**` and one in [ALLOCATION](decisions/ALLOCATION.md) row `168`, which is not this session's row -- taking the invariants to 14 of 16 and the suite red. Separately, `apps/api/src/events.ts` told an operator **in a thrown message** that *"packages/db/src/scope.ts registers no rule for the table"*, and a case asserted `schema.ts` declares no `pgTable('events'`; both are false from this entry. **THE SINK WAS NOT WIRED** -- `db.ts` is still the one file naming `@merit/db`, no writer is composed -- and the admin feed adapter is **unblocked and unwritten**.

Both are refused on grounds that never depended on the type, and both comments recording the type refusal are repaired in the same diff. **This is [ADR-106](decisions/ADR-106.md)'s `affiliate_commissions` shape arriving on a second class.**

**A REGISTRATION IN `packages/db` FALSIFIES PROSE IN `apps/admin` THAT NO GATE READS, AND IT DID SO TWICE IN ONE WAVE.** [`apps/admin/src/index.ts`](../apps/admin/src/index.ts) says `events` *"is unregistered in `packages/db` and therefore is not a `TableKey`"*, and [`account-detail.tsx`](../apps/admin/src/app/accounts/account-detail.tsx) -- which landed in `W6-j` while this branch was open -- tells an operator **on the screen** that *"`events` is not a `TableKey`"*. **Nothing asserts either, so the suite is green over both.** The second blocker's substance survives and only its reason is false: `AdminReadSource.readAccount` still has no adapter. ## 2026-08-28 - Session 358: three controls that passed while covering less than their own words claimed

**All three are repaired, no ADR number and no migration number were taken, and every item was watched failing before a line moved.** Four commits, one per item plus one correction this session made to its own work.

## The in-flight obligation is a TERM in Open Liability, not a figure beside it (2026-08-28, session 361)

**[ADR-195](decisions/ADR-195.md), `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED. `P-M6-01` HAS THREE COMPONENTS AND THE THIRD IS THE FIRM-SCOPED `withdrawals_in_flight` OBLIGATION**, summed into Open Liability and shown separately like the other two. [`M06:59`](plans/M06-admin-ops-console.md)'s new **`INV-M6-15`** is the rule that follows: **Open Liability does not move when a wallet withdrawal is approved, and it falls when that withdrawal's cash leaves.**

**THE DEFECT IS LARGER THAN [ADR-181](decisions/ADR-181.md) SECTION 7 STATED, AND THE EXTRA HALF IS WHAT DECIDES TERM VERSUS FIGURE.** That entry recorded that an approval *"quietly reduces the reported liability while the cash is still Merit's"*, which is true and is one of three. Under the two-term panel `LT-06` moves only `wallet_balances_cents` and **`LT-07` moves NEITHER term**, so the reported liability falls at the APPROVAL and does not move at the SETTLEMENT; and [ADR-189](decisions/ADR-189.md)'s `LT-09` makes it three, because a rail-exhausted withdrawal would make it RISE at a moment when nothing new is owed. **One missing term, three wrong movements, and a figure placed beside a total cannot repair a total that moves on the wrong events.**

**A FOURTH SHAPE WAS AVAILABLE, NEEDS NO COLUMN AND NO MIGRATION, AND IS REFUSED ON A MEASUREMENT.** Folding the obligation into `wallet_balances_cents` and reading *wallet balance* as *what Merit owes this trader out of the wallet, wherever it sits*, costs nothing. It is refused because [`liability.ts:534`](../apps/admin/src/liability.ts) reads that same column as `P-M6-07`'s `floatCents` on the stated ground that *"one quantity read from one column and shown in two places is a quantity that cannot drift between them"*, so folding overstates the float by every cent in transit, and because [`M20:64`](plans/M20-wallet.md)'s `INV-M20-08` requires wallet balances be segregated *"in reporting and in fact"* where the ledger has already segregated them in fact.

**`INV-M5-15` DOES NOT MOVE AND `M05` IS NOT OPENED AT ALL, AND THOSE ARE TWO ANSWERS RATHER THAN ONE.** Its words do NOT cover the obligation, because after `LT-06` the amount is not a wallet balance. **THE TERM IS RULED AND CANNOT YET BE RENDERED, AND [ADR-195](decisions/ADR-195.md) SECTION 6 LISTS WHAT IS OWED RATHER THAN IMPLYING IT.** The dispatch's *"`liability_snapshots` and the ledger already hold what a term would read"* is **half false and the false half decides**: the LEDGER holds it and that table does not, so under [ADR-188](decisions/ADR-188.md) clause 1's column-for-column projection the field has nothing behind it. **Four things are owed**: a `withdrawals_in_flight_cents bigint NOT NULL` column as a MAGNITUDE, the delta id named by position as [`M06:80`](plans/M06-admin-ops-console.md)'s single unclaimed number between `SD-M6-07` and `SD-M6-09`, the field on `LiabilityResponse`, and the renderer. **No migration number is reserved or taken and `packages/db` is not opened.**

**THE ORDERING CONSTRAINT IS FAVOURABLE AND IS THE SENTENCE A SEQUENCING SESSION NEEDS.** Nothing posts `LT-06` today, so the panel is incomplete rather than wrong; and [`0049:97-98`](../packages/db/migrations/0049_reserve_coverage_snapshots.sql)'s `ADD COLUMN NOT NULL` with no default is still available because `liability_snapshots` still has no producer, re-measured rather than inherited. **Both windows close the day a producer is written**, and a defaulted zero would report an in-flight obligation as none.

[`API_CONTRACT:418`](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md)'s `MarkListItem` writes `traded_day: boolean; win_day: boolean;` on ONE LINE, nineteen lines below the section 1 Time rule the sweep was enforcing. **So the control refused a form its own contract declares, two sections away.**

A boolean is not a failed day**, because no date rendering path produces `true`, and a UTC instant, an epoch second, a `Date` and an unpadded date are all still refused on every one of the 14 declared names.

## An identity is born at the first verified contact, the row it writes carries nothing, and `0060` returns to the pool (2026-08-28, session 365)

**[ADR-196](decisions/ADR-196.md) SHIPS `proposed` WITH AN UNSIGNED APPROVAL LINE. IT RULES AND DOES NOT BUILD, AND IT SAYS SO.** The largest gap between what is built and a product is that nothing creates the row everything else needs, and the repair is four rulings deep rather than one route.

**THE ABSENCE HOLDS ON RE-DERIVATION.** Over every non-test `.ts` file in `apps/` and `packages/`, in all three spellings this tree uses -- raw `INSERT INTO identities`, Drizzle's `insert(identities)` and the accessor's `insert('identities', ...)` -- **zero writes**, against 48 files that mention the table. **And it is a type rather than an oversight**: [`scope.ts:591-594`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts) registers `identities` as `class: 'root'` and [`scoped-db.ts:365-368`](../packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts)'s `OwnedTableKey` admits only `owned`.

**THE DISPATCH'S CENTRAL PREMISE IS HALF REFUTED AND THE REFUTATION IS IN ITS FAVOUR: THE TIMING WAS ALREADY RULED, IN A FROZEN DOCUMENT.** [`API_CONTRACT:120`](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md)'s `is_new: boolean` on `VerifyResponse` is meaningless at an endpoint that does not create the row, and its only other occurrence in the workspace is `is_new: false` in a fixture, so **nothing has ever been able to answer it `true`**. [`:104`](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md)'s `OtpResponse` carries no identity, [`:91`](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) says the endpoint deliberately does not reveal whether the destination exists, [`SECURITY:297`](architecture/SECURITY.md) puts the row **before** phone verification by naming the degraded-window residual as *"identities exist that have not proven they hold their number"*, and [`0002:305-307`](../packages/db/migrations/0002_identity.sql) refuses the earlier moment in a merged migration.

**THE RULING.** An identity comes into existence at `POST /auth/verify`, on a code that verifies, when the address resolves to no existing `users` row. **The identity and its first `users` row are one unit of work.** The row is written with **defaults only**, so `INSERT INTO identities DEFAULT VALUES` is the whole statement, and **the root of every scope rule in this corpus holds no personal data at all**: email on `users`, phone a hash on `identity_phones`, signals digests, and `display_name`, `max_accounts_override` and `support_contact_ref` NULL deliberately. **That emptiness is ruled a control rather than an accident of Wave 1**, which binds `M13`, `M14` and `M19` to a second table with a foreign key.

**AT FIRST PURCHASE IS NOT LATE, IT IS UNREACHABLE**, because both checkout endpoints declare `required: 'session'` ([`checkout.ts:2437`](../apps/api/src/routes/checkout.ts), [`:2501`](../apps/api/src/routes/checkout.ts)) and `sessions -> users -> identities`. **That discharges [ADR-183](decisions/ADR-183.md)'s own "most likely wrong" paragraph and confirms `0054`'s instant as merged.** **At OTP request costs four permanent rows per typed address** -- one `identities` plus three `ledger_accounts` from [`0054:144-146`](../packages/db/migrations/0054_identity_ledger_accounts.sql)'s trigger -- under `ON DELETE RESTRICT` everywhere and retention *"forever"*.

**FOUND, IN NO DOCUMENT IN THIS CORPUS, ON THE MONEY PATH: THE `sms` CHANNEL CANNOT REGISTER ANYBODY.** [`0002:248`](../packages/db/migrations/0002_identity.sql)'s `users.email citext NOT NULL UNIQUE` meets a `VerifyRequest` presenting two symmetric channels, so `is_new` is always false there and SMS is a login channel only.

**`LT-01` POSTED END TO END, WHICH NO SESSION HAD DONE.** Against the 58-file schema on PostgreSQL 16: an identity created the ruled way, then the shipped [`lt01`](../apps/api/src/routes/payouts.ts) builder and the shipped [`postTransaction`](../packages/ledger/src/post.ts) over a real connection. The trigger opened all three positions, `resolve` found them instead of throwing, four entries posted, 40,000c to the wallet, 10,000c recognized at approval, withdrawable drained to 0, global sum 0.

**`0060` RETURNS TO THE POOL UNSPENT, AND THE REFUSAL IS A MEASUREMENT.** The candidate `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` constraint trigger was written and executed: it accepts the ruled shape and refuses the OTP-time shape at COMMIT. A clean A/B over all 15 `probe_*.sql` scripts is **15 of 15 pass without it and 14 with it**, the casualty being [`probe_ledger_constraints.sql`](../scripts/db/probe_ledger_constraints.sql), the acceptance script for `0054`'s own trigger. It also has no caller, and an `AFTER INSERT` trigger never sees the `UPDATE` a merge uses. **This is the seventh time the pool has absorbed a number**, per the `0060` row's own naming of three precedents as the fourth, fifth and sixth.

**THE BUILD IS PRICED AND THE HONEST COUNT IS 1 OF 4**: the OTP digest (a keyed MAC with nowhere to keep the key, so a deployment secret or a migration), the establishment door in `packages/db`, delivery, then the handler. **This entry is the one [ADR-126](decisions/ADR-126.md) section 7 asked for by name**, and it supplies what that section said was missing: a named caller.

**TWO LANDMINES, BOTH OUTSIDE THE FENCE AND REPORTED.** [`auth-backend.ts:291-297`](../apps/api/src/auth-backend.ts)'s `NO_PRE_IDENTITY_READ` is **stale** and ships into a live 503's log line, telling an operator that a pre-identity read has no door where [ADR-126](decisions/ADR-126.md) built it as `resolutionDb`; and **`resolutionDb` has no caller anywhere in `apps/`**.

**No migration was written, `packages/db` was not opened, no code was edited and no test moved.** 33 of 33 gates, 16 of 16 invariants, typecheck 0, lint 0, `format:check` clean, `falsify.mjs` clean with its output read, and 227 files / 5,429 passed / 6 skipped against a `main` baseline at `087fa570` of 227 / 5,429 / 6 reproduced exactly before a line changed.
